title: fix(email): make Outlook/Gmail mail show up in the email app
body:
## Why

User connected Microsoft Outlook but no mail appeared in the email app. Diagnosed against the live VPS — the mail was actually synced (200 messages in `email_messages`) but three independent bugs sat between the database and the screen, plus two that would break things shortly after.

## Bugs fixed (all confirmed against production)

1. **Doubled API path → 404.** The email app's `gatewayFetch` prefixed `/api/email` while every caller also passed `/email/...`, producing `/api/email/email/accounts` → gateway `/email/email/accounts` → `404`. Gateway logs showed this repeating. Now prefixes `/api`.
2. **Folder mismatch → empty inbox.** Providers stored opaque provider folder IDs (Outlook `parentFolderId`, Gmail `labelIds[0]`) while the UI/gateway query `WHERE folder='inbox'`. Added `canonical_folder()` and normalize on sync; gateway folder filter is now case-insensitive and treats `starred` as a flag.
3. **Background sync never started.** `start_background_sync()` used structlog-style kwargs on a stdlib logger → `TypeError: Logger._log() got an unexpected keyword argument 'accounts'` (seen in journal as `gateway.email_sync_skipped`). Converted scheduler logging to `%s`.
4. **Token refresh impossible.** OAuth callback stored tokens without `client_id`/`client_secret`/`tenant_id`. Now persisted with the token blob, plus write-back of rotated tokens after sync/folder calls.
5. **Gmail `received_at` always None** (`datetime.timezone` used on the `datetime` class).

## Post-merge steps
- CI auto-deploys (restarts `acb-gateway`, rebuilds workbench).
- Reconnect the Outlook mailbox so the stored credentials include the app client id/secret (old row predates fix #4). Next sync rewrites folders canonically and mail appears.
- Stale `anonymous` duplicate account already removed from prod DB.

## Tests
- `tests/unit/test_email_folders.py` (folder normalization) — passing.
- All changed Python files byte-compile.

title: fix(email,memory): reconnect UI for stale OAuth + route mem0 through LiteLLM tier
body:
## Why
Follow-up to PR #4. Two prod issues surfaced while verifying email sync:

1. **Outlook account stuck on "Provider authentication failed"** with no way to fix it. The OAuth callback rejected re-auth of an existing account (`error=duplicate`), so a stale refresh token could never be repaired from the UI ("it says it's already connected").
2. **mem0 memory extraction failing with OpenRouter `402`** ("LLM extraction failed") — it hardcoded `deepseek/deepseek-chat`, which the gateway `/v1` doesn't recognize as a tier and routed to OpenRouter (out of credits).

## What
**Email reconnect**
- OAuth callback now **updates** an existing account's credentials in place instead of rejecting as duplicate — clears the error state and resets `last_history_id` to force a full re-sync (also re-normalizes mail stored under raw provider folder IDs).
- `/email/accounts` now returns `sync_status`/`sync_error`.
- Integrations → Email: **Reconnect** button per OAuth account + inline error banner with a reconnect CTA, and the status dot turns red with "Auth error" instead of a misleading green "Active".

**mem0 tiering**
- mem0 now sends the `tier-fast` alias so it routes through the configured DeepSeek tier (matching `graphiti_client`).

## Verification
- `python -m py_compile` on both backend files: ✅
- `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in the edited file ✅
- Live VPS tiers confirmed DeepSeek-backed (no OpenRouter) for `tier-fast`/`tier-balanced`.

## Post-deploy (manual)
User reconnects the Outlook account via the new button → next sync authenticates and surfaces the inbox.

title: Make email app a fully-featured, two-way-synced client
body:
## Summary

Fixes the core **"clicking an email shows a blank reading pane"** bug and brings the email client toward Outlook/Gmail parity (folders, statuses, two-way write-back). Based on a full review of the stack against `spec_email_ai_assistant.md` (see `ai-company-brain/email_app_review.md`).

### Reading pane (the headline bug)
Root cause was twofold: Outlook sync stored only `bodyPreview` (empty `body_text`/`body_html`), and `EmailDetail` rendered plain text only and never fetched the full message.
- New **`MessageContent`** renders HTML in a **sandboxed `<iframe srcDoc>`** (no scripts, links open in new tab, auto-sized) with a plain-text fallback.
- **`EmailDetail`** lazily fetches the full message on selection with a loading state.
- Gateway **`get_message`** hydrates the body from the provider on demand when the stored body is empty, persisting body + attachment metadata.

### Two-way sync (write-back to provider)
- New `BaseEmailProvider.apply_flags()` / `move_to_folder()` (no-op defaults so IMAP degrades gracefully).
- **Gmail**: label translation (read/star/important, archive/trash/spam). **Outlook**: PATCH `isRead`/`flag` + `/move`; trash → Deleted Items.
- `update_message` / `delete_message` push changes best-effort; opening an email marks it read on the provider.

### Folders pulled from the mailbox
- Sidebar now shows canonical system folders **+ the provider's own user folders/labels**; stops clobbering the folder tree on each list fetch. Added **Junk**; wired the sidebar search box.
- Initial sync fetches all standard folders (inbox/sent/drafts/archive/junk/trash), not just inbox+sent.

### Statuses (importance / categories / flag)
- New `importance` (high/normal/low) and `categories` captured from both providers, persisted (`migration 18_email_message_status.sql`), and surfaced in the list and detail.

## Testing notes
- ✅ Python files compile (`py_compile`); lucide icons confirmed present in-repo.
- ⚠️ The Next.js build and live-provider behavior were **not** runnable in this environment (no `node_modules`, no mailbox creds) — please validate the frontend type-check and provider write-back against a real account.

## Known limitations (phase 2, documented in the review)
Incremental sync is inbox-only (other folders refresh on full sync/reconnect); Outlook `/move` returns a new message id to reconcile; Gmail user-label names aren't resolved to chips yet; Move/Label toolbar buttons still need a picker UI; no draft autosave or threaded view yet.

title: fix(deploy): apply Postgres migrations 02+ on deploy (fixes email 500)
body:
## Problem

The email app returns a **gateway 500** on open. Root cause: the email list/detail endpoints `SELECT em.importance, em.categories` (`apps/gateway/gateway/routes/email.py:680,721`), but those columns — added by `infra/postgres/18_email_message_status.sql` — were **never applied to the live database**.

The Postgres container only mounts `00_create_databases.sql` and `01_schema.sql` into `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d`, and those only run on **first** DB init. **Nothing in the deploy pipeline applied migrations `02`–`18`**, so the new columns never reached prod → `UndefinedColumn` → 500. (Earlier migrations like 17 had been applied by hand; 18 fell through the gap.)

## Fix

- **`scripts/apply_migrations.sh`** *(new)* — idempotent runner that applies `infra/postgres` migrations `02+` against the `acb-postgres` container via `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`. All migrations `02+` use `IF NOT EXISTS` / `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so it's safe on every deploy.
- **`17_email_accounts.sql`** — make the 3 account indexes `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` so the full migration set is re-runnable.
- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** + **`deploy/hostinger/deploy.sh`** — invoke the runner after the stack is healthy, before restarting the gateway.

Result: the next deploy applies migration 18 (fixing the 500) and all future migrations auto-apply, closing the gap permanently.

title: fix(db): drop invalid mcp_servers seed unblocking email migration
body:
## Problem

The previous deploy (PR #9) added a migration runner that applies `infra/postgres` migrations `02+` on every deploy. It works — but it surfaced a **pre-existing bug in migration 13** that blocks the chain before reaching migration 18 (the email `importance`/`categories` columns), so the email app still 500s:

```
ERROR: new row for relation "mcp_servers" violates check constraint "mcp_servers_transport_check"
DETAIL: Failing row contains (filesystem, ..., http-sse, ..., null[url] ...)
```

The seed `INSERT` declared the `filesystem`/`postgres` rows as `transport='http-sse'` with a `NULL` url, which violates the table's CHECK constraint (`http-sse` requires a url). It went unnoticed because migrations were never replayed through a strict (`ON_ERROR_STOP`) runner before.

## Fix

Remove the `mcp_servers` seed `INSERT` entirely. We're not building out MCP-server functionality right now, so the example rows aren't needed. The `mcp_servers` table and all code paths that reference it (executor injection, integrations CRUD) are untouched — servers can still be registered via the API/UI later.

With the broken seed gone, the runner proceeds through migration 18, the `importance`/`categories` columns land in prod, and the email app 500 is resolved.

title: feat(email): trip reconnect banner immediately on live-call 401
body:
## What

Make the in-app reconnect banner trip **immediately** when a live provider call fails on auth, instead of waiting for the next background sync cycle.

Previously the banner keyed only off `sync_status === "error"`, which is set by the background sync. A freshly-expired OAuth token therefore wouldn't surface in the email app until the next sync ran.

## Changes

- **`lib/api.ts`** — `gatewayFetch` attaches the HTTP `status` to thrown errors so callers can distinguish 401/403.
- **`lib/emailStore.ts`** — new `authErrors{ accountId → message }` state; `fetchFolders` sets it on a 401/403 from the live folder fetch and clears it on a later success.
- **`page.tsx`** — the reconnect banner now shows when `syncStatus === "error"` **or** an account is flagged with an auth error.

Since `fetchFolders` runs on every account/folder selection, the banner appears the moment the inbox can't reach the provider — no sync-cycle delay. Builds on PR #11.

title: fix(agents): prune registry, correct MAF/Copilot SDK labels, fix chat picker scroll
body:
Bundles three related agent-registry / picker changes.

## 1. Honor config.json `runtime` (correct MAF vs Copilot SDK labels)
Runtime was classified by a source heuristic (`repo_name && !local_path → github-copilot`), so every GitHub-sourced agent was mislabelled Copilot SDK — even `email-assistant`, which declares `"runtime": "maf"`. Now the agent's `config.json` `runtime` is authoritative (`_normalize_runtime` + `_declared_runtime`, applied in `_load_dynamic_agents` and `list_agents`). Undeclared agents keep the heuristic, so it's a no-op for anything that doesn't opt in.

**Result:** `task-manager`, `apis-config`, `email-assistant`, `reconciler` → **MAF**; the dynamic GitHub-repo agents (`agent-sales-assistant`, `agent-startup-guru`, `agent-project-manager`) → **Copilot SDK**.

## 2. Prune the registry
Remove **sales, triage, delivery, billing, strategy** completely:
- from `_AGENT_REGISTRY`, `_KNOWN_AGENTS`, and `_WEBHOOK_ROUTES` (zoho→sales, gmail→triage, etc.)
- `reconciler.agent_runtime` set to `maf`
- **Dangling references cleaned** so removal is complete: `email.py` draft-consult delegated to the removed `sales` → redirected to the real `agent-sales-assistant`; orchestrator `delegate_to_agent` prompt drops the billing/triage examples.

Remaining static agents: `task-manager`, `reconciler`, `apis-config`, `email-assistant`.

## 3. Fix chat new-session picker scroll
The agent list could overflow the viewport. The modal is now a bounded flex column (`max-h-[85vh]`) with a single scrollable body wrapping all agent sections; removed the redundant nested `max-h-72` on the MAF list.

## Notes
- `email-assistant` is a static built-in: its **label** is now MAF (from its config), but its execution path is left unchanged (no risk to the email app). Aligning static execution to the label is a separate, riskier change.
- `reconciler` has no repo/config and can't actually run; kept per the removal scope (only the 5 named agents were removed) and labelled MAF.

title: feat(loader): auto-install agent dependencies into the shared venv
body:
## Why
Agents are imported into the gateway interpreter and run **in-process**, so every package an agent (or its skills) imports must exist in the **same venv the gateway runs from**. Nothing installed them — the loader only did `git clone`/`pull`, and `uv sync` in deploy only touches the root workspace, not `~/.acb/agents/repos/`. So cloned agents like `agent-sales-assistant` (which needs `apify_client`/`apollo`/`instantly`) silently lost tools to `ImportError` (caught by their `try/except`). This affects **both** MAF and Copilot SDK agents — for a Copilot agent, the Python tools still execute in the gateway venv.

## What
`_install_agent_deps()` runs after every clone/pull (inside `_ensure_repo`, under the per-repo lock — so it covers agent repos **and** skill repos) and after the local-path sync:
- Installs `requirements.txt` (verbatim) and `pyproject [project].dependencies`.
- Skips platform packages (`acb-*`, `agent-framework-*`, `copilot`) — already in the venv.
- Installs into `sys.executable`'s venv via `uv pip install --python <venv>` (uv resolved via PATH or `~/.local/bin`), pip fallback.
- **Best-effort + idempotent**: a SHA-256 of the dep sources is cached in `.git/acb-deps-hash`; unchanged sets are skipped; failures log a warning and never block an agent run.

## Permissions (verified on prod)
- `uv` is on the gateway's service PATH (`/home/acb/.local/bin/uv`).
- `/opt/acb/app/.venv` is owned by and writable by the gateway user (`acb`).
So installs have the permissions they need, with no infra change. The gateway-startup warm-clone reuses this path, so deps are restored after every reboot/deploy.

## Design note
This is the **shared-venv** approach (one venv, deps installed into it), which is the correct match for the current in-process execution model — a per-agent venv would require running each agent as a subprocess, a much larger re-architecture. Trade-off: all agents share one dependency resolution (incompatible version pins between agents would conflict); fine for a curated first-party fleet.

title: fix(settings/llm): persist model visibility + tiers in Postgres
body:
## Problem

Model visibility (the eye-toggle on **Settings → Models**) and **tier** assignments didn't stick — hidden models reappeared and tiers reverted, in email and chat too.

Root cause: both were saved to **git-tracked files** (`infra/enabled_models.json`, `infra/litellm/tier_overrides.yaml`). The deploy runs `git reset --hard origin/main`, so every push reverted them to the committed version. (A comment even wrongly claimed `tier_overrides.yaml` was untracked.) This is the same class of bug already fixed for the agent registry via `dynamic_agents`.

## Fix

Move both to a new `model_config` Postgres table (key/value JSONB), so config survives `git reset --hard`, restarts, and reboots.

- `infra/postgres/35_model_config.sql` — `model_config` table (idempotent; applied by `apply_migrations.sh` on deploy)
- `packages/acb_llm/acb_llm/model_config.py` — `load_blob`/`save_blob` (sync psycopg, same connection style as `key_store`)
- `apps/gateway/gateway/routes/settings.py` — `_load_catalogue`/`_save_catalogue` (key `enabled_models`) and `_load_tier_overrides`/`_save_tier_override`/`_load_config` (key `tier_overrides`) now use the DB
- `packages/acb_llm/acb_llm/client.py` — tier init reads overrides from the DB so routing survives restart

## Migration & safety

- **Seeding:** on first read, existing JSON/YAML is imported once into the DB, then the files are ignored — nothing lost.
- **Fallback:** if Postgres is unreachable, it gracefully falls back to the files.
- `config.yaml` remains the file-based tier *default*.

## Verification

- `py_compile` clean on all changed files.
- Modules import in the `uv` venv; confirmed the DB-unreachable fallback loads tiers from the legacy file.

title: Task Manager: capture story feature-complete — sync pull, AI clarify + agent rail, atomizer/dedup, email→task, settings
body:
## Summary

Seven feature commits that take the GTD task manager's **capture → inbox → clarify → organize** loop to feature-complete, wire in the `task-manager` MAF agent, and give the app its own settings — every slice browser-E2E-verified against a real Postgres + gateway stack.

### 1. Provider sync pull (`f4d4fe2`)
`POST /tasks/sync` pulls existing ClickUp tasks into the GTD mirror via a new `BaseTaskProvider.list_tasks` (paginated, incremental cursor). GTD lens on pulled rows: closed→DONE, backlog→SOMEDAY, mine→NEXT, others'→WAITING (+`gtd_waiting`), unassigned→team-pool NEXT. Overlay-preserving upsert — re-syncs never clobber user decisions; provider owns completion. Background pull on app open + per-workspace Sync button + `gtd_sync` agent tool.

### 2. Inbox/capture feature-complete + agent rail (`9cb2a7b`)
The server AI clarify proposal (org-knowledge capability matching, project auto-match, stage defaults) now upgrades the Clarify panel in place — human edits always win. The AssistantRail placeholder became a live chat pinned to the `task-manager` agent (email-app pattern: shared AgentChat, sessions, Mem0, live GTD persona, quick actions).

### 3. Harness Tier 1 (`3417476`)
App-level pass against awesome-harness-engineering: risk annotations on all 13 GTD tools (machine-checked invariant: **no destructive tool** — C-04), lethal-trifecta guards (SYNCED text delimited as data), the first agent-quality eval suite (which immediately caught + fixed two real heuristic bugs: substring hint matching misfiling "profile…" as REFERENCE, and duplicate-project proposals), and `tool_scope` adoption. Spec: `ai-company-brain/specs/task_manager_harness_2026-07.md`.

### 4. Mind-dump atomizer + capture dedup (`4311f41`)
`POST /tasks/ai/atomize`: a pasted paragraph becomes individual atomic captures, each judged against open items — `new` / `similar` ("same or different?" — the human decides) / `duplicate` (auto-skipped, undoable). LLM does the split + judgment; a deterministic splitter + token similarity is both the fallback and the guardrail (an unsupported LLM "duplicate" claim degrades to "similar" — a poisoned title can never silently discard a capture). Wired into sweep review, single capture (background check + resolution banner), and the agent's capture tools.

### 5. Email → task capture (`28a1037`)
The email inbox becomes a GTD capture channel: "Add to Tasks" in the email right-click context menu (single + bulk), desktop toolbar, and mobile toolbar. The LLM drafts a capture naming the ask (deterministic fallback); items land in the inbox with an `origin` link (migration 50), idempotent per email. Also fixes the GTD-audit calendar gap: a calendar decision now requires a date.

### 6. Origin through the lifecycle (`2c160a9`)
The email reference follows the task everywhere: chips on every list row, inbox-card line, clarify header, item detail — all with deep links (`/email?account=…&email=…`, consumed via `openEmailById`). Pushing an email-origin item to ClickUp appends the source reference to the description; the agent's `gtd_list` shows it too.

### 7. Per-user settings (`f0aaa5f`)
`gtd_settings` (migration 51) + `GET/PUT /tasks/settings` + a Settings dialog (email-app model-roles parity, per user): AI tier per function — assistant chat / atomizer / email drafting / clarify — with tiers + enabled-models pickers, plus capture-dedup and auto-sync toggles that actually gate behavior. Includes a proxy fix: `/api/tasks` never forwarded PUT.

## Migrations
`50_gtd_item_origin.sql` (origin JSONB + index) · `51_gtd_settings.sql` — both idempotent, picked up by `apply_migrations.sh` on deploy.

## Verification
- **Browser E2E** (Playwright vs real Postgres + gateway + Next): 12/12 capture→clarify→convert, 5/5 atomizer/dedup, 7/7 email→task across both apps, 4/4 origin lifecycle + deep link, 6/6 settings persistence.
- **Tests**: 122 unit + trajectory evals green (GTD golden suite: clarify branches, sync lens, safety invariants, atomizer, settings).
- **Lint/build**: ruff + eslint at zero delta vs baseline; `next build` green throughout.
- Direct gateway curls for every new endpoint (sync, atomize, capture-from-email incl. idempotency, settings partial-update).

## Notes for review
- All provider writes remain human-gated (C-04) — the agent has no destructive tool, and that's now eval-locked.
- `schema.generated.sql` refresh + running migrations 50–51 happen on the deploy box as usual.

title: feat(tasks): clarify × ClickUp live upgrades, dense inbox list, capture attachments
body:
Six-feature batch on the GTD task manager's clarify + capture stages (spec: `ai-company-brain/specs/task_manager_app.md` §9.1 changelog, updated in this PR).

## What's in here

**2. Delegate defaults to ClickUp, auto-push**

**Proxy hardening** (`/api/tasks/[...path]`): multipart uploads and binary downloads pass through byte-exact; idempotent GETs retry once — stale keep-alive sockets to the gateway intermittently 502'd hydration and silently flipped the store to demo/mock data.

title: Dev-velocity tooling: complexity/correctness gates, code-graph MCP, weekly code-health review
body:
Keeps CommandCenter developable by coding agents as it grows. Three layers, grandfather-and-ratchet throughout (current code passes; pressure only on new debt). Full plan + baseline: [`dev_velocity_tooling_2026-07.md`](ai-company-brain/specs/dev_velocity_tooling_2026-07.md).

## Baseline measured (2026-07-04)
Repo-wide avg cyclomatic complexity is healthy (~6.9, grade B) — the problem is a *tail*: `executor.run_agent_stream` is **cc 223** in a **5,020-line** file; 33 files over 800 LOC. That tail is what makes files un-editable by agents.

## Commits

**1. `chore(ci)` — complexity + correctness gates**
- `xenon` complexity ceiling **blocking** (grandfathered: `abs=F` covers cc=223, `avg=B` is the ratchet — a PR worsening the average, or adding a function worse than today's worst, fails).
- `ruff` correctness **blocking** (F821/F601/F602/F502/F7/B006 — catches real bugs).
- `ruff C901` + full `ruff` + `mypy strict` as **report-only** dashboards (the ~1.3k style backlog is ratcheted down by hand — see below).
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (was a dep with no config) — diff-scoped, no big-bang reformat.

**2. `fix:` — three latent bugs the new correctness gate immediately found**
- `imap.py` `get_message` called a nonexistent parser → NameError on every IMAP single-message fetch.
- `runner.py` AI-draft hydration referenced an undefined `account_user` → NameError on that branch.
- `acb_llm/client.py` duplicate `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` dict key → deduped.

**3. `feat(dev-velocity)` — code-graph MCP + weekly code-health review**
- **L2:** `.mcp.json` commits **CodeGraph** (MIT, local SQLite+tree-sitter, Python+TS) so any coding agent in-repo gets symbol/call-graph navigation. Verified working: indexed 615 files / 15,050 nodes / 51,164 edges.
- **L3:** `scripts/codebase_health.py` (radon-based, read-only measurement) + `codebase-health.yml` (weekly issue) + per-PR `--diff` report + `skills/maintenance/codebase_health_audit/` (the flag-and-propose refactor skill). Runs as GitHub Actions, not an in-app agent (the repo deliberately has no in-app cron).

## Reviewer notes / caveats
- **No blanket `ruff --fix`.** A repo-wide auto-fix was attempted and reverted — it silently deletes this repo's intentional re-exports / side-effecting imports (documented as the "Auto-fix hazard" in the spec). The style backlog is paid down by hand.
- **CodeGraph needs a one-time per-dev install** (`npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph && codegraph init`) — a global binary; review before installing. The committed config is inert until then; the local index is gitignored.
- **Refactor queue** seeded in the spec, `executor.run_agent_stream` (cc 223) first — ties into `core_loop_unification`.

title: Observability: live cross-app agent & model activity, cost, and 8-bit office (E2 Phases 5–6.2)
body:
## What & why

Builds out the observability layer into a live, operator-facing view of **every agent and model across the whole platform** — chat AND every app (email, tasks, …) — with cost, live status, and per-agent error drill-down. Complements the existing post-hoc E2 debug layer (`agent_run` + `/debug`) with the *live* signal.

## Highlights

- **Live activity bus** (`acb_common.activity`): a global `cc:activity` Redis stream. `publish_activity()` is best-effort, non-blocking, never raises; presence keys track in-flight runs and self-heal via TTL.
- **Universal, zero-touch app coverage:** activations are published at the shared choke points, so coverage is automatic:
  - Agent lifecycle — the executor run boundary + `copilot_chat` (the default orchestrator bypasses `run_agent_stream`, so it's instrumented explicitly).
  - Model calls — `acb_llm._emit_usage`, `acompletion_with_fallback` (email/tasks, attributed by module via `_infer_app_source`), and **`v1_compat`** — the OpenAI-compatible endpoint every MAF/Copilot agent POSTs through, which previously emitted nothing.
- **Live LLM cost:** every call is priced via litellm (`completion_cost` → `cost_per_token`; unknown model → “—”). Folded into a per-day Redis rollup → `GET /observability/cost` (per-day, by-model, by-app).
- **Per-agent correlation:** agent runtimes stamp `X-CC-Agent`/`X-CC-Source` via `default_headers`; `v1_compat` reads them so model calls + cost attribute to the specific agent (orchestrator + email-assistant). Fail-soft — absent header falls back to `source="chat"`, so it cannot regress.
- **New `/observability` UI:** 3 views — **Office** (8-bit room: agents work at desks / sleep / error live; server rack lights up per active model; today's $ ticker), **Live feed** (stream + per-call cost), **Cost** (daily bars, by-model, by-app). Click any agent → drawer with recent runs + errors. Dependency-free (CSS keyframes, no chart lib), theme-aware.
- **Gateway API** (EXECUTIVE/AGENT-gated, like `/debug`): `/observability/activity/{recent,stream}`, `/active`, `/roster`, `/cost`.
- **Cleanup:** removed the permanently-shadowed duplicate `/v1/chat/completions` in `main.py` (v1_compat is the real implementation).

## Review findings fixed along the way

A full trace of how activations connect to the chat agents surfaced three real gaps, all fixed: (1) chat-agent model calls + cost were bypassing instrumentation via `v1_compat`; (2) the default orchestrator never showed as working (it doesn't go through `run_agent_stream`); (3) the orchestrator wasn't in the roster (not a registered specialist). See `ai-company-brain/specs/observability_e2.md` (Phases 5, 6, 6.1, 6.2).

## Testing

- **Full unit suite: 813 passing** (+ ~20 new: activity bus / event shaping / source inference / cost pricing incl. unknown→None / cost-rollup aggregation / an end-to-end `v1_compat` TestClient drive incl. header attribution + fail-soft).
- **Frontend:** `next build` clean (page + 6 API routes), `tsc` 0 errors, eslint clean.
- Streaming path rebuilds usage via litellm's own `stream_chunk_builder` **after** the stream, so the provider request + forwarded bytes to the agent are unchanged (zero risk to agent streaming).

## Notes / follow-ups

- Model calls via `v1_compat` for `GitHubCopilotAgent`-based agents (task-manager, apis-config) and Copilot-SDK mutation traffic stay app-level (their SDK client has no header hook here) — their start/end lifecycle events still carry the agent. Per-agent model correlation there needs an SDK-level header pass-through.
- Daily cost rollup is Redis-backed (~45-day TTL) — durable if Redis persists; a Postgres cost table is the durability follow-up.
- `SEC-1` (public Postgres/Redis exposure) is unrelated but worth prioritizing separately.

title: Observability: fix blank page (auth gate) + durable History view
body:
Follow-up to #23 — fixes "observability doesn't seem to be working" and adds a durable history view.

## Why it looked broken
The observability page rendered blank for the operator while chat/email worked fine. Root cause: the observability (and `/debug`) routes were `require_role(EXECUTIVE, AGENT)`, but the Next SSO proxy only forwards `X-User-Role: executive` when the signed-in email is in `EXECUTIVE_EMAILS` — which ships **empty** by default (and the operator's domain isn't the `fracktal.in` default either). So every observability call **403'd**, and the proxies degrade to empty arrays → a **silent blank page**. `chat`/`memory`/`tasks` were unaffected because they aren't role-gated.

## Fix
- **Live views open to any authenticated caller.** `recent` / `stream` / `active` / `roster` / `cost` / `runs` now allow `EXECUTIVE + AGENT + EMPLOYEE` — they expose operational **metadata** (agent / model / tokens / cost / status / error message), not message content. The full message-content trace stays **EXECUTIVE-gated** at `/debug/runs/{id}`.

## History ("can I see history of activity?")
Today's live feed is the ephemeral Redis stream (~2000 events, lost on a Redis flush). Added:
- **`GET /observability/runs`** over the durable `agent_run` table (lean rows: metadata + error message, no trace blob).
- A new **History** tab (filter All / Errors) and repointed the per-agent drawer at it.

This surfaces runs going back as far as retention keeps them — **including data recorded since E2 Phase 2 (2026-07-03), before the live bus even existed** — so there's something to see immediately even if nothing has run through the new code yet.

## Testing
- +4 unit tests (employee-role → 200 on `runs`/`cost`; DB-less degrade to `[]`; bad status filter ignored). **Full unit suite: 817 passing.**
- Frontend: `next build` clean (page + 7 API routes), `tsc` 0 errors, eslint clean.

## Note on security posture
This is a deliberate choice: the operator's own live dashboard should not 403 for a logged-in non-"executive" user. If you'd rather keep it executive-only, the alternative is to set `EXECUTIVE_EMAILS` to include operator emails and revert the gate — happy to switch to that if you prefer.

title: fix(evals): pin window in oversized-message compression eval (HH-1 drift)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the HH-1 eval `test_oversized_email_thread_fits_window_and_keeps_newest`, which had gone vacuous due to tier / window-table drift.

**Root cause:** the eval builds a 200k-char (~78k-token) email and asserts it gets trimmed for `tier-fast`. `tier-fast` now resolves to `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` with a **1,000,000-token** window (`context_window_for` → litellm / fallback table), so the payload fits and `truncated=False`. Overflowing a 1M-token window would require a ~4.5 MB string — impractical to build and tokenize in an eval.

**Fix:** the compression invariant under test is window-agnostic — *"an over-budget single message is trimmed and its newest message survives."* The eval now **pins a small window** (`monkeypatch` on `acb_llm.context.context_window_for`) and adds a precondition asserting the payload really exceeds it. This removes the dependency on the tier's configured model, so the assertion can't drift into vacuity again.

## Testing
- `evals/trajectories/test_message_compression_trajectory.py` — **7 passed**.
- CI-blocking ruff gate (`F821` etc.) — clean.

title: Observability: roomed, layered, configurable agent scenes (+ Higgsfield seam)
body:
Turns the office from "characters floating in a box" into a **composed scene per agent, inside a themed room** — the system that lets us mix-and-match layers and later swap in real (Higgsfield/hand-authored) sprites.

## What's new (`src/app/observability/scene.tsx`)
- **Layered composition** — each agent is built from stacked layers: `room → rug → chair → outfit → hands → head → face → hair → accessory → desk props → desk`, all driven by an `AvatarConfig`.
- **Semantic, configurable look** — `deriveAvatar(name)` maps the agent's **role** (coder / sales / planner / triage / reconciler / orchestrator) to a **room + outfit + accessory + prop signature**, with per-agent variation (skin, hair style/colour) from a name hash. title: Email: fix reply threading + signature, categorized AGUI board, Rapid Inbox Cc fix, and consolidate chat tools (64→41)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the reported reply-threading/signature bug, adds an agent-driven **categorized** email board in chat, polishes the reply UI, fixes a dropped-Cc bug in Rapid Inbox, and consolidates the email agent's tool surface from **64 → 41** while cutting the instruction prompt nearly in half.

## 1. Reply threading + signature (the reported bug)

Replies sent via the draft card landed in *Sent* as a standalone message instead of in the conversation. Root cause: when an account signature was set, the draft-send path sent a **fresh** message with no thread reference, so the provider started a new thread. Fixes:

- **Draft-send** now signs the already-threaded provider draft *in place* (`update_draft`, which preserves the thread) and sends it natively. IMAP (no native draft-send) falls back to a thread-aware fresh send.
- **Gmail** threads by the real conversation id (`thread_id`) rather than a message id; emits `Bcc` (was silently dropped); `update_draft` re-supplies `threadId` and keeps a signed HTML body as HTML.
- **`/send` reply path** resolves the reply target's `thread_id` so Gmail threads even when replying to a non-first message.
- **IMAP** sets `In-Reply-To`/`References` from the reply reference.

## 2. Reply UI

- Reply / Reply-All toggle shows Cc/Bcc for Reply-All (and Forward) and hides them for a sender-only Reply, in both the conversation draft card and the detail composer (with a manual "Cc/Bcc" reveal).
- Stopped the Reply/Reply-All toggle button text wrapping to a second line on narrow (phone) widths.

## 3. Categorized email board (AGUI)

Asking the agent for "emails to reply to, by department" produced categorized prose but a single **flat** interactive card underneath. New `present_email_groups` tool lets the agent drive the card's structure (`[{title, email_ids, note?}]`), rendering each category as its own titled, collapsible, interactive section. A side-effect-free `/email/messages/summaries` endpoint hydrates each row's label server-side. When a board is shown, the raw flat list it was built from is suppressed.

## 4. Rapid Inbox review + Cc fix

Confirmed Rapid Inbox is a read-only lens over the rule engine's per-message categories + Reply Zero buckets (no separate classifier), and drafts via the shared contextual drafter (`/email/draft-reply`) with the signature applied at send. Fixed one bug: reply-all **Cc was silently dropped** (the draft write-path carries no cc) — Cc'd replies now route through the full `/send` path (which carries Cc, threads, and signs), matching the main composer.

## 5. Tool consolidation (64 → 41) + prompt trim

Passes generalized redundant clusters into parameterized tools with **no capability lost** — e.g. `find_priority(kind)`, `read_email(full)`, `resolve_execution(decision)`, `digest(send)`, `sync_account(full/purge)`, `save_knowledge`, `list_patterns(kind)`, `send_email` (absorbs replies), `list_senders(view)`, `set_sender_status`, `run_rules(scope)`, `install_default_rules(reset)`, `manage_inbox(move/label)`. `apply_labels` folded into `manage_inbox`; `import_artifact` dropped (redundant with direct `"<agent>:<path>"` attach).

- Verified every remaining tool maps to a **live** gateway endpoint (no stale/orphaned tools) and covers the app's real actions.
- Functions the gateway `/ai/quick-action` endpoint calls by name (`search_emails`, `find_urgent`, `suggest_unsubscribes`) kept as module functions, just unregistered from the model's tool surface.
- **Instructions cut 233 → ~124 lines**: the old "Tools" section re-listed every signature, which the model already receives as tool schemas — pure context duplication. Replaced with a compact tool-family map, keeping the behavioral guidance schemas don't carry.
- Frontend AGUI card routing updated for the new tool names; legacy names kept mapped so older transcripts still render. `get_digest`'s raw-JSON card reformatted into readable bullets.

## Testing

Full email suite **393 passed**. New tests: `test_email_reply_threading.py` (provider threading contract), `test_email_present_groups.py` (categorized board output), `test_email_tool_consolidation.py` (the 41-tool surface + per-arg dispatch for every generalized tool).

## Notes / limitations

- Threading fix applies to newly-sent replies; messages already sent as separate threads won't retroactively merge.
- Gmail and Outlook are fully handled; IMAP threading is inherently weaker (we don't yet store the RFC `Message-ID` per message).

title: fix(copilot): BYOK internal-token precedence + de-hardcode tier/model refs
body:
## Problem

`github-copilot`-runtime BYOK agents (e.g. project-manager) failed in chat with a misleading *"GitHub Copilot session error: Authorization error, you may need to run /login"*. The GitHub token is not the cause — BYOK model calls route to the gateway `/v1`, and the orchestrator's BYOK provider builders presented the wrong internal credential, so the gateway rejected them and the Copilot session surfaced the generic auth error.

## Root cause

The gateway's `/v1` guard (`acb_auth.require_internal_auth`) resolves its expected token as `gateway_internal_token` → `litellm_master_key`. The BYOK builders presented `litellm_master_key` only. When a deployment sets those to different values, the call is rejected.

## Changes

**BYOK internal-token precedence (the fix)**
- New `Settings.gateway_internal_token` (reads `GATEWAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN`).
- Every BYOK/internal `/v1` caller now presents `gateway_internal_token or litellm_master_key or "sk-local"`, mirroring `require_internal_auth`, so BYOK always sends the credential the gateway expects. Sites: `executor.py` (sub-agent, early BYOK, both write_artifact tokens), `_model_resolution.py`, `agents.py`, `mutation.py`.

**ClickUp "not connected / not fully configured" (Agents view)**
- `_is_configured("clickup")` is intentionally `False` (ClickUp is multi-account via `task_accounts`). The APIs tab overrode this client-side; the Agents view didn't. Now resolved from the real `task_accounts` count server-side so both surfaces agree.

**De-hardcode tier/model references**
- Consolidate the tier-alias vocabulary to the single canonical `acb_llm.client._TIER_ALIAS_MAP` (was re-listed as literals in `_model_resolution.py` and `settings.py` ×2).
- Fix malformed model defaults that no tier resolves to: `mutation_model` `openai/tier-powerful` → `tier-powerful`; `.env.example` `COPILOT_MODEL` `tier2-gemini` → `tier-balanced`.

## Not changed (deliberately)
- Tier→model routing is already dynamic (`infra/litellm/config.yaml` + DB `tier_overrides` + `set_tier_model`).
- Settings model-picker catalogs are already live-fetch/cache-backed with the static lists as never-empty fallbacks; a fully-dynamic-only rewrite would risk empty pickers on provider outages.

## Testing
- All changed Python files compile clean.
- Verified the tier aliases resolve and complete through `/v1`.

title: fix(tasks): make ClickUp two-way sync actually two-way
body:
Fixes two ClickUp integration bugs, both confirmed against live production data.

## 1. Synced tasks all showed in "Backlog"
The Next-Actions board and grouped list grouped tasks by the **local** Kanban stage (`workflowStage`) — which is always null on synced ClickUp rows. So every ClickUp task collapsed into the first column, ignoring its real status. The status data itself was fine end-to-end (pulled, stored as `provider_status`, mapped to `providerStatus`); only the display grouping was wrong.

**Fix:** a unified status axis.
- `statusColumns(localStages, providerStatuses)` — columns are the union of local workflow stages + every connected tool's statuses (de-duped, provider order first).
- `statusColumnForItem(item, columns, first)` — a LOCAL row keys off `workflowStage`, a SYNCED row off `providerStatus`, so both land in their real column.
- Drag-to-refile is now **source-aware**: dropping a synced card sets `providerStatus` (back-syncs to ClickUp); a local card sets `workflowStage`.
- Store exposes `providerStatuses` (from `providerStatusesFrom(accounts)`), refreshed on hydrate + account refresh.
- The old opt-in `stageMode` prop is gone; `ProjectTasksView` keeps its explicit `stages`.

## 2. A clarify-delegate never reached ClickUp

title: fix(tasks): keep completed tasks in the Done column until archived
body:
## Problem

Moving a task to **Done** on the My Next Actions board made it disappear. Dropping a card on the Done column marks it `DONE`, which flipped its disposition — and the `next` view filters `disposition = 'NEXT'`, so the card was instantly evicted from the board (it silently jumped to the separate Done list). The user expected it to **rest in the Done column until they archive it**.

## Fix

A `DONE`-but-not-archived task now stays visible in the board's last (Done) stage:

- **`itemsForView("next")`** includes `DONE & isMine` — but only the board and grouped list consume this, and both slice by stage so completed tasks land in the Done column / Done section. The sidebar "My Next Actions" count (`viewCounts`) and the Priority/Engage views still exclude `DONE`, so open-work counts are unaffected.
- **`statusColumnForItem`** routes any `DONE` task to the last stage regardless of a stale `workflowStage` / `providerStatus`.
- **Reopen:** dragging a `DONE` card back to an earlier stage flips disposition → `NEXT` and clears `completed_at` (invariant: `completed_at` non-null iff `DONE`). Upstream reopens naturally via the stage→status map (the target stage resolves to an open ClickUp status).

## Tests

3 new backend tests (110 pass total): DONE stamps `completed_at`, reopen clears it, and the stage-boundary disposition flip works both ways. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` + eslint clean.

title: feat(tasks): bulk select → archive/delete, back-propagated to ClickUp
body:
Stacked on #46 (base = `fix/done-column-stays-on-board`) so the diff shows only this feature. Rebase to `main` once #46 merges.

## What you asked for

> A checkbox to select one or multiple tasks, then Archive or Delete — with an "Are you sure?" popup for multiple — back-propagating into ClickUp. ClickUp can't delete via API, so delete = archive upstream.

## What shipped

**Checkbox multi-select on every Next-Actions surface.** Previously select mode only worked on the flat lists (Done/Waiting/…). Now the **status-grouped list and the Kanban board** support it too:
- Select state lives in the store, so it survives the list ⇄ board toggle and clears when you change views.
- On the board, entering select mode drops you into the grouped list with checkboxes (checkboxes + drag on the same card fight each other). Drag-reorder is disabled while selecting.
- The existing bulk action bar (**Archive** · **Delete**) and the **"Are you sure?"** confirm modal already handled single *and* multiple ("Delete 3 tasks?", Enter/Escape) — now wired across all surfaces.

**ClickUp back-propagation:**
- New `provider.archive_task` → ClickUp `PUT {archived}`, broker-gated, 404-safe.
- **Delete** removes the task locally and **archives (not hard-deletes) the ClickUp task** — recoverable upstream, per your requirement.
- **Archive / Restore** (single + bulk) now mirror the `archived` flag upstream for SYNCED tasks — best-effort, after the local commit, one provider reused per account.
- Confirm-modal copy updated: "archived in ClickUp (recoverable there), not permanently deleted."

## Semantics note

Since both Delete and Archive now archive the ClickUp task, they're identical *upstream*. They differ *locally*: **Delete** is destructive (soft-delete → purge; gone from your app), **Archive** is a reversible hide (stays in your Archive view, Restore brings it back).

## Tests

New `test_tasks_archive_upstream.py` — provider archive PUTs the flag / is 404-safe / routes through the broker; `_delete_upstream` archives (never calls `delete_task`); `_archive_upstream` is synced-only and best-effort. title: feat(tasks): priority pill on every card; drop redundant Urgency sort
body:
Two things from your feedback: a build (priority pill on cards) and a cleanup (the confusing Urgency sort).

## 1. Priority pill on every Next-Actions card

The matrix-cell **pill** (🔥 Critical, 🚨 Urgent, 📈 High-Leverage, …) now shows on **every card in the list and board views**, among the other pills — previously it appeared only on the dedicated Priority view. So you can read a task's priority at a glance wherever you are.

The delegate/schedule/eliminate **nudge** badge stays **alongside** it — they're different signals: the pill is *what the task is* (its priority level), the nudge is *what to do about it*. On the Priority view (already grouped by level) the pill is icon-only and the nudge is hidden, to avoid repetition.

## 2. Dropped the Urgency sort

**Your question was the right one.** Here's the distinction:

- **Priority** = the matrix cell, computed from *important × urgent × leveraged*. The holistic "how much does this matter" rank.
- **Urgent** = a single derived boolean: overdue or due within 48h. It's just *one input* to priority, derived from the due date.
- **Due date sort** = orders by the raw deadline.

So **"Urgency" as a sort was redundant**: it only bucketed tasks urgent(0)/not(1), which "Due date" already does with finer resolution (soonest first), and which "Priority" already folds in. It added nothing but confusion. Removed it from the sort dropdown — **Priority** and **Due date** remain. (Urgency still exists as a *concept* — it drives the priority matrix and the ⏰ signal — just not as its own sort.)

title: fix(tasks): Context view crashes with React #185 (infinite render loop)
body:
## Bug

Opening the **Context** view threw `Uncaught Error: Minified React error #185` ("Maximum update depth exceeded") — an infinite render loop, introduced by the columnar-list change (#53).

## Root cause

`readColumnVisibility()` is the `getSnapshot` for `useSyncExternalStore`, but it returned a **brand-new object every call**. React compares snapshots with `Object.is`; a fresh object always reads as "changed," so it re-rendered on every commit → forever. The Context view is the only surface that mounts this hook, so only it crashed.

## Fix

Cache the parsed visibility map and return the **same reference** until the underlying localStorage string actually changes (a write here, or a cross-tab storage event). Stable ref → `Object.is` true → no phantom re-render. Loop broken.

## Note on validation

`tsc`, `eslint`, and `next build` **all passed with the bug present** in #53 — a render loop only manifests at runtime, not at build time. So this fix is verified by the `Object.is` snapshot semantics (and reproducing/opening the view), not by a green build. All three still pass.

## 1. Columns on every grouping
There were **two** grouped-list components — one for Status (with columns) and one for the other lenses (plain rows). ## 2. The filter design — how I avoided overload

Stacking three pill rows (context, priority, energy) is exactly the noise you wanted to avoid. Instead I used a **facet bar** (Linear/Notion pattern):

```
[Search…]  [Filter ▾ (2)]  [@computer ×] [🔥 Critical ×]      Group: Status ▾   Sort: Priority ▾ ⇅
```

- **Grouping** (how it's sliced into swimlanes) and **filtering** (what's shown) are cleanly separated — you can group by Status *and* filter to @computer + Critical.

This scales to any number of facets with no extra rows, and replaces the old context/assignee dropdowns *and* the @context pill row (one control instead of three). Assignee stays single-select and only on non-Next-Actions views.

title: fix(deploy): propagate GATEWAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN to workbench .env.local
body:
## Problem

The orchestrator chat (and memory reads/writes) intermittently 401 with a misleading *"model API key missing/invalid — re-enter in Settings → Models"* error, while the GitHub Copilot SDK agent works fine.

**Root cause (diagnosed live on the VPS):** a two-env-file split.
- The **gateway / orchestrator / all Python agents** read `GATEWAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN` from the shared `/opt/acb/app/.env` via pydantic Settings.
- The **workbench** (`acb-workbench`, Next.js) is a *separate* systemd service that reads its **own** `control_plane/.env.local` via `process.env`. Its server routes forward that token to the gateway's `require_internal_auth`.

`deploy.yml` injects the token into `.env` only and rebuilds the workbench **without touching `.env.local`**. So `.env.local` was hand-managed and had drifted to the dev default `sk-local-dev-change-me`, while the gateway expected the real 64-char token. Result: every workbench→gateway internal call (`/memory` every ~30s, `/v1/chat/completions` for orchestrator chat) 401'd. Backend agents were unaffected because they share `.env` with the gateway — hence the confusing partial outage.

The live VPS was already hot-fixed (token aligned + `acb-workbench` restarted; `/memory` and `/v1` now return 200). **This PR prevents recurrence on future deploys.**

## Fix

Make `.env` the single source of truth. After `.env` is provisioned, reconcile `GATEWAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN` in `.env.local` to exactly match — in-place, idempotent, preserving every other workbench key.

Handles: drift (update), in-sync (no-op), missing file (create), tokens with shell-special chars (`grep -v` + `printf`, **not** `sed s///` which breaks on `/`), and unset token (skip, never wipe). Backs up before rewriting.

## Testing

- `deploy.yml` re-validated as YAML.
- Reconciliation logic exercised by a 14-assertion fixture covering all cases above — **all green**.
- Only backend agents that share `.env` were confirmed safe; the workbench was the sole drift point, now closed.

title: fix(agents): no-text graceful recovery + guaranteed standard toolset
body:
## Problem

Observability showed **"The agent produced no text output…"** for `technical-project-planner` (a github-copilot / deepseek-v4-pro agent) during a live session.

Root-cause chain (traced from the `agent_run` trace + gateway logs):
- The agent authored markdown by shelling out (`bash` heredocs / `echo` / `base64`), fighting shell escaping.
- Its final tool call's JSON arguments were **truncated at ~13k chars** (`Unterminated string in JSON at position 12997`) — a `max_tokens` cutoff mid tool-call — so it never wrote a closing answer (`text_started == False`).
- The Copilot Tier 1.5 handler then emitted a hard `RUN_ERROR`, recorded the run as `error`, and **wiped all the folded tool work** from the UI.

Two systemic gaps behind this:
1. A per-agent `config.json: tool_scope` could **silently strip the essentials** — `email-assistant` had no `write_artifact`/`web_search`/`manage_todo_list`; `task-manager` no `write_artifact`/`web_search`. With no clean file-write tool, agents fall back to fragile shell heredocs.
2. The no-text stream end dead-ended instead of degrading gracefully.

## Changes

**`executor.py` — graceful soft-finish (`_copilot_no_text_end`)**
- Tool work happened → synthesised closing message + `RUN_FINISHED` (records `completed`, keeps the work; user says "continue" to resume the stored session).
- No tool work → genuine empty response → `RUN_ERROR` (hard stop).

**`_tool_injection.py` — guaranteed standard toolset floor**
- `_resolve_injected_scope` unions every `tool_scope` with `_CORE_STANDARD_TOOL_NAMES` (web_search, fetch_page, write_artifact, share_artifact, manage_todo_list, ask_questions, run_diagnostics, get_errors, save_note, recall_notes). A scope can ADD specialist tools but never strip the baseline.
- Steer file authoring to `write_artifact(path, content)` instead of shell heredocs.

## Tests
- `tests/unit/test_executor_no_text_end.py` + `tests/unit/test_core_tool_floor.py` — 12 pass.
- Adjacent injection/permission/copilot tests still pass (51 pass); zero new lint.
- Verified end-to-end that an agent scoped to only `query_history` now receives the full core floor.

title: fix: real output ceiling (4096→32000) + un-clobber Copilot context compaction
body:
P0 from the context/output-budgeting review. Two defects, both proven against the live gateway.

## 1. The real output cap was 4096 — and the knob we'd been tuning is dead

`/v1` is THE choke point every agent runtime POSTs through, so its `max_tokens` default IS the platform's output cap whenever a caller omits the field — and **the Copilot SDK always omits it**: its create/resume-session wire protocol has no `max_tokens` field, so neither `COPILOT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` nor the SessionConfig `max_tokens` we set ever reached the model.

So every Copilot agent was capped at **4096**, which cut the model off *mid tool-call*: it emits a large file's content as a tool argument, gets truncated, and the malformed JSON fails the call — `"Unterminated string in JSON at position N"` (seen on `technical-project-planner` at 12997 and 16340 ≈ 4096 tokens).

**Measured on the live gateway (deepseek-v4-pro):**

| request | completion_tokens | finish_reason |
|---|---|---|
| no `max_tokens` (what the CLI sends) | **4096** | `length` ← truncated |
| `max_tokens=32000` | **10940** | `stop` ← finished naturally |

Default is now `GATEWAY_DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (32000, env-tunable).

**Why not clamp to the model's registry max_output?** litellm's bundled registry claims this model caps at 8192, yet it demonstrably emits 10940 — clamping to that stale value would reintroduce the truncation. `max_tokens` is a *ceiling* (the model stops when done, per `finish_reason="stop"`), so a generous default only removes an artificial cut. Verified accepted by the whole active fleet (deepseek-v4-pro / tier-powerful / tier-fast / auto all 200 at 32000). A per-model resolver is the follow-up once limit data is trustworthy enough to clamp on.

`.env.example` previously told operators to raise `COPILOT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` when *"the agent stops mid-response with no text"* — exactly this symptom, exactly the knob that does nothing. Now documented as a no-op.

## 2. The BYOK compaction mitigation was dead on the streaming path

`_inject_agent_tools` installs the `_apply_copilot_infinite_sessions` wrap, then `run_agent_stream` **rebinds** `agent._create_session` (executor.py:2361) — discarding the wrap before `agent.run()` calls it. So the Copilot backend kept running its default 0.80/0.95 compaction against its wrong ~90K BYOK window guess: the exact false "context length exceeded" the mechanism exists to prevent.

The policy now lives in one place (`effective_infinite_sessions`) and is applied by the CommandCenter session methods directly, on **both create and resume** (a resumed session rebuilds config from scratch). Independent of binding order; the wrap is kept for shapes that are never rebound and shares the same policy so they can't drift.

**Why the tests missed it:** they exercise the wrap in *isolation* and never simulate the rebind — all 14 stayed green while production bypassed the fix.

## Tests
- `test_v1_compat_max_tokens.py` (new) — fails against the old 4096 default.
- `test_copilot_infinite_sessions.py` — 3 new rebind tests; verified they **fail against the old code** while the 14 original tests still pass (demonstrating the blind spot).
- 53 tests pass across affected areas; zero new lint.

title: fix(context): budget history to the model's real window (was ~2% of it)
body:
P1 from the context/output-budgeting review. Follows #65 (independent files — no conflict).

## Problem

The model-aware assembler (`assemble_run_context`) is correct — but several executor paths **bypassed it** with hardcoded caps that have no relationship to the context window:

| path | cap | share of a 128k window |
|---|---|---|
| `_build_event_message` | last 16 msgs × 600 chars | **~1.9%** |
| Copilot new-session inject | last 30 × 600 | ~3.5% |
| Copilot stale-retry inject | last 30 × 800 | ~4.7% |

So a large-context model was fed **a few KB of history regardless of holding 128k–1M tokens**.

Two aggravating details:
- The **600-char slice also hit the immediately-preceding turn** — a user who pasted a document, diff, or error log had it cut to 600 chars on the very next message.
- The two Copilot ones run on **every session rebuild** (e.g. after a gateway restart), so they decide how much a resumed chat remembers. The new-session block's own comment claimed a *"larger budget"* because diffs/file contents are *"meaningless when cut to a few sentences"* — while cutting them to 600 chars.

## Fix

All three now share `_render_history_block`, budgeting from `context_window_for(model)`:
- oldest turns drop first (mirrors the assembler's whole-turn eviction),
- a single oversized turn is trimmed rather than allowed to eat the budget,
- fails open to a floor when the window can't be resolved (never raises).

**Measured:**

| tier | window | old budget | new budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| tier-powerful | 131,072 tok | 9,600 chars (~2,400 tok) | **262,144 chars (~65,536 tok)** — 27× |
| tier-fast | 1,000,000 tok | 9,600 chars | **2,000,000 chars** |

A 60-turn thread now keeps **60/60 turns** where the old cap kept 16 shredded ones.

Also **drops the `is_byok` gate** on `_compose_maf_run_input`: a non-BYOK native-MAF agent's *streaming* turn fell back to the flat string prompt while its own *batch* turn got the token-budgeted assembly — the same agent remembered a different amount of the conversation depending on whether it streamed.

## Deliberately not changed
The Tier-2 batch fallback's `[-20:]` is a **count-only** cap (no char truncation) in a rarely-hit path with a documented provider-specific rationale — left as-is to keep the blast radius tight.

## Tests
`tests/unit/test_history_budget.py` (new, 9 tests) — budget scales with window, unknown model falls open to the floor, a recent turn isn't shredded to 600 chars, >16 turns survive, chronological order preserved, oldest-first eviction, no current-turn duplication, one giant turn can't eat the budget.

71 tests pass across affected areas; zero new lint.

title: feat(agents): make VS Code-authored Copilot agents first-class in MAF (+ fix MCP never reaching a session)
body:
P2 from the context/output-budgeting review. Independent of #65 / #66.

> "GitHub Copilot SDK agents need to be better configured for being used in MAF because technically they are not inside VSCode anymore. Should be treated as first-class citizens."

Three things were quietly broken for **every** VS-Code-authored agent.

## 1. `tools:` was advisory only — inert

The frontmatter lists VS Code tool ids (`editFiles`, `terminal`, `codebase`, `problems`, …) that map to **nothing** here, so the model saw names in its prompt that exist in no tool schema and had to improvise onto the CLI's native `bash`/`create`/`edit`.

`derive_tool_scope()` now maps them onto the platform tools that actually do the job. On the real `technical-project-planner`:

```
config.json tool_scope : [web_search, fetch_page, write_artifact, manage_todo_list, ask_user, save_note, recall_notes]
+ derived from .agent.md: [github_search, github_repo_search, write_artifact, share_artifact, fetch_page, web_search, run_diagnostics, get_errors]
= gained               : github_search, github_repo_search, share_artifact, run_diagnostics, get_errors
```

**Widening only:** an agent with no `config.json` tool_scope stays unscoped, so adding an `.agent.md` can never silently strip tools.

## 2. `.vscode/mcp.json` / `.mcp.json` were never read

Only `config.json` + the DB table were. `technical-project-planner` declares a **draw.io MCP server in both files** while its `config.json mcp_servers` is `{}` — so it lost the server it was built to use, then failed at the diagramming it exists to do.

## 3. MCP never reached a session AT ALL (from any source)

`_inject_mcp_servers` merged into `agent._default_options["mcp_servers"]` — but the SDK consults `_default_options` for exactly **one** key (`system_message`) and resolves MCP as `runtime_options.get("mcp_servers") or self._mcp_servers` (`_resume_session` reads `self._mcp_servers` only). We pass a fresh per-run options dict, so **that write was dead**.

Now merged into `_mcp_servers` via `merge_mcp_servers()` (DB registry outranks a repo's own files). The DB path also emitted `{"transport": ...}` while the SDK's `MCPServerConfig` wants `{"type": ...}` + command/args split + `tools: ["*"]` (`[]` means "expose none"). Both fixed.

**Blast radius today: nil** — all 5 DB servers are `enabled=false`, so nothing changes until someone enables one; it will then actually work.

## Runtime note (additive)

A short note is appended to a VS-Code-authored body — the author's prose is **never** rewritten — reconciling the IDE names with the real tools and stating there is no Problems panel / `#codebase` / editor UI. It also steers file authoring to `write_artifact` rather than shell heredocs: the exact habit that truncated tool-call arguments mid-JSON.

## Deliberately not included
Mapping `.agent.md model:` (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) onto a tier. "Nearest tier" is a judgement call with cost implications; today it's coerced to `COPILOT_CHAT_MODEL`, which is predictable and works. Left for a decision.

## Tests
`tests/unit/test_vscode_agent_normalization.py` (16 new) — IDE→real tool mapping, IDE-only names contribute nothing, note only for VS Code agents, both MCP file shapes recovered in SDK shape (`type` not `transport`), malformed files safe, merge targets the field the SDK actually reads, DB outranks repo, and scope widens-but-never-narrows.

83 tests pass across affected areas; zero new lint.

title: fix(llm): one source of truth for model limits (five disagreeing copies -> one)
body:
## The problem

"How big is this model?" had **five answers**. For `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` alone the codebase held five context-window values (`0 / 262144 / 840000 / 1000000`) and four max-output values (`0 / 8192 / 32768 / 384000`). Which one you got depended on which file happened to ask.

The worst part: the **curated table with the accurate numbers was only ever read by the Settings UI**. The runtime that actually budgets prompts couldn't reach it, so it asked litellm — which is provably stale for this fleet.

Everything now resolves through **`acb_llm.model_limits.get_limits`**, returning `{context_window, max_output}` plus the provenance of each number.

## Opposite rules for opposite failures

The two fields fail in opposite directions, so they resolve by opposite rules. This is deliberate, not an inconsistency:

| field | rule | why |
|---|---|---|
| `context_window` | **conservative** — lowest positive value any trusted source reports | Over-claiming is unrecoverable: the provider hard-rejects, and `acompletion_with_fallback` answers by switching *model* rather than re-fitting — and agent runs never touch that path. Under-claiming just trims sooner. |
| `max_output` | **trust order, curated first** | litellm claims v4-pro maxes at 8192 output tokens. The live model emits **10940**. Believing litellm is what truncated a tool call's JSON args mid-string and produced *"the agent produced no text output"*. |

## Also fixed

- **A guess, laundered into a fact.** `ensure_model_registered` invented `max_input_tokens: 262144` for any model litellm didn't know, wrote it into `model_cost`, and then `context_window_for` read it straight back *as though litellm had said it* — outranking the real fallback table. Routing stays; `STUB_MARKER` means the numbers are no longer believed. (`client.py` already did exactly this for the stub `$0` price via `_DYNAMIC_STUB_PRICED_MODELS` — the token counts just never got the same treatment.)
- **A pin that overwrote the truth.** `settings.py` hardcoded tier windows "matching config.yaml". They drifted — `tier_overrides.yaml` re-pointed `tier-balanced` at `deepseek-chat` (131K) while the table still said 1M — and the pin ran *after* the dynamic resolution and clobbered it. The endpoint computed the right window, then replaced it with the stale one. The UI's context ring under-reported usage by ~7.6×.
- **A 4× over-claim.** A model id litellm didn't know matched on its **bare suffix**, so `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` inherited the *direct* provider's 1M window when OpenRouter serves it at 262K.
- **Default window 32768 → 128000.** The old default silently starved every unknown model to a quarter of a current model's real window.
- **`ACB_LIMITS__<MODEL>__{CONTEXT_WINDOW,MAX_OUTPUT}`** overrides — a provider raising a limit becomes an env var, not a deploy.

## Tradeoff, stated plainly

A curated entry that is **stale-low now binds**, where litellm's larger number used to win. That's the intended direction of error given the asymmetry above, and the remedy is cheap in a way it wasn't before: one table to correct, or an env var.

13 curated windows shrink — all are corrections of the bare-suffix over-claim, or of the 32K default exceeding a model's real window (Llama-3 is genuinely 8K). None are in the active fleet.

## Verification

- Resolver checked against the real fleet: v4-pro `1M / 384K (curated)`, reasoner `131K (conservative) / 65K`, gpt-4o `128K / 16,384`, unknown `128K / 8192`.
- **All 20 pre-existing context tests pass unchanged** — including the two that pin `tier-balanced` to 1M and 131K, which the conservative rule satisfies naturally.
- 14 new tests pin the resolution **rules, not vendor numbers**, so they don't become the sixth stale table.
- Lint delta **0**; CI blocking gate green.

## Note

`get_limits` is the foundation the rest of the backlog consumes: the `max_tokens` clamp (#65) and the history ceiling (#66) both resolve limits through it.

(Both are dead knobs; the one in prod `.env` is a no-op and should be removed.)

So every Copilot agent was capped at **4096 output tokens**. That's what truncated long tool-call arguments mid-JSON: the model emits a large file's content as a tool argument, gets cut at 4096, and the malformed JSON fails the call — `Unterminated string in JSON at position 16340` (÷4 ≈ 4096 tokens, exactly).

Measured on the live gateway (deepseek-v4-pro):

| request | result |
|---|---|
| no `max_tokens` | `completion_tokens=4096`, `finish_reason="length"` — **cut off** |
| `max_tokens=32000` | `completion_tokens=10940`, `finish_reason="stop"` — **finished** |

`max_tokens` is a *ceiling*, not a target — the model stops when it's done (the `stop` above proves it), so a generous default costs nothing and only removes an artificial cut. Verified accepted by the whole active fleet.

## 2. The clamp — but only against a cap we vouch for

The generous default cuts both ways: a model that caps below 32000 answers an over-large `max_tokens` with a **400** — a total failure, worse than the truncation the default exists to prevent. Nothing in the fleet does that today (all deepseek), which is exactly why the ceiling could be raised safely. `_clamp_max_tokens` keeps it true when a smaller model is added: **gpt-4o now gets 16384 instead of a 400**.

Only a limit we **vouch for** may lower the ceiling — a curated entry or an explicit env override. litellm's registry is excluded **on purpose**: it claims deepseek-v4-pro caps at 8192 while the live model emits 10940, so clamping to it would re-create the exact bug this default was raised to fix. Believing a guess is what broke this in the first place; an unvetted model keeps the generous ceiling. A resolver failure never blocks a call — the lookup is an optimisation, not a gate on inference.

## 3. Infinite-sessions policy survived nothing

The `_apply_copilot_infinite_sessions` wrap was installed at `_inject_agent_tools` and then **thrown away** by `executor.py:2361` rebinding `_create_session`. So BYOK compaction ran against the wrong (~90K) window on the streaming path. The old tests passed because they exercised the wrap in isolation — never through the rebind.

The policy is now extracted to `effective_infinite_sessions` and applied inside `CommandCenterCopilotAgent._create_session` / `._resume_session`, so it survives the rebind by construction. The new tests fail against the old code; all 14 original tests still pass.

Depends on #68 for `acb_llm.model_limits.get_limits`.

title: feat(calendar): timeboxing app — AI planner, roll-over, mobile scheduling, Now/Next, replan + fixed/flexible, actuals + end-of-day review
body:
A **fully-featured, AI-driven calendar + timeboxing** app built into the task manager. **Draft — for review; nothing merged.** Branch off `main`.

The calendar plans your Next Actions, timeboxes them well (energy + capacity aware), and reorganizes/replans when things change — leveraging AI throughout, with deterministic guardrails so the AI can't produce invalid schedules. Spec + full failure-mode analysis: `ai-company-brain/specs/calendar_timeboxing.md`.

## What's built (P0–P3)

**Grid & timeboxing (P0–P1)**
- Day / Week hour-grids + Month grid; tasks render as blocks; current-time line; deadline all-day markers.
- **Drag-and-drop** to schedule (rail → grid) and move (within/across days); **resize** to change duration; 15-min snap; drop-target highlight.
- New `scheduled_start/end` time-block model (mig 76) — only `due_at` deadlines existed before.

**Energy / capacity / buffers (P1)** — mig 77
- Per-user prefs the grid *and* the AI planner honor: working window, daily focus capacity (with an "Xh/Yh over capacity" meter), inter-block buffer, and **energy windows** (tinted on the grid). Gear popover to edit them.

**AI "Plan my day" (P2)** — the headline feature
- `POST /calendar/plan`: the **LLM makes the judgment** (which Next Actions today, order, energy-fit — from your energy note, the priority matrix, and deadlines) and **deterministic code does the geometry** (packs into real free slots respecting the window, existing blocks, energy windows, capacity, buffers). No overlaps/out-of-window possible; degrades to priority-ranked packing when the LLM is off.
- "Plan my day" review modal: energy-note input → re-plan, proposed blocks with rationale, unplaced list, capacity summary, Apply.

**Chat with your calendar (P2)**
- The task assistant is calendar-aware (persona gets the schedule, free time, capacity, current local time + tz) and has `gtd_schedule` / `gtd_unschedule` / `gtd_list_schedule` tools — so "reschedule my deep work to tomorrow afternoon" just works, timezone-safe, without double-booking.

**Reorganize / replan (P3)**
- **Auto-reschedule / roll-over**: `POST /calendar/rollover` packs overdue-incomplete blocks into today (deadline-aware); a banner offers one-click "Roll over to today".
- **Deadline radar**: due-soon badge + a "Due soon" rail section with one-click "Today".
- **Overlap detection**: side-by-side lanes + a red "double-booked" flag.

## Failure modes explicitly addressed
Overcommitment, no buffers, energy mismatch, falling behind, deadline slip, bad estimates, double-booking, fragmentation, tedium, rigid plans, timezone bugs — see the spec's §9b table for how each is handled with UX + AI.

## Deferred
- **P4 — Google/Outlook two-way sync**: needs OAuth client creds; seamed at `/calendar/accounts` + `/calendar/sync` (501), reuses the email OAuth stack.
- **P5**: `gtd_time_blocks` table, continuous auto-scheduling engine, Pomodoro, ideal-week templates, learned estimates. A nightly automatic roll-over job (P3 has the manual trigger).

## Verification
- Backend: `py_compile` + `ruff` clean; **golden evals 21/21** throughout.
- Frontend: `tsc`, `eslint`, and production `next build` clean on every slice.
- Not click-tested in a live browser (Chrome remote-debug needs a manual allow); all scheduling runs through the standard optimistic-PATCH path.

## Mobile
Grid day-view fits; week scrolls; month fits; header wraps; the "N due soon" badge, roll-over banner, and "Plan my day" modal all work on mobile. The unscheduled rail (drag-source + due-soon list) is desktop-only — mobile schedules via the plan modal / task surface (a noted follow-up).

title: fix(tasks): deterministic lowest-status reverse-map on synced stage move
body:
When a synced (ClickUp) task is moved into a local Next-Actions stage — by kanban drag or the new card stage selector — the backend reverse-maps to a concrete upstream status via `_status_for_stage`, which returns the **first** of the task's project statuses that maps to the target stage.

That first-in-order = the *lowest* status feeding the stage (so a move lands the task at the stage's **earliest** ClickUp status). But it depended on ClickUp returning the list's `statuses` already sorted by `orderindex` — true in practice, **not enforced in code**.

title: refactor(email): security fixes + provider factory, llm_json seam, AssistantView split (1/2)
body:
Part 1 of a two-PR stack that pays down the email app's structural debt and closes four security holes found in the accompanying audit.

> **Stack:** `fix/clickup-status-orderindex` (#73) → **this PR** → #75 (layering inversion).
> Based on #73 so the diff stays clean; GitHub retargets this to `main` automatically when #73 merges.

---

## 1. Security (authorized fixes)

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Cross-account mailbox takeover.** `X-User-Email` was trusted *without* the internal Bearer token. The gateway is reachable directly through Caddy, so anyone could set that header and read/send as any user. | [`deps.py`](packages/acb_auth/acb_auth/deps.py) now refuses a bare `X-User-Email` whenever an internal token is configured — the header is only trustworthy when it arrives *with* the token proving it came from the authenticated Next.js proxy. |
| **Postgres + Redis on the public internet.** Docker's `-p` publishing writes iptables `DOCKER` rules that bypass UFW, so `5432:5432` / `6379:6379` exposed both stores despite the firewall. Redis has no auth at all. | [`infra/docker-compose.yml`](infra/docker-compose.yml) binds both to loopback via `${POSTGRES_BIND:-127.0.0.1}` / `${REDIS_BIND:-127.0.0.1}`. |
| **SSRF** via unsubscribe + image proxy. | Unsubscribe uses `follow_redirects=False`; the image proxy revalidates *every* hop and now requires an authenticated caller. |
| **IDOR** on attachments. | Ownership check moved *ahead* of the Redis cache read; filename sanitised. |

### ⚠️ Deploy prerequisite — read before merging

The auth fix **fails open when no internal token is configured** (mirroring `require_internal_auth`'s existing contract) so an unprovisioned/dev gateway isn't bricked. Two consequences:

1. **Prod must actually have `GATEWAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN` set**, or the hole stays open.
2. **The Next.js proxy's token and the gateway's must match.** If they drift, legitimate proxied traffic silently becomes *anonymous* rather than erroring — the same class of mismatch that caused the earlier BYOK/Copilot `run /login` incident.

`GATEWAY_TRUST_UNVERIFIED_SSO_HEADERS=1` is a deliberate temporary rollback hatch for exactly that mismatch. It restores the vulnerable behaviour — align the tokens instead.

---

## 2. Refactor (behaviour-preserving)

- **C3 — one provider factory.** `email_ingestion.providers.factory.build_provider` replaces **8** inline copies; `core._instantiate_provider` adapts `ValueError` → HTTP 400.
- **H4 — `core._llm_json()` seam** de-duplicates **8** JSON-mode LLM call sites. (Guards the known DeepSeek failure mode where a missing `response_format=json_object` returns empty content.)
- **H3 — `AssistantView.tsx` split: 4833 → 234 LOC**, into `automation/assistant/{actionFormat, common, fixDialog, TestTab, HistoryTab, SettingsTab, RulesTab}`.
- Deduped `engine._fmt_recipients` → `core._fmt_addr_list`.
- Fixed a **scheduler engine leak** (`NullPool`), a manual-sync **body clobber** (`COALESCE`), and removed a dead `body_truncated` computation.

## 3. Correctness

**C1 —** the scheduler and inbound webhook paths now persist `unsubscribe_link` off the same provider message (COALESCE on update), matching manual sync. Previously a background- or webhook-synced email was silently **not** unsubscribe-eligible and **not** Reply-Zero classified — only manually synced mail was.

## 4. UX

- **Rapid Inbox removed.** Its job moves to **QuickFilters chips** layered over the normal search/filter pipeline, so it's one code path instead of a parallel one (coloured tag pills; Follow-up mirrored locally).
- **Inbox Cleaner** (`BulkUnsubscribeView`) reworked: category tabs driven by real message labels, provisional guesses dropped, Blocked / Unsubscribed / Auto-archive states shown, per-sender drill-down, optimistic row removal on trash & archive.
- **SearchBar**: coloured tag pills + From/To people search.
- Path-traversal guard on the Next proxy's email upstream URL builder.

## 5. Tests

- `test_rbac` — new secure `X-User-Email` contract, plus escape-hatch and fail-open coverage.
- `test_email_categorization` — rule-projection categorization; inferred rows reconciled.
- `test_email_search_scope` — `FOLDER_ALL_EXCLUDES` frontend↔backend parity guard.
- **`test_email_upsert_unsubscribe_parity` (new)** — asserts all three received-message ingest paths bind `unsubscribe_link`, so the C1 drift can't come back.

---

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff check --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006` | ✅ pass |
| `xenon --max-absolute F --max-modules F --max-average B` | ✅ pass |
| `pytest tests/unit -k "email or rbac or upsert or layering"` | ✅ **403 passed** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ 0 errors |
| `eslint src` | ✅ **109 errors vs 113 on `main`** — net **−4** (RapidInboxView removed, AssistantView split). No new rule categories. |
| `next build` | ✅ green |
