title: feat(email): group learned patterns by the force they actually carry
body:
## The screen

From your screenshots: **21 rows in one flat list**, with rejected patterns interleaved among the ones awaiting review — told apart only by 60% opacity and a small grey word *rejected*.

That's not a styling difference. The three states decide whether a pattern does anything at all:

| state | classifier | Email Cleaner |
|---|---|---|
| **Needs review** | uses it | no |
| **In force** | uses it | uses it |
| **Rejected** | never | never |

So they're three groups now, each with its count in the heading and one line saying what that state *means*. Rejected collapses behind a disclosure — it's a record, not something to act on, and left expanded it padded the list with rows you'd already dismissed. Still reachable, because *"why isn't this sender being filed?"* is answered there.

Note the middle row of that table: a pattern awaiting review is **already shaping classification**. The old copy only said the Cleaner wouldn't use it, which reads as "this does nothing yet". The new header says both halves.

## Two things the screenshots made obvious

- **The amber banner and the amber rows said the same thing twice.** The explanation moved into the group header; the separate banner is gone.
- **A rejected row still showed a green "Always match" chip** — asserting a live effect the engine doesn't honour. Now drained of colour and struck through.

Also, the dialog's own description still described only the pattern half, though it has held both halves since #105. Rewritten in both places it appears.

## The other half of the ask: is teaching actually wired?

It is — but my existing test for it was weak, and worth saying so. `test_both_matchers_pass_guidance_to_the_model` asserted on **source strings** via `inspect.getsource`. It would have stayed green if the prompt came out empty, or if guidance were rendered into a variable nobody sent anywhere.

Replaced with tests that drive the real matcher and read the prompt the model would receive:

- a correction reaches the model
- it renders **between its own rule and the next one** — position is the mechanism, not decoration
- it's labelled `correction from the user:`, so a preset blurb and a human instruction aren't equivalent
- account-wide corrections get their own override block
- every correction for a rule is sent, not just the newest
- blank guidance and no guidance leave the prompt untouched

Critically, two of them run through **`_match_email_to_rules_multi`** — `multi_rule_execution` is ON for this account, so that's the path a real correction has to survive. Proving it on the single-rule branch alone would have proved nothing about this mailbox.

## Verification

667 email tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean; the grouping screenshotted at 900px and 390px via a temporary Playwright harness (removed before commit) with a horizontal-overflow assertion at both widths.

title: fix(agents): a question isn't a failure - stop reporting parked turns as truncated
body:
## The symptom

An agent that ended its turn by **asking the user a question** was reported as a broken run:

> "I finished the steps above, but my final summary was cut off before it could be written — **the response hit its output length limit**. … Say "continue" and I'll pick up where I left off."

Nothing was cut off. The agent had called `ask_user` and was waiting for an answer. The advice was wrong too: the correct move was to **answer the question**, not say "continue".

## Why it happened

`_copilot_no_text_end` had exactly two branches — *tools ran* (assume truncation) or *no tools* (error) — and no notion of a turn **parked on a human**. But `ask_questions` / `ask_user` / `request_confirmation` all stop the agent by design: the card they render **is** the output, so no closing text is due. `ask_tools`' own module docstring says it outright: *"The agent MUST stop after calling this tool."*

The message also asserted a cause the code cannot observe. All it actually knows is *no text arrived*. It named one specific reason — and the first time it fired in production, that reason was wrong.

## The evidence

Production run `252c24dc` (`technical-project-planner`, deepseek-v4-pro):

- last tool = **`ask_user`**
- the gateway's usage log for that run shows a **4,473-token** completion — *above* the old 4096 ceiling and nowhere near the 32000 cap, so **nothing was truncated**
- largest prompt in the window: 73,592 tokens, well inside a 1M model's context

It fired **once in 7 days** — rare, but actively misleading when it does, and it undermines trust in every other message the agent sends.

## The fix

All at the **one site** that produces this message, so every Copilot-SDK agent is covered — not just the one that hit it.

- **Track the last tool started**, read off the **emitted events** rather than any single translator branch. A native SDK tool (`ask_user`) and a platform tool reach the stream through different branches; only the emitted event is common to both. It resets on the stale-session retry, so a name from a discarded attempt can't decide how the real attempt ends.
- **Ending on a blocking HITL tool finishes silently** — no message talking over the question card. It also logs at `info` with `awaiting_user=True` instead of `warning`: a normal wait shouldn't look like an incident, and shouldn't bury real ones.
- **The message no longer asserts a cause.** It now describes only what's known: the summary is missing, the work survived, say "continue".
- **`HITL_BLOCKING_TOOLS` + `is_hitl_blocking_tool`** live in `acb_skills.ask_tools`, beside the tools themselves, so the set can't drift from what it describes.

## Scope: all agents

**Native-MAF agents were never affected** — that path emits `RUN_FINISHED` and no such message. Verified by checking every `text_started` reference: this handler is the only site that makes the decision, and it is shared by all Copilot-SDK agents.

## Verification

- The **6 new tests fail against the old handler** and pass against this one (confirmed by reverting only the source).
- Guards both directions: a normal last tool (`bash`) still gets the fallback message, and a HITL name does **not** rescue a zero-tool run from being a genuine error.
- Translator wiring checked live: a function-call update for `ask_user` sets `last_name` correctly; `nonlocal` scoping verified by AST.
- Lint delta **0**; CI blocking gate green; **118 trajectory evals** pass.

title: feat(email): a conversation has ONE classification, re-evaluated per message
body:
## The screenshot, explained

One `thread_id` wearing **Done + Receipt + FYI**, with the supplier's invoice message physically moved out of the conversation into the Receipt folder. The smoking gun from `email_executed_rules` — both rows, same message, same run:

```
FYI      APPLIED  thread_status  "Thread status: FYI"            [LABEL]
Receipt  APPLIED  ai             "invoice copy from a supplier"  [LABEL, MOVE_FOLDER]
```

The system judged the thread conversational and ripped a message out of it anyway.

## The model change

**The unit of classification is the conversation. A new message is new *evidence* about it, not a new thing to classify.**

| before | after |
|---|---|
| arbitration ran only if the *message* matched a conversation rule | runs whenever the *thread* is a conversation |
| `[determined, *non_conv]` — losing matches ran their actions | losers come back `suppressed`: logged SKIPPED, never applied |
| "ok noted" matched nothing → thread status stale forever | no-match messages still refresh the thread |
| damage stayed | stale cleanup chips shed; our own mid-conversation moves undone |

`_thread_is_conversation` is deterministic and cheap — an existing status row, else ≥2 messages with our side (owner or org domains) participating. **Bulk mail never pays for a determination**: a newsletter blast stays on the per-message path, and a cold-email drip (≥2 messages, all external) stays bulk — a salesperson can't earn conversation treatment by following up with themselves.

## Robustness decisions

- **The suppression guard lives in `_apply_and_log_match`** — the one choke point every apply path crosses (same shape as the pattern-write gate in `rules._teach`), so no future caller can run a suppressed match by accident. History gets a SKIPPED row answering *"why wasn't this filed as a Receipt?"*
- **Move-back undoes only our own work**: a message still sitting in the exact folder an APPLIED rule-move put it in. Proven read-only against prod: the invoice message qualifies; four messages an *Outlook-side* rule filed under "fracktal internal emails" carry no rule move-label and are left alone. No provider → no move (a local-only move would be re-broken by the next sync). Move re-keys are persisted — the #100 lesson.
- **LLM failure degrades to per-message classification**, never to unfiled mail.
- **Corrections taught via Fix now steer the status determiner too** (same contract as the classifier prompt); cleanup-rule guidance is deliberately excluded from that prompt as noise.
- The gate SQL and the `actions_taken @> '"MOVE_FOLDER"'` containment predicate were both exercised against the live database before landing.

## Tests

21 new — gate semantics, the invoice regression, suppression, the choke-point guard, move-back (including "user re-filed → hands off" and one-failure-doesn't-abort), chip-shedding, and corrections **end-to-end into the prompt string**. Two existing tests rewritten because they pinned the old contract; 688 email tests pass.

## What this deliberately does not do

The list view still shows one row per message (conversation collapse is the follow-up), and the 110 ghost rows from provider re-keying still need the `internetMessageId` migration. This PR makes the *chips agree*; those make the *rows collapse*.

title: fix(email): an FYI status row alone does not make a thread a conversation

## Caught in post-deploy verification of #110, before it acted

The gate accepted **any** `email_thread_status` row as proof of conversation. But FYI is also the default stamp for "nothing matched" — **3,226 of the live account's 3,535 threads carry one**, newsletters included. FYI rows fall through to the participation test, where a blast (external-only) stays bulk and a genuine FYI conversation (a colleague thread) still qualifies via back-and-forth.

title: chore(email): one-off repair script for damaged conversation threads
body:
Repair rides the classification path (#110), so a damaged thread heals on its **next inbound message** — and a DONE conversation may never get one. This walks the statused conversations that still show damage (**51 with stale cleanup chips, 16 rule-moved messages** at time of writing) and runs exactly the two repair steps the live runner uses, through the same functions: `_reconcile_thread_labels` + `_restore_conversation_messages`.

title: fix(email): the cleanup sweep must not label conversation messages
body:
## Found while verifying the repair the user asked for

The repair sweep and the Email Cleaner **fought each other, live**:

```
07:24:26  repair strips stale Receipt/Marketing chips (12 threads)
07:25:41  email.cleanup_sweep  scanned: 566, applied: 36   ← re-labels them
07:31:12  email.cleanup_sweep  applied: 0                  ← steady state restored
```

Root cause: most messages of a statused thread legitimately carry **no chip** — the status label sits on the latest inbound message only. The sweep read those bare messages as "uncategorized" and projected the sender's category straight back on. Each system was correct by its own definition; the definitions disagreed about who owns a conversation's messages.

## The fix

The armistice line goes where every other scope decision already lives — `_CLEANUP_SCOPE`: messages of `NEEDS_REPLY / AWAITING / DONE` threads are not the cleaner's to label; the thread's status **is** their classification (#110).

**FYI is deliberately absent from the exclusion**: it's also the default stamp for "nothing matched" (#111), so excluding FYI threads would put 3,226 of the live account's 3,535 threads — newsletters included — beyond the cleaner's reach. The test pins both directions.

690 email tests pass. After deploy: re-run `scripts/repair_conversation_threads.py --apply` (third pass) and verify the chips survive a sweep cycle.

title: fix(email): Phase 1 - stop the lying (11 correctness fixes)
body:
## Phase 1 — "Stop the lying"

Every fix in this branch closes a case where the email app **misreported its own behavior** — told you it saved something it didn't, marked mail processed it never looked at, or showed numbers that weren't true. From the consolidated `email_app_master_plan.md`. No new features; correctness only.

### Fixes (11, each its own commit with a red-before-green test)

| # | Item | What was lying |
|---|---|---|
| 1.2 | Saved pattern reports saved | `_upsert_rule_pattern` fell off returning `None` on success -> "Nothing was saved" after a real save |
| 1.10 | `/messages` OR-search | used `plainto_tsquery` (ANDs everything) -> agent `find_urgent` OR-queries silently matched nothing |
| 1.12 | No boilerplate on outage | LLM failure auto-filed a canned draft **and** wrote it to Mem0 as your style |
| 1.9 | Learn your voice | writing-style learning ingested the **quoted chain** -> learned correspondents' voices |
| 1.7 | Undo-send | dropped Cc / attachments / artifacts and folded the quote into the editable body |
| 1.6 | Digest truth | "awaiting your reply" was a proxy count; category filter didn't match; preview != sent; local-time labels on UTC data |
| 1.3 | Cleaner honesty | auth failure -> phantom APPLIED loop; failed sweeps reported "done"; failed applies uncounted |
| 1.11 | Trust panel | failure count didn't match what the Repair button could act on; dead "Try again" button |
| 1.8 | Confirm destructive | 5 agent tools (trash / unsubscribe / rule-reset / digest-send / account-purge) acted without a confirmation card |
| 1.5 | Provider-first writes | local state updated before the provider -> a refused action left fabricated local truth |
| 1.4 | Outage != processed | LLM outage returned `None`, indistinguishable from "no rule matched" -> whole batches watermarked processed forever. New `LLMUnavailable` tri-state, handled at all 5 call sites |

(1.1 — a sweep/cleaner collision — was already fixed by #113 mid-review.)

### Verification
- **706 email unit tests pass** (+10 new, each fails before its fix)
- CI-blocking lint (`F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006`) clean repo-wide
- Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean (CI has no frontend build)

### Deferred to Phase 2
- 1.4's `'. auto'` self-heal marker -> a real `provisional` column (schema migration; belongs with the `classify_and_apply` refactor)
- Items 1.3 / 1.4 / 1.5 change live-sync behavior only a real cycle confirms — needs a post-deploy check on the live account

title: refactor(email): 2.9 - one token-guarded JobTracker for both background jobs
body:
## Phase 2 — 2.9: one token-guarded JobTracker for both background jobs

The runner's "Process past emails" job and the cleaner's sweep each publish per-account progress that a background task mutates while a request polls it. Both share one hazard: a **superseded (older) run's late write landing on the newer run's row** — marking the newer job done, or overwriting its counts. The runner guarded this with a monotonic token; the cleaner's `_SWEEP_JOBS` did not, and `/cleanup/auto-categorize` had **no concurrency guard at all**, so a double-clicked sweep (or a sweep starting during a backfill's cleaning phase) clobbered the in-flight row.

### Change
- Extract the guard into one `JobTracker` (`automation/jobs.py`); back **both** trackers with it.
- Runner behaviour is unchanged — the token guard is now shared code, not a second copy.
- The cleaner **gains** the guard: `job_token` threads through `sweep_uncategorized -> _sweep_tick`; both sweep jobs write via the token-guarded `finish()`/`update()`.
- Both sweep endpoints seed the row + mint the token **synchronously before scheduling the task**, and auto-categorize gains the same `is_running()` refusal the backfill endpoint already had — closing the check-then-act race.

In-memory, ephemeral by design (a restart drops the state with the job).

### Verification
- `test_email_job_tracker` pins the token guard (a superseded run can't mutate or finish the newer row; `is_running`; tokenless updates still apply).
- Runner/cleaner progress tests moved to the tracker's deliberate API (`get/set/pop/clear`) instead of raw-dict access.
- **724 email unit tests pass**; blocking lint clean. No frontend change.

title: feat(email): 2.10 - sync resilience (backoff, orphan cleanup, category cache, 429)
body:
## Phase 2 — 2.10: sync resilience (backoff, orphan cleanup, category cache, 429)

Four hardening fixes so a failing account stops being hammered and the Outlook apply stops wasting Graph calls / eating throttles (review §2.1, §3.2).

### Scheduler (`scheduler.py`)
- **Exponential backoff on sync failure** — `_next_backoff` doubles from the interval each consecutive failure, capped ~1h, resets on the first success. A revoked/disconnected account was polled every 300s **forever** (a wasted auth handshake + Graph call 12×/hour). `_sync_account` returns `{"error": ...}` rather than raising, so the loop keys backoff on that dict **and** the outer exception.
- **Startup orphan cleanup** — `_close_orphaned_syncs` closes sync-log rows stuck `running` and accounts stuck `syncing`; a crash/restart mid-sync left them in-flight forever, lying to any "sync in progress?" check.

### Outlook provider (`outlook.py`)
- **masterCategories cache** — fetched once per provider instance instead of on every `set_labels`. A warm apply where the category already exists now makes **no** masterCategories call — turning the 3-Graph-call apply into 2 across a sweep. Cache stays consistent when a category is created.
- **Graph 429 Retry-After** — `_graph_send` honours one `Retry-After` (bounded to 30s) and retries the apply once, instead of surfacing the 429 as a phantom failed apply. `set_labels`' GET + PATCH route through it.

### Verification
- `test_email_sync_backoff` (doubling + cap + reset; orphan-close UPDATEs), `test_outlook_labels_cache_and_429` (fetch-once cache; no call when warm; 429 honours + caps Retry-After; success isn't retried).
- Existing tests that mock `set_labels` wholesale are unaffected; `test_email_labels_upstream` (real `_ensure_categories`) still green. Blocking lint clean. No migration, no frontend change.

Generated with Claude Code

title: feat(email): 2.6 - dedupe Outlook re-keys by internet_message_id
body:
## Phase 2 — 2.6: dedupe Outlook re-keys by internet_message_id

Outlook changes a message's `provider_message_id` when it moves folders. The ingest upsert keys on `(account_id, provider_message_id)`, so a re-keyed message didn't conflict with its row — it was **inserted again as a duplicate "ghost"**, then classified twice and skewing per-thread heuristics (review §3.1).

### Change
- **Migration 89** — `internet_message_id TEXT` (the stable RFC 5322 Message-ID) + a partial index `(account_id, internet_message_id)`. Deliberately **not** unique: legacy rows are NULL until re-synced, and forwarded mail can repeat a Message-ID — a hard constraint would reject and lose it.
- **Provider** — `EmailMessage` gains the field; the Outlook `$select` fetches `internetMessageId`, `_parse_graph_message` populates it. (All `EmailMessage` constructions are keyword args — the mid-dataclass field is position-safe.)
- **Upsert reclaim** — `upsert_message` points an existing row at the new provider id before inserting, so the message keeps **one** row (categories + `rules_processed_at` watermark ride along; not re-classified). The reclaim is **collision-free**: renames only when exactly one row carries the id and nothing already holds the new id, so it can never collapse two rows onto one `(account_id, provider id)`.
- `ON CONFLICT` refreshes the id via `COALESCE` (a provider that omits it never wipes a stored id).

### Historical ghosts — deferred to a script (by design)
Existing ghosts have NULL id today; the id must backfill via a sync cycle first, so they can't be merged at deploy time. `scripts/merge_ghost_messages.py` does the one-off pass afterward (dry-run by default) — keeps the newest row, folds the losers' categories + watermark in, deletes them. Same pattern as the #112 repair.

### Verification
- `test_email_persist_upsert`: reclaim emitted before insert with collision guards; no reclaim without an id or on the insert-only inbound path; id carried + refreshed. Existing upsert/label tests unaffected. Blocking lint clean.

Generated with Claude Code

title: feat(email): 2.4 - drafts carry Cc/Bcc (kill composer full-send branch)
body:
## Phase 2 — 2.4: drafts carry Cc/Bcc (kill the native-vs-full-send composer branch)

The draft write-path carried only **To**. A Cc/Bcc reply couldn't be saved as a draft, so every composer special-cased it into a **full send** — which starts a fresh, *unthreaded* message and discards the auto-saved draft. Three composers each carried that three-way branch (review §3.2).

### Change
- **Provider** — `create_draft`/`update_draft` gain `cc`/`bcc`. Outlook sets `ccRecipients`/`bccRecipients` on the draft (createReply PATCHes them on); Gmail/IMAP add MIME `Cc`/`Bcc`. `update_draft` only touches recipients when given, so a body-only autosave can't wipe a Cc the draft already has.
- **Transport** — `DraftUpsertRequest` + `PUT /drafts` carry cc/bcc; `_upsert_local_draft` mirrors them into `cc_addresses`/`bcc_addresses` so a reopened draft shows them at once.
- **Composers** — EmailDetail / ConversationView / ComposePanel now send a Cc'd reply via the **native draft path** (Drafts → Sent, threaded). The full-send detour is reserved for attachments/artifacts only.

Native send preserves Cc/Bcc: recipients live on the provider draft and Graph's send uses the stored message; the sign-in-place `update_draft` passes `cc=None` so it never clears them.

### Deferred (by design)
Attachment **content** on drafts needs an upload flow — still routes via full send. `create_draft` already accepts `attachments` for when that lands.

### Verification
- `test_outlook_draft_cc`: `ccRecipients`/`bccRecipients` on create (standalone + reply PATCH) and update; a body-only update leaves them untouched. 101 draft-related tests pass; blocking lint clean; frontend `tsc` clean (dead `sendEmail` import removed).

Generated with Claude Code

title: feat(email): 2.7 - digest is a projection (aggregates, self-exclusion, HTML)
body:
## Phase 2 — 2.7: digest is a projection (shared aggregates, self-exclusion, HTML, empty-suppression)

The digest re-derived inbox aggregates with its own SQL — the standing risk of drifting from what Analytics computes (the class behind the 1.6 needs-reply lie). Make it a projection and stop it counting itself (review §2.5).

### Change
- **Composed from named helpers** — `_generate_digest` now composes `_digest_totals` / `_digest_categories` / `_digest_top_senders` / `_digest_needs_reply`, each testable and each reading one shared windowed inbound-inbox definition. needs-reply stays on `email_thread_status`.
- **Self-exclusion everywhere** — the account's own address is dropped from totals and the category breakdown too (not just top-senders). The digest email lands in the inbox *from the account*; counting it (plus self-notes / BCC-to-self) inflated the next digest. One shared `_DIGEST_INBOUND` predicate.
- **HTML body** — `_render_digest_html` renders a self-contained, escaped HTML version alongside the Markdown; both send paths pass `body_html`.
- **Empty-digest suppression** — the scheduler skips a digest with no new mail AND nothing awaiting a reply, *without* stamping `last_digest_at`, so a later arrival the same day still delivers. Manual "send now" is never suppressed.

### Deferred (by design)
Unifying with `analytics.py`'s own aggregate helpers (the audited module — not worth destabilising mid-refactor) and merging the two frontend digest config dialogs.

### Verification
- `test_email_digest`: every windowed aggregate excludes self + binds `:self`; totals + both bodies returned; empty detection; HTML escapes sender/category text. Blocking lint clean.

Generated with Claude Code

title: refactor(email): 2.2 - classify_matches, one match→resolve enforcement point (#110)
body:
## Phase 2 — 2.2: one match→resolve enforcement point (`classify_matches`)

A conversation has ONE classification, re-evaluated per message (#110). That invariant was enforced at only *some* call sites — the live runner and the Reply Zero backfill resolved the conversation, but **`/rules/run-message` skipped it**, a bypass that let an explicit re-run splinter a thread the runner would have kept whole (review §3.1/§2.2).

### Change
Put match → conversation-resolve in **one** reusable function, `engine.classify_matches`:
- matches (single or multi per `multi_rule`),
- unless `resolve` is off, re-evaluates the whole thread so it keeps its single status (resolver is cost-aware — no model call on bulk mail; degrades to per-message on failure),
- raises `LLMUnavailable` on a classifier outage (a real no-match still returns `[]`), so callers skip the watermark.

Routed through it:
- **`_run_rules_job`** (highest-volume new-mail path) — behaviour-preserving; the match+resolve it already did is now the shared call, so any future path inherits the invariant.
- **`/rules/run-message` apply** — now resolves (**bypass closed**); `resolve=True` for apply, skipped for the `is_test` dry-run.
- **Reply Zero backfill** — same shared path as the live runner.

`approved_includes_only` is already an explicit engine parameter (cleanup passes `True`), so no change needed there.

### Deferred (own risk/scope)
Routing "Process past emails" through the resolver (it interacts with `_project_thread_status_for_backfill` — needs its own verification) and the provisional-column marker from 1.4 (a schema migration).

### Verification
- `test_email_classify_matches`: resolve-off never calls the resolver; resolve-on does; `multi_rule` uses the multi matcher; an outage propagates; a no-match normalises to `[]`. 64 runner/backfill tests still green; blocking lint clean.

Generated with Claude Code

title: fix(email): 2.1 (core) - manual sync stops losing refresh tokens + wiping cursor
body:
## Phase 2 — 2.1 (core): manual sync stops losing refresh tokens and wiping the cursor

`trigger_sync` (manual) and `_sync_account` (scheduler) are two sync cores that had drifted. Two concrete defects on the manual path (review §3.2):

- **Refresh-token loss** — `trigger_sync` persisted a rotated OAuth token only at the *end* of the sync. Microsoft rotates the refresh token on every refresh, so any failure between auth and the end lost the new token → the account needed a manual reconnect. Now it persists **immediately after auth** (before the sync body), exactly as the scheduler does.
- **Cursor drift** — it wrote `last_history_id = :history_id` unconditionally, but Outlook runs full-snapshot with `new_history_id = None`, so a manual sync **wiped the cursor to NULL**. `COALESCE` keeps the existing one, matching the scheduler.

### Deferred (the risky remainder of 2.1)
Fully collapsing `trigger_sync` into a thin wrapper over `_sync_account`, and **reviving label-change learning on the scheduler path** (dead in production — only the manual path runs it). That needs a shared sync body / per-message hook so the pre-upsert category diff survives the email_ingestion↔gateway layer boundary — its own change, warranting live-account verification rather than a blind smoke-test-only pass.

### Verification
- `test_email_manual_sync_parity` pins the post-auth persist ordering and the `COALESCE` cursor guard on the `trigger_sync` source. Blocking lint clean.

Generated with Claude Code

title: feat(email): drafts carry attachments — no more full-send detour (2.4)
body:
## Phase 2 · item 2.4 (remainder)

The cc/bcc half of 2.4 shipped in #119; this finishes it by carrying **attachment content** on the draft, killing the last arm of the three-way native-vs-full-send branch in the composers.

### Before
Draft transport carried To/Cc/Bcc but not files. Any reply/compose with an uploaded file or an AI artifact fell back to a fresh full send — which starts an **unthreaded** message and discards the auto-saved draft.

### After
- `update_draft` gains an `attachments` param across `base`/`outlook`/`gmail`. Outlook POSTs the files to the draft's attachments collection (the same endpoint `create_draft` already used); Gmail rebuilds the draft as a MIME multipart.
- `DraftUpsertRequest` carries `attachments` (base64) + `artifacts` (workspace refs), resolved to provider bytes by `_resolve_draft_attachments` — reusing the exact resolution the `/send` path does (base64 decode + `load_artifact_attachments`).
- The local mirror sets `has_attachments` **sticky-true**, so a later attachment-less auto-save can't clear the flag.
- Both composers (`ComposePanel`, `EmailDetail`) now save-the-draft-with-attachments → native send whenever there's a draft **or** attachments; a plain no-attachment message still sends fresh.

### Why it can't duplicate
Attachments ride only on the **explicit pre-send save** — the debounced auto-save omits them — so `update_draft` uploads each file exactly once. `/drafts/send`'s body-only re-sign PATCH doesn't touch the attachments collection, so they survive to the native send.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_draft_attachments.py` — Outlook update/create upload the bytes; a body-only autosave never touches `/attachments`; the resolver decodes base64 and rejects bad encoding. All green; blocking ruff + full `tsc` clean.

title: feat(email): Fix strips the wrong label off the corrected message (3.4 / H6)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.4 (review H6)

`rule_feedback` taught patterns + guidance so **future** mail classified right, but the message the user corrected **kept its wrong category chip** — the fix looked ignored until the next matching email arrived.

### What changed
- **`remove_label`** — the mirror of `apply_label`: provider-FIRST (so an authoritative round-trip provider like Outlook doesn't re-add it next sync), then a race-free `array_remove` on the local `categories` mirror.
- **`correct_applied_labels`** — after teaching, strips the label(s) the wrongly-matched cleanup rules applied and, when the correction names a cleanup rule, applies that rule's label. It reads the exact `email_actions` LABEL values the **undo path** already uses, so it strips precisely what the rule put on, and never removes a label it's about to re-apply.
- Conversation-status corrections set thread state (not a category), so they're excluded here.
- The Fix toast now says which label it removed (`Removed "Newsletter" from this email.`).

### Safety
Best-effort and self-contained: a provider hiccup updates the local mirror and returns what it managed, **never unwinding what `rule_feedback` already taught**.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_fix_strips_label.py` — strips wrong + applies correct (provider-first); "none" only removes; never strips a label being re-applied; provider-auth failure still corrects the local mirror. Existing fix/pattern suites still green (16 passed); blocking ruff + full `tsc` clean.

title: feat(email): rule-path draft context parity + compose-assist learning (3.8)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.8 (review §2.4)

The automation drafting paths had drifted from the interactive ones. Four fixes bring them to parity:

1. **Rule-path uses the shared context builder.** `_apply_rule_actions` hand-assembled a reply-context dict carrying neither `sender_scope` nor the To/Cc lines — so the direction note + greet-by-name were **silently no-ops on the highest-volume drafting path**. It now builds through the ONE `_build_reply_context` (same builder `/draft-reply` and "Draft with AI" use), falling back to the old dict only if the row can't be resolved.
2. **compose-assist teaches.** Its reply-from-scratch now stores the AI draft (`_store_ai_draft`) like `/draft-reply` does, so a composer edit before send teaches `_learn_from_sent`. "Draft with AI" taught nothing before.
3. **Follow-up nudge hydration.** The nudge drafter read `body_text or snippet` — a header-only Outlook row gave it a ~200-char cutoff — and now hydrates the full body first (the **last surviving snippet-bug path**).
4. **Pop-out carries `messageId`.** The popped-out composer now passes the local message id so its "Draft with AI" loads the same reply context the inline reply had (it drafted context-blind before).

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_rulepath_draft_parity.py` pins all three backend wirings on the source. Full draft/compose/reply/follow suite green (124 passed, 0 regressions); blocking ruff + `tsc` clean.

title: feat(email): search filter UI — date range, sender category, importance (3.12)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.12

The search backend already filtered on `received_after`/`received_before` and sender category, but the bar exposed **no controls** for them; importance wasn't a search filter at all. This surfaces all three.

### Backend
`/search` gains an `importance` param (case-insensitive match on `em.importance`), composed alongside the existing additive filters.

### Frontend
Four new pill kinds in the search model:
- **after / before** — date range (a bare `before` date runs to the END of that day, so mail that arrived on it isn't excluded)
- **sendercat** — `email_senders.category`, distinct from a `tag` pill (which matches a label on the *message*)
- **importance** — high / normal / low

The filter menu grows **Date** (native date pickers), **Sender category** (chips from `EMAIL_CATEGORIES`), and **Importance** (High/Normal/Low) sections. `after:` / `before:` / `importance:` are also typeable in the bar, consistent with the existing `from:`/`tag:` grammar.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_search_scope.py` — importance predicate is case-insensitive and absent when unset (23 passed). Blocking ruff + full `tsc` clean.

title: feat(email): reject an in-force pattern, restore a rejected one (3.6)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.6

The pattern-review screen let you approve/reject only **pending** patterns. Gaps:
- An **In force** (approved) pattern offered only **Forget** — which *deletes* the row, so the auto-learner re-infers the same pattern within the hour. The sticky verdict (**Reject**, which `_upsert_rule_pattern`'s re-learn guard respects) had no UI. → "endpoint exists, no UI".
- A **rejected** pattern couldn't be restored at all.

### Change
Pure UI. `PatternRow` now renders actions by which handlers it's given:
- **In force** rows gain **Reject** (alongside Forget). Reject is titled "won't be re-learned", distinguishing it from Forget's plain delete.
- **Rejected** rows gain **Restore** (approve).

The `/rules/patterns/review` endpoint already supported reject/approve of any pattern by id — only "approve all" (no ids) is scoped to the pending set.

### Deferred (documented in-commit)
Manual pattern-add UI / dropping the unused `USER` source badge, and re-exposing exclude-teaching from the "None" Fix — lower-value/speculative vs the concrete gap here.

### Tests
`test_email_pattern_approval.py` gains a test pinning that by-id review is **not** gated to pending (the guarantee the new buttons depend on). 17 passed; `tsc` clean.

title: feat(email): digest becomes a daily brief — backlog aging + commitments due (3.11)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.11

After 1.6 (digest honesty) and 2.7 (digest = projection), the digest still only tallied **volume**. A brief's job is to say what needs **doing**, so it now leads with two action sections:

- **Commitments due** — open GTD tasks captured from a sent reply on this account (linked via `gtd_items.origin.account_id/thread_id`, see `tasks/email_link.py`) due within ~3 days or overdue, soonest first. **Best-effort**: a deploy without the tasks feature never breaks the digest.
- **Awaiting your reply** — the oldest `NEEDS_REPLY` threads from the Reply-Zero status table, **aged** ("waiting 5 days"), so the backlog reads as "these are going stale", not a bare count.

Both bodies (Markdown + HTML) render the sections **action-first**, above the category/sender tallies; the in-app `DigestView` shows matching cards. A quiet inbox day with commitments due or an aging backlog is now correctly **not** suppressed — exactly the day a brief earns its place.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_digest.py` — backlog reads NEEDS_REPLY oldest-first; commitments scope to open/due tasks on this account and are best-effort when the tasks table is absent; a quiet inbox with commitments/backlog stays non-empty; both bodies render the sections. 11 passed; `tsc` clean.

title: feat(email): reclassify drains the whole mailbox, resumably + tracked (3.7)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.7

The Reply-Zero rebuild ran a **fixed 8 passes** (200 threads each), so on a real 3,500-thread mailbox it rebuilt only the newest ~1,600 and left the rest on the old classifier — a click that looked like "reclassify everything" but didn't.

### Now it drains
The job loops until nothing still needs a status (`_count_reply_zero_backlog` — the same "needs work" predicate the backfill selects on), with:
- **No-progress stop** — if a pass doesn't shrink the backlog (LLM down → the inbound remainder can't be classified), it stops instead of spinning to the safety cap. Those threads keep their gap, so re-triggering picks up where it left off — **resumable by construction**.
- **Progress tracking** via the shared token-guarded `JobTracker`, polled at the new `GET /email/reply-zero/reclassify/status` (total / remaining / processed).
- **Concurrency guard** — a second reclassify while one is draining is refused (`already_running`), not run in parallel doubling the LLM spend.
- **Synchronous running-row seed** before scheduling, so an immediate poll sees "running", not a gap.

Deterministic FYI-filing already handles the bulk of an old mailbox with no LLM call, so the drain is cheap where it can be and bounded where it can't.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_reclassify_resumable.py` — drains until zero; stops on a no-progress pass; endpoint seeds running state + queues with the token; refuses a concurrent rebuild; status hides the token / is idle when nothing ran. 6 passed; reply-zero suite green (36); blocking ruff clean. Backend-only (no UI trigger exists today).

title: feat(email): draft in my voice — semantic Sent few-shot in reply context (3.1)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.1 (depends on 2.5)

The long-requested **"draft in my voice"**, now cheap. `_fetch_sent_fewshot` embeds what's being replied to and cosine-matches the account's **own Sent mail** (any recipient) via `email_embeddings`, injecting the top-3 quote-stripped bodies into the reply prompt as a **voice block**.

Distinct from `sender_examples` (past replies to *this* sender → the relationship); the few-shot shows the **register** for this *kind* of message.

Wired into the single `_build_reply_context`, so every drafting entry point (`/draft-reply`, "Draft with AI", and the rule path via 3.8) gets it. The current thread is excluded so a reply can't echo itself.

### Safe + dormant until enabled
`embed_query` returns `None` when `email_semantic_search_enabled` is off (no LLM call, no DB query), so this adds **zero cost and no examples** until embeddings are populated — matching the 2.5 dependency.

⚠️ **Enablement is a separate decision:** turning on `email_semantic_search_enabled` starts a **token-costing background embedding sweep on the live mailbox**. I did not flip it here. Say the word and I'll enable it (one-line default change) and watch the sweep populate embeddings so this activates — then verify a draft actually picks up the voice examples on the live account.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_sent_fewshot.py` — true no-op (no DB, no cost) when the flag is off; targets Sent mail ordered by cosine distance and excludes the current thread; strips quoted chains; swallows embed failures. 3 passed; existing draft-context suite green (18); blocking ruff clean.

title: feat(email): KB ranked by relevance, and out of the classifier prompt (3.5)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.5

Two knowledge-base problems, both fixed **always-on** (no embedding dependency, no dormancy):

### 1. Relevance ranking (was recency first-fit)
The KB filled the 4k drafting budget by **recency**, so the newest entries won even when an older one actually answered the email. `_load_assistant_about` now takes a `query` (the message being replied to / composed) and ranks the KB by lexical term-overlap before the budget fill — pulling a wider recency window (40) so there's something to reorder. No query → recency (unchanged). Wired into `/draft-reply` and `/compose-assist`.

### 2. KB out of the thread-status classifier
The same enriched `about` (KB included) fed the thread-status classifier, where drafting facts are **pure noise + token cost** — that prompt only decides whether a thread needs a reply. `include_kb=False` now drops the block **and skips the `email_knowledge` query entirely** on the three thread-status determination paths in `replyzero`.

The embedding-based cosine variant can layer on later once semantic search is enabled; lexical relevance already replaces recency-first-fit today.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_kb_relevance.py` — ranking surfaces the relevant entry; no-query keeps recency; ties stable; `include_kb=False` drops the block without querying the table; default ranks by query. 5 passed; classifier + draft suites green (76); blocking ruff clean.

title: feat(email): calendar-aware scheduling replies (3.10)
body:
## Phase 3 · item 3.10

Re-scoped now that the CommandCenter calendar/timeboxing app is live (#71) — the old blocker "needs a calendar integration" is gone. When an incoming email **asks about timing**, the drafter now sees the owner's upcoming hard-date commitments so it can offer **clash-free slots and never double-book**.

- **`_asks_about_scheduling`** — a cheap keyword heuristic (meeting / available / reschedule / "when are you free" / "let's meet" / …). An LLM check per draft would cost a call for a signal this easy to spot.
- **`_fetch_calendar_context`** — the account user's `gtd_items` with `due_at + is_hard_date` in the next ~10 days (the same "shows on the Calendar" predicate the tasks app uses), open only, soonest first. **Best-effort** — a deploy without the tasks feature never breaks a draft.

Wired into the single `_build_reply_context`: the calendar is pulled **only** when the message reads as a scheduling ask (an ordinary reply never carries the owner's schedule) and injected as a prompt block telling the drafter to avoid clashes. External Google/Outlook calendar sync stays deferred — this reads the **internal** calendar.

### Tests
`tests/unit/test_email_calendar_context.py` — intent heuristic fires on scheduling asks and not ordinary mail; the fetch reads open hard-date items in-window for this account's user; best-effort on a missing table; empty when nothing scheduled. 5 passed; draft-context suite green (17 total); blocking ruff clean.

title: feat(email): conversation collapse in the mailbox list (3.2)
body:
## What & why

The browse list rendered **every message as its own row** — a five-message thread was five rows each wearing a "5" badge. This collapses it: the mailbox reads at **thread level**, one row per conversation (its newest message in the current view represents the thread), and the total counts **conversations, not messages**.

This is the UI half of the one-classification-per-conversation invariant (#110/#113) — master plan **3.2**.

## Changes

- **Backend** — `GET /email/messages` gains `collapse: bool` (default **off**). When on and no `thread_id`, it `DISTINCT ON` the conversation key `COALESCE(thread_id, id::text)` (newest matching message per thread) and totals `COUNT(DISTINCT key)`. A NULL-thread message stays its own conversation. Ignored inside a thread load; default-off keeps the assistant's per-message inbox queries unchanged.
- **Frontend** — `listEmails()` defaults `collapse=true`, so every mailbox browse (folder / label / uncategorized, first page + load-more + backfill) reads at thread level. **Search stays per-message** (keeps its match highlight). The list row already renders the `threadCount` badge, so no row-render change was needed.

title: feat(email): snooze a conversation until later (3.3, part 1)
body:
## What & why

The first half of master-plan **3.3**. A conversation you can't deal with now can be **snoozed** — sent out of the inbox and brought back at a chosen time. One of the two most-missed daily-driver features vs any modern client (schedule-send is the other; it follows as its own PR).

## Design: a stamp, not a scheduler

Snooze sets `snoozed_until` on the message. The **wake is at query time** (`snoozed_until IS NULL OR snoozed_until <= now()`), so the conversation reappears on its own — **no background job, no scheduler**. Applied **per-conversation**: the endpoint stamps every message sharing the `thread_id`, so the whole thread leaves and returns together (a lone message is stamped on its own).

## Changes

- **Migration 90** — `email_messages.snoozed_until` + partial index on the non-NULL rows.
- **Backend** — `core.folder_scope` gains the `snoozed` view (`snoozed_until > now()`); `GET /messages` excludes sleeping mail from **every browse** except the Snoozed view and a thread load (opening a snoozed thread still shows all of it); new `POST /messages/{id}/snooze` stamps the thread, `until=null` un-snoozes. App-local — there's no provider concept of snooze, so nothing is pushed upstream.
- **Frontend** — a **Snoozed** sidebar view; right-click **Snooze until…** with presets (later today / tomorrow 8am / this weekend / next week) and **Unsnooze** in the Snoozed view; optimistic drop-from-list then reconcile; `snoozedUntil` on the `Email` type.

## Verification
- `pytest test_email_snooze.py test_email_conversation_collapse.py test_email_messages_filter.py` — 20 passed (scope predicate, browse exclusion, Snoozed view, thread-load pass-through, thread-wide stamp, un-snooze, lone-message, ownership 404).
- Blocking ruff clean; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Reviewer note
Core mailbox behaviour, no e2e in CI — worth a visual pass: right-click a conversation → Snooze until Tomorrow, confirm it leaves the inbox and appears under **Snoozed**, then Unsnooze it back. Migration auto-applies on deploy.

title: email Phase 2: provider_session helper (2.11 request paths) + stale-plan re-audit
body:
## What this is

The first slice of the Phase 2 "converge the seams" work — plus an important
correction: **re-auditing Phase 2 against the code showed the plan was badly
stale.** Several items were quietly completed alongside Phase 1 / migrations
88–90 and never struck. This PR ships the one clean safe-dedup that genuinely
remained, and records the true state.

### 1. `provider_session()` — 2.11 (partial: helper + request paths)

The instantiate → `authenticate()` → `_persist_rotated_creds` dance was
hand-copied at every provider call site, each a chance to forget the persist
and drop a refreshed OAuth token (next request then re-auths from a stale
refresh token and eventually fails). Now in ONE place — an async context
manager that:

- loads the provider (user-scoped, 404 on miss), authenticates, and persists
  rotated creds in a `finally` **only on a clean exit** — never after the body
  raised (a half-failed request must not commit a token write onto a
  rolling-back session). Preserves the pre-refactor "persist after the work
  succeeds" ordering exactly; the caller still owns `db.commit()`.
- `require_auth=True` → HTTP 401 on auth failure (send/draft write paths);
  `require_auth=False` → yields `authed=False` so best-effort readers branch.

**Converted (clean user-scoped request paths):** `hydrate_message_body`, the two
draft-create handlers, the digest test-send, mailto-unsubscribe. **+6 unit tests**
covering persist-on-clean-exit, no-persist-on-raise, auth gating, and scope.

**Deliberately deferred to Tier A** (documented in the plan): the large `/send`
handler (persist sits mid-body among post-send learning) and the
background/scheduler jobs (digest scheduled-send, cleaner sweep, senders
categorize) — those query by `account_id` with no user, so they need an
unscoped loader variant + a live sync-cycle to validate.

### 2. Stale-plan re-audit (docs)

`email_app_master_plan.md` Phase 2 table corrected against code. Verified **DONE**
(were listed open): **2.8** (mig 88 + inserts name the arbiter), **2.9** (shared

`masterCategories` cache + 429), **2.12** (`count_damaged_conversation_threads`
→ `data_health`). **Schema+code done, one-off remains:** 2.6. **PARTIAL:** 2.1,

title: email 2.2: one apply+watermark enforcement point
body:
## What

Tier-A structural convergence, item **2.2**. The match→resolve half of the
classification pipeline was already one place (`classify_matches`); this collapses
the **apply+watermark** half, which was hand-rolled at **four** sites — the
single-message re-run, process-past, the live runner (`_run_rules_job`), and the
PENDING-execution retry. Each re-implemented the apply loop, the "no rule matched"
SKIPPED row, and the permanent `rules_processed_at` stamp with its "only when the
run could act" guard — four chances for one copy to drift and burn mail the run
never touched (the expired-refresh-token bug class).

### Two shared helpers now own it
- **`_apply_matches`** — the apply loop (with the `sole_match` learning guard),
  the no-match SKIPPED row, and the cold-email blocker.
- **`_stamp_processed_watermark`** — the guarded stamp (`dry_run or provider is
  None → skip`).

After this there is **exactly one** `rules_processed_at = now()` write and
**exactly one** `_apply_and_log_match` call in `runner.py`.

### Deliberate carve-out preserved
`_process_past_emails_job` still classifies **oldest-first with the raw match
helpers** (inline resolve would let a thread's oldest message decide its status —
the exact thing the live runner's newest-first ordering prevents), but now routes
its apply+watermark through the shared helpers. The runner keeps Reply Zero
projection **between** apply and stamp, so the watermark stays last.

## Behaviour
Preserved exactly — guards, ordering, dry-run / no-provider semantics, the
cold-blocker `!= "OFF"` condition. No functional change; pure convergence.

## Testing
- `pytest -k email` → **812 passed**
- New `test_email_apply_and_watermark.py` (9 behavioural tests: watermark
  guard × dry-run/no-provider, per-match apply + sole flag, no-match SKIPPED,
  `log_no_match`, cold-blocker policy)

  updated to assert the invariant at its new single home

full suite green. Wants a live sync-cycle to confirm on the real account before
2.1. No migration.

title: email 2.1: revive label-learning on the scheduler sync path
body:
## What

Tier-A item **2.1**, the **defect half**. Only `trigger_sync` (the manual route)
learned FROM-classification patterns from the label changes a user makes in their
mail client. The **scheduler** — which is what actually polls every ~300s —
never did; its `_sync_account` persist loop just upserted. So every manual
re-label in Outlook between the rare manual syncs was **silently dropped**, and
inbox-zero's LABEL_ADDED / LABEL_REMOVED learning was effectively dead in prod.

## Why a plain hook couldn't do it

The learner needs a message's categories **before** the upsert — the upsert
overwrites them on a categories-authoritative provider (Outlook) — so the
existing `(account_id) → None` post-sync hooks can't recover the "before".

## Wiring (layering preserved)

- **`post_sync.py`** — `PostSyncHooks.learn_label_changes`, a hook that carries
  the per-message `(message, old_categories)` pairs, + `run_label_learn_hook`.
  `email_ingestion` stays standalone: an unregistered hook is a no-op.
- **`_sync_account`** — captures `old_categories` in its persist loop (gated on a
  learner being registered **and** an incremental sync — a deep backfill would
  mislearn, the same gate the manual route uses) and calls the hook after commit.
- **`scheduler_hooks.learn_label_changes`** (gateway) runs the shared
  `sync.learn_from_label_change_events` orchestrator — the **same** learner the
  manual route uses — so both paths learn identically. `email_ingestion` only
  touches the registry; the gateway registers the impl.

Best-effort throughout: a learning failure logs and never fails the sync.

## Deferred (pure dedup)

Collapsing `trigger_sync` into a thin `_sync_account` wrapper + deleting its
duplicated persist/reconcile/watermark loop — that rewrites the **live
manual-sync response path**, so it waits until this learning revival is confirmed
on a live cycle. Tracked in the plan.

## Testing
- `pytest -k email` → **819 passed**; new `test_email_label_learn_hook.py` → **7**
  (invoker gating, orchestrator no-rules/empty/learns-each+applies-corrections,
  and that the hook is actually **registered** at startup)
- CI-blocking ruff clean; compile clean

## Risk
Medium — adds an indexed SELECT-per-message on incremental syncs (small batches)
and a best-effort post-commit hook; no change to fetch/persist/reconcile/watermark
or the manual route. **Watch the first live sync cycle** to confirm learning fires
without noise. No migration.

## What & why

Reworks the Next-Actions UI (cards, list, board, filter) so status, priority, and context all read with one consistent visual language.

### Status control (no more Done button)
- The card's status control is now a single **status indicator** — the "Done button" look is gone. The last stage is just Done like any other stage, coloured by the same `stageAccent` the board columns and list headers use, so status reads the same everywhere. Clicking it is the only way to change status.

title: email 2.6: one-off ghost-row merge script
body:
## What

Tier-A item **2.6**, the remaining one-off. Migration 89 + the `internet_message_id`
reclaim already stopped **new** Outlook re-key ghosts from forming; this cleans the
duplicates that predate the fix.

`scripts/merge_ghost_messages.py` merges rows sharing a backfilled
`(account_id, internet_message_id)`:
- keeps the **richest** survivor — a classified row (`rules_processed_at` set) first,
  then the newest `received_at` ("prefer the newest provider id", mig 89);
- **carries** a sibling's categories / `rules_processed_at` onto the survivor where it
  lacks them, so a merge never drops a classification;
- **repoints** the FKs that `SET NULL` on delete (`email_executed_rules`,
  `email_rule_guidance`) onto the survivor, so audit/guidance history keeps its message;
- **deletes** the ghosts — their `email_attachments` / `email_embeddings` CASCADE away,
  being duplicates of the survivor's.

Rows whose `internet_message_id` is still NULL are **reported, not merged** — their
stable id can't be known until they re-sync (mig 89's note). Dry-run by default.

## How the user runs it (live)
```
# 1) sync to backfill internet_message_id on existing rows
# 2) dry run — see the groups + how many NULL rows still need a re-sync
uv run python scripts/merge_ghost_messages.py
# 3) merge
uv run python scripts/merge_ghost_messages.py --apply
```

## Risk
The **script** is inert — not imported by the app, no runtime effect until run by
hand. It mutates live data only under `--apply`; dry-run reports the exact plan
first. Follows the #112 `repair_conversation_threads.py` precedent. No migration.
CI-blocking ruff + compile clean.

## What

Completes **2.11** (first half was #139). Converts the deferred sites — the `/send`
handler and every background/scheduler job — onto `provider_session`, so the
instantiate → authenticate → persist-rotated-creds dance now exists in exactly one
place across the whole email package.

### New: unscoped mode
`provider_session(db, None, account_id=...)` — `user_email=None` selects an
**unscoped** account loader (`_provider_for_account_any`) for background work that
has no request user (scheduler ticks, webhook tasks, fire-and-forget cleanups).
Message-scoped sessions still require a user (no background path loads by message).

### Converted
| Site | Mode |
|---|---|
| `/send` (full handler) | user-scoped, 401 on auth fail |
| digest scheduled send | unscoped, quiet-skip on auth fail |

contract for zero dedup value.

## What

Completes **2.3** — the mechanical, import-only split of the two monolith modules,
in two commits:

### Commit 1 — `runner.py` → `actions.py` + `learning.py` (2,344 → 1,735)

title: fix(email): digest send 500 — commitments query uuid=text + poisoned transaction
body:
## What broke

`POST /email/digest/send` returned 500 (`InFailedSQLTransactionError`) while the digest preview (GET) looked fine.

## Root cause (reproduced on prod via `PREPARE`)

`_digest_commitments` bound `:aid` twice — once against `email_accounts.id` (**uuid**) and once against `gi.origin->>''account_id''` (**text**). Postgres deduces ONE type per prepared-statement parameter, picked uuid, and every call failed with `operator does not exist: text = uuid`. The `except Exception: return []` swallowed it — but left the transaction **aborted**, so:

- **GET /digest** → 200 (commitments is the last query in the request; nothing after it to fail)
- **POST /digest/send** → 500 (the next query, `provider_session`''s account lookup, hits the poisoned transaction)

The unit test passed because the DB is mocked — asyncpg type deduction never runs.

## Fix

- json side compares to `ea.id::text`; `:aid` now binds once, in the uuid context (fixed SQL PREPARE+EXECUTEs cleanly against prod — and there''s a real commitment due that now surfaces)
- the best-effort catch now **rolls back and logs** instead of silently poisoning the rest of the request

Tests: rollback-on-failure pin + SQL-shape pin updated; 825 email unit tests green.

title: feat(tasks): surface list-level ClickUp statuses (e.g. Done) + multiple assignees
body:
## 1. Investigation: the missing "Done" stage

**Root cause.** ClickUp statuses were only ever collected from the **space workflow** (`get_schema` read `space.statuses`). But ClickUp lists routinely define their own statuses — commonly a "Done" (a `done`-type status) that's distinct from the space-level "Closed". A list-only status therefore never reached:
- the **status-mapping settings** (fed by the schema cache), nor
- a **synced task's Stage picker** (`account.statuses`, also the schema cache),

so the only closing status the user could pick was the space-level "Closed". (Completion itself already worked — `map_pulled_task` treats `status_type in ("closed","done")` as done — it was purely that the *name* "Done" was invisible.)

**Fix — three layers, no extra ClickUp API calls:**
- `get_schema` now aggregates each **list's own `statuses`** (already present on the `/space/{id}/list` and folder payloads) alongside the space workflow.
- Each sync folds the status **names actually seen on pulled tasks** into the cached schema — ground truth for whatever statuses a list really uses.
- The `/status-catalog` endpoint unions **distinct `provider_status` from mirrored tasks**, so a status is mappable immediately, before any schema refresh.

## 2. Multiple assignees

ClickUp allows several assignees but we stored only the first (`assignees[0]`). Now the full set is stored and editable:
- **Migration 91** adds `gtd_items.assignees` (JSONB), backfilled from the single `assignee`. The existing `assignee` column stays as the primary/display owner (`= assignees[0]`), so every single-owner reader (card avatar, Waiting-For "who", delegate flow) is unchanged.
- **Sync** stores every assignee; the item read (`SELECT i.*`) returns the full set.
- **PATCH** accepts `assignees` (the whole set); the ClickUp back-sync diffs new vs previous into an `{add, rem}` assignee delta.
- **UI**: the detail card's Assignee editor is a multi-select toggle list for synced tasks (local tasks keep the single-owner delegate flow, since assigning a teammate must first create the ClickUp task); cards show a "+N" on the avatar when a task is shared.

## Testing
- Backend: `py_compile` clean; `ruff` introduces no new errors (per-file counts identical to main); `pytest tests/unit/test_tasks_gtd.py test_task_broker_handlers.py test_tasks_archive_upstream.py` → **128 passed**.

Adds `ai-company-brain/specs/calendar_ai_review.md` — a comprehensive audit of the calendar application, its integration with the GTD task manager, and every AI surface in the stack — plus the two audit findings that could be fixed frontend-only.

## The review covers

title: feat(email): mailbox Dashboard — open-loop ledgers with actions (+ status truth fixes)

## Why

User audit request: "Is my digest working? It doesn''t provide correct information about due commitments, pending replies, and the actions I should take." The audit found the action half broken, and this PR builds the requested **Dashboard** on top of the fixed data.

## Truth fixes (verified against the live DB)

- **Replying can no longer leave you "owing a reply"** — `recompute_thread_status` clamps a REPLY verdict to AWAITING when the *real* last message is our side (fact over judgment; reason discloses the coercion). 10 of 29 live NEEDS_REPLY rows were threads the user had already answered.
- **Trashed/junked threads leave the ledgers** — a trashed thread sat in "awaiting your reply" for weeks.
- **Undated commitments become visible** — 3 of the user''s 4 open promises had no due date and were filtered out.

## Dashboard (one computation, two projections)

- `_generate_digest(full=True)` = the in-app projection: full lists (cap 50) with `thread_id`/`message_id`/`who`, the **Waiting on them** (AWAITING) ledger, undated commitments. The scheduled email keeps its small-cap brief (+ a waiting-on-them section).
- `DashboardView` (feature key stays `digest`): **Needs your reply** and **Waiting on them** ledgers — every row opens its conversation via `openEmailById`, with row actions **Mark done** (`/reply-zero/resolve`, closes captured tasks too) and **Snooze 1d**; commitments; category + noisy-sender analytics; 5-stat header (adds Waiting-on-them).
- Sidebar/header: **Digest → Dashboard**.

title: feat(tasks): full-width single-header inbox + ground every AI prompt in real system state
body:
## Inbox layout — full width, one compact header

The centered `max-w-4xl` inbox stacked a capture hero, a controls block, and a filter-pill row (~6 rows, list started ~520px down). Now full width like Next Actions, two compact rows (list starts ~150px down):

- **Row 1 (desktop):** Inbox title · capture box (flex-1: "What's on your mind? Capture now, clarify later.") · attach/link icons · Mind sweep · Shortcuts. Mobile keeps its bottom-nav capture (unchanged).
- **Row 2:** `N to process` + source/aging chips · date pills inline · search · sort · density · Tickler · **Clarify next**. On mobile the search/action cluster wraps to its own full-width line.
- **Task list spans the full width**, so long captures display whole instead of truncating in a narrow column.

## AI prompts — every decision grounded in real system state

Audited every LLM prompt in the task manager (clarify, enrich/fill-details, context backfill, title improve, atomize/dedup, parent-step match, email capture, commitment detection). Three systemic gaps fixed:

1. **Hard-coded @context vocabulary** — clarify, enrich, email capture, and commitment detection listed four of the six default contexts in their JSON schemas; a user-configured context (or even `@office`/`@home`) could **never** be suggested. All now inject the user's real `gtd_contexts`, and model output is canonicalized against that list — never invented.
2. **No current date** in clarify/enrich — "by Friday" or "next week" couldn't resolve to a real due date. Both now receive TODAY (weekday + ISO); email capture already had it.
3. **Clarify never proposed a time estimate** even though the proposal UI displays one (heuristic-only before). The clarify schema now includes `time_estimate_mins` (bounded 1–6000, shared parser with enrich), flowing through `propose_with_llm` into the card.

Prompts already well-grounded and left alone: atomize (deliberately preserves the user's wording), title improve, parent-step match (scoped semantic judgment), and the people/projects/stages/memory context in clarify.

Bonus: `ai.py` is now fully ruff-clean — extracting `_parse_minutes` + a validated optional-field update dropped `_llm_propose` below the C901 complexity limit it already exceeded on main.

## Verified
- Backend: `py_compile` + `ruff` clean (`ai.py` better than main; `capture_email.py` unchanged pre-existing noqa notes); `pytest tests/unit/test_tasks_gtd.py` → **115 passed**.
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean; Playwright screenshots at 1920px (full-width two-row header, no overflow) and 390px (clean stacking, no overflow).
- The prompt changes need a live LLM backend to observe end-to-end — worth a spot-check in production (clarify a capture mentioning "by Friday" and a custom context).

title: feat(calendar): AI day-management over chat — planner tools + persisted One Thing
body:
Implements the top recommendations from the AI review (`calendar_ai_review.md` §4.1–4.4) so the chat assistant becomes a real day-manager — plan, reschedule, roll over, and reorganize the day by chat — instead of only moving single blocks. The server does the geometry; the agent proposes then applies on confirmation.

## Backend
- **Persisted day state** — migration `92_gtd_day_state.sql` (`user_id, day, one_thing_id, seed_ids`) + `GET`/`PUT /calendar/day-state`. The ★ One Thing and tomorrow-seeds were localStorage-only; now server-side AI (planner, chat agent, digest) can see them and they sync across devices.
- **One-Thing-aware planner** — `_compute_day_plan` orders the One Thing first, prefers a peak-energy window, and never drops it for capacity; the LLM ranking prompt gets an explicit One-Thing rule. Read from `day_state`.
- **Agent-facing endpoints** — `POST /calendar/{plan,replan,rollover}-today` build the day window from stored settings + timezone (no client geometry), reuse the exact planner cores, and **apply** on `apply=true`. Plus a cheap no-LLM `GET /calendar/day-summary` for the digest.

## Chat tools (`skill-task-gtd`, registered in `agent-task-manager`)
- `gtd_plan_day`, `gtd_replan_day`, `gtd_rollover` — propose → confirm → `apply=true`.
- `gtd_day_digest` (morning "how's my day"), `gtd_estimate_stats`, `gtd_set_one_thing`.
- `gtd_list_schedule` now marks 🔒 fixed / ✓ done blocks.
- `instructions.md` + the chat persona document the propose-before-apply workflow and the never-move-a-🔒-block rule.

## Client
- `apiGetDayState` / `apiSetDayState`; `CalendarView` syncs the One Thing (star toggle + ritual commit) and shutdown seeds to the server and hydrates on open. All best-effort, so demo mode (no gateway) is unaffected.

## Verification
- `py_compile` on all changed Python modules; `tsc` + ESLint clean; `next build` passes.
- Playwright smoke: calendar loads and the One Thing toggles with **zero page errors** while the day-state endpoints are unavailable (best-effort catches confirmed).

## Notes
- `schema.generated.sql` is pg_dump-generated (can't regenerate without a DB here); it already lags `gtd_rollover_log` and refreshes on deploy.
- Still open (future): chat-side undo parity for applied plans, a *scheduled* morning-digest trigger, and dedicated interruption-triage / deadline-risk / NL-timeboxing flows (primitives now exist).

title: GenUI cross-runtime HITL review: watchdog/timeout parity for MAF + Copilot SDK agents
body:
## Summary

Follow-up review of the Generative UI 2.0 implementation (#167) verifying it works end-to-end for **both** runtimes — native Microsoft Agent Framework agents (Tier 1) and GitHub Copilot SDK agents (Tier 1.5).

**Verified working as shipped** (reuses proven machinery):
- Emission: ContextVar queue (native MAF) / `_RUN_QUEUES` registry (Copilot's thread-hopped tools) — both reach the SSE stream.
- Blocking resume: `resolve_user_input`'s `call_soon_threadsafe` handles the Copilot cross-loop case; `wait_user_future` heartbeats the relay on both paths.
- Copilot stall detector suppression engages while a genUI form is parked (shares `_pending_user_input`).

**Three timeout surfaces didn't know about the new blocking mode — fixed:**
1. **Tier-1 idle watchdog**: a `generative_ui` event carrying a `request_id` now selects the 3600s HITL budget instead of the 600s tool-open budget (new `_is_hitl_event` helper at both `_nq` drain sites) — a native-MAF user filling a form for >10 min no longer gets the run killed.
2. **Tier-2 batch shim**: `emit_generative_ui` joins the per-tool-timeout exemption list — a blocking form on the fallback path is no longer cancelled at 300s mid-fill.
3. **Copilot no-text-end**: `emit_generative_ui` joins `HITL_BLOCKING_TOOLS`, so a turn that ends on a rendered card with no closing text is treated as a legitimate ending (the card IS the output), matching `ask_questions`.

Also: `emit_generative_ui` joins the guaranteed tool floor (`_CORE_STANDARD_TOOL_NAMES`) so no `tool_scope` can strip rich-UI capability from an agent; the scope-aware addendum follows automatically.

## Testing

- 5 new regression tests (blocking-tool predicate, Tier-2 exemption guard, Tier-1 watchdog recognition, floor membership via existing suites, and a functional Copilot stall-suppression-while-parked test).

title: fix(email): collapse Outlook-desktop reply chains (no-marker quote boundaries)
body:
The HTML quote splitter only recognised marker ids/classes (#divRplyFwdMsg,
#appendonsend, .gmail_quote, cite blockquotes). Outlook DESKTOP (the Word
renderer — what most corporate/academic correspondents use) emits none of
those: its reply header is a bare short block "From: ... Sent: ... To: ...
Subject: ...", so RE: RE: chains rendered fully expanded instead of behind
the ... toggle.

Adds the same text heuristic the plain-text splitter already uses as an HTML
boundary detector (header block / "On ... wrote:" / "-- Original Message --"),
with a short-text cap so whole-chain wrapper divs never match, preferring the
bordered wrapper so the divider collapses with the quote. The empty-main guard
still prevents hiding a body that IS just a forward. tsc clean.

title: feat(tasks): minimizable Focus Mode — persistent timer dock across the control plane
body:
## Why

Focus Mode was local state inside CalendarView — leaving the calendar (or the tasks app) unmounted the room entirely and the running timer vanished from sight. Its ✕ also "left the room with the timer silently running", which is the opposite of what a close button should do.

## What

**The session is now store-held** (`taskStore.focusSessionId` + `focusMinimized`) **and mounted once in AppShell**, so it survives navigating anywhere in the control plane. It renders in two shapes:

- **Expanded** — the full-screen room (unchanged internals).
- **Minimized** — a compact dock with the live timer, task title, state line, and pause / expand / close:
  - **Desktop:** a floating animated card bottom-right.
  - **Mobile:** a strip that extends the bottom nav bar upward — flush above Menu/Inbox/Lists/Capture/Assistant.
  - The same component instance stays mounted across the switch, so the pomodoro segment, cycle count, and pause state carry over exactly.

**Controls (both shapes):**
- **Minimize** (also `esc` in the room) keeps the timer running, visibly.
- **✕ ends the session**: stops the remote timer (stamps `actualEnd` — the durable server-side actuals signal that feeds planned-vs-actual and learned estimates) and removes the UI.

**Fix found along the way:** entering the room from the task-detail modal left the modal (z-80) covering the room (z-70) — entering a session now closes the detail modal.

title: fix(email): Uncategorized is a state, not a label — recategorize-or-fix on click
body:
## What

The "Uncategorized" pill is an **indicator** (the absence of any known label), not a category — and clicking it should either fix the email or tell you honestly why it couldn't.

**1. Pill click now branches on the outcome** (`EmailList.tsx`, `emailStore.ts`):
- Rule matched → applied, pill resolves in place (unchanged).
- **No rule matched** (classifier healthy) → the Fix dialog opens automatically — the miss becomes a learned pattern, an exclude, or a new rule.
- **Classifier unavailable / transport error** → error banner saying it's a backend fault; the Fix dialog does NOT open, so a plumbing outage is never misread as "your rules are wrong".

**2. "Uncategorized" is unwritable as a category** everywhere a category can be written:
- `apply_label` (the single writer used by rule LABEL actions and the sweep) refuses it — an AI-resolved `{{...}}` label could produce it.
- The manual label endpoint (`PATCH /messages/{id}`) drops it before the mirror and the provider write.
- Ingest canonicalisation (`persist._canon_categories`) strips it if it ever exists provider-side.
- The restore-provider-labels repair now runs the same canonicalisation — it wrote **raw** provider label sets, which would also have resurrected pre-rename "Reply"/"Actioned" names.

**3. Rename regression fix**: `CONVERSATION_LABELS_LOWER` never learned `"needs reply"` in #168, so mail whose only label was "Needs Reply" counted as *uncategorized* in every facet, filter and Cleaner tab. Legacy names stay in the set until the reconciler has replaced them provider-side.

Searchability is untouched: `is:uncategorized`, the QuickFilters chip, and `/messages?uncategorized=true` all still share `core.UNCATEGORIZED_SQL`.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/test_email_uncategorized_indicator.py`: writer refuses the indicator (provider + mirror both untouched), real labels still write, ingest drops it, and `KNOWN_LABELS_LOWER` contains "needs reply". Email suite: 843 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: feat(email): voice & writing-style profile learned from past mail (mig 94)
body:
## What

AI Settings → **Advanced Settings** gains a **Voice profile** card (Your voice section): the assistant learns a writing-style profile — plus knowledge-base suggestions — from emails the user has **already written**, over a **date range and source folders the user picks**.

Also includes (second commit): **mobile layout fixes** for the email compose/reply UI, whose buttons could hide behind the bottom nav bar — see the last section.

### UX flow

1. **Builder** — choose sources (Sent mail on by default; Drafts opt-in, with a caution that the folder can contain assistant-written drafts), pick a date range (Last 3/6/12 months, All time, or custom from→to dates), and see a **live, debounced count** of how many emails the build would study (capped at the 150 most recent). Optional toggle: also propose knowledge entries.
2. **Building** — the build runs as a background job; the dialog polls live progress (collecting → analyzing batches → synthesizing → knowledge) with a progress bar, and can be closed mid-build.
3. **Overview** — the finished profile: trait chips (tone, formality, typical length, emoji use), greeting/sign-off/recurring-phrase panels, an **editable narrative style guide** (the text the drafter actually follows), an **enable/disable toggle**, **"Try it"** (generate a sample email in the learned voice for preset or custom scenarios), a **suggested-knowledge review list** (approve/dismiss), plus Rebuild and Remove.

The Knowledge base manager also shows **Suggested / Learned** provenance badges with inline approve; suggested entries sort first and never feed drafts until approved.

## How

**DB (`infra/postgres/94_email_voice_profile.sql`, idempotent)**
- `email_voice_profiles` — one row per account: `status` (EMPTY/BUILDING/READY/FAILED), `enabled`, `traits JSONB`, `style_guide`, `sources`, `range_start/end`, `analyzed_count`, `last_error`, `built_at`.
- `email_knowledge` gains `source` ('manual' | 'voice_profile') and `status` ('active' | 'suggested'); existing rows backfill as manual+active.

**Backend (`gateway/routes/email/automation/voice_profile.py`)**
- Build job: fetch messages in range → strip quoted chains (`split_quoted_text`) so only the owner's own prose is studied → per-batch observation extraction on `tier-balanced` → one synthesis call on `tier-powerful` producing whitelisted traits + style guide → knowledge candidates stored as `suggested` (never clobbering existing titles). Progress via the shared `JobTracker`; the profile row's status survives restarts, and a BUILDING row with no live job reads as FAILED instead of stuck.
- Endpoints: `GET/PUT/DELETE /email/voice-profile`, `GET /voice-profile/preview` (per-source counts), `POST /voice-profile/build`, `GET /voice-profile/status`, `POST /voice-profile/sample`, `POST /knowledge/{id}/approve`.
- Prompt contract: `_load_assistant_about` injects `<voice_profile>` between the explicit `<writing_style>` (outranks it) and the auto-derived `<learned_writing_style>`; both drafting system prompts (`_llm_draft_reply`, `_llm_compose_assist`) updated. The KB block now only includes `status='active'` entries. JSONB traits are parsed defensively (asyncpg may return str).
- `voice-profile/sample` added to the Next proxy's `AI_SLOW_POST_PATHS` (120s timeout).

## Mobile fix: compose/reply UI vs bottom nav bar (commit 2)

Reported from phone use: while drafting, sending, and replying, buttons/sections sat behind or past the mobile bottom menu bar. Three layout causes, all fixed:

- **`ComposePanel` had no height cap and no internal scrolling** — on a phone (especially with the keyboard open) the card ran past the screen, taking Discard/Send with it. Now a flex column capped at `calc(100dvh-6.5rem)` with a scrollable middle and pinned header/footer. Verified in a Playwright harness at 390×500 (keyboard-open height): old structure puts Send at y=527 (off-screen), new keeps it at y=412.
- **App shell reserved `pb-14` but the nav also pads itself with the safe-area inset** — on devices with a home indicator the last inset-height of page content (the inline reply composer's Send row) hid behind the bar. New `.pb-nav` utility reserves `calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`.
- **Modals capped at 85/88vh** — mobile `100vh` includes browser chrome, so a "fits in 85vh" card could overrun the visible viewport and clip its action row. The shared automation `Modal`, `TaskCaptureModal` (the commitment popup after sending a reply), `EmailPreviewModal`, and `MessageTimelineModal` now cap against `100dvh`.
- The **undo-send** and captured-to-Tasks toasts are lifted above the bottom bar on mobile so "Undo" is tappable during the send window.

Desktop geometry is unchanged (`sm:` caps preserve the previous values).

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/test_email_voice_profile.py` (13 tests): quote-strip sample prep, observation merge/dedupe, trait whitelisting, `<voice_profile>` block rendering (incl. str-JSONB), stale-BUILDING → FAILED, and `_load_assistant_about` ordering (`<writing_style>` → `<voice_profile>` → `<learned_writing_style>`).
- Updated `test_email_knowledge.py` fakes for the extra profile query.
- Full unit suite: **1620 passed** (the 5 failing integration tests fail on `main` too — they need live Postgres/services). Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean; ESLint clean on all touched files; `next build` passes and the generated CSS was inspected for the new `dvh`/safe-area rules.
