## What

Completes the display unification: the Rules tab now shows **every mechanism that acts on the mailbox**, not just the AI rules.

- **`note_taker_research_2026-07.md`** — evidence base: source-level Meetily deep dive (verdict: inspiration, not donor — desktop-only capture, diarization paywalled in its PRO tier), an 18-project landscape survey (WhisperLiveKit / Vexa / Scriberr ranked as top donors; Screenpipe disqualified — no longer open source; Amurex dormant), mid-2026 open ASR/diarization SOTA with licenses, browser-capture constraints, and a license watch-list.

## What

Two Dashboard v2 items that make the dashboard actionable rather than a summary.

**1. Priority ordering of the needs-reply queue.** The live dashboard now ranks the reply queue by an urgency score — `high importance (+100) + unread (+25) + capped age (≤30)` — instead of pure oldest-first. Click-through analytics.** The "By category" rows and "Noisy senders" rows are now buttons: a category opens the inbox filtered to that label (same path as clicking a label chip); a sender opens the mailbox filtered to that sender, so you can triage/unsubscribe from the actual mail instead of staring at a count.

title: feat(email): draft-from-dashboard — ✍️ a needs-reply row opens the thread with an AI draft

## What

The last high-value Dashboard v2 item: a **✍️ action on each needs-reply row** opens the conversation and kicks off an AI reply draft in one click — so you go from "these need answering" to a drafted reply without hunting for the thread.

Drafts only. Nothing is sent — the AI draft lands in the reply composer exactly as the manual "Draft with AI" button produces it, auto-saved to Drafts like any reply, for you to edit and send.

## How

Reuses the existing viewer-command channel instead of driving the composer across component boundaries (which is why I flagged this as the risky one — this keeps it contained):

- New `"reply-ai"` viewer command. `EmailDetail` handles it by opening the reply composer (`startReply`) and bumping a nonce; a follow-up effect fires the existing `runAiDraft` (`composeAssist`) once the fresh reply state has committed. The two can't chain synchronously — `runAiDraft` reads recipients/mode that `startReply` sets on the next render — so the nonce effect sequences them. Routed through a ref because the effect sits above the component's early return.
- The page handler `await`s `openEmailById(id)` so the message is loaded and its reply handler bound before the command fires (`openEmailById` clears `viewerCommand`, so the command is set *after* the await).

Frontend-only. `tsc --noEmit` clean. `composeAssist` drafts server-side from the message id, so no client body hydration is required first.

## Try it

Dashboard → hover a "Needs your reply" row → ✍️ → the thread opens with a draft composing. (Hard-refresh for the new bundle.)

title: feat(email): per-thread Nudge — one-click AI follow-up draft on waiting-on-them rows
body:
## What

A 🔔 **Nudge** action on each "Waiting on them" dashboard row opens the thread with an AI-drafted follow-up ready to review — so chasing a stalled thread is one click. Drafts only; confirm-before-send is untouched, nothing is sent.

## How

Reuses the draft-from-dashboard machinery — a new `"nudge"` viewer command that opens the composer and auto-runs the AI draft. Two differences from `reply-ai`:

- **Reply-all, not reply.** On an awaiting thread the last message is usually *ours* (we replied, we're waiting), so a plain reply would address us and filter out to nothing. Reply-all keeps the original recipients — the people we're waiting on.
- **Seeds a follow-up instruction** ("write a brief, friendly follow-up… gently nudge for a reply") via a ref the draft consumes once, so a manual AI draft still uses the user's own typed instruction.

Frontend-only. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: feat(agents): coding skill for MAF agents — code_task + run_script with durable script store
body:
## What

Gives every MAF agent the GitHub Copilot SDK as a **capability, not a peer agent** (the framework review's dual-runtime verdict): agents can now write programs when their built-in tools fall short, and reuse those programs forever.

Two tiers, injected into every agent and added to the guaranteed core tool floor:

- **`code_task(task)`** — a one-shot, 600s-bounded Copilot SDK coding session running inside the calling agent's own workspace (`orchestrator/code_session.py`). Follows a manifest-first script contract: read `agent-data/SCRIPTS.md` first, keep reusable scripts under `agent-data/scripts/`, edit existing scripts in place, update the manifest before finishing. Routes BYOK through the gateway `/v1`, so model tiers, the context-window guard, and cost observability all apply.
- **`run_script(path, args?)`** — zero-LLM re-execution of a saved `.py`/`.sh` workspace script. Cheap, fast reuse of capability built in earlier sessions.

## Durability (across operations, restarts, and updates)

- Scripts live under blob-store-backed `agent-data/` (Postgres authoritative, disk is a rehydratable cache; the workspace sits outside the app dir so deploy `git reset --hard` never touches it).
- The Copilot CLI writes with its **native** file tools and scripts write their own outputs — both bypass the `write_artifact` write-through mirror. Both tools therefore finish with an explicit sweep (`_sweep_to_blob_store`) that mirrors changed files under `agent-data/` + `outputs/` into the store. `code_task` sweeps **even when the session fails**, so partial work is never lost. Sweep bounds: 2 MB/file, 200 files/run.

## Harmonisation with agent mutability

The agent's chat workspace **is** its persistent git clone, so the coding skill plugs into the existing self-mutation governance instead of forking it:

- Two script homes with different gates: **workspace scripts** (`agent-data/scripts/`, blob-durable, no approval) vs **repo-baked skills** (`skills/*/scripts/`, `agents.py` — git-tracked source). The coding-session contract teaches both: a broken built-in skill is edited **in place** and committed locally, never pushed — the executor's post-run commit scan registers every local commit as a `pending_commit` inbox row, and the loader's pre-push hook blocks direct pushes (same pipeline as failure-driven mutation and loader skill auto-sync).
- **Fail-safe** (`_commit_repo_changes`): if a session edits tracked source without committing, `code_task` commits the residue itself — the loader's next `_pull_latest` stash-drops/hard-resets uncommitted tracked changes, so an uncommitted skill fix would otherwise be silently destroyed. `git add -A` respects the loader-managed `.gitignore` (`agent-data/`, `inputs/`, `outputs/` never leak into a commit).
- Promotion path: a script proven under `agent-data/scripts/` can graduate into `skills/<skill>/scripts/`, where `loader._sync_new_skills` auto-wraps it as a first-class agent tool (also via inbox approval).

## Execution hygiene (agent-use standards)

- **Workspace jail** — script paths resolve through `resolve_in_workspace`; traversal/absolute escapes fail closed.
- **Secret-scrubbed subprocess env** — allowlist (`PATH HOME LANG LC_ALL TZ TMPDIR PYTHONPATH`) plus a `TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL` deny pattern; gateway tokens, provider keys, and DB URLs never reach script code (proven by a live-subprocess test).
- **Timeouts** — `RUN_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 120s) per script; 600s per coding session. Output middle-truncated at 8k chars.
- Both tools registered **open-world** in `TOOL_ANNOTATIONS` and wrapped by the injected-tool permission gate (B6). Process-level hygiene; the BO-7 container sandbox remains the hardening path for untrusted code.

## Wiring

- `_tool_injection.py`: injected into all agent shapes, added to `_CORE_STANDARD_TOOL_NAMES`, documented in the full + compact system-prompt addendum (`### Coding skill (durable scripts)`).
- Spec: `ai-company-brain/specs/agent_coding_skill.md` (+ AGENTS.md index row), including §7 on the script taxonomy and the three mutation paths converging on `pending_commit → approve → push`.

## Tests

- 29 new unit tests (`tests/unit/test_code_tools.py`): containment, env scrub, timeout, output cap, sweep selectivity (mtime cutoff + size bound), always-sweep-on-failure, fail-safe repo commit against a mini agent-clone fixture (clean tree afterwards, no noise commits, gitignore respected), floor/addendum/annotation wiring.
- Full suite: **1664 passed** unit tests, **118 passed** trajectory evals, CI-blocking ruff selection clean.

title: feat(agents): proactive "render UI by default" directive for MAF + Copilot agents (genUI Phase 2)
body:
## Why

Agents *can* create interactive generative UI, but they weren't *reaching for it* — and one whole agent type couldn't be reached by the guidance at all. This closes both gaps. The review confirmed the emit path and frontend render are fully runtime-agnostic (one shared `queue.put({CUSTOM, generative_ui})` via `resolve_run_queue(session_id)`, rendered on payload alone), so nothing was wrong with UI *creation* — the problem was entirely on the prompting side.

## Two root causes

1. **No answer-time nudge.** The "reach for it eagerly" guidance lived only in the `emit_generative_ui` tool docstring (a weak signal the model consults *after* it decides to look at tools) and, at system-prompt level, buried mid-addendum among ~15 other tools. Nothing prompted the model, at answer time, to convert a data / status / comparison / choice reply into UI.
2. **Native MAF agents saw none of it.** `_build_injected_tools_addendum` (which carries the genUI guidance and `design.md`) is applied **only** on the GitHub-Copilot `_tools` branch of `_inject_agent_tools`. Native MAF agents — e.g. `email-assistant`, which explicitly scopes in `emit_generative_ui` — got the tool + its docstring + at most the delegation registry. The agent type most set up to render UI had the weakest guidance.

## Fix — `_ui_first_directive`

A static, byte-stable (KV-cache safe), tool-gated **"Rich UI by default"** directive delivered to **both** runtimes:

- **Template-first ordering** is the token-thrift + on-brand lever: it names the 11 templates as the cheapest, on-brand-by-construction path (you supply data only), the component tree next, and custom HTML as the costly last resort (with the `--cc-*` CSS-token hook for when it's unavoidable). This directly answers "don't burn tokens on custom generation" and "use the proper design language, fonts, themes, icons."
- **Placement:** leads the Copilot addendum (full + compact) instead of being buried among tool specs.
- **Parity fix:** appended to native-MAF agents' instructions — both the `default_options` and `agent.tools` shapes — marker-guarded for idempotency, with a compact variant for sub-agents. MAF and Copilot agents now get the identical answer-time rule.
- Pick/set flows steered to `formCard` / `optionPicker` + `"hitl":true`.

**Design-language scope note:** the full 16 KB `design.md` is intentionally *not* dumped into every MAF prompt — templates are on-brand without it, and that's the path the directive steers to. Injecting `design.md` for MAF agents that lean on custom-HTML reports is left as an optional follow-up (documented in the spec); the `--cc-*` hook covers the common custom-HTML case.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/test_genui_proactive_directive.py` (7 tests): native-MAF instructions injection for both MAF shapes, idempotency (marker guard), compact-vs-full variant selection, byte-stability, template-first ordering.
- `evals/trajectories/test_tool_addendum_drift_trajectory.py`: new assertions that the directive **leads** both addenda, templates precede the custom-HTML escape hatch, and the directive is gated on the tool being present. Also refreshed the drift set to cover the coding-skill tools (`run_script`/`code_task`/`list_integrations`) that were injected but untracked.
- Full suite green: **1678** unit tests, **120** trajectory evals, CI-blocking lint clean.
- Spec: `ai-company-brain/specs/generative_ui_2.md` §7.

title: feat(calendar): configurable planning philosophy + a humane planner (breaks, lunch, whitespace)
body:
The planner used to fill the whole day wall-to-wall with focus work "as if I am not a human being." Now it plans like a person — and **how** it plans is configurable at two levels: a standing philosophy you set once, and an optional per-run instruction for today.

## Two levels of "how to organize my day"
- **Standing planning philosophy** (Settings → "How should the AI plan your day?"): a free-text instruction the LLM planner obeys on **every** run. Blank falls back to a humane default ("leave breathing room — don't cram every minute; front-load deep work; batch calls; protect time to think").
- **Per-run instruction** (Plan-my-day input, broadened from "How's your energy?"): today's mood/constraints/theme — *"calls only"*, *"deep work"*, *"low energy"*, *"free after 3pm"*, *"commitments at 2pm"*. Flows to the chat planner tools too (`gtd_plan_day(energy_note=…)`).

## A planner that leaves room to be human
- **Breaks** — after `max_focus_run_mins` of continuous focus (default 90), the packer works in a `break_mins` break (default 10). `0` disables it.
- **Protected lunch** — an optional midday window the planner won't book over (off by default; toggle + hours in Settings). Also honored by rollover, replan, and the nightly job.
- **Whitespace** — the philosophy prompt tells the LLM not to fill every minute; combined with breaks/lunch the day breathes. Lunch/break decisions surface in the plan notes.

## Changes
- **Backend:** migration `93_gtd_planning_prefs.sql` (planning_prompt, max_focus_run_mins, break_mins, lunch_start/end_hour on gtd_settings); `settings.py` model/patch/load; `calendar.py` — `DEFAULT_PLANNING_PROMPT`, `_planning_prefs`/`_lunch_interval`, break insertion + lunch protection in `_compute_day_plan` and lunch in the other three planner paths; philosophy fed into the LLM ranking prompt.
- **Frontend:** Calendar-settings popover gains the philosophy textarea + break/lunch controls; `api.ts` + store defaults extended; the Plan-my-day per-run input broadened; chat persona notes the standing philosophy is applied server-side.

title: feat(calendar): recurring windows — block out habits + reserve times for kinds of work
body:
Answers: *"let me block out recurring habits like lunch/rest, and reserve days/hours for specific kinds of work like calls, meetings, or deep work — flexibly, easy to change."*

A single flexible list of **recurring windows** the AI planner reasons over, editable freely in Calendar Settings.

## Two kinds of window
- **Block** = protected time — the planner treats it as busy so **no tasks land there** (lunch, rest, gym, family, workout). Honored by Plan, Rollover, Replan, and the nightly job.
- **Focus** = reserve time for a **kind of work** (deep work, calls, meetings, admin, R&D). These become themed energy-preference windows (deep→high, calls/admin→low, meetings→medium) so matching tasks are drawn in *geometrically*, **and** their labels are handed to the LLM so it batches the right work there.

Both surface in the plan notes ("Protected: Lunch, Gym"; themed windows fed to the ranker). The chat planner benefits automatically (persona updated).

## Flexible by design
Each window has: **days** (a compact S-M-T-W-T-F-S picker; none selected = every day), **hours**, **kind**, **label**, and **theme** (focus only). Add / edit / remove freely — it's one JSONB list (`gtd_settings.day_templates`, migration 94), no schema churn per change.

title: feat(tasks): Deep Work axis — flow-state tasks judged at clarify, protected by the planner
body:
Adds a **work-mode axis** to the task manager, grounded in Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi's flow research: `deep_work` marks tasks that need an unbroken flow state (creative, design, writing, coding/building, architecture, strategy). It is deliberately **not** an `@context` (contexts are single-valued place/tool axes; deep-ness is orthogonal — deep work happens `@computer` or `@home`) and **not** a priority flag (a task can be shallow yet critical).

## Why flow needs first-class support
- Flow takes ~15 minutes to enter and one interruption to lose — deep tasks must get **unbroken** blocks, never be sandwiched between reactive work.
- Flow needs challenge–skill balance at high capacity — deep tasks belong in **peak-energy** windows, early, before the day fragments.
- Shallow/administrative work should be **batched around** the deep blocks, not interleaved.

## Backend
- **Migration 96**: `gtd_items.deep_work boolean not null default false`
- `core.py` / `items.py`: model field + PATCH support (`deep_work`)
- `ai.py` clarify: the LLM now judges `deep_work` (prompt rule + JSON schema + parse; only for actionable items). The eval-locked deterministic `propose()` is untouched.
- `calendar.py` day planner: candidates carry a `DEEP WORK (needs unbroken flow)` tag and the planner prompt enforces placement rules (peak energy, early, protected, shallow batched around).

## Frontend
- Full plumbing: `types.ts` / `api.ts` / `clarify.ts` / `taskStore.ts` (`deepWork` ⇄ `deep_work`)
- **Clarify**: 🌊 Deep work pill in the Priority row, AI-seeded from the proposal, with a sky-toned chip in the "Assistant recommends" block

- **Focus Mode**: deep-work tasks default to the 50/10 timer instead of 25/5 (short pomodoros fragment flow)

title: harden(agents): post-review hardening for the coding skill + genUI wiring
body:
## Why

A comprehensive review of this session's merged work (coding skill, proactive genUI directive, on-demand design system) confirmed the core is sound but surfaced a set of real hardening gaps. This PR closes them, with regression tests for each.

## Hardening

- **Durability sweep — symlink escape (was the most serious):** `rglob` follows symlinked directories on Python < 3.13, so a `code_task` session could have dropped `agent-data/x → /` and mirrored host files (service-account keys, other agents' creds) into the agent's downloadable blob store. Each swept file's **real** path must now resolve inside the workspace. Also moved the tree walk + file reads **off the event loop** so a large sweep can't stall concurrent runs.
- **Commit safety:** `_commit_repo_changes` now explicitly unstages `agent-data/`, `inputs/`, `outputs/` after `git add -A`, so a secret a script wrote under `agent-data/` can never be committed even for an external `workspace_root` repo that lacks the loader's `.gitignore`.
- **Injection idempotency + parity:** the Copilot addendum append is now idempotency-guarded (parity with the MAF path); native MAF agents now also receive the output-discipline block (files → `outputs/`, and the `load_design_system()` pointer) they were missing.
- **Honest docstring:** corrected the `_script_env` concurrency claim to match the executor's documented Tier-0 limit (process-global env; hard multi-tenant isolation is Tier-2 / BO-7).

## Also: unblock CI — migration prefix collisions on main

Two other teams' PRs each landed migrations `93` and `94`, breaking `test_migration_numeric_prefixes_are_unique` for every PR. Renumbered the two **additive** gtd/calendar migrations out of the collisions (`93_gtd_planning_prefs → 97`, `94_gtd_day_templates → 98`) — both are additive `ALTER TABLE gtd_settings`, depend only on migrations 48/77, and no code references migration numbers, so running them later is safe. The email migrations keep their numbers.

## Tests

- Sweep: symlinked-dir escape blocked; in-workspace files still mirrored.
- Commit: runtime dirs excluded even without a `.gitignore`.
- Injection: Copilot addendum idempotent; native-MAF output-discipline parity.

```
93: 93_gtd_planning_prefs.sql   +  93_rename_reply_to_needs_reply.sql (#170)
94: 94_gtd_day_templates.sql    +  94_email_voice_profile.sql (#176)
```

Both clashes came from the calendar work (`80722e1`, `2ec1be5`) picking numbers that #170 and #176 had already merged.

## What

Renumber the **later-merged file in each pair** (the calendar ones) to the next free slots — 95/96 are already taken by note-taker + deep-work:

```
93_gtd_planning_prefs.sql  →  97_gtd_planning_prefs.sql
94_gtd_day_templates.sql   →  98_gtd_day_templates.sql
```

Pure `git mv` + a one-line note in each file's header. No SQL body changes.

## Why this is safe against production

`scripts/apply_migrations.sh` has **no tracking table** — it re-applies every `NN_*.sql` on each deploy, idempotently, in `ls | sort` order. So a migration's number is *only* its relative apply-order, not an identity the DB has recorded; renaming a file cannot make it "re-run" or "double-apply" (it already runs every deploy and no-ops via `IF NOT EXISTS`).

The only real constraint is ordering, and both moved files are safe to move later:
- Each is an additive `ALTER TABLE gtd_settings ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS …`.
- Both depend only on `48_task_manager_gtd.sql` / `77_gtd_calendar_prefs.sql` — far earlier, still ordered before them.

title: Calendar review: fix planner correctness + a chat-tool crash
body:
A full PM + senior-engineer review of the calendar surfaced a handful of verified, low-risk defects. This fixes those; the larger follow-ups (real confirmation gate, injection fencing, settings consolidation, geometry tests) land separately.

## Fixes

- **Planner ignored a stored day-start / capacity of `0`.** `_day_window` used the `x or default` idiom, silently rewriting a midnight day-start back to 07:00 and a zero capacity to 360 on every AI-planning endpoint — which broke the "plan across all 24 hours" case. Now guards on `is not None`, matching the nightly rollover job and `settings._int_or`.
- **Capacity of `0` disabled the cap** instead of enforcing it (`if capacity_mins` treated 0 as "unlimited" and packed the whole day). `0` now means "no focus work today"; the ★ One Thing is still protected.
- **Free time could start in the past.** When `now` sat exactly on a 15-min mark but mid-minute (e.g. `10:00:30`), the next-slot rounding added 0 and booked before `now`. Now ceils to the next mark whenever `now` isn't exactly on one.
- **Chat-tool crash.** `_fmt_plan` was defined twice at module scope; the day-plan version shadowed the project-plan one, so `gtd_plan_project` called it with the wrong arity and raised `TypeError` on every run. Renamed the project renderer to `_fmt_project_plan`.
- **Stale settings label.** The working-hours control still read "Day window" after the single always-24h grid landed. Renamed to "Working hours" with a line clarifying the grid always shows 24h and these hours only shade off-time and seed the planner's default placement.

## Verification

- `python -m py_compile` clean on both Python files; module parses; `_fmt_plan` now has a single definition with all call sites matching arity.
- Dependency-free logic checks confirm the 15-min ceil never books in the past and capacity `0` schedules nothing while the One Thing stays placed.

title: Calendar review follow-ups: confirmation gate, injection fencing, settings IA, geometry tests
body:
The four larger findings from the calendar review (the verified quick bugs shipped separately in #199).

## A — Structural confirmation gate for AI calendar writes
The agent path relied on the model choosing `apply=false` first; `apply=true` then **recomputed** a fresh plan and wrote it — not what the user reviewed. Now:
- *propose* stashes the computed plan on the day-state row (migration `97_gtd_pending_plan.sql`);
- *apply* replays that reviewed plan **verbatim** and clears it;
- an apply with nothing pending **degrades to a propose** (never a blind write), and stale proposals (>30 min) don't auto-apply.

`DayPlan` gains an `applied` flag so the chat renderer reports what actually happened. The browser "Plan my day" panel is untouched — it already proposes, then applies the reviewed blocks client-side.

## B — Fence external content in every chat-tool output
Only `gtd_list` fenced untrusted text before; `gtd_people` emitted résumé/role text **completely unfenced**. Added a `_data()` helper that wraps externally-authored strings (titles, names, résumé lines, plan rationales) in `«guillemets»` — stripping any embedded guillemets so the boundary can't be broken — applied across `_fmt_item`, `gtd_people`, `gtd_list_schedule`, `gtd_day_digest`, and the day-plan renderer. The persona and agent instructions now declare the guillemet convention so the model treats fenced spans as data, never instructions.

## C — Consolidate the calendar settings IA
The popover had grown into a flat wall with two overlapping control pairs. Grouped it into labelled sections (**When you work · Breaks & protected time · Automation · Energy & themed time · Recurring windows**) and added copy that disambiguates the overlaps: lunch is the quick preset for a recurring **Block**; energy windows are *when you're sharp* vs a **Focus** window's *kind of work*. No stored fields changed.

## D — Geometry unit tests + a frontend test runner
The correctness-critical packing/free-slot code had no tests on either end. Added **vitest** (`npm run test`) with tests for `scheduling.ts` (`blocksForDay`, `firstFreeSlot`) and `shared.ts` (`layoutBlocks` overlap lanes), plus Python tests for the planner geometry (`_free_intervals` overlap-avoidance + past-start ceil, `_place_one` earliest-fit/buffer/energy-pref/interval-mutation, `_day_window`'s 0-preserving window) — locking in the fixes from #199.

## Verification
- `python -m py_compile` clean on all touched Python (incl. the new test module).
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean, `next build` succeeds, **10/10 vitest tests pass**.
- Dependency-free simulations confirm the apply-gate semantics (writes the reviewed plan, degrades when nothing pending, ignores stale proposals) and the guillemet fence (single unambiguous boundary under an injection attempt).

title: fix(infra): 3-digit-safe migration numbering + fix 97 collision & stale gtd eval (unblocks all PRs)
body:
## Why

`main` is red on **two** independent, recently-merged issues, and because CI tests every PR *merged onto `main`*, this blocks **every open PR** — not just the ones that introduced them.

1. **Migration `97` collision** — `97_gtd_pending_plan.sql` (#201-era) vs `97_gtd_planning_prefs.sql` (from #197). The 2-digit numbering space (`00`–`99`) was already **full**: `main` occupies `95/96/97/97/98`, so there was *no free number left* to resolve the clash with.
2. **Stale eval** — #201 changed `skill_task_gtd` to delimit untrusted data with guillemets `«»` (a good anti-injection convention, `core.py:_untrusted`), but `evals/trajectories/test_gtd_quality_trajectory.py::test_synced_text_is_delimited_as_data` still asserted straight quotes.

## What

**Migration numbering is now length-agnostic (the real fix for the exhaustion):**
- `scripts/apply_migrations.sh` matches 2-**or-more**-digit prefixes and applies in **numeric** order via `sort -V`. This matters: plain lexical `sort` orders `100_` **before** `99_`, which would run a later migration first. Numeric sort keeps `…98, 99, 100, 101`.
- `tests/unit/test_migration_prefixes.py` matches the same set and keys prefixes as **ints**, so a zero-padded `097` and a bare `97` are still flagged as the same number.

**Resolve the `97` collision using the reopened space:**
- `97_gtd_pending_plan.sql` → `100_gtd_pending_plan.sql` (the newer collider moves; #197's `97_gtd_planning_prefs` keeps its number).

**Fix the stale eval:**
- `test_synced_text_is_delimited_as_data` now asserts the `«…»` delimiter.

## Why the renumber is safe against production

`apply_migrations.sh` has **no tracking table** — it re-applies every `NN_*.sql` on each deploy, idempotently, in order. A migration's number is *only* its relative apply-order, not an identity the DB recorded. The moved file is an idempotent `ALTER TABLE gtd_day_state ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pending_plan` that depends only on `92_gtd_day_state.sql` (far earlier) with no downstream dependents, so applying it later is a no-op.

## Verification
- `test_migration_prefixes` passes.
- Runner ordering **simulated**: `[0-9][0-9]*_*.sql | sort -V` on `02/50/98/99/100/101` yields them in that exact order, and `schema.generated.sql` is correctly excluded.
- All **21** tests in `test_gtd_quality_trajectory.py` pass against the guillemet source (verified with the skill's actual code on the path).

## Note for maintainers
This reopens headroom above the exhausted 2-digit space, but it does **not** prevent two concurrent PRs from picking the same next number again — that's a coordination issue inherent to file-numbered migrations. Worth considering a longer-term scheme (timestamp prefixes or a sequence) if the collision rate stays high.

title: feat(notes): diarization hint + re-transcribe + create-flow template picker
body:
Two related note-taker UX improvements that make "who said what" and "the right kind of notes" discoverable and self-service.

## 1. Diarization hint + one-click re-transcribe

**Why** — Only **Deepgram** returns speaker labels; **Whisper** (the default STT) returns none. So a meeting transcribed on a non-Deepgram model silently shows **no speakers**, with no clue why and no way to fix it. This closes that footgun.

**What**
- Backend `POST /notes/meetings/{id}/retranscribe` (`recordings.py`): re-runs the pipeline on the meeting's **existing recording** with the **current** STT model — reusing `run_transcription` (deletes + replaces segments, updates `transcript_source`) and the same `summary_run` / `_spawn_pipeline` path as upload/complete. Picks the best channel (`mixed` > `upload` > `mic` > `system`); `404`s when there's nothing to re-transcribe.
- Frontend: the Transcript tab shows a hint when a transcript **has segments but no speaker labels** and the model isn't `deepgram/*` — pointing to **Settings → Models** plus a **Re-transcribe** button. Path to named speakers: switch the STT tier to Deepgram → Re-transcribe.

## 2. Pick the notes template at record/upload time

**Why** — Templates could only be chosen *after the fact* (re-cutting a summary). Now the meeting can be set up in the right shape from the start.

**What**
- `api.createMeeting(title, platform, templateKey)` — `POST /meetings` already accepted `template_key`; this wires it from the UI.
- The `/notes` header gets a compact template `<select>` (defaults to `standard_meeting`); **Record** and **Upload** both pass the selected key. Optional — falls back to the standard template if the list doesn't load.

## Scope / safety

No schema change (reuses `meeting_recording` / `summary_run` / existing `meeting.template_key`). Additive — already-diarized meetings and existing create flows are unchanged.

## Verification

- `retranscribe` route registered; `49 passed` — notes / stt / live unit tests.
- Blocking ruff clean (`F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006`); frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- The Deepgram diarization output still needs a real key + audio to confirm end-to-end at runtime (documented in the spec); the re-transcription and create paths reuse code already exercised by the upload/complete flow.

title: fix(email): salutations on AI drafts + mobile bottom nav no longer cuts off composer UI
body:
## Summary

Two user-reported email-app fixes:

### 1. AI-drafted emails now always open with a salutation
Drafts sometimes jumped straight into the body with no greeting line ("Dear <name>," / "Hi <name>,"), reading abrupt and informal. The reply drafter's prompt asked for a greeting but nothing enforced it, and two paths (compose assist, notes meeting recap) never asked at all.

- **`_ensure_salutation` backstop** (`drafting.py`): if a draft's first line isn't a greeting (recognised opener word, or a short comma/colon-terminated line so other-language greetings are never doubled), prepend `Dear <first name>,` — honorific-aware (`Dear Dr. Smith,`) — or `Hello,` when no name is known. Applied to every reply draft (`/draft-reply`, compose "Draft with AI", rule REPLY/DRAFT_EMAIL actions, follow-up nudges) and to fresh compose-assist drafts; never when improving the owner's own text, and never to the NO_DRAFT sentinel.
- Compose-assist drafting prompt now demands a greeting line, matching the reply drafter's rule.
- Notes meeting-recap prompt now opens with a "Hi all,"-style greeting.
- Email-assistant agent instructions: every reply opens with a salutation addressing the recipient by name.

### 2. Mobile bottom nav bar no longer covers page content
The fixed bottom nav is `pb-safe` padded, so its real height is its content (~3.5rem) **plus** the device safe-area inset — but the shell only reserved `pb-14` under pages. On iPhones the bottom ~30px of every page hid under the bar (the reply composer's attach / AI files / Pop out / Discard / send row was half cut off).

- New `.pb-nav` utility (`calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`); the mobile shell's `<main>` uses it instead of `pb-14` — fixes the email app and every other page rendered in the shell.
- Pop-out `ComposePanel`: window height capped to the viewport with the fields scrolling inside, so the Send/Discard footer always stays on screen (matches the automation modal's existing pattern).
- Email task-capture + undo-send toasts sit above the nav bar on mobile instead of overlapping it.

## Testing

- New `tests/unit/test_email_salutation.py` (17 cases): backstop behaviour, no-double-greeting (incl. non-English greetings), honorifics, reply/compose integration, NO_DRAFT sentinel untouched.

title: WhatsApp Manager — companion + intelligence layer (groups, nudges, voice, agent, snooze, Pulse)
body:
Builds the "companion + intelligence + management" layer on top of the existing WhatsApp triage/automation core. Six self-contained features, each independently tested. **Zero Zoho/Odoo dependency**, official WhatsApp Cloud API only, carrying the vertical's doctrines throughout (deterministic-first, sentinel-on-failure so the LLM never fabricates, watermarked idempotency, human-in-the-loop for anything outbound).

## Features

- **Group intelligence** — one cached AI summary per group chat (what was discussed, sentiment, whether the founder was addressed, ≤5 points worth their eye). The model's `mentions_you` is OR'd with a deterministic @mention check so a direct address is never missed. Bounded, watermarked schedule/digest trigger — never the hot webhook path.
- **Waiting-on nudges** — the promises others owe the founder become one-tap AI chases. Gentle draft in the thread's language, reviewed and sent through the existing composer (the nudge seam never sends). Surfaced in the digest and the per-chat drawer.
- **Voice-note transcription** — voice notes stop being invisible `[voice]` blobs: transcribed via the platform STT tier, folded into `transcript_text`, and re-run through the *same* deterministic classifiers so a spoken "kal AWB bhej dunga" becomes a real waiting-on commitment. Searchable (FTS already covers transcripts), with a one-tap Transcribe chip.
- **Companion agent** (`apps/agents/agent-whatsapp-assistant`) — a MAF agent giving conversational command of the vertical: brief, triage, search, waiting-on, group summaries, transcription, and reply/nudge drafts. **Drafts only — there is deliberately no send tool**, so a free-form reply stays the founder's own tap and one-to-many goes through the Action Broker. Runs on the BYOK LiteLLM tier.
- **Chat snooze / remind-me** — defer a chat out of the queue until a chosen time; it auto-expires (a pure queue filter, no batch), and a new inbound message wakes it while an outbound reply never does. New "Snoozed" nav stream + a Snooze menu in the composer header.
- **Pulse (analytics)** — the founder-CEO's "am I keeping up?" view: typical reply time (median + p90), who has waited longest, inbound load by intent, busiest chats. Read-only projection at `/whatsapp/insights`.

## Schema

Adds migrations `108_whatsapp_group_summaries.sql` and `109_whatsapp_chat_snooze.sql`. Voice transcription and Pulse need no migration (the media/status columns were pre-provisioned in W0; Pulse is pure projection).

title: feat(notes): free local diarization via sherpa-onnx — 4 GB trial, Deepgram fallback
body:
A **$0, CPU-only, self-hosted** path to named speakers — the "try sherpa, roll back to Deepgram if it doesn't work" experiment. Merging this **provisions + enables it on the VPS** as a flag-gated trial.

## Proven end-to-end before shipping
Tested in a CPU sandbox against the **real** models on a real 4-speaker sample:
- **Peak RSS ~162 MB** (not the ~500 MB I'd feared) → comfortably fits the 4 GB box; **OOM risk is effectively off the table.**
- **~8.6× real-time** (a 1-hour meeting diarizes in ~7 min, batch).
- **Threshold 0.7 recovers the correct speaker count** where 0.5 over-split (6 vs the true 4) — so 0.7 is the default (env-tunable via `SHERPA_DIAR_THRESHOLD`). Uses the **int8** segmentation model for size/speed.

## What it does
- `packages/acb_stt/acb_stt/local_diarization.py`: additive post-process — when `NOTES_LOCAL_DIARIZATION=1`, models present, and the STT result has no speakers (Whisper): decode via ffmpeg → sherpa-onnx (pyannote seg-3.0 int8 + CAM++ embeddings + clustering) → merge each segment onto its max-overlap speaker turn, labelled `S1/S2/…` (same as Deepgram, so the rename UI just works). Heavy work in `asyncio.to_thread`.
- Wired into `run_transcription` (guarded, no-op by default).
- **`deploy.yml` [trial] block** (idempotent): installs the optional extra, downloads the two ONNX models (~6 MB + ~27 MB, URLs verified through the proxy), and upserts the flag + model paths + threshold into `.env`. Gated on `LOCAL_DIAR=1`.

## How to try it (after merge → deploy)
Make sure the STT tier is a **Whisper** model (Deepgram already diarizes, so sherpa is skipped for it), then **record/upload a short clip** or hit **Re-transcribe** on an existing meeting → speakers should appear, free.

## Rollback (your "fall back to Deepgram" plan)
- Flip `LOCAL_DIAR=0` in `deploy.yml` (or `NOTES_LOCAL_DIARIZATION=0` in `.env`) + redeploy, **or** just select a `deepgram/*` STT model.
- Fail-safe throughout: package/models/ffmpeg absent, decode/inference error, OOM → silently returns the speaker-less transcript; never fails a run.

## Verification
- sherpa-onnx installs CPU-only in ~15 MB (no PyTorch/CUDA); module imports without it (`available()` → `False`).
- `deploy.yml` valid YAML; blocking ruff clean; **6 unit tests** (merge + opt-in/fail-safe) + notes/stt suite green.

title: fix(notes): audio playback fails on iOS — forward Range, serve inline
body:
The seek-player showed **"Error"** on iPhone. Root cause: **iOS Safari won't play `<audio>` unless the server honours HTTP Range** — it sends a `Range: bytes=0-1` probe and requires a `206 Partial Content` back. The Next proxy was buffering the whole file and returning a plain `200` with the range headers stripped, so iOS bailed. (The transcript loaded fine because that's JSON, not media.)

**Fix:**
- **Proxy** (`/api/notes/[...path]`): forward the browser's `Range`/`If-Range` upstream, and pass the response **status (206)** + `content-range` / `accept-ranges` / `content-length` / `cache-control` through. Streams `res.body` instead of buffering — lighter and preserves range semantics.
- **Backend** `get_audio`: serve **inline** (drop `filename` → no `Content-Disposition: attachment`) so the browser treats it as playable media. Starlette's `FileResponse` already answers Range with `206`; the proxy now relays it.

**Scope note:** iPhone recordings are mp4/AAC (the recorder picks `audio/mp4` on Safari), so they play once range works. webm/opus files recorded on **desktop Chrome** still won't play on iOS — that's an inherent iOS codec limitation, out of scope here.

Verified: `tsc` + eslint + `next build` clean; backend ruff clean.

title: WhatsApp W15: connect a personal number by QR (whatsmeow bridge)
body:
## What this adds

A second WhatsApp transport so you can link a **personal number by scanning a QR code** (the way WhatsApp Web works) — no Meta developer account, no Business API, no app review. It flows into the **same** normalized store and AI triage brain (Reply Zero, intent, drafting, search, pulse …) as an official Cloud API number. The Cloud API path is untouched; the two live side by side.

Built behind the existing provider abstraction, so the whole vertical is reused unchanged — only a new `provider` value (`whatsmeow`) and a new inbound seam were added.

## How it fits together

```
Your phone ──scan QR──▶ whatsapp_bridge (Go, holds the session)
                              │ normalized JSON        ▲ /send /media
                              ▼                         │
                    gateway POST /whatsapp/bridge/ingest│
                              │                         │
                  persist_sync_result + post-sync hooks │
                              ▼                         │
                    the SAME triage brain a Cloud API number gets
```

The gateway holds **no** WhatsApp session and never talks to WhatsApp; the bridge holds the session and speaks only normalized HTTP to the gateway. They authenticate with a shared secret in both directions.

## Changes

**Gateway seam (W15.1)**
- Migration `112`: `wa_accounts.provider` column (`cloud_api` default | `whatsmeow`) + index. No-op for existing rows; idempotent (verified on pg16).
- `BridgeProvider` registered in the provider factory; `_provider_for_account` honors the `provider` column.
- Routes: `POST /whatsapp/bridge/{connect,ingest,paired}` + `GET /whatsapp/bridge/status`. Inbound runs through the identical `persist_sync_result` + post-sync hooks as the Meta webhook. `parse_bridge_payload` / `bridge_secret_ok` are pure/tested.
- 18 unit tests.

**whatsmeow Go bridge (W15.2, `apps/services/whatsapp_bridge/`)**
- Pairs a personal number by QR, holds the session in sqlite (survives restarts), streams normalized messages to the gateway. HTTP API: `/session`, `/session/{id}`, `/send`, `/media`, `/read`, `/health`, all shared-secret guarded.
- Renders the pairing code to a data-URI PNG. Pure-Go / CGO-free → static binary + distroless Dockerfile. `send_template` intentionally unsupported (personal WhatsApp has no templates/24h window).
- README with architecture, run/Docker steps, and an explicit ToS/ban warning.

**Connect UI (W15.3)**
- `/whatsapp/connect` opens on a transport chooser — **Personal WhatsApp (Fastest)** vs **WhatsApp Business (Cloud API)**. Personal path shows the QR, polls status every 2.5s, refreshes the code, and advances to "connected" when the phone links. Graceful bridge-unreachable state; honest ToS note on-screen. Same entry serves the app and the Integrations page.
- `.env.example`: documents gateway `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_URL` + `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_SECRET`.

## Heads up — Terms of Service

Linking a **personal** number via an unofficial multi-device client is **outside WhatsApp's ToS** and the number can be banned. The gateway/app side is ToS-safe (it only ever receives normalized messages); the risk lives entirely in the external bridge running against your own line, which is why it's an isolated, opt-in service. Use it for a personal line at your own risk — use the Cloud API path for a business number.

- Bridge: `go build` / `go vet` / `gofmt` clean; boot smoke test (health + shared-secret auth 403/200).
- Frontend: `eslint`, `tsc --noEmit`, and `next build` all pass.
- Merged latest `main`; no conflicts.

Cannot be paired in CI (needs a real phone scan) — that path is exercised manually per the README.

title: deploy: run the whatsmeow WhatsApp bridge as a localhost systemd service
body:
## What this does

Wires the personal-number **whatsmeow bridge** (shipped in #221) into the VPS deploy so it actually **runs** in production — the last step to make QR pairing usable. Until now the gateway + UI knew about the bridge, but nothing started the bridge itself.

## Changes

- **`deploy/hostinger/acb-whatsapp-bridge.service`** — a systemd unit for the bridge. Binds **`127.0.0.1:8790` (localhost only — never exposed through Caddy)**; only the co-located gateway talks to it. Reads the shared `/opt/acb/app/.env`, persists its sqlite session store under a `StateDirectory`.
- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** — before the gateway restart (so the gateway picks up the vars on the same deploy):
  - Ensures `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_*` in `.env`, generating a strong `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_SECRET` once (shared by gateway + bridge).
  - When `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_ENABLED=1`: installs a Go ≥1.24 toolchain on demand, builds the CGO-free binary, installs + enables + restarts the unit.
  - **Fail-safe**: a build/toolchain/start hiccup only skips the bridge — it never aborts the whole deploy. Set `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_ENABLED=0` to stop + disable it.
- **`.env.example`** — documents the co-located self-host vars.

## Wiring

```
gateway  ──WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_URL=http://localhost:8790──▶  bridge (127.0.0.1:8790)
bridge   ──WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8080──▶  gateway
                      both authenticated by the shared WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_SECRET
```

The bridge routes on the gateway authenticate by that shared secret (like the public `/whatsapp/webhook`), so the localhost bridge reaches them without the internal Bearer token.

## Safety / ToS

The service sitting idle is harmless (no paired session = no WhatsApp connection). The unofficial-multi-device ToS/ban risk begins only when a number is actually paired via the app's QR flow. It's localhost-only and one env flag away from off.

## Validation
- `deploy.yml` parses as valid YAML; the added shell is `set -e`-safe (systemd calls made non-fatal; build guarded by `if`).
- The exact VPS build command (`CGO_ENABLED=0 GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go build`) produces a static ELF binary locally.

After this deploys: **Integrations → WhatsApp → Connect → Personal WhatsApp → scan the QR** works end to end on the VPS.

body:
A full clean-up pass over the entire WhatsApp vertical (~13k lines: gateway routes, ingestion, frontend, Go bridge), driven by five parallel focused code reviews. No feature changes — dead-code removal, consolidation of duplicated logic, a few real bug fixes, and consistency/practice cleanups. Four commits, each validated independently.

## Bugs fixed
- **Expired 24h window read as open** (`rules.py`): the preview computed `expires.timestamp() > 0`, so any real timestamp — even an elapsed one — showed the window open (wrong `via_template`). Now compares against `now`.
- **Template send on a personal number 500'd** (`send.py`): `BridgeProvider.send_template` raises `NotImplementedError`; it's now caught and returned as a clean `409`.
- **Chat draft bled across chats** (`page.tsx`): `<Conversation>` had no `key`, so switching chats kept the previous composer text/panels. Added `key={chat.id}` + an out-of-order-fetch guard on `openChat`.
- **Settings pages targeted the wrong number**: insights/rules/replies/categories used a bare `accounts[0]` instead of the default account the inbox uses. Added a shared `pickDefaultAccount()`.
- **Categories edit had no rollback**: an optimistic policy change ignored the result; now rolls back and shows an error on failure.
- **Bridge media cross-account collision + session races** (Go): media cache now keyed on `(account_id, media_id)`; `StartSession` does an atomic check-and-insert with cleanup on failure (fixes a client/goroutine leak and a permanent-empty-QR zombie); graceful shutdown closes the whatsmeow container; disconnected/unknown errors return `409/404` not `502`.

## Consolidation (removed real duplication)
- **6 byte-identical ownership guards** → shared `assert_account_owned` / `assert_chat_owned` in `whatsapp/core.py`.
- **webhook.py + bridge.py duplicated the entire persist→hooks flow** → one `fire_post_sync_hooks` runner (which also gives the previously-dead `core._log` a purpose).
- `list_streams`' **5 sequential COUNT queries → 1** conditional-aggregate query; `classify_chats` no longer does a per-chat `SELECT kind` (N+1).

## Dead code removed
`chats._user_account_ids`, `outbound.WA_SEND`, an unused `UUID` import, the never-constructed `WhatsAppChat` dataclass + `MESSAGE_KINDS`/`CHAT_KINDS`, the dead `send_digest` hook field, the dead `updateSavedReply` export, an unused SELECT column, and the Go `DeleteSession`/`AccountForJID` + unpopulated wire fields.

## Practice / consistency
Stale "only cloud_api" docstrings corrected; parser `result.errors` now logged instead of swallowed; `bridge.mark_read` logs like `cloud_api`; `zip(strict=True)`; bounded `rules_preview` limit; scheduler stop() error logged; Go idiom (`strings.Contains`/`TrimPrefix`, drained response bodies, `MaxBytesReader`, LID-safe phone formatting).

## Consciously deferred (noted, not done)
A DB-session context manager across ~15 handlers (the reviews found **no** leaks — every handler closes correctly, so it's churn without a bug to fix), a full shared UI-kit extraction, and unifying the outbound-send write with the inbound persist path (behavioral, out of scope for a cleanup).

title: deploy: recover a dead Caddy and gate success on the public site serving
body:
## Summary

The site is currently fully down (both `commandcenter.fracktal.in` and `api.commandcenter.fracktal.in`) while deploy runs stayed green. Two compounding blind spots in `deploy.yml` caused this:

1. **`systemctl reload caddy || true` swallowed a chronically failing reload** — visible in the logs of the last two deploys (`Job for caddy.service failed.`). The on-disk Caddyfile is broken, so the running Caddy served its stale in-memory config until it next restarted, at which point it could not come back up and every public hostname went dark.
2. **`verify()` gated only on the gateway `/health`**, with a direct-IP fallback that passes even when Caddy — which fronts everything users see — is dead.

## Changes

The remote deploy script now, at the Caddy step:
- prints Caddy's systemd state and last 25 journal lines into the CI log (remote diagnosis)
- validates the live `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`; if invalid, backs it up (timestamped) and reinstalls the repo's known-good `deploy/hostinger/caddy/Caddyfile`
- reloads Caddy if running, restarts it if dead
- fails loudly (`CADDY FAILED TO START` + journal dump) instead of `|| true`

`verify()` now requires the **public workbench URL** to answer 2xx/3xx in addition to gateway health, so a dead proxy can never ship as a green deploy again.

Merging this triggers a deploy that should bring the site back up, and its logs will show exactly why Caddy was failing.

## Testing

- Workflow YAML parses; both embedded bash scripts pass `bash -n` syntax checks

title: fix(chat): inline AG-UI cards erased by lean re-saves; table headers rendered [object Object]
body:
## What was wrong

Two independent bugs, both visible in one screenshot.

**1. Inline generative-UI cards vanished from earlier turns** — and the agent explained it away as *"the chat interface renders inline UI cards per turn, and they don't persist permanently when new messages arrive"*, which is false. Cards are persisted with the message and re-rendered from `message.customEvents`.

Traced on prod (session `708e7144`): `agent_run` and the Redis stream both show `emit_generative_ui` fired, and the gateway logged `chat_fold.persisted … message_id=nvyskjicv tools=2` — yet the row ended up with **0 tool events and 0 custom events**, written by a later, leaner upsert.

Three writers upsert the same `chat_message` row — the Next translator's 3s checkpoints, the run-boundary `chat_fold`, and the browser re-POSTing its whole message list on every change — under blind `= EXCLUDED.*` last-writer-wins. The leanest writer won. Two client paths fed it lean data: the poll merge spread the remote message wholesale (so a poll firing only because server *content* grew also replaced cards the client had already rendered), and the mount-time "is the DB richer?" check ignored custom events entirely.

**2. Table headers rendered as `[object Object]`** — the agent emitted `columns: [{key:"deal",label:"Deal"}, …]` and the renderer did `String(col)` on each.

## Fixes

- `routes/chat.py` — run artifacts are **monotonic**: an empty incoming `tool_events`/`progress_lines`/`custom_events` never erases a stored non-empty one; `reasoning`/`agent_state` COALESCE. `content` stays a plain overwrite (it is genuinely rewritten in place as the answer streams). One choke point for the whole damage class.
- `useAgentChat` — poll merge keeps the richer side per artifact list; custom events count toward "server is richer".
- `AgentChat` — mount-time richness check counts custom events, so a lean local cache can't win and then be saved back.
- `lib/genUiText.ts` — coercion extracted, pure and framework-free; every node type funnels through it, so *nothing* an agent puts in a tree can render as `[object Object]`. Tables accept string or object columns, object rows keyed by column, and derive headers from row keys when columns are missing.
- `write_artifact.py` — table shape spelled out with an example, plus an explicit statement that a card is part of the transcript, so the model stops offering a file as "something more durable".

## Guards

- `tests/unit/test_chat_message_upsert.py` — contract tests on the SQL (run in CI, no DB) fail if any monotonic column reverts to a blind `EXCLUDED` overwrite; a live round-trip replays the exact prod failure and skips where no Postgres is reachable.
- `src/lib/genUiText.test.ts` — 14 tests covering the shipped case and the shapes around it.
- **`pr-check` gains a frontend job** (`npm ci` + `tsc --noEmit` + `vitest`). The workbench had no CI at all — type errors only surfaced when the VPS rebuilt after merge.

## Verification

- Monotonic SQL validated against prod Postgres in a rolled-back transaction: a lean re-save no longer wipes cards, tools, reasoning, or state.
- 29 frontend tests pass (14 new); `tsc` clean; eslint clean on changed files.
- Python: 6 contract tests pass, 2 live tests skip locally; blocking ruff + xenon gates pass.

## Not included

The two damaged prod rows aren't repaired. Turn 4's events are still in Redis so its card can be rebuilt by re-running the fold once this is live; turn 2's stream has been trimmed, so that card is gone for good.

title: feat(whatsapp): backfill recent history on link (whatsmeow HistorySync)
body:
Makes a freshly-paired personal number **import its recent history** instead of starting blank — using the same `events.HistorySync` payload WhatsApp pushes to WhatsApp Desktop when you link it. No Business/Cloud API involved.

## How it works
When a number pairs, WhatsApp sends a history-sync blob to the new device. The bridge now handles that event, normalizes each conversation's messages, and streams them into the **same triage inbox** as live messages.

- **Bridge (Go):** request the larger ~1-year desktop-profile sync on link (`RequireFullSync` + `FullSyncDaysLimit`), gated by `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_FULL_HISTORY` (default `true`) / `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_FULL_HISTORY_DAYS` (365); `false` → default ~3-month window. `history.go` maps each `WebMessageInfo` through the existing `classifyMessage`/media/context path, names DMs + groups from the conversation header, skips status/broadcast/newsletter pseudo-chats, and posts 200-message **backfill** batches. A ~90s debounce fires one reclassify once payloads stop. Media protos are cached so recent media re-downloads (old media 404s gracefully).
- **Gateway:** `/bridge/ingest` honors a `backfill` flag — **persist but skip the post-sync hooks**, so auto-reply rules never fire on months-old messages. New `/bridge/reclassify` runs **only** the chat-status classifier once, so imported chats get their reply state without any automated replies. Re-added the `group_subject` wire field (now populated by history) so group chats are named.

Persist already dedupes on `wa_message_id`, so backfill + live messages never double up.

## Honest limits (documented in the bridge README + .env.example)
- It's **recent history, not a full archive**: ~1 year reliable, ~3 years is the server ceiling, and you only get what your phone still stores.
- **Old media often 404s** (expired from WhatsApp's CDN) — text/metadata lands, the download just fails.
- The bootstrap sync is **one-shot at link time** — can't be re-requested (only unlink + relink).
- On-demand "load older" pagination is a possible follow-up; it's best-effort (needs the phone online, WhatsApp may drop companion-device requests), so it's intentionally not wired in yet.

This is grounded in how mautrix-whatsapp (also whatsmeow-based) and Baileys implement backfill — see the design notes for the specific limits.

## Validation
- Bridge: `go build` / `go vet` / `gofmt` clean (can't be run without a phone scan).
- Gateway: +5 unit tests (backfill skips all hooks; reclassify runs only classify_chats + auth/validation); ruff + xenon + **full unit suite 2015** green.

title: Calendar: Rebuild my day / Fit what's left — reshuffle + evict overflow
body:
Reworks planning for the "my day is already half-planned but things changed" case. The two actions now do genuinely different, clearer jobs — and, importantly, **both reshuffle what's already on the calendar and trim the overflow back to your list** (previously Plan treated existing blocks as immovable walls and only stuffed new tasks into the gaps).

## The model

| | Reshuffle existing (not-done) | Trim overflow → back to list | Add new from list |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **Fit what's left** (`gtd_replan_day`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| **Rebuild my day** (`gtd_plan_day`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Both honour 🔒 fixed meetings, done blocks, lunch, recurring windows, energy windows, capacity, and the protected ★ One Thing (never evicted).

## Backend — unified `_replan_core` (replaces `_compute_day_plan`)
- One query for today's scheduled blocks, partitioned into **movable** (flexible + not-done → reshuffled), **obstacles** (fixed meetings + done → avoided), and the **done-minutes** tally.
- Reshuffles movable blocks into the time **actually left** (from now) — including blocks whose time already slipped past **earlier today**, which get swept forward. Movable blocks keep their length (never padded).
- Whatever no longer fits is **evicted**: its schedule is cleared on apply, so it returns to the unscheduled list (`DayPlan.evicted`, distinct from `unplaced`).
- **Trim target = whichever is tighter: time left, or daily capacity minus what's already done today.**
- `include_new=True` (Rebuild) also fills remaining room from unscheduled Next Actions; `include_new=False` (Fit) adds none.
- `_apply_plan_blocks` now clears evicted blocks as well as placing new ones.

## UX
- Buttons renamed to intent — **Rebuild my day** and **Fit what's left** — everywhere (header, rail, startup ritual, schedule sheet, settings copy).
- The proposal panel now **groups** the plan: *Reshuffled · Added from your list · Back to your list (evicted) · Left for another day*, with a one-line headline (`N moved · N added · N back to list · used/capacity`). Apply commits placed + evicted in one undoable op; a Fit that only evicts is still appliable.
- "Fit what's left" shows whenever there's any movable block today (incl. earlier-today overdue).
- Chat tools + persona docstrings + the chat plan renderer updated (shows moved/evicted).

## Verification
- `py_compile`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean; 15/15 vitest pass.
- A dependency-free simulation of the pack loop proves: reshuffle, eviction-to-list, capacity-minus-done trimming, `include_new` gating, and One-Thing protection. (The grouped panel can't be rendered in demo mode since it has no gateway to produce a plan.)

title: Email: fast, streamed, iterative "Draft with AI"
body:
Manual drafting in the composer was slow, opaque, and one-shot. This makes it fast, legible, and iterative.

## 1 — Why it was slow

The interactive path ran on the account's `draft_model`, which is `tier-powerful` → **`deepseek/deepseek-reasoner`**: a reasoning model, called non-streaming with `max_tokens=3000`. That alone is 20–60s of blank spinner. Around it, the orchestrator stacked avoidable serial hops:

- two Mem0 `remember()` lookups, run one after the other;
- an always-on consult-plan LLM call;
- optionally a full specialist agent run (18s timeout) before drafting even started;
- **`await add_memories_background(...)`** — despite that function's own docstring saying fire-and-forget. Mem0's `add` runs an LLM extraction pass, so the user waited several extra seconds *after* the draft was already written.

**Fixes:** a new per-account **`compose_model`** (migration 113, default `tier-fast`) drives `/compose-assist` and `/draft-reply`; background rule/follow-up drafting keeps `draft_model`, where nobody is waiting. Memory recall and the qualifier now run concurrently, and the Mem0 write is properly fire-and-forget.

## 2 — Consults are necessity-gated

The planner now classifies the email (scheduling / courtesy / newsletter / sales / project / support) and calls a specialist **only when the reply must state facts the thread doesn't contain and that agent's system holds them** — with "when unsure, consult nobody" as the explicit default. Ordinary mail skips the agent hop entirely. Decisions are logged (`email.draft_consult_plan`) so gating can be audited against real traffic.

## 3 — You can see what it's doing

New `POST /email/compose-assist/stream` (SSE) — a thin event wrapper over the **same** `_compose_assist_run` pipeline as the JSON endpoint, never a second drafting path — plus a dedicated Next proxy route, since the generic `/api/email/[...path]` proxy buffers POST bodies.

The composer renders a real activity panel instead of a spinner: ordered steps with live state, the qualifier's verdict, **which specialist was asked and the exact question put to it**, its answer, and the model's reasoning in its own scroll region. It collapses to a one-line summary (`Drafted in 5.4s · asked task manager`) once settled.

Every round is kept as a revision (`Yours`, `v1`, `v2`…) that can be restored non-destructively, with an undo for the previous version. A failed or declined round rolls the body back rather than leaving half-streamed tokens behind.

All three composer surfaces (compose window, inline reply, conversation draft card) share one `useDraftSession` hook, so they behave identically.

title: Calendar: Rebuild my day sweeps in prior-day unfinished tasks
body:
## The gap
Unfinished tasks left on a **previous** day were stranded: they weren't in today's movable set (wrong day) and weren't in the unscheduled list (still scheduled), so **Rebuild my day silently ignored them** unless you rolled over first.

## The fix
**Rebuild my day** (`gtd_plan_day`) now also loads prior-day overdue-incomplete **flexible** tasks and treats them exactly like today's movable blocks:
- re-ranked into the time you actually have left, **or**
- if they no longer fit → **evicted back to your unscheduled list**.

So leftovers are always folded into a fresh plan, and overflow lands on your list **non-destructively** — no silent auto-unschedule of a block you deliberately placed. Fixed meetings are never swept.

**Fit what's left** stays strictly today-only, keeping the two buttons cleanly different. Auto-rollover (on by default) still covers hands-off mornings; this makes the manual path correct regardless of its state.

## Why this over "auto-move overdue → unscheduled"
Silently wiping a scheduled block's time to make it reappear in the list loses intent and fights auto-rollover. Folding leftovers into Rebuild (and only evicting genuine overflow) gives the same "they show up so I can re-plan" outcome without the data loss.

## Changes
- **Backend:** `_OVERDUE_CARRY_WHERE` + carry-forward load in `_replan_core` (Rebuild only); `PlanBlock.carried_over`; a "Carried N forward" plan note; the chat renderer tags carried blocks; `gtd_plan_day` docstring updated.
- **Frontend:** the Rebuild proposal panel shows a distinct **"Carried over from earlier"** group so you *see* leftovers fold in, with the headline counting them; `api.ts` maps `carried_over`.

## Verification
`py_compile`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean; 29/29 vitest pass. A dependency-free simulation confirms: Rebuild's candidate pool includes prior-day overdue (carried) while Fit's does not; carried items evict-if-no-fit back to the list; and the ★ One Thing (even when carried) is protected.

title: Calendar: roll-over returns unfinished tasks to your list (not onto a day)
body:
Per the preferred UX: instead of auto-cramming overdue-incomplete tasks onto today, **roll-over now releases them back to your unscheduled list** so you re-plan them deliberately (drag, or Rebuild my day). Applied everywhere roll-over happens:

- **Nightly auto job** (`_rollover_one_user`): clears the schedule of overdue *flexible* incomplete blocks once per local day (logged as released), instead of packing them onto today.
- **Browser endpoint** `/calendar/rollover`: returns the overdue tasks as `evicted` (no blocks) — the client apply clears their times and they land in the unscheduled rail. Removed the now-dead `_pack_rollover` + `_TODAY_BUSY_WHERE`.

Auto-placing overdue work onto the next day silently re-crams the calendar and takes control away. Returning it to the list keeps you in charge of when things get scheduled — and pairs cleanly with Rebuild (which pulls from the list).

title: App Workshop & Custom Apps — RFC, mockups, Phase 0–3b (build/deploy loop, durability, integrations, testing, sharing, agent tools)
body:
## What this is

The **App Workshop / Custom Apps** feature: team members build small internal web apps by chatting with an LLM builder (live sandboxed preview beside the chat) and publish them inside CommandCenter for the whole team — filling the `/build/apps` "Custom Apps" nav slot that previously 404'd.

## Contents

**Planning (docs/app-workshop/):** full RFC — architecture, `window.cc` capability bridge, data model, security/execution model (client-side sandboxing, dependency isolation, T3 forward path), testing model, 4-phase roadmap, prior-art survey.

**Phase 0 — the loop works:** migration `114_custom_apps.sql`; gateway `routes/apps/` (lifecycle, containment-guarded files, publish/rollback with immutable versions, App Runtime API); `agent-app-builder` + executor `allow_session_workspace` binding; `/build/apps` gallery, Workshop, and run pages with the `window.cc` bridge. **Platform contract (RFC §4.0, binding):** CommandCenter is the app's only backbone, enforced by builder refuse-and-redirect instructions, sandbox physics, a publish-time conformance scan, and runtime scope checks.

**Phase 1 — durability & workshop UX:** migration `115_app_files.sql` mirrors draft workspaces into Postgres with lazy rehydration; git checkpoint on every sync with additive restore; console drawer with "✦ Fix with AI"; "Make live" rollback UI.

**Phase 2a — platform integrations:** migration `116_app_tool_grants.sql`; `cc.tools.call()` — a scope-checked, human-confirmed, fully-audited proxy to platform integrations (ClickUp first), reusing the existing Action Broker end-to-end — the Approvals inbox needed zero UI changes. Windmill-style frozen-param scopes; per-use confirm or remembered grant; org-wide write-scope publishes get an always-on admin-review gate keyed to the scope set. Broker actions namespaced `app._` to avoid colliding with each product surface's own actions.

**Phase 2b — testing & evaluation:** test scenarios (`tests.json`, a workspace file — no new backend route) run against an **ephemeral, in-memory `cc` store**, never the real backend — a test run never creates a real ClickUp task, spends real AI budget, or touches real app data, which is what makes it safe to auto-run after every builder turn. A hidden offscreen iframe + small in-frame `click`/`type`/`select` helpers (zero new capability — the app already owns its own DOM) drive real interaction, so a scenario catches UI-wiring bugs, not just backend logic. Scenarios are authored conversationally by the builder (mirroring the platform's own `evals/` "one golden case per behaviour" convention) and reviewed as a plain-English checklist in a new Workshop Tests tab, with a pass/fail badge near Publish, "✦ Fix with AI" on regression, and a publish-modal status banner.

**Phase 3a — sharing & consent:** `app_grants` CRUD (`GET/POST /{slug}/grants`, `DELETE /{slug}/grants/{subject}`, edit-gated upsert) behind a new "Specific people…" publish-visibility option — an email-chip picker, prefilled from existing grants. A blocking first-open consent interstitial on the run page lists the app's LIVE (published+reviewed) scopes in plain language before the bundle is even fetched; `GET /{slug}` computes `needs_consent` server-side (always false for owners/editors), and `POST /{slug}/consent` re-verifies the client's claimed scope-set hash against the real LIVE version, 409ing `scope_set_changed` on a stale view rather than silently recording consent to outdated scopes.

**Phase 3b — apps as agent tools:** a new manifest `actions` block (`storage.list`/`storage.get`/`storage.set`/`tool.call`, `gateway/routes/apps/actions.py`) is the reverse direction from `cc.tools` — named, typed capabilities that let callers OTHER than the app itself (the REST API, and now platform agents) invoke into an app's data and logic. `readonly` is derived, never manifest-trusted. Granting an app to `agents:*` or `agent:<name>` (the same `app_grants` row Phase 3a introduced) makes its actions callable as ordinary tools on every orchestrator run (`orchestrator/app_tools.py`, dynamically-built per-action tools with a real per-action JSON schema) — routed through `_inject_agent_tools()`'s existing risk-gated pipeline (`_gate_injected_tool` → `permission_policy.decide()`), deliberately **not** the `_load_specialist_agents_as_tools()` whole-agent-as-delegate path, which bypasses that permission gate entirely. Storage actions and readonly reads auto-apply for any caller; a non-readonly `tool.call` auto-applies only for a person who can also edit the app, else always queues for human approval — no bypass for an unattended agent caller.

## Verification

- 2189 backend unit tests pass (267+ new across all phases); frontend changes are `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean throughout.
- Scaffold starter passes its own conformance scan.
- All CI checks green (unit tests, frontend, lint, secret scan, harness/eval suites).

## Deploy notes

- `deploy.yml` applies migrations 114–116 automatically on merge.
- Rebased on top of intervening `main` work (email compose, WhatsApp triage/history, notes mic picker) — the branch's own migrations were renumbered 113–115 → 114–116 to resolve a collision with `113_email_compose_model.sql`, which landed on `main` after this branch was created.
- `infra/postgres/schema.generated.sql` needs regeneration against the live DB (`scripts/dump_schema.sh`) — no reachable Postgres from the dev session.
- First smoke test: create an app, ask the builder for a small tracker, publish org-wide, restore a checkpoint. Then: add a ClickUp scope, approve the confirm toast. Then: ask the builder to "test that X" and watch the scenario run in the new Tests tab. Then: publish as "Specific people…", open as a non-owner and clear the consent interstitial. Then: add an `actions` block, share the app with an agent, and confirm the agent sees `app_<slug>_<action>` as a callable tool.

title: feat(notes): mic picker + live level check, and auto-name speakers from self-intros
body:
Two recording-quality improvements to the AI Note Taker.

## 1. Microphone picker + live level check ("green room")
Fixes the Windows case where recording silently fails because the browser's default mic is the wrong or muted device.

- **Choose your mic** on the ready screen (Google-Meet style device dropdown), with the choice **remembered across sessions** (localStorage).
- A **live input-level meter** confirms the mic is picking up sound *before* you record — a flat bar tells you to switch devices instead of discovering an empty transcript afterward.
- The chosen `deviceId` is threaded through the recorder; if that device is gone at record time (unplugged headset), it **falls back to the system default** rather than failing to start (`OverconstrainedError`/`NotFoundError`).

## 2. Smart speaker naming — auto-detect self-introductions
- New `speaker_id` module runs an LLM pass over the **diarized** transcript and maps each anonymous label (`S1`/`S2`) to the name that speaker states about **themselves** ("Hi, I'm Priya", "Alex here").
- **Precision over recall:** being addressed/mentioned by another speaker never names anyone; unsure → stays anonymous.
- **Non-destructive** merge (never overwrites a name the user set) and **fail-safe** (any error leaves the transcript unchanged, never raises).
- Runs **automatically** after diarization so notes/action owners/follow-up email use real people. Also exposed as an **"Auto-detect names"** button on the meeting detail and a `POST /meetings/{id}/identify-speakers` endpoint for already-transcribed meetings.
- Only engages when the transcript is diarized with ≥2 speakers (a solo recording is correctly skipped).

## Testing
- New unit tests (`test_notes_speaker_id.py`) cover the pure merge/label/sample logic — especially the non-destructive merge that must never clobber a manual name.
- Verified green: production `next build`, `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` (no new errors — only the pre-existing `void refresh()` warning remains), backend `ruff`, and 49 backend unit tests.

## Files
- Backend: `speaker_id.py` (new), `pipeline.py` (wire auto-inference after diarization), `notes/__init__.py` (register route).
- Frontend: `MicPicker.tsx` (new), `recorder.ts` (device enumeration + deviceId + fallback), `recordingStore.ts` + `session/[id]/page.tsx` (thread deviceId + green room), `meeting/[id]/page.tsx` + `api.ts` (auto-detect button + client).

title: App Workshop: live token tracking, response-shape fix, design-system reuse
body:
## What this is

Follow-up to #236 (merged). Three things, in commit order:

1. Wires Custom Apps into the existing live-activity/office observability system instead of building a separate "app usage" view.
2. Fixes a real, pre-existing bug: the App Workshop frontend expected a `{app: ...}`/`{apps: [...]}` response envelope that the gateway's `/apps/*` CRUD endpoints never actually send.
3. Makes Custom Apps reuse CommandCenter's existing design system/block-kit instead of hand-duplicating it.

## 1. Live token-consumption tracking (office view)

Research before writing any code found the app-attribution signal already existed but was split across two disconnected, incomplete paths:
- `publish_app_activity` (`kind="app"`) already carried the real per-app slug identity onto the activity bus, but that `kind` was invisible to both the presence-key gate (hardcoded `kind=="agent"`) and the cost rollup (hardcoded `kind=="model"`) — so it never showed up as "working now" or in per-app cost.
- The automatic `kind="model"` event that DOES carry cost collapses every Custom App into one generic `source="apps"` bucket, because the stack-inference helper (`_infer_app_source`) can only ever resolve the calling Python module's path — every app's AI call runs through the same `gateway.routes.apps.runtime` module regardless of slug.

**Backend:** `acb_common.activity`'s presence gate widened to `kind in ("agent", "app")`; `acb_llm.context.acompletion_with_fallback` gained an optional `source` override; `ai_complete` emits a start/end presence pair around the real provider call and passes `source=f"app:{slug}"` explicitly (no double-counting — the presence event carries no cost); `/observability/roster` surfaces a live app as its own `kind="app"` entry (real name/icon from the `apps` table), visible only while actually consuming tokens.

**Frontend:** `office-topdown.tsx` gained `AppSeat` — a glowing terminal kiosk showing the app's icon, instead of falling into the character-sprite pipeline. `page.tsx`'s Feed tab no longer mislabels app events as an anonymous "Model" call.

## 2. Fix: App Workshop frontend never read the real response shape

Every `gateway/routes/apps/{lifecycle,files,publish}.py` endpoint returns a bare FastAPI `response_model` — a plain array or plain object, no envelope. The `build/apps` frontend across all three pages (gallery, run page, editor — 9 call sites) assumed a `{app: ...}`/`{apps: [...]}`/`{files: [...]}`/`{versions: [...]}` wrapper that was never actually there. Concretely: `list_apps` always rendered an empty gallery, `create_app`'s response never yielded a slug to redirect to (surfacing as "Create failed" even on a genuine 200), and every app-meta refetch (initial load, consent scope-change, rollback, `refreshAppMeta`) silently no-op'd. Fixed all 9 sites; left untouched the sites that were already correct (grants, checkpoints, publish, usage, and `ccBridge.ts`, which read the real shapes already).

## 3. Reuse the platform design system instead of rebuilding it per app

Custom Apps render through `SandboxedHtml.tsx` — the SAME component that backs every CommandCenter report and generative-UI card — so its `buildSrcDoc` already injects the identical `--cc-*` tokens and `.cc-*` block-kit classes (`cc-card`, `cc-btn`, `cc-stats`, `cc-bars`, `cc-donuts`, `cc-table`, `cc-callout`/`cc-note`, `cc-chart`, …) into every app's sandbox, unconditionally, today. Verified this actually applies through the double-nested `<html>` structure (`buildAppSrcDoc` wraps the app's own full document inside `SandboxedHtml`'s outer one) by rendering the real starter template through the real pipeline in a headless browser and reading back computed styles. Neither the starter scaffold (`starter_index_html`) nor the builder's instructions knew this existed — both hand-duplicated a separate copy of the palette from scratch, and the builder had no idea the block-kit classes existed at all (regenerating buttons/cards/stat-tiles from scratch every round). Both now point at `design.md` (via `load_design_system`, already in this agent's `tool_scope`) as the single source of truth, and the builder's instructions map the specific reusable blocks to the data shapes an internal app actually needs.

## Verification

- 2202 backend tests passing (16 new), `ruff` clean.
- `tsc`/`eslint` clean across all frontend changes (identical pre-existing baseline warnings only, nothing new).
- Manually verified: sim-mode office screenshot; `AppSeat` kiosk and the starter template both rendered through their real pipelines in a headless browser with computed-style assertions, not just visual inspection.

## Deploy notes

No schema changes, no new migration. Nothing existing changes behavior except: the two widened `kind` checks in `acb_common.activity`, the `source` override default (falls back to the exact previous stack-inference behavior when omitted), and the 9 frontend response-shape fixes (which fix broken behavior, not change working behavior).
