title: fix(whatsapp): stop a slow call from surfacing as "gateway unreachable"
body:
Fixes the error hit when placing a call from **WhatsApp → Calls** on production.

## The defect

The gateway waited up to **30s** on the bridge, and the workbench proxy (`api/whatsapp/[...path]/route.ts`) aborts at **exactly 30s**. So a slow call tripped the proxy at the same moment the gateway timed out, and the user got the proxy's generic `gateway unreachable` — which names the wrong service and hides the real failure.

## The fix

The timeout budget is now a chain that shortens at every hop, so the innermost failure is always the one reported:

| Hop | Budget |
|---|---|
| workbench proxy → gateway | 30s (unchanged, not ours) |
| gateway → bridge, placing a call | **20s** |
| gateway → bridge, reads and actions | **8s** |
| bridge → WhatsApp, accepting an offer | **12s** |

A bridge that accepts the connection then goes quiet now returns its own **504** naming the service and the command to watch, instead of being indistinguishable from the gateway being down. An offer that times out no longer leaves a live call the caller never learns about. The dialer rewrites the two plumbing errors users actually hit into which service to check.

## Verification

24 call tests (3 new, covering the 504 path and asserting the budget stays under the proxy abort), 3288 Python tests, Go builds/vets/tests clean, `next build` clean.

## Note

This makes the failure *legible*; it may not make the call succeed. If the underlying cause is WhatsApp not acknowledging the call offer, the new error will say so directly — which is the diagnosis we currently can't get.

title: fix(whatsapp): dial from a chat, and normalise typed numbers before dialling
body:
Fixes the "WhatsApp did not accept the call offer in time" error, and adds the debugging needed when a call still fails.

## Root cause

The dialer's own placeholder taught `+91 98765 43210` — **with spaces** — and nothing stripped them. `meowcaller` builds the call offer's JID directly from that string, and a JID containing spaces is one WhatsApp never acknowledges. The offer goes out malformed, no ack ever arrives, and it surfaces as a bare timeout with no error to explain it.

## Fixes

- **Normalise before dialling.** Targets reduce to bare digits, so `+91 98765 43210`, `+91-98765-43210` and `(+91) 98765 43210` all work. Anything already a JID or LID passes through untouched. Sub-7-digit input is rejected up front rather than becoming a silent offer timeout.
- **Call from a chat.** Every chat header now has a **Call** button that hands the dialer that contact's JID instead of a typed number — the parsing that broke this can't happen at all. Group chats dial as group calls. It prefills and does **not** auto-dial; a URL that places a call on navigation is too easy to trip.

## Debugging added

The bridge now logs what was actually dialled next to what was typed, how long the offer took to reach the wire, and every phase transition with elapsed time — where a call stalls is what says which side went quiet:

```
call: placing 1:1 from <acct> to "919876543210" (typed "+91 98765 43210") as <own-jid>
call <id>: offer on the wire in 412ms (peer ...)
call <id>: calling -> ringing (+1.2s)
call <id>: peer accepted (+6.8s)
call <id>: media active (+7.1s) — recording="/.../<id>.wav"
```

Plus `GET /calls/diagnostics` and a **Calling readiness** panel in the UI, reporting whether the session exists, is connected, is logged in, and has the calling stack attached — with a verdict naming the specific missing precondition. It appears on any call failure via a "Check what's wrong" button, so a timeout with nothing to inspect becomes a question with an answer.

title: feat(whatsapp): play back a call's audio, and prove any of it arrived
body:
Follow-up to the first successful connected call, where nothing was audible.

## Why nothing was audible

Two separate gaps, both expected but poorly signposted:

1. **No outbound mic path** — the far end hears silence.
2. **Inbound audio goes to a WAV on the server**, not to your browser — so you hear silence too.

Neither was a failure. But there was no way to tell that apart from a genuinely broken media path, which is the real problem this fixes.

## Changes

**Prove audio arrived.** The sink now counts frames, so every call reports `audio_seconds` — how much peer audio actually landed. A call that ends with zero is logged as a warning naming the condition:

```
call <id>: ended (hangup) after 18.3s with NO audio received —
  signalling connected but no media arrived
```

A connected call that captured nothing is otherwise indistinguishable from one that worked: same phase, same recording path, no error.

**Play it back.** Ended calls with audio get an inline player in **Recent**. Ended calls without one say the recording is empty rather than offering a file that plays silence. Audio resolves through the bridge's own call registry — never a request-supplied path — so it can't be walked into an arbitrary file read.

**A dedicated Next route** (`/api/whatsapp/calls/[callId]/recording`), because the WhatsApp catch-all proxy parses every reply as JSON and would silently turn a WAV into `{}`. A more specific route wins over the catch-all.

**Say it up front.** The page now states calls are listen-only *before* the first call instead of leaving it to be discovered.

## Verification

3293 Python tests (2 new: audio_seconds passthrough, recording ownership), Go builds/vets/tests clean, `tsc` and `next build` clean with the new route registered.

## Still not done

No microphone path — this makes the recording audible *after* the call, it does not make the call two-way.

title: docs(board): WS-9 audited NO-GO — third 🟢 row with no testable acceptance
body:
## Cycle result: NO-GO (no implementation attempted)

`/next-ticket` selected **WS-9 — Memory tiers 3b/3c/4**, narrowed to the §6.7 correction UX, because the board itself calls it *"the highest-leverage UX item in the corpus."* `spec-auditor` returned **NO-GO**.

## Why — and it's the same reason as the last two cycles

`memory_architecture.md` §9 supplies acceptance criteria for **3a′ only** — which is **WS-10's work and already shipped**. **3b, 3c and 4 — the entire scope of WS-9 — have none.** §6.7 is experience prose (*"that's wrong · forget this · always remember this"*) with no endpoint, no data model, no assertion. §6.5 ends on *"there are two honest paths… don't do both"* — an owner decision presented as acceptance. The header still reads `Draft / RFC · 2026-07-26` above a body stamped 2026-08-01 (R4 violation: the doc-truth pass edited the body only).

**This is the third consecutive 🟢 row to fail contract point 3.** WS-6, WS-5, WS-9 — all marked ready, none dispatchable. See "What this says about the board" below.

## What the substrate actually provides (verified, not assumed)

- `MemoryClient` exposes `search` / `add` / `get_all` / `delete` — **no `update`**. The API has **no PUT/PATCH**. `add()` passes no metadata, so rows carry only id, text, `created_at`, and the repurposed `user_id`.
- **§5.5 understates the shipped surface.** `/memory` already does list + debounced semantic search + per-item delete + clear-all. What's actually missing is **edit**, **provenance**, and a **compartment selector** — the page hardcodes one of the **five** scope shapes the gateway authorizes (`<email>` · `prefs:` · `room:` · `agent:` · `org:global`; the spec says three).
- **Provenance and supersession are absent entirely** — no `superseded_by`, no `valid_from`, and `agent_run` has no memory-block column, so §6.6 is wholly unbuilt. Migrations 136–139 shipped blob instance-keying, quarantine, groups and room authorship — **nothing** about vector-tier provenance.

## Two traps worth recording

**The activation trap is inverted from what I expected.** The correction slice is **not** owner-gated: `routes/memory.py` deliberately duplicates the scope constants so authorization still works when Mem0 isn't installed (*"a router that fails open because an optional dependency is missing is not a gate"*), and the gate logic tests green against a fake — 41 passed in 0.58s. **The real hazard:** this box's `.env` already has Mem0 enabled, and **`tests/unit/test_memory_integration.py` hangs** (measured, exit 124 at 100s). Assume `test_memory_e2e.py` does too. Verification must name test files — never `tests/unit/` as a directory.

**D4 would make a correction UX lie.** `orchestrator/agents.py:520-534` builds its memory block from the user scope only — no `agent:`, no `org:global`. So a user could correct an org-scope fact, watch the inspector show it fixed, and get no behaviour change on that path. That gap is **WS-15's** (D4), but it constrains WS-9's first PR: restrict to `<email>`/`prefs:`/`agent:`, or say plainly that `org:global` isn't read everywhere yet. An implementer must not pick silently.

## The slice, once specced (3c-0 — AGENT-SAFE)

`PATCH /memory/{scope}/{memory_id}` reusing `_authorize_scope(write=True)` plus the **404-not-403** membership probe `delete_memory` already does; `MemoryClient.update`; provenance carried in **Mem0's own metadata** (`corrected_by` / `corrected_at` / `supersedes`) so no new table and no schema decision; PATCH in the Next proxy; inline edit + compartment selector on `/memory`. Five acceptance criteria are drafted in the audit, all testable without prod and without flipping anything.

## Changes in this PR

WS-9 row → **🟡 Docs**, carrying the verified substrate, both traps, the D4 constraint, and the slice shape. The row also **loses scope it should never have claimed**: §6.1 instance-keying belongs to WS-14 and the 3a′ remainder to WS-10 — WS-9 was double-counting two other workstreams' work.

## What this says about the board

Three cycles, three NO-GOs, same failure. The 🟢 states came from the 2026-07-31 audit, which asked *"does an owning spec exist?"* — not *"does it satisfy the seven-point contract?"* Those are different questions, and the board is currently answering the first while claiming the second. **Recommendation:** before dispatching further, run one pass that re-bases every 🟢 against contract point 3 alone (*does this row have a testable done-when?*). That is cheap — one grep-and-skim per spec — and it stops each cycle from spending a full audit to rediscover the same thing.

title: fix(whatsapp): unmute the calling library's own media diagnostics
body:
Result of auditing our implementation against `meowcaller`'s source, after calls connect but carry no audible audio.

## What the audit cleared

**Attach order is correct.** `Receive` is attached immediately after `Call()` returns, before the peer answers — the same order the library's own `examples/cli` uses.

**Not subscribing a Player is correct**, and was my leading suspicion until the source ruled it out. From `engine_media.go`:

> Send loop: frame-paced from connect, **NOT gated on the Player**. WhatsApp starts media on relay connection and the relay learns our SSRC from our FIRST RTP — it won't bridge the peer's media until it sees our stream. So we send silence frames until the Player has real audio.

So outbound silence flows without `Subscribe`, and the relay bridge forms. That was worth verifying rather than assuming, since "you must send to receive" would have been a real bug.

## What was actually wrong

We made the library mute. `resolveConfig` defaults to `zerolog.Nop()`, so without `WithLogger` **every media diagnostic is discarded** — including the four lines that diagnose a call you can't hear:

- `first RTP sent to relay, outbound media flowing`
- `relay silent after allocate, no bytes back yet (allocate undelivered or rejected)`
- `first authenticated peer SRTCP received`
- `peer SRTCP failed authentication`

That's why the bridge log has had nothing to say about media. The library's own example passes `WithLogger(*zerolog.Ctx(ctx))`; we passed nothing.

## Change

`WithLogger` wired to stdout (where journalctl captures it), tagged `component=meowcaller` and per-account so one call is greppable out of a busy bridge, with `WHATSAPP_BRIDGE_CALL_LOG_LEVEL` for the full per-packet trace.

## Verification

Go builds, vets and tests clean; `zerolog` promoted to a direct dependency.

## What this does and doesn't do

It does not make audio audible. It makes the reason visible — which, for a connected call with no media, is the necessary next step and currently impossible.

title: feat(whatsapp): two-way call audio — browser microphone and speakers
body:
Makes WhatsApp calls actually conversational. Until now the peer was recorded, heard nothing back, and none of their audio reached your speakers.

## Path

```
mic  ──► AudioWorklet ──► WS ──► gateway ──► bridge ──► Player ──► MLow/SRTP ──► peer
spkr ◄── AudioWorklet ◄── WS ◄── gateway ◄── bridge ◄── callSink ◄── decoded peer frames
```

Wire format is raw **little-endian int16 mono, 16 kHz, one 960-sample (60 ms) frame per binary message** — meowcaller's native framing, so nothing resamples or reframes in the middle. The `AudioContext` is opened at 16 kHz for the same reason: the browser resamples once in native code rather than us doing it in JS, which is where drift and crackle come from.

## Decisions that matter

- **Uplink starves to silence, never EOF.** A `Player` that hits EOF stops, and a stopped Player means permanent silence for the rest of the call — a momentary gap has to stay momentary.
- **Downlink fan-out is non-blocking.** It sits on meowcaller's media path, so a slow socket drops frames rather than stalling the call for every consumer including the recorder.
- **Playback holds a jitter buffer** (~180 ms, re-primes on underrun). Network frames don't arrive on the audio clock; playing them on arrival guarantees constant underruns.
- **Attaching is optional and per-call.** With no browser attached the call still sends silence, which is what holds the relay bridge open. Recording is unaffected either way.
- **Direct to the gateway, not through Next.** App Router can't upgrade a connection, so the browser opens the gateway origin using an absolute URL the server supplies (only it knows the public origin).
- **Short-lived HMAC token, scoped to one call.** A WebSocket can't carry the internal bearer and the workbench cookie is a different origin, so the signature *is* the authentication. Same shape as the notes app's live-STT token.

## Honest limitation

Echo cancellation is best-effort: the browser's AEC references what the browser renders, and this plays through WebAudio rather than a WebRTC peer connection. **Headphones are the reliable fix**, and the UI says so rather than pretending otherwise.

## Verification

3308 Python tests (15 new on the token: round-trip, expiry, wrong secret, payload tampering, malformed input, call scoping, URL derivation), Go builds/vets/tests clean, `tsc` and `next build` clean.

Also fixes four pre-existing tests that assumed every route has `.methods` — this adds the app's first WebSocket route, which has a path but no methods.

## Untested

I can't exercise real audio from here. Frame formats, buffering and teardown are unit-tested and reasoned from the library's own framing constants, but first-call behaviour on real hardware is unproven.

title: fix(tasks): expected_by means an explicit promise — the Waiting-For badge stops going stale
body:
Closes the open item WS-18 recorded when Waiting-For shipped.

## The diagnosis

`gtd_waiting.expected_by` was a **derived copy**. Four insert sites snapshotted a due date into it and nothing ever updated it, so a renegotiated deadline left the Overdue badge judging against a dead date — wrong in both directions.

The recorded options were "add an updater" or "make it editable". Neither is the real fix: **the copy itself was the bug.** It isn't really *the date I asked them for* — nobody was asked, it was inferred — and storing an inference that then rots is the worst of both worlds.

## The semantics

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `NULL` | No explicit promise. The overdue line is the item's own `due_at`, read **live**. Nothing is copied, so nothing can go stale. |
| non-`NULL` | Someone actually promised this date. It stands on its own, deliberately independent of `due_at`. |

This keeps the two-facts distinction `lib/waiting.ts` documents, while making the common case self-correcting — no updater, no trigger, no sync logic to maintain.

## What changed

- **All four insert sites stop writing it** (delegate, clarify-delegate, email capture ×2, ClickUp sync). Each was verified individually: every one was writing *the item's own due date under another name* — the same variable stored to `gtd_items.due_at` in the same transaction. None was a distinct fact. The sync case is the clearest — the provider field **is** the task's due date, and the copy could never follow an upstream reschedule.
- **One writer remains:** `PATCH /tasks/items/{id}` carrying `expected_by` (ISO sets, empty string clears), updating the open `gtd_waiting` row under a re-stated ownership `EXISTS`. This fit the existing item-PATCH seam — same auth, same `_parse_ts` convention, no new endpoint invented.
- **Read-time fallback:** the client judges `expectedBy ?? dueAt`. A new pure `waitingLine()` lets the row say *which* fact it is showing — a bare date previously meant two different things.
- **UI:** `ItemDetail` gains a "Promised by" field in the Waiting-on section, same input+clear pattern as Due. Empty reads `not promised — judged on due <date>`.

## Migration and existing data

**No migration and no backfill.** Rows delegated between the last deploy and this change carry a snapshot `expected_by`; they keep it and stay judged on it, which is exactly what the new rule says a stored value means. Clearing one is a normal edit.

## Verification

```
pytest tests/unit/test_tasks_gtd.py + evals/.../test_gtd_quality_trajectory.py  → 150 passed
npm test                                                                         → 163 passed (22 in waiting.test.ts)
npx tsc --noEmit / eslint src/app/tasks / npm run build                          → clean
```

Tests updated to match the rule: the obsolete pin on the old coalesce default is gone, replaced by one asserting **no insert site derives `expected_by` from a due date**, plus a pin on the new PATCH path. Vitest gains the fallback cases and both directions of explicit-promise-wins. `ai.py` untouched, so the golden eval lock held. Ruff findings under `routes/tasks` are the same pre-existing 43 as on `main` — none on a changed line (I checked the one that could plausibly have moved: `_build_item_update`'s C901 is `17 > 15` on main too).

I ran the gates myself rather than accepting them as reported, and reviewed the new cross-table UPDATE's ownership check directly.

`POST /items/{id}/delegate` and the Delegate dialog still can't capture a promised-by date *at the moment of delegating* — the PATCH covers it in one extra click. title: fix(whatsapp): the call-audio socket never survived its handshake
body:
Recording worked but **Talk** did nothing in either direction. The socket was dying before the handler ran.

## Root cause

The audio WebSocket was mounted on the feature-gated router. `require_feature_router`'s check declares `request: Request`, and **FastAPI only populates that for HTTP routes** — on a WebSocket the dependency is invoked without it:

```
TypeError: require_feature_router.<locals>._check() missing 1 required positional argument: 'request'
```

Raised during the handshake, so there was no handler, no close code the client could interpret, and nothing in the log to suggest audio had even been attempted. Confirmed by reproducing it directly rather than inferring it.

Exempting the path could never have helped: the dependency still has to run in order to read the path and decide.

## Fix

WebSockets now live on their own ungated router (`core.ws_router`), included separately in `main.py`. That's the only correct shape — a gate that requires an HTTP request cannot guard a socket. Anything mounted there must authenticate itself, as this one does with a call-scoped HMAC token.

## Why no test caught it

Every unit test passed throughout, because none of them opened a socket. Three now do:

- a **bad token** must produce a clean `1008` — which only happens if the handler runs at all
- a **missing token** likewise
- a third pins the underlying FastAPI behaviour, so if gated routers ever become websocket-safe the test fails and this workaround can be removed

Plus a guard asserting the audio path is not on the gated router.

## Verification

title: feat(observability): WS-6a + WS-6c — D1's attribution stamp exists as a substrate
body:
**WS-6 — Observability wiring + attribution.** First dispatchable slice, after #319's remediation cleared the docs gate.

## Why only a+c

The re-audit narrowed WS-6a–e down to **a + c**. The substrate is clear; the three consumers are not, and are **HELD**:

- **WS-6b** — its security amendment names *no workable mechanism*. `bind_run_context` has exactly one call site (`executor.py`), contextvars don't cross the HTTP hop into `v1_compat`, and `agent_run` rows are written at the run *boundary*, so a mid-run join finds nothing. The one mechanism the code actually supports at request time is the presence key `cc:activity:live:{run_id}`, which for the orchestrator path carries a **server-established** `user`. §7 must name that (or another) before this dispatches.
- **WS-6e** — has no token source (`build_run_trace_row` is pure over events + folded), so it sequences *after* WS-6b rather than independently.
- **WS-6d** — additionally waits on the retention/PII answer (Q3), which §7 itself calls a schema decision that is expensive to undo.

## What shipped

- **`instance` joins the run context.** Resolved once in `run_agent_stream` via a **second additive bind** after `load_agent` — deliberately *not* by moving the first. The early bind is what correlates a failure *during* the load; moving it trades five fields for one.
- **`_emit_usage` carries the full four-tuple with zero call-site changes.** It arrives by inheritance through `activity._INHERIT`, which already carried four of the five fields — so this **extends** an existing mechanism rather than rebuilding it. No production caller changed.
- **Shared agents produce an absent key, never `''`** — double-guarded and pinned, because `''` and NULL are different values in the table WS-6d will build.
- **`refresh_run_presence()`** patches `cc:activity:live:{run_id}` after the late bind. Without it, the presence key is written from the `start` event — which predates the bind — so `/observability/active` and `/roster` could **never** carry `instance` for **any** run. Chose a presence patch over re-publishing `start`: a snapshot overwrite is invisible and idempotent, a duplicate stream entry is permanent and reads as a second activation.
- **Interim `by_instance` cost dimension** on the Redis rollup, so the substrate answers a per-partition question before WS-6d lands.
- **Drift gate** pinning `set(_INHERIT) == set(_RUN_CONTEXT_KEYS)` — the invariant was prose-only, and the two tuples must extend together or attribution silently half-lands.

**Nothing durable is written.** The stamp reaches logs and the Redis feed only.

## Verification

```
pytest test_observability + test_activity_bus + test_llm_usage_telemetry
       + test_v1_compat_telemetry + test_instance_wiring   → 89 passed (+17 new)
ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006          → All checks passed!
xenon --max-absolute F --max-modules F --max-average B      → exit 0
```

`cost_summary`'s complexity went **down** (22 → 20) while gaining a dimension — the identical `source`/`agent`/`instance` arms collapsed into one branch. I ran the gates myself rather than accepting them as reported.

## Reviewer findings

`ws-verifier` PASSED (re-deriving acceptance for four instancing modes, and probing request-path safety with no run context, no event loop, in a bare thread, and with four malformed responses — no exception, response unmutated). `diff-reviewer` then returned 2×P1 + 2×P2, **no P0**; all four were fixed in one repair round, including the presence-key gap above, which is why that fix is in this PR at all.

**Two asymmetries recorded rather than papered over:**
1. The `phase="start"` event predates the bind. The presence patch fixes the live view; a start↔end join still must not assume both ends carry the field.
2. **A delegated sub-run inherits the *caller's* partition** while its blobs key to `''`. So `instance` is **not** a foreign key onto `agent_blob.instance` — WS-6d is warned explicitly. Fixing it needs `unbind_contextvars` + restore around the sub-run, plus a product call on whether a delegated *shared* agent should be billed to the caller's tenant at all.

## Known coverage gap, disclosed

The single junction line `_bind_run_instance(_agent_instance, run_id)` inside `run_agent_stream` is covered by **no executing test** — `test_run_agent_stream_e2e.py` hangs on this box. Both halves either side of it are tested, and the verifier reproduced the composition independently for personal / team / shared / cron and confirmed by reading that the bind is unconditional, correctly ordered, exception-proof, and ahead of every model call. Stating it rather than letting the green count imply otherwise.

## Deferred

Giving delegated sub-runs their own partition; `run_agent`'s missing run boundary (it resolves an instance but binds no context — a pre-existing gap, and adding one would newly correlate that path's logs); surfacing `by_instance` in the Control Plane cost view; everything in WS-6b/6d/6e and the owner-gated WS-6f–i.

title: docs(WS-4): remediate BO-20 — the event-bus row was dispatching a build that already exists
body:
## WS-4 — Event-bus consumer + durable queue (BO-20)

**Cycle outcome: NO-GO on implementation → doc remediation instead.** No application code. `§BO-20` stays ☐ — nothing is built.

### Why the row was not dispatchable

`spec-auditor` failed §BO-20 on **all seven** points of the `work_plan.md` §1 contract. Point 3 was decisive: **zero acceptance criteria**, not weak ones — absent. This is the **fourth 🟢 row in five** to fail the same way; the 2026-07-31 audit that set those states asked *"does a spec exist?"*, not *"does it satisfy the seven points"*.

### The finding that mattered most

**§BO-20 rested on a claim that is false today.** It said webhooks *"trigger no agent"*. They do:

```
ClickUp → ingestion/event_hooks.emit_event → workflows/triggers.dispatch_event → start_run
```
live since `e20ea830` (Workflows Slice 2), plus a **second** live path at `/agent/webhook/{source}` (`routes/agent.py:3428`, which also calls `dispatch_event`). **An implementer handed this row as written would have built a third, parallel dispatch path for work that already has one.**

What *is* missing is narrower than the row implied: `xreadgroup`/`xgroup`/`xack` appear **nowhere in the repo**, so `ingestion:*` and `ingestion:dlq` are write-only and trimmed unread (`maxlen=10_000, approximate=True`) — no durability, no replay, no retry, no drainable DLQ, no rate limit, no bounded concurrency — and only **1 of 3** receivers emits at all (`gmail/webhook.py:66`, `zoho/webhook.py:59` are TODO stubs).

### What shipped

§BO-20 rewritten (7 lines → ~430) as **BO-20a–f**, each with a testable done-when, a `Verify` command, and an AGENT-SAFE/OWNER-GATE label. Modelled on `observability_e2.md` §7, the previous cycle's remediation.

- **No Verify command requires live Redis or the VPS** — all use the `monkeypatch.setattr(queue, "_client", …)` MagicMock pattern from `tests/unit/test_clickup_ingestor.py`.
- **Constants are prescribed, not left open** (`MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5`, `_backoff = min(2**a, 60.0)`, reclaim `min-idle-time = 60_000`, `INGESTION_RATE_PER_SEC`, `INGESTION_MAX_CONCURRENCY`). Without this, a ticket titled *"retry with backoff"* closed green with `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 1` and `lambda a: 0.0`.
- **BO-9 resolved as not blocking**: its clause concerns the producer's per-call *sync* client; a consumer needs a long-lived *async* one, precedent at `acb_common/activity.py:54-66`.
- **`FOUNDATION_CONTINUATION.md`**: the *"ship `worker.py` **OR** drop the event-bus claim"* fork withdrawn at both sites (`:223`, `:243`) — §BO-20 is the single owner (contract point 6).
- **`work_plan.md`**: WS-4 row 🟢 → **`🟢 BO-20f · 🔴 a–e`**; `INGESTION_CONSUMER` registered in §6; the discharged *"when the board is next updated"* deferrals removed.

### 🔴 OWNER DECISION — §BO-20.0, and it is not the one-liner it looks like

> Answer with one line: **`BO-20 = Option A`** or **`BO-20 = Option B`**

- **Option A — in-process supervised asyncio consumer, gateway lifespan. ✅ RECOMMENDED.** Ships by ordinary merge, no VPS action. `workflows_app.md` §9 **D6** names this the house style *about this very item* (*"…no APScheduler process … **Revisit under BO-20**"*); five such loops are already wired.
- **Option B — separate `python -m ingestion.worker`.** Needs a systemd unit an agent cannot install (the four checked-in units are gateway/workbench/whatsapp-bridge/health-watchdog; `bootstrap.sh` generates a fifth for Docker infra; none is a worker). **And it leaves the dispatch step undefined:** a separate process starts with an empty module-level `event_hooks._SINKS`, so it would `XREADGROUP`, `XACK`, and dispatch to **nothing**. Ingestion doesn't depend on gateway, and importing upward is what `event_hooks.py` exists to prevent.

**Only Option A unblocks BO-20a–e as written.** Answering B buys a design round plus a rewrite of BO-20a, not a dispatch. The doc says so rather than promising a one-line answer it can't honour for both branches.

**BO-20f is dispatchable today** — no consumer, no flag, no owner decision.

### ⚠️ Board correction the reviewer caught (P0)

The row claimed BO-20f is what **WS-11 Slice 4** needs. It is not. `workflows_app.md:217` defines Slice 4 as *"(post-BO-20/BO-7): durable queued runs; sandboxed module execution; MCP exposure; retention policies"* — durable queued runs need the consumer + retry + DLQ, i.e. **BO-20a–e plus BO-7**. Left uncorrected, the owner would read "the thing WS-11 waits on is dispatchable today" and de-prioritise the decision that actually gates it. BO-20f unblocks **multi-channel event triggers only**.

### Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_clickup_ingestor.py -q                    → 10 passed in 0.54s
uv run ruff check --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006 \
  apps/services/ingestion/ingestion .../routes/workflows                → All checks passed!
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006                → All checks passed!
git diff --name-only | grep -v '\.md$'                                  → empty
grep -c "^| WS-4 " ai-company-brain/work_plan.md                        → 1   (6 pipes / 5 cells, matches neighbours)
```
Full `pytest` / bare `tests/unit/` not run — hangs against the live DB on this box.

### Loop findings — four agents, four classes of defect

| Agent | Caught |
|---|---|
| `spec-auditor` | Missing acceptance criteria; the stale "triggers no agent" premise; the process-model fork nobody had decided |
| `ws-implementer` | **`emit_event` swallows every sink exception** (`event_hooks.py:41-49`) — BO-20b's retry/DLQ logic would have been **dead code as specified**; the double-dispatch risk at cutover; a latent packaging defect (gateway `pyproject.toml` omits `ingestion`) |
| `ws-verifier` | **FAIL** — a *false* claim the fix itself introduced ("three loops are stopped on shutdown"; all five are) |
| `diff-reviewer` | **P0** Slice 4 overclaim; Option B's undefined dispatch step; "only apscheduler, never as a process" (false — `ingestion/scheduler.py` is exactly that, checked in and undeployed); the zero-retry-satisfies-the-ticket holes |

Two repair rounds used (the budget). Every agent in the chain had at least one claim corrected by the next one down.

### Known findings carried, not fixed

- **P2** — BO-20a names `acb_common/settings.py` as the flag's home, but sibling flags (`SKILLS_INDEX_ONLY`, `SKILLS_FAIL_CLOSED`) read `os.environ` in their owning module. Placement decided at implementation.
- **Noted, out of scope** — `observability_e2.md:709` carries the identical stale-deferral pattern for WS-6's flags, which are *already* in §6. That's WS-6's row.

### Deferred

BO-20a–f themselves. Dispatchable in sequence once §BO-20.0 is answered — except BO-20f, which is dispatchable now.

title: feat(ingestion): BO-20f — Gmail and Zoho webhooks reach ClickUp parity, and two structlog bugs fall out
body:
## BO-20f — Gmail + Zoho receivers reach ClickUp's enqueue + emit parity

**Stacked on #335** (the §BO-20 doc remediation this builds against). Merge #335 first, or retarget this to `main` with `gh pr edit --base main` **before** merging #335 — merging the base with `--delete-branch` auto-closes this PR.

### The dead switch

`TriggerPanel.tsx:266-268` already offered **`gmail`** and **`zoho`** in the workflow event-trigger source dropdown. Nothing could ever fire them — both receivers verified their credential, wrote an audit row, and returned `{"status":"accepted"}` **without enqueueing or emitting anything**. A user could bind a workflow to a Gmail event and wait forever, with the only signal in Google's delivery dashboard.

Both receivers now do what ClickUp already did: a best-effort `enqueue(...)` to their own stream, plus a `BackgroundTasks`-scheduled `emit_event(...)` — so `event_hooks` → `dispatch_event` → `start_run` reaches them. Warn-and-continue on Redis failure; never 5xx a provider.

### 🐛 Two live production bugs, same root cause

These surfaced from writing the first tests that had ever driven these endpoints through a `TestClient`.

**1. Every authenticated Zoho push has been returning 500.**

```python
_log.info("zoho.webhook", event=event, module=module)   # TypeError, every time
```

structlog's bound logger takes `event` as its **own message parameter**. Verified by extracting the file at `HEAD` and driving it through `TestClient`: `status 500`, and at `LOG_LEVEL=WARNING` too — the filtered no-op method has the same signature, so raising the log level would not have masked it. The raise landed **before** `record()`, so the audit row was never written either. **Every Zoho notification has been silently dropped since the file was written.** Fixed to `zoho_event=`, mirroring `clickup/webhook.py:91`'s existing `clickup_event=`.

**2. Every successfully-normalised ClickUp task has been dead-lettered.**

Same collision in `_normalise_task`, but **inside a `try:` whose `except` calls `enqueue_dlq(...)`**. Observed order, verified end to end: `normalise_tasks` ran → session **committed** → audit row written → `_log.info(..., event=event_type)` raised → caught → `clickup.task.normalise_failed` → **DLQ write**. `audit rows = 1, DLQ writes = 1` for a task that persisted correctly. `clickup.task.normalised` has **never** appeared in the logs.

No test caught it because `test_clickup_ingestor.py` stubs `_normalise_task` wholesale (`:99`, `:121`).

### ⚠️ Scope call I made deliberately

The audited contract **forbade touching `clickup/webhook.py`**. I folded the one-token fix in anyway. The reviewer's argument, which I accept: that fence exists to protect BO-20a's premise that `test_clickup_ingestor.py` stays **exactly 10 passed and unmodified** — it is, byte-identical (`git diff` empty) — and that is a *behavioural* fence, not a file taboo. Shipping a PR whose entire subject is this bug class while knowingly leaving **the last remaining instance in the repo**, twenty-five lines below the line that demonstrates the fix, is the worse outcome. It also gets more expensive later: BO-20c prescribes a drainable DLQ with an admin view, whose first screen would be a queue of false failures with a "retry" button that re-normalises them for nothing.

A **repo-wide AST guard test** now asserts zero `event=` kwargs in logger calls, so instance #3 fails CI instead of dead-lettering in silence. `event=` was probed empirically and is the **only** structlog kwarg that raises — `level=`, `timestamp=`, `logger=`, `msg=`, `exc_info=`, `stack_info=`, `error=`, `source=`, `module=` all pass.

### Hardening from adversarial review — each pinned by a test that fails without it

| Fix | Was |
|---|---|
| `_decode_envelope` honours its own `-> dict` annotation (`# type: ignore` gone) | A push decoding to valid **non-object** JSON (`null`, `"hi"`, `[1,2]`, `3`) → **500**, making Pub/Sub retry a push that can never succeed |
| Zoho coerces its event token to `str` | A dict event silently voided the enqueue (redis `DataError`, swallowed) and logged **`zoho.queue.unavailable`** — blaming Redis for a payload-shape problem — while the workflow run still started |
| `hmac.compare_digest` on **bytes**, both receivers | A non-ASCII token → **500**, not 401 (failed closed, but noisy on a `PUBLIC_ROUTES` endpoint) |
| Emit stays **deferred** | Pinned by direct coroutine call asserting the task is on `BackgroundTasks` and has **not run** at return. An inline `await` would put a DB round-trip + an `INSERT` per matching trigger inside the provider's ack deadline → retries → duplicate runs |
| Undecodable Gmail push acks 200, dispatches nothing | Otherwise a malformed push starts a run whose trigger payload is empty |
| Test fixture snapshots/**restores** `_SINKS` | Teardown cleared it, so a future "webhook → run" test would silently see no sink depending on file order |

### 🔴 OWNER-GATE — the feature is inert until you provision it

The **code-side** switch is closed. In prod, `zoho_webhook_secret` and `gmail_pubsub_token` both default to `""`, so `_verify` fails closed and **every push 401s**. Neither key appears in any env template.

1. Add to `.env.example` and to the VPS env:

   ```
   GMAIL_PUBSUB_TOKEN=        # acb_common/settings.py:106
   ZOHO_WEBHOOK_SECRET=       # acb_common/settings.py:100
   ```

2. Point the Zoho webhook at `/webhooks/zoho?token=…` and the Pub/Sub push subscription at `/webhooks/gmail`.

**`plan-guard` blocked the agent from writing `.env.example`** (WS-2: env files hold live credentials). Correct block — recorded here and in all three docs instead of routed around. The fail-closed-on-unset posture is deliberate and must not be "fixed".

### Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ingestion_receiver_parity.py \
              tests/unit/test_clickup_normalise_dlq.py \
              tests/unit/test_clickup_ingestor.py -q      -> 36 passed in 2.04s   (22 + 4 + 10)
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_clickup_ingestor.py -q      -> 10 passed  (byte-identical to HEAD)
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_workflows_trigger_reliability.py -q -> 23 passed  (fixture blast radius)
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006  -> All checks passed!
frontend: git status --porcelain workbench/               -> empty (untouched)
no xreadgroup / xgroup / xack added to any .py            -> doc prose only
```

Offline throughout: only Redis (`queue._client`), `get_settings`, and `acb_audit.record` are faked — `emit_event` is **never** monkeypatched, so the sink assertions are not vacuous. The `record` stub was necessary, not cosmetic: unlike ClickUp, both these receivers call `record()` on the accepted path, which opens a real `acb_graph` session — a unit test would have reached the **live remote Postgres**.

Each fix's pre-fix red was captured by reverting the hunk in turn.

### Loop record

`spec-auditor` **GO-NARROWED** (BO-20f only; a–e held on §BO-20.0) → `ws-implementer` → `ws-verifier` **PASS**, killing **6 of 7 mutants** it built against the new tests → `diff-reviewer` **no P0**, 2 P1 + 5 P2 → one repair round, all fixed.

The auditor found the `TriggerPanel` dead switch the spec hadn't noticed. The implementer found the Zoho 500. The verifier found the ClickUp DLQ bug. The reviewer found the four hardening gaps — and one of its own P1s was half-wrong (`.env.example` does exist). Every agent corrected the one before it.

### Deferred

- **BO-20a–e** — owner-blocked on §BO-20.0. No `consumer.py`, no lifespan change, no `INGESTION_CONSUMER` flag, no stream-consumer verbs anywhere.
- Zoho still 500s on a non-dict JSON **body** (same class as the Gmail fix; the reviewer scoped its finding to Gmail and the response semantics aren't specced).
- `TriggerPanel.tsx`'s helper text names only ClickUp's `taskUpdated` — a user has no in-UI hint that Gmail's event type is `historyUpdated`. Copy change, frontend deliberately untouched.
- `queue.enqueue` builds an unpooled, unclosed sync `redis.Redis` per call and blocks the loop — BO-20a's.

title: docs(WS-10): remediate the multiplayer specs — and specify the subject: surface that was missing
body:
## WS-10 — Multiplayer Phase 2 + 3b

**Cycle outcome: NO-GO on implementation → doc remediation instead.** Docs only, plus one stale skip-message string. Nothing is built.

### Why the row was not dispatchable

`spec-auditor` failed WS-10 on **five of seven** contract points. It is the **fifth of six 🟢 rows** to fail the same way — those states came from a *"does a spec exist?"* pass, not a *"does it satisfy the seven points?"* one.

### The row was four things, only one of them work

| Item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Steer** | **SHIPPED** (`15c8933f`, ancestor of `main`). Struck from the row title. README's own top blockquote still said it was *"designed here and NOT built"* and that *"the 409 is still the only thing standing between two people and one thread"* — both false, and contradicted by §5.2 of the same file |
| **Floor control** | Owner re-decision. Now in `work_plan.md` §6 **by name**, so an agent refuses it instead of inferring |
| **`prefs`/`user` backfill** | Not a spec item — §8 open question 1, ending *"it should be a deliberate, communicated choice."* The apply half mutates live Mem0 data. Also registered in §6 |
| **`subject:` compartments** | The one real slice. Board ID **WS-10 S1** |

### Why the real slice was still NO-GO — and what this PR does about it

`memory-clearance.md` §7's acceptance for 3a is genuinely good, and is **preserved byte-unchanged** (verified by diff). It failed anyway because **the surface it presumes does not exist and was specced nowhere**: no compartment tables, no `chat_session.subject_ref`, no create or add-member endpoint, and `_authorize_scope` 404s on any unknown shape. An implementer would have invented five endpoints, a permission vocabulary and a group mapping against a spec that could not contradict them.

This writes that surface as **§7.1**: scope-key grammar, endpoints using **permissions that already exist**, the `subject_ref` writer folded into the shipped `PATCH /sessions/{id}/room`, `audience='team'` derived from the shipped `org_group`, and one *testable* consequence for `sensitivity='restricted'`. Every agent-proposed choice is marked `DECISION (agent-proposed, owner may overrule)`, and the product calls I would not make on your behalf are **named rather than answered**.

### 🔒 The finding that justifies the exercise

The first draft told an implementer to compute the clearance cap *"the way `_capability_cap` (`rooms.py:191`) already computes the credential cap"*.

That function **drops `group:` and `org` participants on purpose** — `emails = [m for m in members if "@" in m]`, then `if len(emails) < 2: return {"capped": []}`. Its own comment says why: it is a **display** cap, safe to under-report, because the authority fold expands groups elsewhere. Promoted to an access decision it turns an intersection into a **union**:

> Room bound to `subject:falcon` (`restricted`); participants `[owner@x (a member), group:sales]`. Cap comes back empty → "no non-member participants" → the compartment enters `Clearance.read` → `search()` runs and its facts render into a transcript **all forty `group:sales` members can read**.

Built faithfully, the document would have shipped the disclosure it exists to prevent. And the old done-when said *"a **non-member** participant"* — which any implementer satisfies with two email addresses, so it would have passed while the group case leaked.

§7.1.4 now names the site and the helper, requires participant **expansion before** the intersection, **fails closed** on expansion failure, and forbids reusing `_capability_cap` in one bolded line with the reason. Done-when 4 is five parts asserting the `group:`, `org` and **partial-membership** cases specifically.

### Corrections en route — each re-derived from the tree, not transcribed

- **`mark_active(reset=True)` does not raise `SupersedeRefused`.** The header claimed the transcript-destruction guard sits *"at the destructive site"*. It does not — `mark_active` deletes the stream with **no ownership check**; the guard is in `run_detached`, which is itself a caller, so a future direct caller bypasses it. The doc now states the weaker property honestly and says plainly that **no test in the tree demonstrates the bypass** — the one previously cited passes identically either way, because it never seeds an owner.
- **README §2's anchor table: 7 of 8 anchors wrong**, three resolving to real-but-different code (`run_detached` → `publish_control`). Six more stale anchors repeated elsewhere. Fixed, with the companion doc's *"line numbers move; re-verify at dispatch"* caveat promoted into the header.
- **`memory-clearance.md` §3.5: 5 of 7 stale**, 2 rows already built.
- **The prior-art map contradicted its own PR** — still called steer *"unbuilt"* and QM-2 *"absent"* while README and the board (edited in this same diff) called them built.
- **`acting_identity` has never existed in code.** The board wanted it replaced; migration 138 rejects it in a comment. That prior-art item maps to **WS-2/WS-1**, not here.
- **R2 phase-ID collision** — `subject:` compartments were "3b" in one doc and the 3a remainder in another. Owning spec wins; the other is corrected.

### 🔴 Owner decisions this surfaces

1. **Read §7.1 before WS-10 S1 dispatches.** All three docs now say "AGENT-SAFE **once §7.1 is accepted**" — the unqualified cell would have let an agent build five endpoints, a migration and a live-table column before you saw any of it.
2. **One judgement call left in the slice:** §7.1.4's fix now requires factoring `expand_session_subjects` out of `resolve_session_access` in `acb_auth`. It is not a behaviour change — the extracted helper keeps the shipped fail-open posture — but §7.1.9's own rule is "no behaviour changes to live code in this slice", and an implementer is entitled to ask whether an extraction counts. **One sentence from you settles it.**
3. Registered in §6, not decided here: the **floor-control re-decision** and the **`prefs`/`user` backfill apply**.

### Verification

```
uv run python -m pytest tests/unit/test_memory_compartments.py \
  tests/unit/test_memory_authorization.py tests/unit/test_concurrent_run_guard.py \
  tests/unit/test_steer_routing.py tests/unit/test_supersede_guard.py \
  tests/unit/test_rooms.py -q                              -> 93 passed, 14 skipped in 21.33s
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006   -> All checks passed!
git diff --name-only | grep -v '\.md$'                     -> tests/unit/test_rooms.py (skip string only)
grep -c "^| WS-10 |" ai-company-brain/work_plan.md         -> 1   (6 pipes / 5 cells, matches neighbours)
```

**The 14 skips are all of `test_rooms.py`** — no reachable Postgres with migrations 138+139 on this box. No code changed, so nothing regressed, but do not read the green as covering `gateway/rooms.py`.

Both owning specs now carry a verification block quoting **real** output — including the full `ruff check .` as **`Found 1970 errors`**, the pre-existing non-blocking backlog, rather than the convenient green. The implementer reports it initially wrote "All checks passed!" there and corrected it; that would have been the exact failure this pass exists to remove.

### Loop record

`spec-auditor` **NO-GO** (5 of 7 points) → `ws-implementer` → `ws-verifier` **FAIL** (P0: the `mark_active` claim) → repair → `diff-reviewer` **no P0, 5 P1** (the `_capability_cap` union) → repair. Two repair rounds, the budget.

Each agent corrected the one before it — the auditor's route list was short by one, its `add_memories_background` call site was wrong, the reviewer's P2 anchor pointed at the wrong table and it under-counted the stale repeats by four. Every correction is recorded in the docs rather than in this thread.

### Deferred

title: fix(whatsapp): the Talk button never appeared, so there was nothing to press
body:
Live audio couldn't work because **the control to start it was hidden.**

## Root cause

`Talk` rendered only when the tracked phase read exactly `"active"`. That phase comes from meowcaller's `OnStateChange` — and a call can carry media without ever emitting it. Recording worked the whole time, which *proves* media was flowing while the button stayed invisible.

So the reported symptom — "can't speak, can't hear live, but the recording is fine" — was exactly right, and it was a UI gate, not the audio path.

## Fix

- **Talk is offered for any live call**, except one still ringing inbound. Attaching early is harmless: a call with no browser attached sends silence anyway (that's what holds the relay bridge). Hiding the control is unrecoverable from the UI.
- **Readiness no longer rests on a phase string.** The bridge reports `media_ready` from `OnReady`, and treats any received frame as proof media is up in case that callback never fires — belt and braces, since we've now been bitten once by trusting a single signal.
- **The call card shows state**: `media up` plus the live audio state (`mic + speakers live`, `mic muted`, or `audio failed`). A socket that fails is now visibly different from a socket nobody opened — which is precisely the ambiguity that made this take two rounds to find.

## Verification

Go builds/vets/tests clean, `tsc` and `next build` clean, 326 WhatsApp tests pass.

## Note

This is the second bug in this feature whose signature was "everything looks fine and nothing happens." The first was a WebSocket dying at handshake with no close code; this was a button that never rendered. Both are now surfaced in the UI rather than being silent.

title: feat(whatsapp): engage mic and speakers when placing the call, not after
body:
Audio used to wait for a button press *after* the call connected. That left the caller in silence through the part of a call where feedback matters most — and silence was indistinguishable from the audio being broken, which is exactly the ambiguity that made the last two bugs take three rounds to find.

## Change

- **Mic opens first**, inside the click that places the call. `getUserMedia` needs user activation, and spending that activation on a network round-trip loses it — so `prepare()` (mic + audio graph) and `attach()` (socket) are now separate phases.
- **Local ringback starts immediately** and stops the instant real audio arrives from the far end. Pressing Call is audible straight away.
- **The socket joins as soon as the call has an id**, while it's still ringing — no waiting on a phase transition, which is what previously left the caller with no way in at all.

## Failure modes handled

- **Mic refused** → the call still places; that leg is simply listen-only. Denial doesn't block calling.
- **Call fails to place** → audio tears down, rather than leaving a tone playing into a failure with the microphone still open.
- The button remains for joining a call this page didn't place (e.g. an inbound one you answered), relabelled **Join audio**.

## Note on the ringback

It's generated locally, not WhatsApp's. Whether the far end's real ringback arrives as early media is up to WhatsApp; if it does, it replaces the local tone immediately. The tone exists so "still ringing" and "audio is broken" stop sounding the same.

## Verification

`tsc`, `eslint` and `next build` clean; 326 WhatsApp tests pass.

title: feat(ingestion): BO-20a — the stream consumer, wired but switched off
body:
## BO-20a — the ingestion stream consumer, wired but switched off

**§BO-20.0 answered: Option A** — an in-process supervised asyncio loop started from the gateway lifespan. Option B (a separate `python -m ingestion.worker`) is recorded as **rejected, not deleted**: it needs a systemd unit an agent cannot install, and it would start with an empty module-level `event_hooks._SINKS`, so it would `XREADGROUP`, `XACK`, and dispatch to **nothing**.

The `ingestion:*` streams have been written and trimmed **unread** since they were built — `xreadgroup`, `xgroup` and `xack` appeared **nowhere in the repo**. This adds the reader.

### 🔴 Ships OFF. The flip is yours.

`INGESTION_CONSUMER` defaults **off** and is set **nowhere in the tree** (verified). Nothing in this PR runs until you flip it.

| Flag | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **OFF** (today) | **Dispatch-identical** to before: receivers still emit inline, consumer never starts, **not one Redis verb is issued** |
| **ON** | All three receivers cut over to enqueue-only; the consumer becomes the dispatch path |

The cutover had to be **all three receivers at once**. Gating only ClickUp would have double-dispatched Gmail and Zoho, which gained the same inline emit in BO-20f.

Consumer group `cc-ingest` is created on all three streams at **`$`**, and that is load-bearing: `0` would replay up to **10,000 buffered entries per stream** into real `start_run` calls the moment you flip the flag. A test pins `id="$"` per stream — one that only asserted call count would not close this ticket.

### Two regressions this PR would otherwise have introduced itself

**1. A hung sink would have stalled the entire bus.** On `main`, a hang is confined to one request's `BackgroundTasks` and the other two sources keep flowing. After the cutover a single serial loop drains all three streams, so the same hang stops everything — *silently*, because `emit_event` swallows sink exceptions and it could not even surface as a failed cycle. Now bounded at `_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECS = 30.0`, chosen against what the one registered sink actually costs: `start_run` inserts the run row and `create_task()`s the execution rather than awaiting it, so the timeout **cannot truncate a workflow run**.

**2. "Redis down ⇒ events dropped" was not the only lossy state.** An `XACK` failure mid-batch **strands the entries already returned by that read** — they sit in the PEL, and the loop only ever reads `">"`, so nothing redelivers them in this process. BO-20b's reclaim pass recovers them — **but only until `_MAXLEN = 10_000` trims them out of the stream.** All three states are now written down, and **BO-20b's done-when now requires the reclaim to run at startup**, so a previous process's PEL is drained before the flag can strand more.

Guarding the `XACK` was considered and rejected: swallowing that error would hot-loop against a dead Redis instead of reaching the backoff, and honest-ack semantics are BO-20b's.

### Two tests falsified during review rather than trusted

- **Cancellation.** The test asserted `task.done()` — which a loop that *catches* `CancelledError` and returns also satisfies. Changing it to `task.cancelled()` turned out to be **only half a fix**: it still passed a deliberately swallowing loop, because `stop()` ran before the task had ever been stepped, so asyncio's `_must_cancel` fast path throws in at the coroutine's first instruction, **above the `try`**. The assertion was pinning asyncio, not our code. It now waits for the loop to reach its blocking read first, and was re-verified red against the swallowing loop.
- **Ack ordering.** `sink_calls` and `xack_calls` were independent lists, so an **ack-before-dispatch** implementation passed — exactly the line BO-20b will be editing. Both now append to one shared timeline.

Every new pin was proven red against a deliberately broken source, then reverted.

### Also in this PR

- **Packaging defect fixed:** the gateway declared `email-ingestion` and `whatsapp-ingestion` but **not `ingestion`** — the sink registration resolved only via the root umbrella `pyproject.toml`. Declared, and `uv.lock` regenerated.
- **Six lifespan loops, six unconditional stops** — and the wiring is pinned by a test for the first time. Previously a future edit could have deleted the stop call with all tests still green.
- The stop is a genuine no-op when the flag kept the loop from starting, per the `stop_whatsapp_enrichment` precedent.

### Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ingestion_consumer.py tests/unit/test_clickup_ingestor.py \
  tests/unit/test_ingestion_receiver_parity.py tests/unit/test_clickup_normalise_dlq.py -q
  -> 77 passed in 2.54s   (41 + 10 + 22 + 4)

uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006   -> All checks passed!
uv run python -c "import ingestion.consumer as c; print(c.consumer_status())"
  -> {'running': False, 'enabled': False, 'group': 'cc-ingest', 'streams': [...3...],
      'block_ms': 5000, 'read_count': 8}
```

Offline throughout — Redis is faked at `queue._client` per the `test_clickup_ingestor.py` pattern; `emit_event` is **never** monkeypatched, so the sink assertions are not vacuous. `test_clickup_ingestor.py` (10) and `test_ingestion_receiver_parity.py` (22) are **byte-unmodified** and green. `queue.py`, `routes/agent.py` and `.env.example` are untouched.

The verifier additionally ran `pytest tests/unit/ --collect-only` → **3515 tests collected, zero import errors**, and every lifespan-touching test file → 55 passed.

### Reviewer findings carried, not fixed

- **The pooled `aioredis` client is never closed.** The sharper form is a *stale* client: a second `start` in one process reuses a pool bound to the old event loop. Real only for in-process restarts, which this systemd unit does not do. → BO-20b.
- **RESP2 assumption** at the `_drain_once` unpack — `from_url` defaults `protocol=2`; only a `redis_url` carrying `?protocol=3` breaks it, and nothing sets that. Recorded as a comment, no code change.
- **No liveness signal** — `consumer_status()` has no caller outside tests, house-consistent with `scheduler_status()`. Worth a route in BO-20c.
- **4 × RUF100 unused `noqa`** — the reviewer ruled *not a finding*: `clickup/webhook.py` already carries 8 identical on `main`, and `# noqa: PLC0415` is the house convention.
- `clickup/webhook.py:95` still lacks the `str()` coercion Zoho has. Pre-existing on `main`; `apps/AGENTS.md` now names it as the known exception rather than asserting a rule one receiver breaks.

### Loop record

`spec-auditor` **GO-NARROWED** — and it earned its keep: it found **three ways to close this ticket green without doing the work** (`$` unasserted, ClickUp-only done-whens, flag-ON+Redis-down unspecified) and added acceptance B/E/F to close each. → `ws-implementer` → `ws-verifier` **PASS** (75 tests, lifespan `+23 −0` confirmed by reading, and it falsified the cancellation test) → `diff-reviewer` **APPROVE, no P0/P1**, 4 P2 → one repair round, 77 tests.

Multi-worker safety was checked rather than assumed: `acb-gateway.service` runs a bare `uvicorn` with **no `--workers`**, so one process ⇒ one consumer in the group. The pid-bearing consumer name still matters — BO-20b's reclaim needs it to identify a dead worker.

### Deferred

**BO-20b/c/d/e** — open and now unblocked; dispatch one at a time. No `raise_on_error`, no DLQ write, no retry/backoff, no `XAUTOCLAIM` in this PR. `queue.py`'s per-call sync client stays BO-9's.

title: fix(whatsapp): audio tore itself down moments after every call connected
body:
Proactive audit of the calling path. It found a race that would have broken the auto-engage flow shipped an hour ago, before anyone had a chance to hit it.

## 1. The teardown race — would have broken every call

Audio attaches the instant a call is placed. That's **before the next poll lands**, so the attached call isn't yet in the `calls` list the teardown effect reads. The effect treated "not in the list" as "ended" and closed the socket milliseconds after it opened — every time, on the exact flow meant to make calling seamless.

It now waits until the call has actually been *seen* in a poll before concluding it's gone. A call that vanishes afterwards (reaped, or hung up elsewhere) still tears down correctly.

## 2. Normal hangup reported as an error

Hanging up closes the audio socket by design; surfacing that close as a failure ended every normal call with a red banner. Now only unrequested closes are reported.

## 3. Ringback could ring forever

It only stopped on the first inbound frame, so a call that connected *without* media rang indefinitely — precisely the state we most need to be legible. It now also stops once the call is observably up.

## 4. Shared silence buffer

The uplink handed the encoder the same slice on every starved read. If the library ever mutated a frame in place, that buffer would stay corrupted for the rest of the call. Sixteen small allocations a second is a cheap price for not depending on it.

## Tests

The audio plumbing had **none**. It now has thirteen, chosen for the failure modes that actually bite:

- PCM round-trip and clamping (un-clamped `+2.0` wraps to a loud negative click)
- Starvation returns silence, **never EOF** — EOF stops the Player permanently
- Drop-oldest under pressure, without blocking
- Fan-out that a slow listener cannot stall (it's on meowcaller's media path — one wedged browser must not silence the recording)
- Idempotent detach, and detach racing a closing call
- The socket refusing unknown calls, missing secrets, and ended calls

Race detector clean. 3313 Python tests, `tsc`/`eslint`/`next build` clean.

title: feat(ingestion): BO-20b slice 1 — emit_event can be strict, and the blocker that isn't closed yet
body:
## BO-20b Slice 1 — `emit_event` strict mode, and the blocker that **isn't** closed yet

**Stacked on #340** (BO-20a). Merge #340 first, or retarget with `gh pr edit --base main` **before** merging it — merging the base with `--delete-branch` auto-closes this PR.

### What shipped

Retry and DLQ logic needs to know a sink failed. `emit_event` swallows every sink exception, so today it cannot. This adds a **keyword-only** `raise_on_error: bool = False`:

- **`True`** — the first sink exception propagates; remaining sinks are skipped.
- **`False`** (default) — unchanged, and unchanged **deliberately**. All three webhook receivers schedule `emit_event` through `BackgroundTasks` with three *positional* args, so nothing they do can reach the new parameter, and a webhook must never 5xx because a workflow failed.

### 🔴 The finding three passes missed — and why this PR claims less than it looks like

**Making `emit_event` capable of raising does not make it raise.**

The only sink registered in production is `_wf_dispatch` → `dispatch_event` (`gateway/main.py:1074` — the sole `register_event_sink` call site in the repo). Its **entire body** sits inside `try:` / `except Exception`, with the docstring:

> *"Best-effort and **never raises** — event delivery must not break the webhook receivers that call it."*

Its return value carries no signal either: `started` is `[]` **both** when no workflow matched and when the DB threw.

So Slice 2 would have called `emit_event(..., raise_on_error=True)` against an unreachable Postgres, seen it return cleanly, `XACK`'d, and **dropped the event** — exactly the silent loss BO-20b exists to abolish, reproduced *through* BO-20b, with a full retry/DLQ suite green against a raising **fake** sink that does not exist in production.

The spec said *"blocker — SHIPPED in slice 1; do not rebuild."* It now says **necessary but not sufficient**, and Slice 2 grows to give `dispatch_event` a matching strict path.

### 🔴 Owner decision this creates

Striking that non-goal **grows Slice 2 into the gateway package** (`triggers.py` joins its Files list). Marked `DECISION (agent-proposed, owner may overrule)` in three places, with the rejected alternative stated: *leave `dispatch_event` alone and accept that BO-20b cannot deliver its guarantee.*

The failure boundary is drawn where **nothing has run yet**:

| Propagate | Do not propagate |
|---|---|
| `_get_db()` failure, the trigger `SELECT`, `load_version_serialized` raising, `RunRejected` — no `workflow_runs` row written, no task scheduled, so re-delivery is honest | anything inside `_execute_run` — fire-and-forget after the row is written (`service.py:226`); re-delivering it would start a **second** run on the same payload |

### Also fixed in the spec — all the same class of defect: criteria that pass without the behaviour they name

- **The two prescribed constants contradicted each other.** `_backoff` yields `1,2,4,8,16 s` while `_RECLAIM_MIN_IDLE_MS = 60_000` floors re-delivery at 60 s — so under the section's own PEL-and-reclaim prose, the backoff function was **dead by construction**. Mechanism chosen and recorded: **PEL-and-reclaim**, `_backoff` struck, `_RECLAIM_EVERY_SECS` prescribed instead. The deciding argument is that the attempt counter becomes Redis's own `times_delivered`, which **survives a consumer restart** — an in-process dict resets, so a poison entry would loop forever and never reach the DLQ.
- **Nothing pinned `_backoff`'s call site.** Every criterion asserted its *shape*: define it, assert the algebra, never call it from the loop, all green. The replacement done-when is behavioural through the loop against a faked client.
- **`XAUTOCLAIM … JUSTID` is now forbidden in writing.** It suppresses the counter increment the whole design depends on — `times_delivered` freezes at 1, `MAX_ATTEMPTS` is never reached, no entry ever reaches the DLQ, **every prescribed test passes**. It also returns a bare id list that unpacks *silently* into a three-element destructure, so the trimmed-entry tripwire wouldn't catch it either.
- **The done-whens sourced `times_delivered` from `XAUTOCLAIM`, which doesn't carry it.** Only `XPENDING` does. Read order is now pinned, because before-vs-after the increment is the difference between a threshold of **5 and 6** — and the fake-based test passed either way.
- **"A reclaim can never steal an entry this process is still working on" was true by accident.** It holds because the loop is *serial*, not because `60_000 > 30_000`: entry *k* of a 24-entry batch idles (k−1)×30 s **while still queued in-process**, so the bound breaks the moment BO-20e adds concurrency or a second worker appears. Constraint recorded on BO-20e's ticket.
- **Three accepted costs were unstated:** per-stream **ordering** is given up (a stale payload can start a run after a fresher one); `times_delivered` counts *deliveries* not *failures*, so a crash-loop burns retry budget on a healthy event — and lands it in the DLQ during exactly the incident where you least want silent loss; and the counter does **not** survive a *Redis* restart — the group is re-created at `$`, and there is no `appendonly` anywhere in `infra/`.
- **A `ValueError` in a top-of-iteration reclaim wedges the whole drain loop**, not just the reclaim — the `try` spans both `_ensure_groups` and `_drain_once`, so the bus stops draining entirely at ~1 Hz. The reclaim must be wrapped to degrade to "no reclaim this cycle".

### Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ingestion_consumer.py tests/unit/test_clickup_ingestor.py \
  tests/unit/test_ingestion_receiver_parity.py tests/unit/test_clickup_normalise_dlq.py \
  tests/unit/test_workflows_slice2.py -q                   -> 90 passed in 3.45s
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006   -> All checks passed!
```

The three new tests were verified **non-vacuous by mutation**, twice over — the implementer's two, plus two the verifier added:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| delete `if raise_on_error: raise` | strict test fails — `DID NOT RAISE` |
| flip the default to `True` | default-behaviour and signature tests fail |
| **remove the `*` keyword-only marker** | only the `.kind` assertion catches it — the parity file stays green |
| **strict mode runs all sinks then raises at the end** | `second_calls` compare fails — *"skips the rest"* is genuinely pinned, not implied by the raise |

The verifier hash-restored the working tree after mutating (`sha256` identical before and after).

`consumer.py` has a **0-byte diff**. Fence files `test_clickup_ingestor.py` (10), `test_ingestion_receiver_parity.py` (22), `test_clickup_normalise_dlq.py` (4) are byte-unmodified. No `MAX_ATTEMPTS`, no `XAUTOCLAIM`/`XPENDING`, no DLQ write. `INGESTION_CONSUMER` still ships **OFF** and is set nowhere.

### Loop record

`spec-auditor` **GO-NARROWED** — it caught the constant contradiction and held Slice 2 → `ws-implementer` (chose the mechanism, wrote the remediation) → `ws-verifier` **PASS**, adding two mutants of its own and two doc findings → `diff-reviewer` **P0** — the one nobody else found, because all three earlier passes reviewed `emit_event` against a *hypothetical* raising sink and never traced strict mode to the sink that is actually registered → one repair round.

Corrections found in *both* directions: the reviewer's "the trim hole is silent" was wrong (it's loud but total — a `ValueError` every cycle), and its `two_sinks` and `main.py` try-block line citations were each off by a few lines. Ninth cycle running where each agent corrected the one before it.

### Deferred

- **Slice 2** — the loop change. Dispatchable **once you ratify the `dispatch_event` scope growth**; the doc-side holes it would have fallen into are now closed.
- `clickup/webhook.py:95`'s missing `str()` coercion — pre-existing, documented as "fix in the next PR that touches that receiver".
- A pre-existing `RUF100` at `test_ingestion_consumer.py:669` (BO-20a's), in a file this ticket was forbidden to touch.

title: docs(WS-0): truth pass across six workstreams — the board was describing a codebase from weeks ago
body:
## Truth pass across six workstreams

**Thirteen of thirteen board rows have now failed the seven-point contract**, always on the same point: no testable done-when. The six that had never been audited were audited together — **all six NO-GO**.

The cause turned out not to be missing work. **The specs describe a codebase from weeks ago**, so they ask for things that already exist — and in one case would have caused an implementer to break working code.

### 🔴 The one that would have done damage

`permissions_sandbox_b6.md` asserts, as *"grep-confirmed"*, that the mutation container runs with **zero** `--cap-drop`/`--memory`/`--cpus`/`--pids-limit` flags. **Four of those six have been present since 2026-07-27.** An implementer dispatched on WS-3 would most likely have re-added flags that already exist.

The same spec never recorded that Tier 0 shipped, that a **containerized Copilot CLI runtime shipped and is wired at two call sites** behind a flag that ships `""`, or that `isolation_tier()` has been **computed and thrown away into a log field** since it landed.

### The pattern, row by row

| Row | What the spec asked for vs. what is true |
|---|---|
| **WS-1** | *"Remaining: Zoho handlers"* is **fiction** — the Zoho client is read-only (six `list_*` calls, two GETs), with **no write path anywhere to broker**. Two real flip-blockers surfaced instead, neither previously written down |
| **WS-3** | Above. Plus *"T2 for non-first-party agents"* — **no such field exists anywhere in the code**; it is a heading with no data model |
| **WS-8** | `manifest.py` and `declarative.py` are **built, tested and unwired** — ~60% of Phases A+B is on disk. `manifest.py`'s own docstring said *"nothing here is wired into the run path yet"*: the single sentence most likely to cause a duplicate build |
| **WS-11** | Full-graph copilot authoring **shipped as F14** — the same document said so twice. Parallel fan-out shipped too. The real content is fan-**in** and loops |
| **WS-12** | ~90% delivered elsewhere. A **high-severity risk had retired itself** — `openai` is already on 2.x, so Phase 4 drags one SDK major, not two |
| **WS-21** | Two of four deliverables already shipped, and **two of the three `gtd_time_blocks` acceptance clauses were satisfiable by doing nothing** |

### Two findings that are live defects, not documentation

**WS-1, and both block the `ACTION_BROKER_ENFORCE` flip:**

1. The two **irreversible** ClickUp actions (`delete_task`, `archive_task`) are gated but have **no registered handler** — six action names gated, four handlers. Approving a queued delete hits the no-handler branch and marks the row **`failed`**. The existing test pins the set to a four-element literal and is structurally blind to it.
2. A broker-queued push is written as **`sync_state='synced'` with an empty `provider_task_id`** — items marked synced to nothing.

The kill-switch's own docstring now says not to flip it until both land.

### Corrections that change sequencing

- **"Phase A unblocks D3" is false in the direction that matters.** `config.json`-based instancing already ships via `AgentManifest.instance_key()`, so **Centers C was never waiting on WS-8 Phase A** — the board has claimed otherwise for weeks.
- **WS-11's two new tickets must each *invert* a currently-pinned test** (`test_fan_in_rejected_v1`, `test_cycle_rejected`). Without that inversion they close green having built nothing — the same failure shape BO-20b was caught on.
- **`calendar_timeboxing.md`'s "non-breaking `TimeBlock[]` swap" claim was false.** The real blast radius is **17 TS files + 3 gateway modules + a skill + an agent**, so `gtd_time_blocks` is 4 PRs, not 1.

### 🔵 Owner decisions recorded as D10

1. **Command Center is an internal Fracktal tool.** WS-3's full run sandboxing (T2) is therefore **parked** under a trusted-colleague threat model — design intact, schedule removed, with an explicit un-parking condition (a second org, or agent authorship from outside Fracktal) rather than carried as debt.
2. **Loops in the workflow engine are approved**, against `workflows_app.md` §11's standing anti-n8n rule — which is clarified to govern the *node catalog*, not the *control-flow vocabulary*, so it can't be mis-cited as a blocker later. The engine-complexity cost is stated honestly.

### What all six specs now have

Each leads with **what is actually built**, carries per-item done-whens a command or an assertion can settle, names verification commands **by file** (never `tests/unit/` as a directory, which hangs against the live DB), and labels every item **AGENT-SAFE** or **OWNER-GATE** — there were **zero** such labels across all six before.

Board-side: four rows added to the single-owner registry, six to the owner-gate registry (including `copilot_sandbox_scope`, which routes real Copilot sessions into containers and was registered nowhere), one wrong gate anchor fixed, two §5 residuals closed and one opened. The **Horizons ownership dispute** between WS-21 and WS-18 is assigned rather than left to be rediscovered.

### Verification

```
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006     -> All checks passed!
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_action_broker.py tests/unit/test_actions_routes.py \
  tests/unit/test_provider_broker_gate.py tests/unit/test_task_broker_handlers.py \
  tests/unit/test_agent_manifest.py tests/unit/test_declarative_builder.py -q
                                                              -> 94 passed in 1.98s
23 WS rows, no duplicates, pipe counts uniform within every table block
```

Per-spec fences measured by their own agents and now recorded in the specs: 32 (broker) · 102 (isolation) · 78 (agent architecture) · 73 green-in-CI (workflows) · 157 (calendar) · 21 + 81 (orchestration).

**Docs plus four docstrings.** Verified docstring-only by AST comparison — worth noting the first *two* attempts at that check reported false positives, because `subprocess.run(text=True)` and `open(encoding="utf-8")` were decoding with different encodings, which made every em-dash compare unequal. The third run, with both sides decoded identically, is the one that holds.

### Corrections the agents made to each other

Every one of the six caught something its own auditor got wrong: three extra stale anchors in WS-3, a fifth permission site in WS-8 that the auditor's replacement list had dropped, six wrong table names in WS-11 rather than four, `_pending_user_input` at `executor.py:339` rather than `:257` (the auditor's line was a *comment* mentioning the name), and — in WS-11 — that the "known Windows-only failure" is **four** tests, not one, three of them golden-eval trajectories. Anyone running that command with the audit's note in hand would have reported three regressions.

The board sweep then corrected two of *those*: `calendar_ai_review.md` is cited by migrations 92/97/**100**, not 98, and `first_party` does appear in six files — all comments, docstrings and a test helper, no field anywhere.

### Deferred

- `ai-company-brain/AGENTS.md`'s spec index has **no calendar row at all** and is missing `agent_architecture.md`; `AGENTS.md:190` and `apps/AGENTS.md:23` still carry the struck *"broker ships with zero handlers"* line. Filed as §5 residual 6.
- Two live docstrings in `calendar.py` cite migrations 93/94 for what shipped as 97/98 — recorded in the spec, not fixed (code change, out of a truth pass).
- `calendar_ai_review.md` and `calendar_ux_review.md` are unregistered sub-docs; `ux_review` is the sole home of the silently-dropped block-reminders deferral.
