title: P0: nobody could connect a mailbox — the OAuth authorize leg was unreachable
body:
## The outage

`GET https://api.commandcenter.fracktal.in/email/oauth/microsoft/authorize?…` → `{"detail":"Authentication required"}`, **for every user, since 2026-07-29**.

Surfaced when a colleague tried to connect his mailbox. It is not about him: the owner's account was connected before that date, which is the only reason six days passed without anyone noticing.

### Why

1. Both **Connect** buttons do `window.location.href = ${gatewayUrl}/email/oauth/${provider}/authorize?…` — a top-level browser navigation **straight at the gateway host**, deliberately skipping the BFF, because the response has to be a 302 onward to Microsoft/Google.
2. That request carries no Bearer and no `X-User-Email`: session cookies live on the workbench origin, not `api.*`, and a browser navigation cannot add headers.
3. `57ec82d9` ("Make authentication default-deny app-wide") attached `require_authenticated` at the app level. The OAuth **callback** legs were exempted; the **authorize** legs were not — `main.py` says they "stay gated".
4. So the route 401s before its handler runs. The handler's own `user_email` query parameter — added precisely so "the workbench can pass the authenticated user's email when the browser navigates directly to the gateway" — has been unreachable the whole time.

`git log -S` confirms the authorize leg was **never** in `PUBLIC_ROUTES`. A route was made default-deny and the one entry point that structurally cannot carry credentials was never re-checked.

### 🔴 Why the obvious fix is worse than the bug

Adding the authorize leg to `PUBLIC_ROUTES` makes the button work. It also hands over accounts: the handler stored `"user_id": user_email or user.email`, so an anonymous authorize leg taking identity from a **query parameter** lets anyone bind a mailbox to somebody else's account.

**This PR does not do that, and pins that it stays that way** (`test_the_authorize_leg_is_not_public_and_must_not_become_public`).

## The fix

A BFF route the browser navigates to instead — `src/app/api/email/oauth/[provider]/authorize/route.ts`. It runs server-side, so it has the session; it calls the still-gated gateway route with `gatewayHeaders()` + `redirect: "manual"`, reads `Location`, and re-issues its own 302. **No gateway route change, no new public surface.**

Plus the half without which the first half is a hole: `user_id` was `user_email or user.email` and is now `user.email or user_email` — the authenticated identity outranks the query parameter.

### Verification found why both halves were needed

Probing for a route-precedence bypass:

```
GET /api/email/oauth/microsoft/%61uthorize?user_email=victim@fracktal.in
```

Next decodes the segment, so it falls through to the `[...path]` catch-all, which forwards every query parameter verbatim. **With only the BFF route and the old precedence, that URL is a live mailbox hijack.** The one-line precedence change is what closes it.

Residual, pinned deliberately: a caller holding the internal bearer with no identity header can still name `user_email`. That requires total platform compromise, and was reachable by *anonymous* callers before 29 July.

## Proven live, not by inspection

Stub gateway on `:8099` reproducing default-deny, `next dev` on `:3099`:

```
the outage   : curl :8099/email/oauth/microsoft/authorize  -> 401 "Authentication required"
the fix      : GET :3099/api/email/oauth/microsoft/authorize -> 302
               location: …/fake-consent?bound_user_id=dev%40fracktal.in&saw_user_email_param=<none>
               stub log: auth=yes  x-user-email=dev@fracktal.in
the contrast : same shape via the [...path] catch-all -> 200 text/html "PROVIDER CONSENT PAGE HTML"
```

That last line is the point: the existing catch-all **follows the redirect server-side** and returns the consent page as HTML instead of navigating the browser to it. A `fetch` through the normal proxy could never have worked.

## Every direct-to-gateway navigation, with a verdict

| Site | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `integrations/page.tsx` `handleConnect` | **same bug — fixed** (this is what the screenshot hit) |
| `email/page.tsx` `handleConnect` | **same bug — fixed** |
| `integrations/page.tsx` `handleReconnect` | **same bug — fixed** (delegates to `handleConnect`) |
| `email/lib/api.ts` `getOAuthUrl` / `getOAuthAuthorizeUrl` | **same shape, zero callers — fixed anyway** |
| `/integrations/oauth/{service}/authorize` | **not the same bug** — returns JSON, not a 302, and has no frontend caller at all |
| `BulkUnsubscribeView`, `<a href>` docs links, `/email?addAccount=imap` | fine — third-party or internal |

`NEXT_PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` now survives in client code only inside two explanatory comments.

Also fixed: `email/page.tsx` fed `encodeURIComponent(...)` **into** `URLSearchParams` — the exact double-encoding bug `integrations/page.tsx` carries a warning comment about. Round trip verified end to end:

```
OLD, at the callback page: http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3099%2Femail%3Ftab%3Dinbox   -> relative path -> 404
NEW:                       http://localhost:3099/email?tab=inbox                  -> intact
```

## 🔴 The test written to stop false passes had one

`_code_only()` strips comments so a comment explaining why `user_email` is no longer sent doesn't read, to a substring check, exactly like sending it. It was **line-based**, so it only dropped comments that *began* a line. Verification found:

```ts
redirect: "follow", // was redirect: "manual"
```

passing **all 11 tests** — the trailing comment left the banned string in the assertion input. It also deleted real code: on a line where a block comment *ended*, everything after `*/` went with it, which can make a `not in` assertion green by removing the very token it looks for.

Replaced with a character scanner that tracks string state, so `//` inside a string survives and `{/* … */}` in JSX does not. **`_code_only` now has its own test** covering every position the line filter got wrong plus the two converse cases where it must not eat code. Regex literals are not modelled and the docstring says so rather than implying total coverage.

That mutant now fails. This is the seventh test in this repo to assert less than its docstring claimed — the first was caught during the build (an assertion satisfied by the route's own comment naming `manual`), which is why the helper existed at all.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_email_oauth_authorize_wiring.py -q                 -> 12 passed (was 11)
uv run pytest test_email_oauth_authorize_wiring + test_org_access_enforcement \
              + test_default_deny_auth -q                                        -> 59 passed
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006                         -> All checks passed!
npx tsc --noEmit                                                                 -> exit 0
npx vitest run                                                                   -> 171 passed
npx next build                                                                   -> compiled; route table lists
                                                                                    /api/email/oauth/[provider]/authorize
```

13 mutations killed, each reverted sha256-identical — authorize added to `PUBLIC_ROUTES`, callback *removed* from it, precedence swapped back, `manual`→`follow` in both comment positions, `gatewayHeaders`→`serviceHeaders`, `Location` unread, BFF relaying `user_email`, gateway-host navigation restored per call site, route file deleted.

## Recorded, not fixed

- **`_oauth_states` is a module-level in-process dict.** Any deploy landing mid-flow loses the state and the callback fails validation; not shared across workers; entries never expire. Written up on the dict, in `AGENTS.md`, and in the spec.
- **The catch-all re-sends the internal bearer when it follows a redirect.** No evidence of a real leak — undici strips `Authorization` across origins — but the catch-all stays reachable for gateway routes that answer 3xx, and `%61uthorize` proves it. Pre-existing.
- A signed-out navigation to the BFF route returns a JSON 401 in the address bar rather than redirecting to `/signin`. Deliberate: it must stay a refusal.

**No migration.** Spec: `email_app_master_plan.md` §7 Tier 1 item 1 is now 🟡 partially closed, and records what that item got wrong — it ranked this "not an active incident" because the owner had a working mailbox, while it was a total outage for everyone else.

title: N8 — delete a member permanently, everyone except yourself
body:
## N8 — delete a member permanently, everyone except yourself

**WS-24 / N8** · owning spec `ai-company-brain/specs/colleague_onboarding.md` §2 Step 5.

Asked for: *"allow the owner to be able to remove and completely delete everyone else apart from themselves."*

`DELETE /admin/members/{email}` stays exactly as it was — a soft remove (`status='removed'`, roles dropped, row kept). This adds a **second, harder action beside it**: `DELETE /admin/members/{email}/purge`. `remove_member`'s diff has **zero removed lines**.

### What a purge destroys, and what it keeps

**Deleted** — the identity and everything that exists only to grant them access: role grants, permission overrides, group membership, room participation, app grants, remembered "always allow this tool" decisions, all three credential-bearing accounts (email, WhatsApp, tasks), their **private** chat sessions, their `access_request` row, and finally `app_user`.

**Kept** — the audit trail, their apps, workflows, meetings, notes, **shared** rooms, locally-created tasks and projects, and their CRM `person` record.

The audit trail is not negotiable. `app_audit` already says so in its own schema — `app_id UUID` with no FK, commented *"audit survives hard delete"*. An audit trail that disappears with the person is not one.

**Nothing is anonymised, deliberately.** The address is the join key across ~50 tables, so blanking `owner_email` would not hide the person — it would orphan their apps. "Delete the identity" means removing the `app_user` row and every credential and grant keyed to it, not erasing the address everywhere.

### 🔴 The blast radius is much larger than "one person"

Deleting a credential means deleting the row it lives on, and those rows cascade:

```
email_accounts  ->  17 direct, 20 transitive   the entire mirrored mailbox
wa_accounts     ->  14 direct, 16 transitive   the entire WhatsApp history
task_accounts   ->  gtd_projects, gtd_items (SYNCED only), gtd_waiting
```

Their actual mailbox at Microsoft is untouched; what goes is our mirror plus every rule, label, learned pattern, embedding and contact derived from it. **The confirmation dialog says this before you can confirm**, and the response reports it table by table.

### 🔴 The first version reported destroyed rows as *kept*

Verification caught this and it is the reason for a repair round.

`gtd_items` was on the **keep** list under `lower(user_id) = :email`. `task_accounts` was on the **delete** list. And `48_task_manager_gtd.sql:93` declares `account_id ... REFERENCES task_accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, while the sync path stamps **both** `user_id` and `account_id` on every synced row.

So a member with 847 synced tasks got `kept: {"tasks": 847}` **while all 847 were destroyed**. `gtd_projects` was destroyed and appeared on neither list. The dialog said "tasks... they authored" under **Kept**.

That is worse than failing to report a destruction — it reports it as a survival, on the one action that cannot be undone.

Fixed: the keep clauses now carry `AND account_id IS NULL`, and synced items and projects are counted and reported on the **deleted** side as `synced_tasks` / `synced_projects`. The dialog names them.

**Why nothing caught it:** the existing fence compared `count_sql` to `delete_sql` *within one row-spec*, and the test fake models no foreign keys at all — so neither a structural nor a behavioural test could see a DELETE on one table silently emptying a table on the KEEP list. There are now two cross-table fences driven by a cascade graph derived from `infra/postgres/*.sql`, plus the fake's docstring stating it models no cascades and why that makes the claim structural.

### Two more gates that were unfenced

**The permission on the most destructive route in the product.** Deleting `require_permission("admin:members:manage")` — leaving the package floor `Depends(require_admin_user)` — left **162 tests green**. The floor is `admin:members:read`, which a seeded `manager` holds, so that mutation silently hands hard-delete of any member to every manager. Now pinned by reading the slug out of the dependency.

**The type-to-confirm gate.** `const confirmed = true;` left 32 pytest and 173 vitest green. The rule is now its own module with its own tests — including that an empty address confirms nothing, which a bare `typed === member.email` would get wrong.

### Self-protection

The purge goes through `_common.assert_not_self_lockout` — invariant 4's shared home — and `assert_owner_survives`. The door-enumeration test now covers **four** doors. Deleting the self-guard fails **8** tests across two files; deleting `assert_owner_survives` fails exactly **1**. The failure sets are disjoint, which is only possible because every case discriminates on detail text (*"cannot permanently delete yourself"* vs *"no owner"*) plus what was and was not written. **No bare status-code assertion anywhere in the file** — both guards answer 409, and that trap has now shipped seven times here.

### Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_admin_member_purge.py -q        -> 39 passed  (32 before the repair)
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_admin_member_offboarding.py -q  -> 28 passed  (27 on main)
uv run pytest test_signin_requests + test_org_access_control \
            + test_org_access_enforcement + test_admin_groups -> 152 passed (= main)
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006      -> All checks passed!
npx tsc --noEmit                                              -> exit 0
npx vitest run                                                -> 178 passed (171 on main)
```

I re-ran the three decisive mutations myself rather than taking the report:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| tasks KEEP stops excluding cascaded rows (the shipped bug) | **5 failed**, incl. the new cross-table fence |
| `require_permission` deleted from the purge route | **1 failed** (was 0 before the repair) |
| `purgeConfirmed` returns `true` | **4 vitest failed** |

Audit survival, single-transaction, the `chat_session` private filter, and the fake's raise-on-unparseable-predicate were each mutation-verified during verification and are unchanged here.

### 🔴 One decision still open for the owner

`task_accounts` holds an encrypted credential **and** cascades into synced tasks. So a purge deletes a person's ClickUp-synced tasks while keeping their local ones — an asymmetry that falls out of where a foreign key sits, not from anything anyone chose.

- **As built:** delete the row. The credential is genuinely gone, synced tasks go with it, and the confirmation and counts say so.
- **The alternative:** null the credential and keep the row, so the task mirror survives and a husk account row stays behind.

Recorded in the spec as an open question. The reporting is now truthful under either choice.

### Also found

- **`infra/postgres/schema.generated.sql` is stale** — it predates migration 130, so it has no `user_role`, `org_group`, `access_request`, `chat_session_participant`, `workflows` or `app_grants`. The table map was derived from the numbered migrations instead, and the cascade parser skips the dump for that reason. `scripts/dump_schema.sh` is owed.
- **`acb_audit.log.record` swallows every exception**, so a failed audit write still lets the purge commit. "The audit entry survives a rollback" is true; "a completed purge always leaves an audit row" is not. Recorded at every point where the audit guarantee is claimed; not fixed, because that is a change to `acb_audit`'s contract.

### Not done

- `remove_member`'s permission is still unpinned — same one-line hole, same class; F2 was scoped to the purge route.
- The fifth self-lockout door (`PUT …/overrides`) still guards with its own inline comparison against a different permission. Pre-existing, flagged in N7, still owed a consolidating pass.
- No purge-preview endpoint; the dialog names categories and the counts come back after.

**No migration.** No new permission slug.

title: The user-management contract every app must not deviate from
body:
## Why

App work starts next. The knowledge an app needs — how a caller becomes a principal, what an app may assume about them, what it must never do — was spread across four specs, a board row, and eight incident write-ups. **None of it was reachable from the files an agent actually reads before touching code.**

## `specs/user_management_contract.md` (new)

**It owns RULES, not FACTS.** Every fact is cited to the spec that owns it (`org_access_control.md` for the model, `colleague_onboarding.md` for the gate and matrix, `tenancy_and_visibility.md` for D11/D12), so it cannot become a fifth competing description of the access model — which is exactly what the 2026-07-31 audit found wrong with this corpus.

**Anchors are symbols, not line numbers**, deliberately. That audit found ~12 wrong migration citations and a WS-24 pass corrected six stale `rooms.py` anchors. A symbol survives an edit above it; a line number does not.

Contents: the four-hop identity chain and what each hop guarantees · the member lifecycle with every door between its states · the permission vocabulary and the one rule about extending it · **ten build rules, each learned by breaking it** · a trap list naming the incident that found each · and §6, what is *not* closed.

## Where builders will actually hit it

- **Root `AGENTS.md` constraint 10** — it said *"All gateway endpoints require auth (Bearer token + optional user identity)"*, which is no longer the whole truth: auth is default-deny **by construction**, and the interesting part is `PUBLIC_ROUTES` and where identity comes from.
- **`apps/services/gateway/AGENTS.md`** — six route-level rules: the app is default-deny so don't opt out to make something reachable; the `/admin` floor is per-route; owner-scoped reads answer 404 not 403; never take identity from a query parameter; what a destructive route owes; verify don't predict.
- **`workbench/AGENTS.md`** — the BFF is where identity comes from. Never point the browser at the gateway, and a `fetch` through the `[...path]` catch-all **cannot** replace a BFF route for a redirecting endpoint, because the catch-all follows the redirect server-side.

## Gate rows corrected against the running deployment, not against intent

| Gate | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **G1** | "strip applied, live" | 🔴 **has a bypass** — `:8080` and `:3001` answer from the public internet, so Caddy is not on the only path. Verified by probe from outside; `5432`/`6379` correctly closed |
| **G2** | "unprovisioned" | 🔴 **worse than unprovisioned** — `GATEWAY_INTERNAL_TOKEN` is *set* and **byte-identical** to `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` (same length, same sha256), so a "is it configured" check reads green while the service identity is the key every agent holds |
| **G3** | "nothing exists" | 🟡 **the first real backup landed** — #347's pre-migration gate fired ahead of migration 143 and left a 22 MB data dump. Still owed: the timer is not installed, and no restore has ever been run |

Both G1 and G2 are OWNER-GATE and now registered in `work_plan.md` §6 with the measurement and the remedy. Stated plainly there and here: **neither blocks app development; together they block trusting it.**

The WS-24 board row is rewritten to reality — every AGENT-SAFE item is built, merged and deployed (`main` @ `74082882` is live, migration 143 applied), and what remains is two owner actions on the identity boundary plus two on backups.

## Verification

The contract's own verification block runs:

```
uv run pytest test_org_access_control + test_default_deny_auth + test_org_access_enforcement
            + test_admin_member_offboarding + test_admin_member_purge + test_signin_requests
            + test_notes_owner_scoping + test_tasks_people_scoping
            + test_email_oauth_authorize_wiring -q        -> 320 passed
```

I also spot-checked a fact rather than inheriting it: the claim that `feature:memory`, `feature:artifacts` and `feature:observability` are enforced nowhere server-side holds — `memory.py`, `workspace.py` and `observability.py` each contain zero `require_feature` calls.

**Docs only.** No code, no migration, no `deploy/` change.

title: BO-23: two of five backup anchors named tables that do not exist
body:
## The defect

`MANIFEST.txt` states, in its own words:

> `# anchor row counts (a restore that does not reproduce these is wrong)`

and then lists `app_user`, **`email_message`**, **`gtd_task`**, `meeting`, `agent_run`.

Two of those are not tables. The real names are `email_messages` and `gtd_items`. So every backup this deployment has ever taken printed:

```
email_message:       n/a
gtd_task:            n/a
```

and `n/a` reads as benign.

## What was actually behind those two slots

Measured on the box:

```
email_messages:      7398
gtd_items:            717
```

**A restore could have lost the entire email mirror — the largest dataset in the system — without contradicting a single anchor.** The integrity check that exists to catch exactly that was pointed at nothing.

## The fix

Correct names, plus: an unresolvable name now reports `MISSING — anchor names a table that does not exist`, and a failed count reports `QUERY FAILED`. A wrong anchor is worse than no anchor, because it occupies the slot where the check should be and looks like it is doing the job.

## Verified against the live schema before committing

```
app_user:            3
email_messages:      7398
gtd_items:           717
meeting:             16
agent_run:           184
email_message:       MISSING — anchor names a table that does not exist
gtd_task:            MISSING — anchor names a table that does not exist
```

## Found while doing the first real restore test

`backup_db.sh --verify-restore` has now been run on the box for the first time:

```
==> Deep verify — restoring acb.dump into a scratch database
    public tables: live=228 restored=228
    restore verified
```

That is BO-23's hardest done-when — *a restore has actually been performed* — satisfied rather than asserted.

Two things it also surfaced, **not fixed here**:

- **`BACKUP_REMOTE` is unset**, and the script says so itself: *"this backup exists ONLY on this box. It protects against bad migrations and dropped tables, NOT against losing the VPS."*
- **`deploy/hostinger/acb-backup.{service,timer}` do not exist.** The runbook's §5 install step is `sudo install -m 0644 /opt/acb/app/deploy/hostinger/acb-backup.{service,timer} /etc/systemd/system/` — pointing at files that were documented inline and never committed. So the scheduled half of BO-23 cannot be installed as written. I have the unit contents ready but `deploy/` writes are owner-gated and the guard blocked me; they are in the handover.

Until a timer exists, backups happen only when a migration runs — which is why one exists today at all.

**Docs + one script.** No migration, no `deploy/` change.

title: BO-23 backup fix + WS-25: deploys have not reached the box since #347
body:
## What broke

The BO-23 timer was installed on the box today and **failed on its first real run**:

```
/opt/acb/app/scripts/backup_db.sh: line 142: /tmp/verify_restore.log: Permission denied
!! pg_restore FAILED — see /tmp/verify_restore.log
acb-backup.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
```

## Why

`--verify-restore` wrote pg_restore output to `/tmp/verify_restore.log`. Ubuntu sets
`fs.protected_regular=2`, which forbids opening an existing file in a sticky
world-writable directory owned by a different user — and **root is not exempt**, unlike
ordinary DAC permissions.

So the first manual run as `acb` created the file, and every subsequent root-run systemd
invocation hit EACCES. The dump itself was always fine; the unit reported FAILURE, which
is the worst shape for this bug — a backup that looks broken while the data is actually
there, discovered during an incident.

## Fix

The log now goes to `$DEST/verify_restore.log`, beside the dump it describes. Immune to
the ownership problem, and the evidence for a backup now travels with that backup instead
of being clobbered by the next run.

## Verification (on the box, after clearing the stale `/tmp` file)

```
Result=success
ExecMainStatus=0
public tables: live=228 restored=228
restore verified
4 backup(s) retained, 90M total
```

## How it was found

By running `systemctl start acb-backup.service` instead of trusting the timer. The unit
would otherwise have failed silently at 02:30 every night.

## ⚠️ Not fixed here — deploys are not reaching the box

This PR cannot take effect until deploys work. `main` is at `d7d5c79b`; the box is at
`74082882` (#347). **#354, #355, #356, #357 and #358 are merged but not live**, including
the OAuth authorize fix.

Failed deploy runs show `ssh: connect to host ***: Connection timed out` and
`workbench=000000`. The box logged **four** SSH lines across the entire 55-minute window,
load average 0.16, no reboot, and it answers my machine in 240ms. GitHub's packets are not
arriving — the block is upstream of the VPS, on any port, not SSH-specific.

title: fix(WS-25): repoint the deploy guards at the extracted apply script
body:
## What broke

Extracting `DEPLOY_SCRIPT` into `scripts/vps_apply.sh` (#359) broke `test_meeting_bot_deploy_wiring.py`. Seven of its guards grep the deploy script's **content** and were reading `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, where that content no longer lives.

**CI caught it — 1 failed, 1883 passed — and correctly skipped `publish-release`**, so the box was never offered a build whose tests failed. That is the new gate doing exactly what it was built for, on its first run.

## Fix

All eleven asserted strings were verified present in `vps_apply.sh` and absent from `deploy.yml` **before** repointing anything, so this follows the subject rather than relaxing the assertion.

## The guard that makes the other seven mean anything

`test_both_delivery_paths_execute_the_same_apply_script`. The seven guards now read a *file*; that is only meaningful while something actually **runs** it. Without this, re-inlining the script into the workflow would leave every guard green against an orphan while the real deploy logic lived elsewhere — precisely the drift the extraction exists to prevent.

It pins both consumers (workflow → push path, poller → pull path) and asserts `DEPLOY_SCRIPT` is not reintroduced alongside, because two copies are worse than either alone.

## ⚠️ My first version of that guard was itself too weak

`assert "scripts/vps_apply.sh" in workflow` — a bare substring check. Mutating the workflow to copy a **different file** left it **green**, because the header comments discuss `vps_apply.sh` by name. It certified the documentation, not the wiring.

Now it requires a non-comment line. Three mutants measured red, tree byte-identical after revert:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| workflow copies a different file | 🔴 red |
| poller runs its own private copy | 🔴 red |
| script re-inlined as `DEPLOY_SCRIPT` | 🔴 red |

13 passed at baseline.

title: docs(WS-25): correct the pull unit — two defects found on first real run
body:
Both defects surfaced only by starting the service. Neither is visible by reading the unit.

**Defect 1 — could not bootstrap.** `ExecStart` installed the poller *from the checkout*. A machine older than the poller has no such file; it arrives only via the update the poller is meant to perform. First run:

```
install: cannot stat '/opt/acb/app/scripts/vps_pull.sh': No such file or directory
```

Reading the script from `origin/release` via `git show` needs nothing in the working tree — and also solves the self-rewrite hazard the original comment was already worried about. One fix for both.

**Defect 2 — `User=root` breaks git auth.** Second run:

```
Host key verification failed.
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
```

The remote is an SSH URL; the key and `known_hosts` belong to `acb`, and root has neither. CI has always invoked this script as `acb`, and the script elevates with `sudo` ~30 times — it is written to start unprivileged. Running it as root was the deviation, not the fix.

Also records that `/var/lib/acb` must exist and be `acb`-owned, or the last-success marker is skipped silently (the script degrades with `|| true`, so a missing directory would not announce itself).

## ⚠️ Needs an owner

The unit currently installed is still the broken first version and is failing every 5 minutes. Correcting it and starting it needs the owner — plan-guard blocks the agent here, correctly, because starting the service runs the apply script, which applies migrations and restarts services.

Corrected unit and the one-line state-directory setup are in `deploy_delivery_path.md` §8.3.

title: WS-26: native CRM — spec, board registration, and the WS-26a slice (schema + core API)
body:
## What this is

Mints **WS-26 — the native CRM that replaces Zoho** — and ships its first slice.

**Research inputs (2026-08-05):** `frappe/crm` (AGPL — data-model concepts only, zero code copied), `trycompai/crm` (MIT — patterns ported, stack does not translate), and a full-tree sweep of our Zoho footprint. Key finding: Zoho today is a **read-only nightly mirror** (no UI, no write path, no Leads pull), so leaving it is *import-and-retire*, not a live cutover.

## Contents

**Docs:** `specs/crm_app.md` (seven-point contract: data model, API, UI plan, import→coexist→cutover→retire path with the measured retirement inventory, decisions D-CRM-1..6 + B1..B6, tickets WS-26a–e with gate labels) · work_plan WS-26 board row, §4 owner-registry entry, three §6 owner gates (import run, `CRM_AUTO_LEAD` flip, cutover + Zoho token revoke — the last one executes part of WS-2's standing P0).

**Code (WS-26a):**
- `infra/postgres/144_crm.sql` — 10 tables: organizations / contacts / leads / deals / deal-contacts / statuses-as-data (color, position, type, probability) / activity spine / status-change log (funnel dwell) / lost reasons. Idempotent, statically asserted.
- `gateway/db.py` — the shared engine seam the board's BO-10 exception asked for; `routes/tasks/core.py` converted as proof. **The CRM is not engine #13.**
- `routes/crm/` — 40 routes behind `feature:crm`: CRUD + list contract (sort allowlist, 422 on unknown keys), pipeline/kanban endpoint, status transitions (dwell log + activity + `closed_at` + lost-reason enforcement on both verbs), lead→deal convert (email dedup, 409 while the deal exists), timelines (a deal inherits its source lead's history).
- 190 new CRM tests + extended org-access invariants (FEATURES⟷feature_catalog both-ways fence, GATED_ROUTERS entry). **279 passing named**; correctness-ruff and xenon clean; tasks regression fence 194 passed.

## The supervisor chain this went through

1. **spec-auditor** — GO-NARROWED; both blockers folded into the spec before build (schema.generated.sql clause struck as unsatisfiable; import-endpoint permission corrected — mig 131 grants `member` `integrations:use:*`, so the floor is `admin:access:manage`).
2. **ws-implementer** — built the slice; mutation-tested its own fences; reported five unrecorded decisions, now in the spec (B1–B5).
3. **ws-verifier** — FAILed the branch on a proven CI landmine (a test asserting the CRM migration is highest-numbered — red the moment any later migration lands, silently blocking deploy) + a `closed_at`-on-create gap. Repaired, re-proven against the verifier's own probe.
4. **diff-reviewer** — APPROVE, no P0; its P1 (deleting a converted deal stranded the lead invisibly forever) and three P2s all taken (B6 + review-repairs block in spec §8).

## Not in this PR, on purpose

No UI (WS-26c), no Zoho importer (WS-26b), no `schema.generated.sql` resync (needs a migrated live DB; ~43 migrations stale repo-wide — separate owner chore). **The migration has never been applied to a real database** — it will apply on the first deploy after merge via the normal ladder.

## Owner attention

- Decisions D-CRM-1..6 and B1..B6 in spec §8 are all `agent-proposed, owner may overrule`.
- Open question recorded, deliberately unbuilt: reopening a won/lost deal leaves `closed_at` stale.
- `feature:crm` ships `is_default false` — visible to owner/admin only until granted.

title: WS-26c: CRM UI — kanban, lists, record sheets, convert modal + the API addendum
body:
The /crm app: deals kanban (drag with optimistic undo), four list views on the shared contract with URL-state sort/filters, record sheets (?deal= deep links), timeline with inherited lead history, convert modal with interactive dedup, quick-create; BFF proxy; nav/access/centers registration with a type-level live-requires-href fence. Gateway addendum: deal-contacts endpoints (one-primary enforced atomically), organization_name joins, residual 422 guards, hand-edited lead_name preserved.

Chain: spec-auditor GO-NARROWED -> built -> verifier PASS (all claims re-run + mutation-tested) -> diff-review REQUEST-CHANGES (P0: sort never reached the wire; stale lists after create/patch; convert dedup duplicate; owner-filter widening; Firefox drag; two more) -> all seven repaired. 320 pytest + 281 vitest + tsc clean.

Owner-verified after migration 144 applies: live rendering, drag persistence, deep links (no DOM test env exists; helpers are fixture-tested). feature:crm is is_default=false - grant it to demo to a member. Merge AFTER #362 (stacked); reconcile with the 26b PR on spec/work_plan + import_zoho one-primary INSERT (both sides already enforce independently).

title: fix(WS-25): the deploy that reported success without happening
body:
Found during WS-26 activation: main was three merges ahead of what the box was actually running, and every signal said green.

**Defect 4a — `release` never moved.** `publish-release` uses the default depth-1 checkout, and `git push` proves fast-forward client-side — the runner doesn't have the commit `release` points at, so every publish after the ref-creating one was rejected with "fetch first". `release` sat at #360 while #361/#362/#365 merged. Fix: `fetch-depth: 0`.

**Defect 4b — the 900s SSH timeout is shorter than the backup.** The BO-23 pre-migration backup takes ~11 minutes on the 4GB box, so `timeout 900` killed the apply mid-flight: migrations never ran, services never restarted — and `verify()` then blessed the still-healthy OLD deployment. Fix: `timeout 1800`, matched to the pull unit's `TimeoutStartSec`.

**Defect 3 (recorded, not fixed here)** — the pull poller skips on `HEAD == origin/release`, but `git reset` moves HEAD before migrations run, so an interrupted push-path apply reads as "already current" to the pull path too. The durable fix (skip keyed on the end-of-apply `/var/lib/acb` marker) is written into the spec for WS-25's next slice.

Spec updated in the same PR (§8.3 Defects 3/4 + the corrections-exist-on-paper warning). Box-side remediation already done by hand today: corrected `User=acb` unit installed, `release` fast-forwarded, forced apply run.

title: WS-27: mint the Projects app — Paca research, the native PM spec, and WS-27a+b (schema, grant read model, ClickUp importer)
body:
Mints **WS-27** — native org-level project management in the People Center, sliced into every other Center — and builds its first two tickets.

## What this is for

The company's work lives in ClickUp; CommandCenter's `/tasks` is a *personal* GTD lens over it. This adds the missing middle: departments → projects → subprojects → tasks → subtasks, owned natively, with each Center seeing its own slice and every member's assigned work still reaching their personal inbox.

## The documents

**`specs/paca_pm_research_2026-08.md`** — a deep read of `Paca-AI/paca` v0.11.0 (Apache-2.0; patterns adopted, no code translated — the stack doesn't survive translation). Verified against the tree rather than its docs, which mis-state the web framework (chi, not Gin) and still describe an automation design migration `000027` dropped. Ends in a 14-row adopt/adapt/refuse table. Reference-only; owns no work.

**`specs/project_management_app.md`** — the owning spec, in the `crm_app.md` shape: vision/non-goals → measured current state → data model → API → UI + Center projections → integrations → migration path → decisions → tickets → verification.

## The decisions, and what changed after owner review

Three questions were opened for the owner and answered as **D-PM-8/9/10**; two changed the build:

- **D-PM-8** — no portfolio/program layer. Grants are the only grouping axis; a cross-department project simply carries several.
- **D-PM-9** — agent edits to ClickUp-linked tasks are treated **exactly like human edits** (*the agent proposed queueing agent-originated pushes for approval and was overruled*). The accepted cost is stated once in the spec: while `ACTION_BROKER_ENFORCE` is off, a mistaken agent edit reaches the live workspace with no human in between. The three properties that bound it — attribution, timeline-reversibility, and the enforce flip — are labelled as **not** being a gate, so a later reader can't quote them as if the risk were handled.
- **D-PM-10** — ClickUp Spaces map to Centers **explicitly**, from agent-proposed suggestions, owner-confirmed, applied as `group:<slug>` grants. This one grew a whole endpoint (below).

## WS-27a — schema and the grant read model

**Migration `146_projects.sql`**, eleven tables. The whole hierarchy is two self-referencing foreign keys (`pm_projects.parent_project_id`, `pm_tasks.parent_task_id`) with types-as-data — no table per level, no depth column. Statuses are per-project rows with a semantic `category`, so the importer can represent ClickUp's real status names. **No rank column on tasks**: ordering lives in `pm_view_task_positions` as fractional indexes, which is what lets the People Center board and a Center slice order the same task differently.

**`routes/projects/`** — behind `feature:projects`, consuming the shared `gateway/db.py` seam rather than adding engine thirteen (BO-10), asserted by grep in the suite.

Two rules that had to live in code rather than schema:

- **A task assigned to you is visible even when its project is not.** Delegation across a Center boundary is normal work; without it the task 404s for the person expected to do it.
- **One status transition, three effects** — status, `completed_at` stamped *or cleared* on the done boundary, and a timeline entry. A PATCH that writes only the column looks correct in the UI while silently emptying the timeline.

### Visibility is a data boundary here, not a nav one

Unlike `/crm` (D-CRM-3, org-visible by decision), a project is visible only when a grant on it *or an ancestor* matches the caller. `pm_project_grants` speaks exactly the shipped `email | group:<slug> | org` vocabulary — a second one would mean two answers to "who can see this". Non-visible is **404, never 403**.

The full-portfolio read requires **`data:org:read`**, which D14 measured at **zero consumers**; this is deliberately its first, which is why granting it is now registered as an owner gate.

## WS-27b — the ClickUp importer, and a mapping the owner confirms

Two endpoints, because D-PM-10 makes the mapping the owner's act. `POST /projects/import/clickup/plan` proposes a Center per Space and **writes nothing**; `POST /projects/import/clickup` applies only what came back in `mappings`. **An agent may propose a mapping and must never apply one** — a wrong auto-map grants one Center visibility of another department's work. The plan's claim is asserted against the session (no INSERT reaches it, nothing commits), not against the response, because a plan that quietly created projects would look identical from the outside.

Three signals, cheapest first: **assignee overlap** against `org_group` membership (deterministic, no LLM, and the strongest signal the platform already holds — who does the work is what a department is); a **name match** where a whole word beats a substring accident; and an **EVAL-LOCKED** title classification. Every signal that fired returns as evidence, because a confidence with nothing behind it is a number the owner cannot check. Below a floor it proposes nothing — a weak guess presented as a suggestion means reviewing our noise instead of deciding — and still returns the scores, so a blank suggestion is distinguishable from a signal failure. The classifier degrades to no-signal on any failure and the plan still arrives.

**An unmapped Space still imports in full** with no group grant, staying reachable for `data:org:read` holders and its assignees; refusing would make the mapping a precondition of seeing the data needed to decide it. Unmapped Spaces are **named**, not counted.

ClickUp's Space/Folder/List zoo flattens onto the one `pm_projects` self-FK, with `clickup_kind` remembering which was which. Re-import is keyed on `clickup_id`. Reuses the Tasks app's `ClickUpProvider` rather than adding a second ClickUp client — one less thing to retire at WS-27g — and makes two API calls regardless of Space count. Floor is `admin:access:manage`, **not** `integrations:use:clickup` (migration 131 grants `member` `integrations:use:*`, so that slug gates nothing — the WS-26b finding, applying unchanged).

## Verification

**231 passed** across the projects + org-access suites and **387 passed** across main's six CRM suites on the merged tree; 140 of the projects cases are new and hermetic (no DB, no ClickUp, no LLM). Ruff's correctness selection and xenon clean on the new files.

The migration's idempotency is asserted **statically over its text**: the suite runs no database, so an idempotency claim nobody can fail is not a claim.

Every scoping case runs as a colleague holding only `feature:projects`, never as the owner — an owner-only suite passes against a completely unscoped route.

**Nine mutants measured red and reverted byte-identical.** WS-27a: visibility clause forced to `TRUE` (9 red), assignee escape dropped, status activity skipped, `completed_at` never cleared on reopen, Epic-root rule removed. WS-27b: applying the suggestion instead of the confirmed mapping, refusing to import an unmapped Space, a plan that writes, a re-import that duplicates.

One real bug the tests caught before review: the event seam logged its swallowed failure with `event=`, structlog's reserved key — it raised inside the logger and turned a best-effort emit into the 500 that function exists to prevent.

## Merge with main (WS-26b/c)

Two text conflicts in `work_plan.md`, both additive — resolved keeping main's WS-26 rows and this branch's WS-27 rows.

⚠️ **The conflict git did not flag is the one that mattered.** Main landed `145_crm_zoho_sync.sql`, so `145` was taken twice on the merged tree — exactly what R1 exists to prevent, and it does not surface as a merge conflict because the two files have different names. Ours is renumbered to **`146_projects.sql`**, with its header and all three citations updated. The rename is safe by construction: `test_projects_migration.py` finds the file by **content**, not by number, for this precise reason.

`main.py` auto-merged with both routers registered; no `feature_catalog` `sort_order` collision (crm 55, projects 56).

## Not in this PR, on purpose

No UI (WS-27d), no sync (WS-27c — blocked on WS-1's **BO-1a and BO-1b**, named as prerequisites rather than discoveries), no `centers.ts` flip, and no edit to `department_centers.md` C1 — `pm_project_grants` is recorded as a *sibling* of D13's `gtd_project_grant`, not a replacement. `schema.generated.sql` was not regenerated: it needs a migrated live DB and is stale repo-wide, so it stays an owner-run chore (the WS-26a precedent).

## ⚠️ Deployment

**Migration 146 has not been applied anywhere, and neither import endpoint has ever been run.** Executing either against the live ClickUp tenant stays owner-gated, and confirming a Space→Center mapping is the owner's act. Per WS-25 the deploy delivery path is currently broken, so merging will not ship this on its own. The root `AGENTS.md` constraint-8 amendment ships only in the final cutover PR (WS-27g), never before.

title: fix(db): one wedged handler could freeze the whole database — three bounds
body:
## The incident

Sending mail stopped working on 2026-08-06. It was reported as "I can't send emails — is it the multi-user work?" It was not an auth or scoping regression: the send path's ownership and feature gates were intact. It was a database freeze, and email was simply the first surface anyone noticed.

Verified live on the box with `pg_blocking_pids`:

```
pid 1208980  idle in transaction, 14h44m
             SELECT org_domains FROM email_assistant_settings WHERE account_id = $1
                 ↓ holds ACCESS SHARE
pid 1210326  ALTER TABLE email_assistant_settings ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ...   (waiting)
                 ↓ ACCESS EXCLUSIVE parks at the head of a FIFO queue
pid 1209232, 1209228, 1216158, ...  every later reader of that table, indefinitely
```

The chain:

1. An LLM completion hung — `acompletion` was awaited with **no wall-clock bound**.
2. The caller held a SQLAlchemy `AsyncSession` across that await. A session opens a transaction on first `execute()` and holds it until commit/rollback/close, so the hung call parked a Postgres transaction `idle in transaction` for **14h44m**.
3. The migration runner asked for `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` on that table and **waited**. Postgres's lock queue is FIFO, so every later reader queued behind the *waiting* `ALTER` — including `SELECT signature FROM email_assistant_settings`, which the send path makes on its way to the provider.
4. Each blocked reader pinned a pooled connection until the email engine's `10+20` pool drained, and unrelated endpoints started answering `QueuePool limit of size 10 overflow 20 reached`.

The BFF aborts the send POST at 30s, so the user-visible symptom was a failed send with **zero `POST /email/send` lines in three days of gateway logs** — the request never completed, so uvicorn never logged it. Absence of the access line *was* the symptom.

Terminating the stale backend cleared it: the blocked query went from indefinite to **1.5ms**. A **new** session took the same lock six minutes later and the freeze reproduced identically. That is what makes this a code fix rather than an operational one.

## The fix — three independent bounds

Any one of them breaks the chain. All three are here because there was no bound at all, and the cheapest way for this to come back is for someone to restore one link while the other two still look fine.

| Link | Bound | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Unbounded await | `asyncio.wait_for` at 90s per attempt (`LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS`) | `acb_llm/client.py` |
| Unbounded held transaction | `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=600s` via asyncpg `server_settings` | `gateway/db.py` + 7 engines, `email_ingestion` |
| Migration waits for a lock | `SET lock_timeout=5s` + 5 bounded retries | the migration runner |

Three details worth reviewing rather than skimming:

- **`except TimeoutError` sits ABOVE the generic handler.** `asyncio.wait_for`'s TimeoutError stringifies to `''`, so the existing `any(token in str(exc).lower() ...)` transient check reads it as *non-transient* and re-raises. Getting the order wrong would convert one slow provider response into a hard failure on attempt 1 — the fix becoming a new, quieter outage. A test pins it.
- **600s, not 300s.** A rules run legitimately awaits a completion with a session open, and `complete` retries 3×90s + 6s backoff ≈ 276s. If the DB ceiling dropped under that, Postgres would start killing *healthy* transactions mid-retry, which reads as random unattributable failures under load. `test_idle_ceiling_clears_the_llm_worst_case` fails if someone raises one number without the other.
- **The idle ceiling is scoped to the app's own connections**, not set via `ALTER ROLE`. `pg_dump` and the migration runner connect as the same role and must not inherit an app-tuned deadline.

`test_every_gateway_engine_carries_the_bounds` is a structural guard: per-site opt-in is exactly how the email engine ended up as the one that drained.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_stalled_session_cannot_freeze_the_db.py -q   -> 10 passed
uv run pytest tests/unit -q -k email                                       -> 973 passed, 1 skipped
uv run pytest tests/unit -q -k "llm or db or engine or connect or migration"
    -> 410 passed, 1 failed (test_workflows_engine::test_module_node_runs_generated_code,
       PRE-EXISTING — red on a clean stashed tree too)
uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006                   -> All checks passed!
uv run xenon --max-absolute F --max-modules F --max-average B apps packages -> exit 0
```

Not just green — confirmed **red without the fix**. With the `asyncio.wait_for` removed, both LLM tests fail (in bounded time; each carries an outer CI guard so a broken build fails rather than hangs). The retry loop was exercised against a fake `psql`:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| clean apply | exit 0, 1 attempt |
| lock busy 2x then succeeds | exit 0, 3 attempts, retries logged |
| lock busy forever | exit 1 after exactly 3, prints the `pg_stat_activity` query that finds the holder |
| real SQL error | exit 1 after exactly 1 — no retry, real error surfaced |

## Where multi-user came in

As the amplifier, not the bug. A second mailbox (`Ishaanpilar@fracktal.in`) was connected 2026-08-05 08:56 UTC, doubling every per-account background loop against pools sized when there was one mailbox. The sweep for the *new* account ran seconds after the lock was taken. Suggestive, not proven — `pg_stat_activity` does not expose the bound `account_id`.

## Not in this PR

- **The email automation package holds DB sessions across provider and LLM calls throughout.** That is now *bounded*, not removed. Restructuring those transaction boundaries is its own change.
- **`acb-pull.service` was exiting 128** (`git fetch -q origin release`) on repeated ticks around 06:42–06:58 UTC. It has since recovered on its own — last successful pull 07:20:49Z, box at `8d83ca10`. Worth a look at why it flapped, but it is **not** blocking this deploy.
- The unit file `acb-pull.service` lives only on the box, not in the repo, so the concurrent-tick hazard in it (a fixed `/tmp/acb-pull-run.sh` that a later tick can overwrite while an earlier one is still executing it) cannot be fixed here. Two overlapping `apply_migrations.sh` runs were observed during the incident, so the `flock` in `vps_pull.sh` is not covering everything it looks like it covers.
- **The leak is still live on the deployed code.** Re-checked after opening this PR: the same `resolve_org_domains` session was 20 minutes `idle in transaction` with a migration and two readers queued behind it. Cleared again by hand. Until this merges, the box stays one long LLM hang away from a repeat.

No migration. No `.env` change required — both new knobs have working defaults.

title: fix(WS-26): every note skipped on the first real backfill
body:
First real backfill (2026-08-06): 737 orgs, 1,189 contacts, 1,516 leads, 551 deals imported cleanly, zero dirty — but **all 1,909 notes skipped**.

Zoho sends `Parent_Id` as a lookup object (`{"name": …, "id": …}`; verified against the live tenant). `_text()` stringifies any non-None value, so `_text or _lookup_id` produced a truthy garbage string and the correct `_lookup_id` branch was dead code — no parent ever resolved. The sync engine's pull phase delegates Notes to this same path, so the two-way sync would have silently skipped every Zoho-side note too; the `CRM_ZOHO_SYNC` flip waits on this.

Fix is one reorder (`_lookup_id` first, `_text` fallback for bare strings). The real gap was the fixtures: they used a string `Parent_Id` the API never sends, so the dict path had zero coverage. Re-pinned all note fixtures to the live shape — **proven to fail against the old code** (2 failed / 39 passed pre-fix; 130 passed post-fix across import + sync files) — plus a test keeping the bare-string fallback contract.

After merge: rerun the (idempotent) backfill to land the 1,909 notes onto their timelines.

title: fix(BO-23): one unremovable old backup dir blocked every deploy
body:
Found live during WS-26 activation, third defect of the day in the delivery chain: every apply after ~08:29Z failed with "pre-migration backup FAILED — refusing to apply migrations", yet the dumps were all succeeding.

The failure was **retention pruning**: the oldest backup dir was root-owned (a leftover from the pull unit's `User=root` era), `rm -rf` hit permission-denied, and `set -euo pipefail` took the whole script down non-zero *after* the dump and checksums had completed. The migration runner fail-closes on that exit code by design — so one stale directory silently blocked every deploy on the box, push-path and pull-path alike. It surfaced today only because today's repeated applies crossed the 14-backup retention threshold.

The dump is the product; pruning is housekeeping. Pruning failure now warns loudly (with the chown remediation in the message) and leaves the exit code alone. Box-side ownership already repaired by hand (`chown -R acb:acb /opt/acb/backups`) and the backup verified green (exit 0, 14 retained).

title: fix(deploy): the lock_timeout prelude was invalid SQL and blocked every deploy
body:
fix(deploy): the lock_timeout prelude was invalid SQL and blocked every deploy

#368 shipped `SET lock_timeout = 5s;` — unquoted. Postgres answers "trailing
junk after numeric literal", and under ON_ERROR_STOP=1 that failed the FIRST
migration in the ladder. So a guard whose entire purpose was to stop a stalled
session from blocking deploys blocked every deploy itself. Caught on its first
real run; no DDL executed, because the prelude is the first statement in the
session and the ladder stops there.

Two things were wrong, and the second is the one worth keeping.

1. Quote the value. '5s' and '5000' are both accepted by Postgres; a bare 5s is
   a syntax error. Verified against the live server, not inferred.

2. A safety feature must not be able to brick the thing it protects. The prelude
   is now PROBED once, before the ladder runs. If the server rejects it — a
   typo'd MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT, a server that spells it differently — the
   runner says so loudly and applies migrations WITHOUT it. Degrading to the
   previous behaviour is survivable; an undeployable box is not. With the probe
   in place, the original unquoted bug would have produced a warning and a
   successful deploy instead of an outage in the deploy path.

Why the tests missed it, and what changed so they cannot again:

- `test_migrations_set_a_lock_timeout` asserted the string was PRESENT, not that
  it was valid SQL. Presence is not validity. `test_the_lock_timeout_value_is_
  QUOTED` now parses the emitted statement and requires a quoted value. It scans
  only non-comment lines — the runner quotes the broken form in its own
  explanation of this bug, and a test that cannot tell an example from an
  instruction would fail on the documentation that prevents the next occurrence.
- The shell harness's fake psql drained stdin without looking at it, so any SQL
  passed. It now mimics Postgres's actual rule and rejects a bare unit. Re-run
  with the original bug reintroduced, it reproduces "trailing junk" exactly —
  and the deploy still succeeds, via the new fallback.
- `test_a_bad_prelude_degrades_instead_of_bricking_the_deploy` pins the fallback
  path itself, so a future edit cannot quietly make the guard fail closed again.

Verify:
  uv run pytest tests/unit/test_stalled_session_cannot_freeze_the_db.py -q
      -> 12 passed
  uv run ruff check . --select F821,F601,F602,F502,F7,B006  -> All checks passed!
  bash -n on the runner                                     -> OK

  Red-first confirmed: with the unquoted form reintroduced,
  test_the_lock_timeout_value_is_QUOTED fails and the fixed form passes.

  Behavioural, against a SQL-validating fake psql:
    valid prelude, clean apply         -> exit 0, 1 attempt
    lock busy 2x then succeeds         -> exit 0, 3 attempts
    lock busy past the retry budget    -> exit 1, exactly 3 attempts
    MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT=nonsense    -> exit 0, warns, applies without the
                                          timeout (the new fallback)

No migration. No .env change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: feat(WS-26d): the CRM agent reads - and only the CRM, only GET
body:
The spec-audit narrowed WS-26d to the half that was actually dispatchable. This is that half.

## What lands

- **`apps/agents/agent-crm/`** — `crm-assistant`, a native MAF agent with four **read-only** tools (`search_crm`, `get_pipeline`, `get_record`, `get_timeline`) that call the gateway's CRM routes and never touch the DB. Built on the `agent-email-assistant` template **including its fail-closed identity rule**: no acting user, no request — it refuses rather than degrading to service identity.
- **Registration** in `_KNOWN_AGENTS`, `_AGENT_REGISTRY` (with `local_path`) and `agent_registry.json`. Orchestrator routability comes from the `_AGENT_REGISTRY` import in `orchestrator/agents.py` — the JSON file is catalog-only, which this PR also corrects in the spec.
- **WhatsApp `_KNOWN_SYSTEMS` gains `"crm"`, parse-only** — `crm:lead:<uuid>` refs parse; nothing writes `wa_contacts.entity_ref` yet, and the `crm` context block stays `None`. Both pinned by test.
- **Spec/board truth pass (R4)** — the status header claimed nothing was deployed; migrations 144+145 have been applied on prod, `/crm` is live, and the backfill completed (737 orgs / 1,189 contacts / 1,516 leads / 551 deals / 1,909 notes, zero dirty, zero unmatched owners). "Nothing has ever written the Zoho tenant" is retained — still true.
- **D-CRM-9 recorded** (owner ruling): agent-originated and future auto-lead CRM writes enter the Zoho push queue exactly like human writes. No held-back tier; the safety boundary is the confirmation gate on write tools, not a fork in sync semantics.

## What does NOT land (audit NO-GO, doc-blocked)

The email-thread timeline join (B3 — must be caller-scoped or it discloses one member's mailbox to every `feature:crm` holder), the `CRM_AUTO_LEAD` build (B4 — no hook point named; **no settings field added**), and every CRM write/delete tool (B5 — needs a named mechanism, not a property). Recorded in §9 with B6/D-CRM-9 resolved.

## The defect this chain caught

The first commit shipped a **path traversal**: `record_id` went straight into the URL, and since HTTP clients resolve `../`, `get_record("deals", "../../admin/members")` became an authenticated `GET /admin/members` — escaping a boundary that the agent's instructions, its registry description and this PR's own AGENTS.md edit all assert. All 48 tests missed it, because every fixture passed `str(uuid4())`. It matters here specifically because `record_id` is model-filled and the model's context is counterparty-authored text — lead names, note bodies, the 1,909 notes just imported from Zoho.

Fixed structurally, at the layer that already validates `entity`: `_record_uuid` **canonicalises** (so braced, `urn:uuid:` and unhyphenated spellings all normalise to 36 separator-free chars), plus an AST fence over every `/crm` path expression. Mutation-tested — removing the guard turns 32 tests red; applying it to only one of the two tools still turns 15 red. Independent re-review ran 21 adversarial spellings, captured the wire URLs, and enumerated every path expression: could not defeat it. Verb allowlist was structural; now the path is too.

Also fixed along the way: a docstring in three agents that called a real settings attribute fictional (a "cleanup" would have 403'd every call), `sharing.shareable` flipped to `false` to match siblings (run permission folds on `agents:run:*`, never `feature:*`), and a Windows-only `read_text()` encoding bug that had been leaving the identity-fence test **red on main** on this machine.

## Verification

- `tests/unit/test_crm_agent.py` → **84 passed** (48 before the repair)

title: docs(WS-26d): close B3, B4, B5 and B7 - the three held-back slices become dispatchable
body:
The spec-audit held back three of WS-26d's items — not on engineering grounds, but because each stated a *property* where a dispatchable ticket needs a *mechanism*. "Caller-scoped", "confirmation-gated fail-closed" and "attaches to the email pipeline" are all satisfiable by building the wrong thing. This closes B3, B4, B5 and B7, so all three become dispatchable as separate tickets.

**Every anchor in this text was read off `origin/main` at `af3d3fc8`, not recalled** — the repo's standing rule after an earlier spec cited an inverted precedent. Three of my own assumptions were corrected in the process (the scope seam is at `core.py:424-435`, not `:421-427`; `schema.generated.sql` is stale for `email_messages`; and there is no `email_threads` table at all).

## B3 → WS-26d-email

The failure mode is specific: the CRM is **org-visible** to every `feature:crm` holder (D-CRM-3) while a mailbox is **owner-scoped**. An unscoped join publishes one member's inbox to the whole company. So the rule is now stated as non-negotiable — the join is **caller-scoped, never record-scoped**: two people opening the same lead may legitimately see different email, and a holder with no mailbox sees none.

It reuses the email app's own `_account_scope` (`routes/email/core.py:424-435`), **copied into `routes/crm/` rather than imported**. That's a real decision, not a shrug: cross-package imports are precedented (`notes/dispatch.py:280`), but `routes/crm` already declined exactly that once on D-CRM-4 grounds (`broker_handlers.py:61-64`). The rule for next time is written down — a third copy anywhere means promote it to a shared module.

Also settled: the unit is the **thread**, not the message (there is no `email_threads` table; `thread_id` is the grouping column and the conversation is already the app's unit of classification and snooze); inbound `from_address` only in v1; organizations do **not** join by domain (an `@fracktal.in` match would attach the entire mailbox to our own org record); and the join needs an address index that **does not exist today** — the two FTS GINs bury the address in a `to_tsvector` expression, usable only via `@@`.

## B4 → WS-26d-autolead

The hook is **`process_new_mail`** (`routes/email/scheduler_hooks.py:57`) — the one seam the background scheduler, the manual-sync route and the webhook all funnel through, with per-step try/except isolation a CRM step can copy so it can never break mail sync.

The tempting alternative is **recorded as rejected**, with reasons: the per-message rules loop already holds the parsed sender and the classification, but a classifier outage there `continue`s *without stamping the watermark* (so a hook double-fires on retry), and it only sees INBOX mail with `rules_processed_at IS NULL` (so history backfills never reach it).

"Unknown sender" mirrors `_maybe_block_cold` rather than being reinvented, and colleague suppression goes through `is_own_mail`/`sender_scope` — because a lead row for your own CFO, pushed into the live Zoho tenant under D-CRM-9, is exactly what this paragraph exists to prevent.

## B5 → WS-26d-write

The mechanism is **`request_confirmation`** (`acb_skills/ask_tools.py:345-348`), awaited at the top of each tool before the HTTP call — a plain async function, not a decorator, that blocks on a card and **fails closed with no delivery channel** (`:446-448`). No CRM write tool may pass the `non_interactive_default="approve"` opt-out.

`@_annotate_risk` is the risk half and is a **shared platform convention** (read by `permission_policy.py`), but **annotation is not enforcement** — the policy layer explicitly defers to the tool's own confirmation. Annotate *and* confirm.

The sharpest line, and the reason these were conflated: **confirmation and the Action Broker fail in opposite directions.** `request_confirmation` denies on error; `_broker_gate` proceeds on error, deliberately ("a broker-layer error never blocks a user-approved write"). They are not interchangeable. The PR includes the division-of-labour table: tool confirmation covers the native write, the broker covers the Zoho push, and for `CRM_AUTO_LEAD` — where no human is in the loop at all — the flag itself is the gate.

## B7

Each slice names its test file before its code exists: `test_crm_email_timeline.py`, `test_crm_auto_lead.py`, `test_crm_agent_write.py`, each to run *with* the existing CRM block rather than alone.

Docs-only. Board row, the `CRM_AUTO_LEAD` §6 gate (now naming its hook), and §10 updated in the same change (R4).

title: WS-27 + WS-28: the Projects app becomes usable, the People Center ships, and the Tasks app narrows to personal
body:
Follows PR #367 (WS-27a/b/d), which is merged. **12 commits across three workstreams.**

> ⚠️ **This PR grew past what it was opened for** — it started as WS-27e and now spans WS-27d/e/f/i, WS-28a/b, and a Tasks-app scope change. 69 files, +7,956/−1,494. That happened because each step was directed in sequence and the branch is pinned, not because it was planned as one change. **If you would rather review it in pieces, say so and I will split it** — that needs your go-ahead because it means pushing to branches other than the designated one.
>
> ⚠️ **CI has not run on any of this.** GitHub Actions stopped picking up jobs at ~18:11 today: pushes produce no check runs at all, and one stale run is still queued against a long-dead sha. It is not this diff — the same suites went green on `d4667a6` at 14:28 in ~90 seconds. Everything below was verified **locally**, and each commit records its own counts. Likely Actions minutes/billing or an org runner outage; worth a look at Settings → Billing.

---

## What this makes true

`/projects` was deployed and inert: the schema was applied and the feature granted, but the UI could **read and drag and never create**. A member could only work with rows a ClickUp import had put there, and "stop using ClickUp" was impossible on its face. It can now be used — and the People Center it depends on exists.

## 1 · Projects (WS-27d/e/f/i)

**One task store, not a mirror.** D-PM-6 was specced as a mirror between `pm_tasks` and `gtd_items`; revised, owner-directed, to one store. A task assigned to you *is* the row in your inbox — completing it there completes it for the project, same instant, same row. Private work is a personal project (`personal_owner`); the GTD overlay is **per-member**, so the person doing a task can say NEXT while the person who delegated it says WAITING. Dispositions are **derived, never written** when untriaged — storing one on first read would permanently empty the Weekly Review.

**"My work"** sits above the project tree in the same app. Four lanes not eight; empty work lanes still render ("you have triaged nothing into today" is a real state); undated tasks sort *below* dated ones; untriaged is counted in the header.

**Authoring**: new department, subproject (from the node — the parent is already on screen), task, subtask, and **assignees as chips where an agent and a person share one field**. That is where D-PM-4 stops being a schema note, and it is the precondition for dispatch being reachable.

**Automation (WS-27f)** — both halves of `workflows_app.md` §13. A `pm_task` node lets the one engine act on a task, writing through a transport-free *service* so an automation's edit is indistinguishable in validation from a human PATCH. Status is set by lane **name**, never by `status_id` — a graph carrying one project's UUID could only ever automate that project. Assignment to `agent:<name>` starts a real run, from an event **sink** so a broken agent cannot fail the act of assigning somebody a task.

**Attachments (WS-27i)** — one file store: `gtd_attachments` reused, upload rules imported. `pm_task_attachments` is a thin join that carries the **access** decision, so a file is readable by whoever can see the task rather than only its uploader. There is deliberately **no attach-by-id endpoint**: naming an arbitrary attachment id would let a caller attach somebody else's private capture to their own task and read it back.

## 2 · People Center (WS-28a/b)

**WS-28a** fixes `gtd_people`'s key shape: migration 49 made `name` UNIQUE and left `email` unconstrained, which is backwards for a directory that joins on email. Its unnamed consequence — the HR importer upserts `ON CONFLICT (name)` and would have broken — is handled with a `source_key`. **Neither new constraint can block a deploy**: a duplicate address is quarantined into `email_conflict` rather than failing `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`, and the status CHECK is `NOT VALID` then validated in a guarded block.

**WS-28b** ships `/people` — directory, person page, four panels. Its own feature slug, but the HR **projection is imported** from `tasks.core` and a test asserts the function's *identity*. Three filters drop without `admin:members:read` so search cannot become an oracle for the hidden field, and the response says `hr_visible` so the UI shows "restricted" rather than a blank strip that reads as "nobody filled it in". Load is **computed** from open assigned tasks and carries `unestimated`, because a bar built from the estimate sum alone shows someone holding thirty un-estimated tasks as completely free.

## 3 · Tasks app narrows to personal

Owner-directed. The Projects and People views are removed — the first was literally the ClickUp Space → Folder → List tree, the second the HR roster. `GtdProject` survives as an association; what went is the browsing surface.

`loadPeople()` had exactly **one** caller: opening the People view. Deleting it naively would have left the delegate picker offering nobody — a broken picker that reads as a company with no people. Both callers now load the roster where they need it.

## 4 · Plans, not code

`workflows_app.md` §13 — the Paca engine backlog, U1–U8, each with a done-when. `project_management_app.md` §11 — the **ClickUp-parity gap, measured against the built tree**, ten items ordered by what stops you using this on a Monday. One finding worth surfacing: **bulk edit gates the cutover**, because an import nobody can re-triage in bulk is one somebody abandons halfway, leaving two live systems.

---

## Three bugs caught before shipping

- The projects **BFF proxy re-serialised every POST as JSON** — a multipart upload would have reached the gateway with **no file at all, while still answering 201**.
- **`TaskPanel` read the selected project's statuses**, wrong for a task opened from My work, offering transitions to lanes that do not exist on that task's project.
- **`templating.resolve_value` keeps an unresolvable `{{ref}}` as-is at run time by design**, and `{{trigger.missing}}` passes `validate_graph` because its *root* is legal. Fixed for the new node; every other node type has the same exposure, recorded as its own ticket rather than widened here.

## Verification (local)

- **435 Python cases** at the widest run; **377 vitest** (was 315); `tsc --noEmit` clean; ruff clean on every new file; **xenon passes CI's actual gate**.
- **~60 mutants measured red and reverted byte-identical.** Four survived first time and **every one exposed a weak assertion rather than a weak guard** — a balanced fixture, a check watching for a diff when `updated_at` was the thing that moved, a substring passing on a file's own explanatory prose, and a traversal test checking a path that was already safe by construction.

## What this does NOT do

- **Does not run either ClickUp import endpoint.** Both are built and tested; neither has ever been run. Production execution is a registered owner gate.
- **Does not apply any migration.** 146–150 are unapplied.
- **Does not touch `gtd_items`.** WS-27h owns that retirement.
- **Leaves one capability unreachable, on the record:** creating/editing a person and uploading a résumé. `PersonEditor` was its only UI. The API and store wrapper are untouched — nothing was deleted — but until the People Center grows the write half an admin cannot do it from the product. Filed as **WS-28b-write**.

title: fix(WS-26b): the Deals cursor could never advance, so the pull never converged
body:
**Found by watching the first live sync cycles**, minutes after `CRM_ZOHO_SYNC` was enabled on prod. Every module converged to pulling 1–2 changed records per cycle. `Deals` pulled all 551, every cycle, and would have done so forever.

## Root cause

Zoho returns **no `Modified_Time` for any module on this tenant**. Leads, Accounts, Contacts and Notes survive on `modified_time()`'s `Created_Time` fallback. `Deals` has neither — 0 of 551 parse, and naming the fields in `fields=` returns them empty, so it is a per-module field permission on the tenant, not our query.

That left `advance_cursor` unable to distinguish two very different situations, because both produce `newest_applied is None`:

- nothing landed (must stand still, or a failed record is never offered again), and
- **everything landed, but Zoho gave us no timestamp to cursor on**.

It correctly chose the conservative reading, so the `Deals` watermark stayed NULL, `If-Modified-Since` stayed empty, and the pull never converged — ~79k redundant record-applies a day against the API and the DB.

## The fix

`advance_cursor` now takes the applied count. Everything applied + zero failures + no readable timestamp → adopt the cycle's start. The safety argument is the existing "nothing fetched" branch's, verbatim: every record Zoho returned for this window applied cleanly, so everything up to the cycle's start *is* reconciled — the missing timestamps are Zoho's, not evidence of unfinished work. **Any failure still stands still**, because a failure we cannot place in time must be re-read.

## What is deliberately NOT fixed

**LWW for deals stays one-sided.** With no Zoho timestamp, `_zoho_changed_since_agreement` reads "changed" and `_later` reads "not later", so a dirty deal always resolves **native-wins**. That is the recoverable direction the helper's own docstring argues for — the other silently discards a colleague's typing. `Last_Activity_Time` and `Stage_Modified_Time` *are* returned for deals, but neither means "last modified", and substituting a semantically-wrong field would flip conflicts toward the unrecoverable side. Documented in spec §7.1 rather than papered over.

## Verification

- `tests/unit/test_crm_zoho_sync.py` → **95 passed** (was 89); full CRM suite → **478 passed**; ruff clean.
- **Mutation-tested behaviourally**, not just by signature: removing only the new branch (leaving the parameter in place) turns exactly the two cases that describe the fix red, while the three guard cases — failure present, zero applied — pass either way, which is what they are for.
- The five parametrised cases cover both the fix and its safety boundary, plus a rewind guard: `fallback` is normally later than the previous watermark, but clock skew must never drag a cursor backwards over a reconciled window.
