title: Projects: beyond-parity queue WS-27u–z + Tasks↔Projects UI continuity
body:
Builds the entire beyond-parity queue minted from the Plane research (`specs/project_management_app.md` §9.1) plus the owner-directed UI-continuity pass between the Tasks and Projects apps. Six tickets, built by six parallel agents in isolated worktrees and integrated in two waves. ⚠️ All interaction designs are re-derived in this repo's idiom — nothing is copied from AGPL-licensed Plane (see the AGPL wall in `specs/plane_pm_research_2026-08.md`).

## What's in here

**WS-27u — intake/triage** (migration **164**)
- `pm_intake` wrapper table (status pending/accepted/declined/duplicate/snoozed, provenance permanent) + `triage` status category.
- ONE exclusion predicate in `core.py` beside the visibility clause: triage-parked tasks appear on no board/list/calendar/timeline/search surface unless `include_triage` is passed; the parameter-coverage structural test now enforces it can't be dropped per-surface.
- `POST /projects/intake` (task+wrapper in one transaction) and the four rulings; accept flips status in place, decline/duplicate archive with provenance, snooze reappears past `snoozed_until`. All rulings write `pm_activities`. TriageRail UI with lane/duplicate/date pickers.

**WS-27v — watchers & mentions** (migration **165**)
- `pm_task_watchers` (casefolded, agents fenced; seeds task authors so the old audience survives the switch).
- Auto-subscribe on comment/edit/assign/mention (delivered mentions only), watch/unwatch endpoints, audience = watchers ∪ assignees minus actor, still gated by `resolve_visibility_for`.
- Mention diffing: editing notifies only newly-added mentions (proven by an edit-twice test). Unread endpoint returns `{total, mentions}`; the bell renders mentions distinctly.

**WS-27w — read-path/history hardening** (no migration)
- Archive endpoints did not exist (`archived_at` had no writer) — added `POST …/archive` + `/unarchive` with the 422 guard naming the category.
- `record_field_change` single door: FK-valued history carries `{field, old_id, new_id, old_label, new_label}`, enforced by an AST structural test over call sites.
- Same-actor consecutive description/comment edits coalesce. Semantic status sort (category rank, then lane position) and a structurally-asserted `(created_at, id)` tiebreaker on every `TASK_SORTS` entry.
- `GET /projects/search?exclude_relatives_of=` filters self/ancestors/descendants/already-related so pickers can't offer what writes will 422. Human task refs on cards/panel with copy-deep-link.

**WS-27x — spreadsheet layout + shown-fields contract**
- Per-view `shown_fields` joins the saved-view config (client round-trip + server `normalise_view_config`, old views stay byte-identical). Chip rendering on every surface gates on it.
- `TableView`: columns = shown fields, inline cell editors over the existing PATCH/PUT paths, header sorts verified against `TASK_SORTS` by a cross-language test, indented sub-task expansion, bottom quick-add rows, arrow-key cell cursor (Enter edits, Esc cancels).

**WS-27y — board/list interaction upgrades**
- Swimlanes (second grouping axis), per-lane collapse + show-empty persisted with the view (server preserves the keys — gap found and closed during integration).

title: docs(D28): the development doctrine - engineering_practice.md + R6/R7/R8
body:
docs(D28): the development doctrine — specs/engineering_practice.md, and R6/R7/R8 that bind it

Owner-requested: write down how we build now that the product is being sold with
live customers and most code is agent-authored.

Two premises, both argued from measured incidents in this repo rather than from
general advice:

  (i) Our failures are DELIVERY AND INTEGRATION failures, not coding failures.
      §0.1 tabulates seven from one fortnight — three migration-number
      collisions, two green-alone/red-together PR pairs, four deploys that
      reported success while shipping nothing, a statement that could not run
      sitting in the hand-applied production promotion script, a migration that
      broke three write routes predating it, and five SQL bugs invisible to
      hermetic fakes. Not one of them is a unit-test gap. Spend the effort on the
      seams between changes.

  (ii) A rule binds an agent only when a test refuses to break it. R5 already
      said this; R7 now generalises it.

Binding (work_plan.md §1, where every dispatch reads them):

  R6  expand/contract migrations. The deploy applies migrations BEFORE
      restarting services, so old code always meets new schema for a window —
      nullable-with-default, never rename in place, constraints NOT VALID then
      validated, tightening always a later migration. Plus the honest corollary:
      forward-only ladder and no blue/green means we CANNOT roll back, only roll
      forward or restore.
  R7  name the fence or label the rule advisory; prefer structural fences over
      example tests, because those are what defend against future agents.
  R8  SQL verified against a real Postgres; verified-red-first for every fence
      and bug fix; mutation testing for money, auth, tenancy, outward writes.

Doctrine, not enforced: deploy != release with a ring order (us -> one friendly
customer -> all; the silo phase makes rings free, and D25.2 already fixed per-org
flags as the only version-skew mechanism); seam-based work partition with short
branches and a 3-4 in-flight cap — long branches are the single root cause behind
the renumber trap, the cross-PR fences AND the duplicated tenancy design; the
verifier-is-not-the-implementer and adversarial-reviewer rules; and a definition
of done in which delivery is verified by evidence, never by a green job.

§8 names five things to close before customer #1, each pointed at an existing
board row rather than minting new ones: SHA-in-/health (WS-25), off-box backup
(BO-23, owner-deferred and now flagged for revisit), migration rehearsal against
a prod-shaped restore (WS-5, proposed), RLS promotion (MT-1b), lifecycle-sweep
tenant binding (MT-1d).

§9 states what the document is NOT: it binds new and changed work only, and is
explicitly not a licence to refactor the existing tree into conformance.

Registered in INDEX.md under CONTRACTS & DOCTRINE and in project-docs/AGENTS.md;
INDEX navigation now sends agents to §1's rules before §2's board.

title: docs(D28 fix): silo is placement, not architecture - multi-tenant from customer #1
body:
docs(D28 fix): "silo" is placement, not architecture — we are multi-tenant from customer #1

The doctrine's ring paragraph said "during the silo phase (customers 1-5)"
without qualifying it, which reads as though multi-tenancy is deferred until the
pooled cutover. It is not. §5.1 condition 2 requires every silo to run the pooled
schema with organization_id populated and RLS enabled from day one — a silo is a
pooled deployment with N=1, and cutover is a data move rather than a migration.
Skipping that is precisely what turns the bridge into a rewrite. D15 demoted the
deployment from "the tenant boundary" to "a placement, a priced tier", and R5
binds every PR regardless of customer count. There is no phase in which
single-tenant code is acceptable; what changes at the 8-12 cutover is only N.

Consequence made explicit in §8: promoting the RLS set is a HARD GATE for
customer #1, not a nice-to-have — "the policies are still un-promoted" and "we
have a paying customer" cannot both be true.

Caught by the owner reading the doctrine, which is the review the doc wanted.

title: feat(D29): track the agent harness - cloud instances inherit plan-guard and the review loop
body:
feat(D29): track the agent harness — a cloud instance now inherits plan-guard and the review loop

`.claude/` was a blanket gitignore. Every checkout that was not the owner's
laptop — a cloud Claude instance, a fresh clone, a headless run, an agent's own
worktree — therefore ran with NO plan-guard, i.e. no enforcement of work_plan.md
§6's owner gates at all, plus none of the supervisor-worker agent definitions and
no /next-ticket. The control that refuses VPS reach, deploys, commits on main and
.env edits was travelling by accident, and only to one machine.

Tracked (doctrine in executable form, scanned — no secrets):
  .claude/AGENTS.md
  .claude/agents/{spec-auditor,ws-implementer,ws-verifier,diff-reviewer}.md
  .claude/commands/next-ticket.md
  .claude/hooks/{plan-guard.mjs,plan-guard.test.mjs,rtk-bash.sh}
  .claude/settings.json

Still ignored (local or derived), each with its reason written into .gitignore:
  settings.local.json   per-machine permissions, may name local paths
  worktrees/            ephemeral full checkouts made by parallel agents
  scheduled_tasks.lock  runtime state
  skill-observations/   local observation logs
  skills/               third-party skill bundles (impeccable v3.9.1) — tooling a
                        developer installs, not project doctrine

Derived indexes stay ignored and get REBUILT: the CodeGraph symbol index would be
large, churn on every commit and conflict on every merge. Its config (.mcp.json,
codegraph.json) was already tracked, so a fresh environment installs the tool and
builds its own index. The general rule, now written down: anything derivable from
source is rebuilt on the new machine; only sources of truth are tracked.

The fence (R7 — a rule names its enforcing test): `node
.claude/hooks/plan-guard.test.mjs` runs BLOCKING in pr-check's lint job, 21 cases.
Break the guard and CI goes red, instead of the guard silently permitting
everything on a machine nobody is watching.

Recorded as D29 in work_plan.md §3 and engineering_practice.md §5.1.

title: feat(D30): CLAUDE.md - the always-loaded briefing so cloud instances never start blind
body:
feat(D30): CLAUDE.md — the always-loaded briefing, so a cloud instance never starts blind

Claude Code auto-loads CLAUDE.md into EVERY session, including cloud and headless
ones. This repo had none, and the 16 KB root AGENTS.md is not guaranteed to be in
context at session start — measured this session: it was not. So an instance that
was not this laptop began with no knowledge of the architecture, the board, the
owner gates or the method, and would discover them only by accident.

CLAUDE.md is a ROUTER plus the minimum that must be known before the first tool
call. It duplicates nothing; every claim points at its owner:

  §1 Where truth lives, in reading order — INDEX (what is ACTIVE) → work_plan §1
     (rules R1-R8) → §2 (the board, the only current-state authority) → §6 (owner
     gates to refuse by name) → §3 (decisions D1-D30) → engineering_practice
     (how we build) → the owning spec.
  §2 The architecture in one screen — Centers are projections; cross-cutting apps
     have two access paths and ONE permission model; modules are billing atoms
     while Center packages are what customers buy; tenancy is a ROW and we are
     multi-tenant from customer #1; visibility is private → Center → org.
  §3 The non-negotiables — never commit on main, refuse owner-gated work by name,
     R5 tenant-ready, R6 expand/contract, R7 name the fence, R8 real database for
     SQL, R1 migration numbers at build time, verify delivery by evidence.
  §4 How development proceeds — feature by feature, app by app, one narrowed
     slice: audit → implement → verify → review → PR → stop before merge; the
     verifier is never the implementer; the reviewer hunts for the failing case;
     re-verify anchors; EXTEND seams, never fork them; short branches.
  §5 What not to do — re-litigate decisions, refactor the tree to conform, invent
     a second way to do an existing thing, mark done from the write-up.
  §6 Environment traps that waste the most time.

One correction made while writing it, because an always-loaded file must not
carry a false claim: the board's "never run tests/unit as a directory" warnings
are narrower than they sound. Measured today, a directory run with a -k filter
that deselects the memory and calendar suites completes fine — what hangs is
running those tests, not collection. Stated that way rather than as an absolute I
had just contradicted a dozen times.

Standing rule recorded with D30: CLAUDE.md stays a router. Anything that grows
into content belongs in an owning spec with a pointer here — a briefing nobody
finishes reading is a briefing nobody follows.

title: WS-29 H2: central tenant binding + routes/projects converted to tenant_session()
body:
Starts H2 — the long pole of the multi-tenancy workstream (`saas_multitenancy_handover.md`) — with the runbook's "do this first" step and its largest single package slice. Includes today's `main` merged in (D28–D30 harness + #409 tenancy alignment); no conflicts.

## The central binding (the prerequisite for every conversion)

- `_with_resolved_access` (acb_auth/deps.py) now calls `bind_tenant(organization_id)` the moment identity resolves — from the `app_user` row, never a header/query/body (R11). One place, so the 500+ call sites need no tenant argument.
- New `TenantScopeMiddleware` in the gateway (pure ASGI): opens a fresh empty tenant scope per HTTP request, releases it after the response — a binding can never leak between requests on any server task model. `clear_tenant()` added to `acb_common.db` for it.
- `tests/unit/test_tenant_request_binding.py` (new, 6 tests): binds on resolution, tenant comes from identity not caller-controlled headers, unresolved identity binds nothing, `system:internal` binds nothing (jobs bind explicitly — H4), no leak across sequential same-task requests, non-http passthrough.

## The Projects slice (84 of the ~580 sites)

- Every request handler in `routes/projects` (21 files) is now `async with _tenant_session() as db:`. The per-package alias is asserted to **be** `acb_common.db.tenant_session` (seam-identity test extended), so there's exactly one GUC discipline.
- Explicit mid-flow `db.commit()` calls removed — the wrapper commits on clean exit, and a mid-block commit would end the transaction and silently drop the `SET LOCAL` scope for everything after it. (Recon first proved no handler queries after its final commit, so the rewrite is behavior-preserving.)
- **One named exemption:** `agent_dispatch.py` (2 sites) is an event consumer, and the runbook forbids jobs inheriting an ambient tenant — it stays on `get_db()` with a loud H4 marker until H4 threads an explicit tenant through the event payload.
- **Ratchets** (test_db_engine_seam.py): `routes/projects` pinned at zero unconverted sites; the 494 sites elsewhere frozen as a baseline that only ratchets down, with a bank-your-progress guard so headroom can't become new-debt budget.

## ⚠️ Live run found `tenant_session()` itself broken (shipped in #404)

The seam issued `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = :tenant` — a Postgres **syntax error** through the extended protocol (`SET` cannot take a bind parameter). Every hermetic test was green because fakes don't parse SQL; `test_tenant_session.py` even pinned the broken spelling. The first converted handler against real Postgres refused it — had this survived to H3, every request would have 500'd at its first query.

Fixed to `SELECT set_config('app.tenant_id', :tenant, true)` — identical transaction-local semantics (`is_local = true` IS `SET LOCAL`), parameterizable. The pin test now enforces the working form and refuses both the literal and an `is_local = false` variant. Both tenancy specs annotated at their illustrative snippets; the handover's new H2 box tells the remaining packages' converters to run at least one live smoke each.

## Verification

- Backend: `uv run python -m pytest tests/unit/` → **5798 passed** (49 skipped are the documented needs-live-Postgres checks); ruff CI gate clean.
- Frontend (untouched by this change, run for the merge): `npx vitest run` → **1278 passed**; `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Live scratch Postgres 16** (migrations applied through 166): `test_tenant_session.py` green against the real engine, plus an end-to-end smoke — unbound `tenant_session()` raises `TenantUnbound`; real converted handlers (`create_node`, `create_task`, `list_tasks`) write and read under the bound GUC; `current_setting('app.tenant_id')` observed inside the wrapper's transaction; handler-written rows stamped with the bound `organization_id`.
- Test seams updated coherently: `_projects_fakes.bind_db` patches the package's `_tenant_session` with a commit-on-clean-exit context manager (one-transaction contracts stay observable as `committed == 1`); read-path tests that used `committed == 0` as a "writes nothing" proxy now assert on statements/rows, since the wrapper commits read transactions too — exactly as real Postgres does.

## Not in this PR

- The remaining 494 `get_db()` sites (email, whatsapp, crm, tasks, notes, workflows…) — next H2 slices, package-by-package per the handover's new conversion notes.
- H3 (applying the generated RLS policies) — gated on all of H2, per the runbook's cliff warning.
- `agent_dispatch`'s explicit-tenant conversion — H4.

title: WS-29 H2 (waves 1+2): nine gateway packages converted to tenant_session — 111 classified sites remain
body:
Completes the request-handler half of H2 (`saas_multitenancy_handover.md`), on top of #416's central binding + Projects slice. Seven parallel slice-agents across two waves, integrated with recomputed ratchets, followed by an adversarial diff review (D29 loop) whose two confirmed findings are fixed in the final commit.

## Converted (this PR)

| Package | Converted | Left (classified) |
|---|---|---|
| routes/email | 98 | 27 — webhook, OAuth callback, scheduler hooks, BackgroundTask jobs |
| routes/notes | 61 | 33 — transcription pipeline, bot poller, copilot tasks, one bot-token route |
| routes/tasks | 73 | 6 — broker handler, sync scheduler, nightly rollover sweep |
| routes/whatsapp | 38 | 14 — Meta webhook, bridge-secret pushes, post-sync hooks, enrichment loop |
| routes/workflows | 26 | 17 — cron loop, engine, dual-use run lifecycle, hook-token route |
| routes/apps | 32 | 6 — orchestrator-invoked `execute_app_action` path, broker publish-review, audit helper |
| routes/crm | 28 | 3 — auto-lead job, Zoho sync engine, broker handler |
| routes/people | 4 | 0 |
| routes/admin | 23 | 0 |

`H2_BASELINE_ELSEWHERE` banked stepwise **494 → 111**. Every remaining site carries an in-place `# H4:` (background consumer) or `# H4/H6:` (service-identity route) marker naming its tenant-derivation source — the classification IS the deliverable for H4/H6. Ratchets: zero-remainder packages pinned by the parametrized `test_converted_packages_stay_converted` (+ `H2_EXEMPT_FILES` with reasons); whatsapp/apps pinned at exact per-file counts; the elsewhere baseline only ratchets down with a bank-your-progress guard.

## The adversarial review's two catches (fixed here, both invisible to every hermetic suite)

1. **Auto-lead would have died today**: the background mail path (`process_new_mail` → `_create_lead`) calls the now-converted `create_record` with no ambient tenant → `TenantUnbound` on every message → `_consider` counts it failed → the watermark never advances. Fixed the H4 way, early: the mailbox owner's organization is resolved from their `app_user` row and bound explicitly around the call. A new AST ratchet (`test_exempt_files_do_not_reach_converted_sessions_unreviewed`) now catches this whole class mechanically — the exemption markers are file-scoped but the call graph is not, so any exempt file calling a `tenant_session`-opening function needs a reviewed edge in `H2_EXEMPT_CALL_EDGES`.
2. **A mid-block commit inside three email handlers**: `_store_ai_draft(db, …)` defaulted `commit=True` under the tenant wrapper — ending the transaction and dropping the GUC for everything after it (partial commits today; zero-row tails under RLS phase 4). Now `commit=False` at the one call site whose callers all hold wrapper sessions.

## Conversion discipline (uniform across slices)

Every site classified BEFORE converting: user-identity request handler (convert — the central binding from #416 has the tenant) vs. service-identity route (`system:internal` binds nothing — leave) vs. background consumer (ambient inheritance forbidden by the runbook — leave). Explicit `db.commit()` calls removed (the wrapper commits on clean exit; mid-block commits drop the GUC), with honest two-block restructures where local-commit-before-provider-sync ordering matters (tasks, email helpers, apps publish). Hermetic fakes re-pointed to `asynccontextmanager` seams with commit-on-clean-exit; `committed == 0` "writes nothing" proxies replaced by statement/row assertions.

## Verification

- Full unit suite on the final tree: **5807 passed** (49 skips are the documented needs-live-Postgres checks); ruff CI gate clean.
- **Live-Postgres smokes (R8), per wave, on the merged tree**: one converted read per package under a bound GUC on a migrated scratch cluster (email/whatsapp/tasks wave 1; crm/people/admin/workflows/apps wave 2); notes proven on its slice's own full cluster (create/list/patch meeting + note read); the tasks slice additionally demonstrated **FORCE-RLS org-A/org-B row isolation** with a non-superuser role; unbound sessions raise `TenantUnbound` everywhere.
- The P0 finding was runtime-reproduced (no DB needed) before fixing, and the fixed path is covered hermetically (fakes now seed/answer the owner-org lookup).

## Not in this PR

- H4: explicit tenants for the 111 marked sites (jobs, consumers, service-identity routes) — the markers name each site's tenant source.
- H5 (Redis prefix conversion), H6 (identity cutover), H3 (applying the generated RLS policies — gated on H2+H4 per the runbook's cliff warning).

title: WS-27: one design language for /projects and /tasks, the themed categorical ramp, the house shell, and the last two Projects tenancy residues
body:
Driven by two owner directives:

> *"the appearance of the Kanban board and its lists, color schemes, task cards… Please fix the UI for the shared components."*
> *"I want the UI for the projects to match the theming configuration used in the Command Center… ensuring future development considers it."*

Four slices: **aa** (tenancy residues), **ad** (shared visual language), **af** (themed categorical ramp), **ag** (house shell + mobile). `ab`/`ac` were deferred behind the UI work by owner priority.

---

## ⚠️ Read before merging — this deploys, and it applies four migrations

`deploy.yml` triggers on push to `main`, and the deploy auto-applies migrations before restarting services. Merging this therefore applies **164, 165, 166** (already outstanding on the box) **and 167** (new here) to production, in one go. Per R6 there is no rollback — only roll forward or restore.

167 is data-only (two narrow `UPDATE`s, no schema change, idempotent by construction). 164–166 are additive schema from the previous wave. Worth a glance at `schema_migrations` first to confirm what the box actually has.

---

## What a user sees

**The Projects board was grey because it was throwing away colour it already had.** `pm_task_statuses.color` has been stored since migration 146, carried to the frontend as `StatusRow.color` — and rendered nowhere. Every column drew `bg-muted` while the Tasks board next door was colour-coded per stage.

There were three colour vocabularies that never met: a real accent system in `tasks/lib/stageColors.ts`, a tag-only `chipClass` in `projects/lib/tags.ts`, and the stored column nothing drew.

Now there is one — `src/lib/statusAccent.ts` — resolving by precedence: **stored colour → category → name keyword → position**. Projects knows what a lane *means* (`STATUS_CATEGORIES`); Tasks can only read what it is *called*. Both routes now land on the same hue.

Also shipped: `TaskCardShell` and `StatusChip` consumed by both apps, the drop-gap reorder (Projects previously appended on drop, so dragging a card two rows up sent it to the bottom), one selection grammar, and the shared cursor on the Tasks flat lists — a third of that app's surfaces where the arrow keys did nothing.

**`/projects` had no mobile UI at all.** It imported neither `useViewMode` nor `useMobileDrawer` and had no `AppShell` branch, so a phone got a fixed 256px sidebar beside the canvas plus a third column when a task opened. It now has the single-pane branch, the tree in the drawer, a bottom-nav tab set, the slim `h-10` house bar over a collapsible rail, and the seven-way header split into three rows. The error strip also stopped rendering failures as calm `bg-muted`.

**The theming engine now covers categorical hues.** `--cat-1 … --cat-8` in all four manifests in both modes (64 values), bridged to Tailwind, with slots chosen by hashing an item's *name* rather than its array position. `/tasks` carried 142 raw Tailwind palette classes that ignored the theme entirely; `/projects` carried zero.

## The defect caught in review

The shared vocabulary landed, and the boards still would not have matched. `CATEGORY_HUES` had been written to mirror the *seeded* colours rather than to agree with Tasks:

| lane | /projects | /tasks |
|---|---|---|
| Backlog | gray | gray ✅ |
| To do | **blue** | **gray** ❌ |
| In progress | **amber** | **blue** ❌ |
| Done | green | green ✅ |

Two of four default lanes still divergent — the original problem one layer down. Fixed by making the category map follow the keyword semantics and moving the seed to match, since a stored colour *outranks* a derived one and a disagreeing seed silently overrides the shared vocabulary on every uncustomised project.

**And the seed only governs new projects**, so migration 167 repaints existing ones — matching the full pre-change tuple (name **and** category **and** old colour), so a renamed lane or an owner-chosen colour is skipped. Verified against a real database, applied twice: two repainted, two correctly skipped, second run a no-op.

## Tenancy (closes the last Projects blocker on RLS)

`run_lifecycle_sweep` swept **every tenant's** projects with no predicate on a scheduled path, and `agent_dispatch` was the H2 ratchet's one Projects exemption. Both closed: the sweep takes a required `organization_id` and refuses without one, resolved from a stored fact (`workflows.owner_email` → `app_user`, never request input); dispatch carries the task's own `organization_id` on the `pm.task.assigned` payload. Proven on live Postgres — 23 checks including a two-org isolation case where org A's sweep leaves org B's stale tasks untouched, with each guard mutation-measured red. `routes/projects` is now at **zero** unbound sites and the exemption is gone.

## Fences

- `conformance.test.ts` gained a **fifth rule** — raw Tailwind palette classes, per-file baselines that only go down. `bg-sky-500/10` passed every previous regex (a named class, not a bracket class), which is how ~950 accumulated tree-wide.
- `test_category_and_keyword_agree` — every category and a name a person would type for it resolve to one hue.
- `test_seed_status_colours_match_the_shared_vocabulary` — reads `CATEGORY_HUES` out of the TypeScript rather than mirroring it, because a mirror goes stale and then lies.
- Four fences on 167: whole-tuple matching, idempotency by construction, targets agreeing with the vocabulary, and the companion direction.

## Verification

`tsc` clean · **1586 tests / 73 files** (from 1278) · theme suite **353** (from 208) · production `next build` compiles and prerenders all 39 pages · backend `253 passed` on the touched suites, full directory `5720 passed` with the two recorded hazard suites deselected.

## Owed, and not claimed

**The visual check did not happen.** Playwright cannot install in the build environment, so neither the phone-viewport pass nor the Fluent → Material → Graphite sweep was performed. Compensations: production build, icon names verified against the theme registry, hand-traced z-order, and the ramp's shipped values rendered to PNGs and inspected — including under a simulated deuteranopia transform, which found that **eight qualitative hues collapse to about four under dichromacy**. No eight-hue palette survives that, so every use pairs the hue with its label and the limit is written into the code. None of it substitutes for looking at the running app.

This matters more than usual because **there is no structural or layout test anywhere in this tree** — nothing asserts panel counts, shell adoption, mobile branches, or that two apps draw a card the same way.

**One contradiction left for the owner rather than settled by coin-flip:** `ad` standardised the *shared* card title on `text-[13px]`, choosing Tasks' size as the common one; `af` then established the house scale and removed every other off-grid size. The survivor now sits in a component both apps render, so changing it repaints Projects too.

**Known and deliberate:** `backlog` and `todo` share a muted hue, so a board with both draws two grey lanes. That is what `/tasks` does today and matching it was the ask; `status.color` is the lever, and it finally works.

title: WS-27 S1–S4: Tasks becomes a real slice of Projects — one card, one detail surface, one selection grammar; plus the one-store decision and the fences that found three latent defects
body:
Driven by the owner's reframing:

> *"Technically, the Tasks app is only a slice of the Projects app… do a comprehensive review of the Tasks app to ensure there's at least parity in terms of the UI/UX."*

Ruling applied throughout: **Projects is canonical, Tasks conforms** — except where Tasks is demonstrably better, which S4 handles in the other direction.

**No migrations, no backend changes.** Frontend, specs and tests only. (167 shipped in #418 and is already applied.)

---

## The three divergences the owner named, from looking at the deployed app

**Cards.** Tasks' board adopts Projects' column shape, surface and gutter. The shared shell's `completed` and `atCursor` props are finally passed by their Tasks caller — done tasks were never dimmed or struck through, because the shell supported it and nobody wired it. The private `AvatarStack` copy is deleted for the shared one. Titles clamp in `TaskCardShell` so both apps move together rather than forking.

**Detail surface.** `/tasks` docks a `w-[380px]` pane instead of opening a pop-up. This was a bug against an existing rule, not a design difference: `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` already specifies a side panel, and Tasks was the only overlay in the product (email uses a reading pane, notes a route, projects an aside). The modal survives as the phone branch and as an explicit maximise, because Tasks' detail is genuinely denser than Projects' and 380px cannot give it the `max-w-3xl` reading width. Two pieces of dead code — a side-panel entry imported nowhere and a maximise button that could never render — came back to life rather than being deleted.

**Selection.** The checkbox is permanent and sits in its own gutter beside the row. `selectMode` is now a *derived* mirror of "something is selected" and gates only the bulk bar. The bar moved to the top on Projects' chrome and primitives; select-all exists.

The previous slice had deliberately kept Tasks' modal select-mode, reasoning a permanent checkbox would steal the drag-grip gutter. That reason did not survive: Projects puts its checkbox *outside* the card as a sibling with `stopPropagation`, so there are two targets and the card surface stays the open affordance. Tasks put it *inside*, overlapping the grip — it created the collision and then documented it as a constraint. The comment now says what is true.

**And the other direction (S4)** — three findings where Projects carried the defect: the `bg-accent` active token (house norm is `bg-primary/10 text-primary`), a fourth bespoke task row in `MyWork` that bypassed the shared card vocabulary entirely, and no distinct filtered-empty state (Projects conflated *no data* with *filtered to nothing* and asked the user to guess).

## The architecture decision

Owner question: one database with per-user separation, or two apps? **One store**, and the mechanism was already built and unused — `pm_projects.personal_owner` (a personal project, granted to one email) plus the per-member `pm_task_personal` overlay. "Local" is a *visibility* property, not a storage location.

The argument that settles it is already in migration 147's header: a single `disposition` column on a shared task cannot express delegation — one person doing it, another waiting on it — and two separate stores cannot either, because the task would exist twice and the copies disagree the moment either moves.

**§7.5.1 is new and is the substance here.** WS-27h said the move is "a copy rather than a translation." True of the seven overlay columns; false of the rest. `gtd_items` carries 31 columns plus `gtd_waiting`, and fifteen have no `pm_tasks` home — the founder priority matrix, all of timeboxing, `deep_work`, the email-capture badge, and the entire Waiting-For view. Executed on that sentence the migration would have been a **feature deletion reporting success**. Every column now has a named destination, decided by one question: *if Ana and Ben are both on this task, can their answers legitimately differ?* Two sequencing constraints recorded — the provider columns cannot drop before WS-27g, and `horizon_id` belongs to WS-21, which is DO-NOT-DISPATCH.

## Three latent defects the fences found — none of which was the ticket

**A rule I wrote in the previous PR was wrong.** `rounded-xl` is not a fixed 12px: `--radius-xl: var(--radius)`, identical to `rounded-lg`, and the whole named scale is derived. Acting on my claim would have baselined ~274 correctly-themed occurrences across ~70 files as debt — a fence against a non-violation, worse than no fence. Corrected in `AGENTS.md` with the correction visible, and `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` spelled out so the misreading cannot recur.

**Two source files contained literal NUL bytes.** ripgrep stops at the first one — so every grep-based fence in this repo, and every `grep` a human or agent ran, silently saw only the first third of `projects/TaskBoard.tsx`, and stayed silent even when the file was named explicitly. The fences passed because they never looked. `sourceHygiene.test.ts` now fails on any NUL under `src/`; it found a second offender on its first run and a third *in its own docstring*, where the warning had pasted the very byte it warns about.

**Local `main` was ~50 commits stale**, so three agents cut branches backwards; one noticed only because half the WS-27 files vanished. Reset.

Also: `sharedTaskUi`'s fence caught a genuine cross-slice gap — S4 built on the shared shell without declaring `atCursor`, which is indistinguishable from forgetting it. Now stated with its reason.

## Verification

`tsc` clean · **1629 tests / 76 files** (from 1586) · theme suite **356** · production `next build` compiles and prerenders all 39 pages · backend `189 passed` on the touched suites. Every new guard was mutation-measured red and reverted byte-identical.

## Owed, and not claimed

**No visual check was performed, by any slice.** Playwright cannot install in the build environment, so neither the phone-viewport pass nor the Fluent → Material → Graphite sweep happened. Each agent compensated with what it could inspect — class strings against the theme tokens, icon names against the registry, a production build — and each said plainly that it did not look at the running app.

This matters more than usual because **there is still no structural or layout test anywhere in this tree**. Nothing asserts panel composition, shell adoption, or that two apps draw a card the same way. The docked pane in particular is held by review alone.

**Known, deliberate, and worth seeing before judging:** `WaitingForView` still gates its checkbox on the old mode, so its first pick must come from select-all until it gets the same treatment. The shared card title is still `text-[13px]` against the house scale — the one contradiction left for the owner rather than settled by whichever slice touched the file last.

title: WS-27 S5 + the docked-pane overflow fix: the Projects detail panel stops being a plain form
body:
Both changes come from the owner testing the deployed app and sending screenshots of the two detail panels side by side. **Frontend only — no migrations, no backend.**

---

## 1. The overflow was my regression

`ItemDetail` was built for the `max-w-3xl` modal, where its `grid-cols-2` details block is comfortable. #419 docked it into DESIGN_SYSTEM §6's 380px pane, which left each cell ~170px and collided labels with values.

A media query cannot fix this — **the pane is 380px on a 4K monitor too**, so the viewport tells you nothing about the space the component actually has. The switch is `focused`, the prop that already distinguishes the modal from the pane. One column docked, two when maximised.

## 2. Direction reversed: Projects conforms to Tasks here

The standing ruling this wave has been *"Projects is canonical, Tasks conforms."* **Not on this surface.** Measured on `54e4b880`, `/projects`' `TaskPanel` was the weaker one:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Status | bare native `<select>` | `<Select>` in a `StatusChip` field cell |
| Files | raw `<input type="file">` → *"Choose Files / No file chosen"* | `<Button>` raising a hidden input, filenames listed by the app |
| Comment | raw `<textarea>` + raw `bg-primary` button | `<Textarea>` + `<Button>` |
| Layout | flat stack of labels | header · DETAILS · DESCRIPTION · PROPERTIES · LINKS & SUBTASKS · FILES · ACTIVITY, one scroll region, pinned composer |
| `@/components/ui` imports | 1 | 4 + `StatusChip` |

A native control expresses neither Material's pill buttons nor Graphite's uppercase labels, and *"Choose Files / No file chosen"* is the browser's string in the browser's font — no theme can reach it. This was a breach of rule 3, not a style preference.

Projects' richer status data is used rather than flattened: `accentForStatus` takes the owner's stored colour first, then the category, so the chip reads **better** than Tasks', not merely equal.

## Two seams the product needed anyway

- **`ui/Input.tsx` gains `Select`.** There was no single-choice field at all, so **38 files had each copied their own class string**. 37 remain, baselined and ratcheted down-only. Honest limit recorded in the doc comment: the popup option list belongs to the browser and does not take our tokens.
- **Conformance rule 7** — raw `<select>` (ratcheted per file) plus an absolute rule that a file input must be hidden behind a control. Both mutation-measured red, file restored byte-identically. `SOLID_BUTTON_DEBT` 30 → 29.

## The mistake that did not repeat

The Projects panel is single-column with **no responsive variant**, deliberately. The page lifts its width cap on a phone, so a `sm:` breakpoint would key off the viewport and split the column on a large monitor — which is exactly the error I made in `ItemDetail` an hour earlier. Fixed there by prop, avoided here by construction.

## Also fixed: the spec's own verification command was broken

§10 named `test_projects_sync.py` and `test_projects_personal_mirror.py`. **Neither exists** — the second is `test_projects_personal.py`, the first never landed under that name. pytest exits non-zero on a missing path *before running anything*, so anyone pasting that block got a red run unrelated to their change, and anyone "fixing" it by deleting the path silently dropped coverage. Corrected and run: **384 passed**.

## Verification

`tsc` clean · **1634 tests / 76 files** · theme suite **361** · production `next build` compiles and prerenders all 39 pages · the corrected spec block **384 passed**.

## Owed, and not claimed

No browser ran — Playwright cannot install here — so the phone viewport and the Fluent → Material → Graphite sweep on `/projects` **and** `/tasks` beside it are still owed. Every icon name introduced was checked against the theme registry for all packs; two pre-existing names (`Repeat`, `BellOff`) are **not** in it and fall back to Lucide regardless of theme, which is a finding, not something this PR caused.

Also recorded: `SectionLabel` is now a deliberate second copy, labelled as such in its doc comment — promoting it to `src/components/` touches `src/app/tasks/**`, which another change holds open.

title: WS-27 S6 — the Projects card draws the pills its row already carries
body:
Answers *"we should have the relevant pills to show up in the cards of the projects app"*, plus the `/tasks` list column fix from the same review and one docs fence.

## What the card drew before / after

**Before:** status chip · title · `{blocked, due, subtasks, "🏷 3"}` · `#101` + avatars.
**After:** the same, plus a **priority chip** and up to **three named, registry-coloured tag pills** (then `🏷 +N`). `estimate` is now wireable — it was dropped by omission, not by design.

Richest card observed is two chip lines, so the density budget holds.

## Why each fact earns its place

- **`importance`** — the true analogue of the `/tasks` priority pill. It has been in `DEFAULT_SHOWN` since WS-27x and the Table column has always drawn it; the card was the one surface ignoring a promise the view already made. Unset draws nothing, but **`0` (Low) draws** — the select's empty row PATCHes `null` precisely so "nobody said" and "Low" stay different things. Only `Urgent` escalates to the danger tone; a scale where three of four levels shout is a scale nobody reads.
- **`tags`** — named, not counted. `"🏷 3"` is the shape of a fact with the fact removed; `regression` `supplier` tells a reader what the task is *about*. Colour comes from `pm_tags.color` through the same `statusAccent` chip class the picker, the manager and the filter bar use, so one tag is one colour everywhere.
- **`estimate_mins`** — a plain omission. `TaskModel` returns it and `TableView` reads it; the card's adapter never mapped it and its comment asserted the column did not exist. Gated on `estimate`, which stays OFF by default.

**No `SHOWN_FIELDS` default changed.** `FIELD_KEYS`, `DEFAULT_SHOWN` and the gateway's mirror are byte-identical to `main` — this makes the card obey a contract that already existed rather than taking a new decision.

Deliberately left off, with reasons in the spec: `start_date` (a floating `DATE` needs a day comparison that belongs to the app adapter, not a shared module), blocking-count (`blocked_by_count` only — a gateway ticket), watchers/recurrence (not on `TaskRow`), triage (the status chip already says it), custom fields (unbounded density on a 288px card).

## Two design seams, kept as seams

A chip's `hue` is an **identity** (which tag), a chip's `tone` is a **measurement** (how late, how blocked) — which is why they draw as two shapes. Both stay *names*: `TaskMeta.tsx` remains the only file that turns either into a class, so `warning` never appears as `text-warning` at a call site.

Chip keys may now be namespaced `<kind>:<discriminator>` (`tags:ops`, `tags:more`), and everything classifying a chip reads `chipKind(key)`. This was the trap worth fencing: the visibility gate was keyed on the whole key, so a task with three tags would have fallen out of every lookup and silenced its tags on every view — silently.

## Also in this PR

- **`/tasks` list Name column** — the fix for the truncation in the same review. The column already flexed (`minmax(140px, 1fr)`), but six fixed sibling tracks took 670px of an 865px row, so `1fr` could only ever resolve to the leftovers: **147px** against content wanting 312px, 39 elements truncating. Raising the floor *alone* pushed Due date off the right edge — a browser showed that immediately — so both halves ship together: ~120px reclaimed from the fixed columns (each sized against the widest real chip it draws) and the floor raised to 240px. Measured after: **241px**, Due date back inside the row, nothing overflowing.
- **A rule-count fence.** Three files quoted three different numbers for the same gate — "five regexes", "six", seven — each true when written and each stale by the next rule. The count is now parsed from the suite's own numbered header and both docs are checked against it. Scoped so `AGENTS.md`'s "Four rules on top of the three above" (a true statement about a different list) does not trip it, with a parser guard and a floor that stops the docs passing by deleting the sentence.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `npx vitest run` | **1668 passed**, 76 files, exit 0 |
| `npx vitest run src/lib/theme/` | 364 passed, exit 0 |
| `npx next build` | exit 0, `/projects` prerendered |
| `pytest test_projects_routes/_filters/_org_access_control` | 171 passed |

Zero `.py` files in the diff.

**Looked at, not just reasoned about.** The board was driven in Chromium on the merged tree with fixtures at the network boundary only (`page.route` over `/api/projects/*`; the real `TaskBoard`/`TaskList`/`TaskMeta` rendered real `TaskRow`s — no product code touched to make it render). Confirmed: the three-tag cap plus `+2` overflow, an unset `importance` drawing no chip while `0` draws `Low`, and every tag pill matching its filter-bar chip. Then the **DESIGN_SYSTEM §8 sweep — four themes × two modes** — with the computed tokens read out of the DOM: every chip repaints from theme tokens in all eight combinations, and `/tasks` is unaffected.

The new fence was checked by **mutating `CLAUDE.md` back to "six" and watching it fail**, not by observing it green.

## One honest finding, not papered over

Material dark's `--warning` is a pale peach (`hsl(35 90% 78%)`) and its `--destructive` a pale pink, so `High` and `Urgent` sit closer together in that theme than elsewhere. The four glyphs and the four words are what carry the level there — which is why the levels have four distinct glyphs. That is the theme's own token, so it was left alone rather than hardcoded around; recorded in spec §11.23.

## Deferred, found not fixed

1. `TaskList`'s Status and Assignees columns render unconditionally, ignoring `shown_fields` — a pre-existing WS-27x gap. The new chips gate; retro-gating the existing columns is a visibility decision with its own before/after.
2. `MyWork.tsx` has no single tag registry to read (it is cross-project), so its tag pills fall to the gray fallback while the same tag is coloured on the board. Fixing it needs a cross-project tag lookup — a gateway question.
3. `blocks` (this task blocks others) is not on the list endpoint; it is arguably the more actionable half of the pair.

Not deployed and no flag flipped.

title: Projects: drain the queue (ab/ac/ae), fix a join-table authz gap, and read both references end to end
body:
Two halves. **Code**: the last three dispatchable Projects tickets plus a security fix. **Plan**: Plane and Paca read end to end, our own research corrected, and every feature linked back to the file that inspired it.

`main` is unchanged until this merges; **migration 168 is not applied on prod.**

---

## Part 1 — code

### WS-27ab · view ergonomics *(P-14/15/16)*
Panel **peek → side → full**, persisted (measured: 448 → 320 → 448 → 766). `FilterBar` says when live state has drifted from the saved view — divergence is **one exported pure function** over the `toConfig`/`fromConfig` round trip, so it compares *meaning*, not bytes. The palette's commands became a **declared registry**; `g`/`v` sequences run it and the `?` sheet is *printed from it*. Plus the `shown_fields` gap S6 found.

**The ticket's Escape wording was wrong and the browser said so** — focus after a card click sits on the card, so the panel's handler never sees the key. Built as two handlers with one rule, struck wording recorded rather than quietly reinterpreted.

### WS-27ac · calendar week layout, per-day quick-add, exact overflow *(P-19)*
The week is **the month grid's own row** — `CalendarView.tsx` contains no `new Date(`, `getDay()`, `setDate(` or `86400` at all. Mutation-measured: rewriting `weekGrid` the way nearly everyone writes it (`-anchor.getDay() + 1`, which breaks on Sundays) turns exactly two tests red.

### WS-27ae · CSV export + delta-sync *(P-26/27/28)*, migration 168
**The ticket named a pattern that does not exist** — no export-job anywhere in the tree. So: a synchronous bounded CSV, where **the cap is a refusal, not a truncation** (a short month is drawn with a banner beside it; a downloaded spreadsheet has no banner and is byte-indistinguishable from a complete one).

Delta-sync answers the deletes question rather than dodging it: `removed[]` fed by an **AFTER DELETE trigger**, because `pm_projects` cascades and an app-level write would only record deletions that went through an endpoint. Losing *visibility* stays inexpressible — documented and pinned as silence.

**Two defects the live database caught that no fake could:** the first version of migration 168 made an `organization` row **undeletable**; and a tombstone from a project cascade named a project that no longer existed, so **the deletion stranding the most rows was the one the feed could not report.**

### 🔴 Security · `views.set_positions`
Reading Plane's **GHSA-4w5x-wc9w-f47x** (a join write scoped at one end) found the same shape in ours: it validated the *view*, then wrote every caller-supplied `task_id` **unchecked**. Ours was narrower — the PK is `(view_id, task_id)` and the view *is* validated — but it still wrote rows referencing tasks the caller cannot read, while every sibling endpoint resolves visibility per task.

**The fence needed rewriting before it was worth anything.** My first version used `projects_user()`, which holds `*` including `data:org:read` — it passed whether or not the fix existed. `member_user` is the principal the fake's own docstring says every scoping test needs. Mutation-measured after the rewrite.

**This shape has now been sighted three times** — Plane's advisory, ours, and Paca's `MoveTask` (which validates neither). It is a category, not an incident; the remaining `task_ids[]` endpoints are ticketed as WS-27as.

---

## Part 2 — the plan

### Both references read end to end, with the licences distinguished
~3,000 TS files in Plane, ~740 in Paca. **§9.0 pins both to a commit SHA** and states the two rules, because conflating them is the real risk: **Plane is AGPL-3.0** (read and reimplement, never copy) and **Paca is Apache-2.0** (reuse legally available with attribution; we still default to reimplementing, for design-system reasons rather than legal ones).

### Our own research was wrong in ~32 places
- **Plane (4):** §5 refused rich text and the collab server as *one* thing — they are separable, verified, and only the collab refusal survives. We credited them with a per-board "kill switch" that **no code reads**. The public-roster refusal was incomplete. `apps/web` is not Next.js.
- **Paca (28):** we wrote that their migrations *"independently converged"* with our idempotency discipline — **they have no ledger at all**, and one migration drops a column in the same file that backfills it. We credited them with the presentation-vs-query-constraints split — **their saved filter config is never read by the server.** We hold that property; they do not.

### The cross-reference — the one thing neither single-repo pass could produce
1. **Both ship Base UI.** Paca for 17 of 24 primitives; Plane's `propel` likewise. Two independent products chose the same substrate for exactly the set WS-27ak enumerates — **D-PM-15 is now evidenced rather than argued.** Riders: Base UI has no Combobox, so that item is a build either way; and Paca carries a *second* primitive library that arrived via a vendored registry — the failure this decision exists to prevent, caught happening.
2. **Paca is ahead on exactly one axis, and it is ours** — its agent surface has no Plane counterpart.
3. **On everything Plane covers, Paca is the weaker reference** (no multi-select, no bulk edit, no keyboard cursor in 61k lines, native HTML5 drag only). Importing from it there would be a regression. Where they disagree, we now know which to follow.

### The most important finding is an absence
**Neither reference has any approval or human-in-the-loop primitive for agents.** Paca's autonomy is its permission set exercised unilaterally; its "you MUST invoke a skill first" rule is a paragraph in a prompt with nothing enforcing it. For an AI-driven company OS that is the biggest gap in both, so **D-PM-19** records that neither is prior art and we design it — at the tool layer. The UI contract, usefully, is an MIT library.

### 66 verified reference links
§9.6 indexes them, pinned to both SHAs. Every one mechanically checked to exist with a real line range; **two failed that check and were corrected before inclusion.** Fenced by `tests/unit/test_reference_links.py`, which **found a real defect on its first run** (§9.0's own link-prefix strings matched the pattern) and was then mutation-measured. It **skips loudly** rather than passing quietly when the clone is absent, since that is the only check proving a path is real.

Six items are **NO UPSTREAM**, which is the useful answer: the kill switch, collaboration cursors, RTL, timeline dependency arrows (so **D-PM-12 stands unchallenged**), page-batched list badges (their implementation is the anti-pattern our rule prevents), and per-tenant OAuth callback routing.

### Decisions owed — I have not made these for you

title: docs(D31): D15 re-tested against Odoo, Salesforce and SAP — it stands, one gap found
body:
Owner asked whether shared-database is still ideal, given that Odoo — a large app with many sub-apps for one company — runs database-per-tenant. Reviewed Odoo, then Salesforce/ServiceNow/NetSuite, then SAP.

**Outcome: D15 stands. One genuine gap found.**

## The rule the comparison yields (`saas_multitenancy.md` §0.9.9, new)

> What forces a database per customer is not customization. It is **customization implemented as DDL**.

Odoo adds a custom field by issuing real DDL — a physical `x_…` column, registered in `ir.model.fields` — and keeps modules, views and record rules as rows in the tenant database. That is the forcing function, and it is a fact about Odoo rather than a verdict on row security: Odoo already ships row-level filtering (`ir.rule`) and trusts it to separate legal entities inside one database.

We are already on the other side of that rule and shipped it three weeks ago — `155_projects_custom_fields.sql`: definitions as rows, values as JSONB behind a GIN index, schema unmoved. Apps are rows too (migration 114).

Salesforce/ServiceNow/NetSuite run the deepest per-tenant extensibility in the industry **pooled**. SAP constrained *how* extension is expressed rather than siloing.

## Recorded against ourselves

SAP CAP ships §7 item 1c's schema-per-tenant in production at scale. That contrary evidence is written **into** §7 rather than argued away. It survives rejection for a reason that is ours: CAP automates schema deploy across containers on a quarterly cadence; we ship continuously against a 160+ file ladder applied before restart with **no rollback**. §7 item 1c now names itself the first rejection to re-open if our cadence changes.

Also recorded: SAP re-invented pooling (CAP's shared container for cross-tenant master data = our control plane, reached from the opposite direction), and SAP's own guidance says HANA MDC suits a *trusted* environment — so "SAP uses tenant databases" is not "SAP treats one as a hard customer boundary".

## The one finding — new §6.6: there is no per-tenant restore

BO-23 restores the **cluster**. Under one tenant that is right. From customer #2 it is a §6 cross-tenant defect in that section's own terms: the only way to answer *"restore us to 3pm yesterday"* is to roll every other customer back.

Fix and its order: filtered logical export driven by the **same** `discover_tables()` set the RLS policies use → staging-schema re-import + reviewed swap → rehearsed in CI the way `rehearse_restore.sh` already rehearses the cluster path.

Deliberately **not** added to `engineering_practice.md` §8 — it is not a pre-customer-#1 gate, since with one tenant the cluster restore *is* the per-tenant restore. It lives in §6 (which already means "before a second tenant") and on the WS-29 row, rather than minting a second home for tenancy gates.

## Changed

- `saas_multitenancy.md` — new §0.9.9 (prior art), new §6.6 (the gap), §7 item 1c gains the SAP counter-evidence, §10 gains sources with a caveat that the two Odoo references are an agency guide and a single forum respondent whose RAM figures are directional, not measured.
- `work_plan.md` — **D31** recorded; WS-29 row carries the §6.6 gap.
- `CLAUDE.md` — decision range D1–D30 → D1–D31 in both places.

Docs-only: pr-check's `paths-ignore` (`**.md`, `project-docs/**`) means zero jobs run.

title: Projects Wave 1: the papercut wave (WS-27al/am/bd), sequenced by impact
body:
**WS-27 — Wave 1 of the usability sequencing (spec §9.7).** Owner directive 2026-08-11: rank the 21 minted tickets by what gets Projects to clean, organized and usable soonest. §9.3–§9.5 had ranked by which research pass surfaced a thing, which is an archaeology order, not a build order.

Frontend only. **No migration, no API change, no new dependency.** One `.py` file touched, and only to add a test.

## The audit is the headline, not the build

All three tickets came back **GO-NARROWED**. **Five of fourteen enumerated done-whens described work that already existed or had no target in this tree:**

| Struck | Measurement |
|---|---|
| al(6) selection self-heal | **Already shipped** — `page.tsx:722-733` prunes off `onScreen` via `selection.ts:105`. The shipped comment even uses the ticket's own "select forty, narrow to three" example. |
| bd(3) clipboard honesty | **Already true at all eight `writeText` sites.** /projects' own carries a comment explaining why. |
| al(3) lazy tooltips | **No target** — zero `Tooltip` components exist. Moved to WS-27ak(2), Wave 2, where the dependency is visible. |
| al(4) selected-first ordering | Names no multi-select; the nearest candidate is a permanently-visible chip strip with no "open" moment. |
| bd(4) signature-keyed dismissal | No banner exists. `dismissedTools.ts` is already id-keyed. |

And **bd(5) was a trap as written**: "context menu on cards and rows" reads like a build, but a generic one already existed at `app/tasks/components/ContextMenu.tsx` wired at five sites, plus a second in email. The likeliest outcome was a *third* implementation — the CLAUDE.md §5 defect authored by the ticket meant to prevent it. Built as a promotion instead.

## What shipped

**WS-27al** — `ControlLink` in the task **title cell** of `TaskList`/`TableView` (an `<a>` cannot wrap a `<tr>`): the app's first `<a href>` on a task, so cmd/ctrl/shift/middle-click finally open a new tab · the `data-prevent-outside-click` walker · MyWork's overdue predicate folded onto the shared one.

⚠️ The outside-click walker's **motivating case does not exist yet** — nothing in /projects portals a picker out of a dropdown. Built for Wave 2's Modal/Combobox and recorded as such rather than implied.

**WS-27am** — `LayoutBoundary` around all six /projects canvases. **The tree had zero error boundaries** — no `componentDidCatch`, no `error.tsx` — so one malformed group shape blanked the whole app. Retry re-mounts by bumping a key. `EmptyState` gains a disabled-not-hidden third arm.

**WS-27bd** — ContextMenu promoted to `src/components/` behind a re-export shim (/tasks' five call sites unedited), wired to /projects cards off a new `lib/taskMenu.ts` · per-row pending/error in `RelationsBlock`.

## Verification

```
npx tsc --noEmit                    exit 0
npx vitest run                      exit 0 — 84 files / 1866 tests
uv run pytest <4 named files> -q    exit 0 — 138 passed
```

Independent verifier: **PASS**. It confirmed all three al refusals by diff (`grep '^+.*<='` empty; `filters.py` and `waiting.ts` absent from `--name-status`), checked merge losslessness per file, and specifically confirmed **nobody faked a fence** — no `.test.tsx`, no jsdom introduced, `vitest.config.ts` untouched, no `.only`/`.skip`/`expect(true).toBe(true)`.

## The reviewer's P1 was refuted, and the method is the point

The adversarial reviewer argued that Enter on a now-focusable task title escapes the canvas keydown handler and performs a full-document GET, rebooting the SPA and discarding filters, selection and view mode. **The first half is exactly right** — `stepCursor` returns null at `cursor < 0`, and `TaskList.tsx:171` returns *before* `preventDefault` at line 172. The conclusion does not follow: the default action of Enter on an anchor is *to dispatch a click*, which `ControlLink` intercepts.

Reproduced in real Chromium with React-style **root delegation** (React 17+ delegates from the container, not the element — which is precisely where a late `preventDefault` would fail):

```
canvas keydown Enter -> stepCursor null -> return, NO preventDefault
root-delegated click: button=0 detail=0
INTERCEPTED -> onActivate(open panel)
NAVIGATIONS: []
```

Zero navigations, URL unchanged. A repair round for a non-bug was avoided by running it rather than reasoning about it.

## Findings that were real, and are fixed

- **`ControlLink` had no themed focus ring** — ~200 new focus stops on a long table drawing Chrome's default outline. Fixed by extending the **existing** `.cc-control:focus-visible` declaration with a `.cc-link` selector: one ring, two kinds of focusable thing. Deliberately **not** by applying `.cc-control`, which bundles the ring with control label weight, tracking, text-transform and a hover state layer, and would have restyled every task title.
- **The anchor was natively draggable**, stealing click-drag text selection from titles. `draggable={false}`.
- **`mywork.ts`/`mywork.test.ts` carried a retracted claim.** They said a finished task "rendered overdue in My Work". It did not — that export has **no in-app caller**; `MyWork.tsx` draws the chip through `cardChips` → the shared predicate. A latent divergence, not a visible bug. The spec was corrected earlier; the source comments were not, which is the same disappearance one level down.
- **The empty-`positions` write had no test.** The context menu's "Change status" sends `positions: []` on every use. Added `test_an_empty_position_list_is_a_no_op_and_never_wipes`, asserting `written == 0` **and that pre-existing rows survive** — the second half is the point, since `written == 0` alone passes a wipe-then-write-nothing. Mutation-measured: an authoritative DELETE turns it red on the survival assertion.
- **`LayoutBoundary`'s own rationale was wrong.** React unmounts the subtree below a boundary *before* rendering the fallback, so the key bump is belt-and-braces; the bump that earns its place is `page.tsx`'s `canvasKey`.

## 🔴 One deviation needs owner sign-off — not an agent's to close

§9.5.2's done-when said the menu's items derive from `app/projects/lib/commands.ts`. **That registry holds `go.*`/`view.*`/`panel.*`/`project.*`/`help.shortcuts` and nothing task-scoped**, so satisfying it literally yields a card menu reading *"Widen the task panel · Custom fields · Import from ClickUp"*.

The implementer built a second registry at task scope and **rewrote the acceptance criterion**, fencing disjointness in both directions instead. The argument is sound and documented in three places — but an implementer editing its own acceptance is a reviewer/owner call. The literal alternative (extend `commands.ts` to task scope) also moves the `g`/`v` key sequences and the printed `?` sheet, so it is a ticket, not a side effect.

## Deferred / owed

- **The four-theme sweep** (Fluent → Material → Graphite) on the error fallback, the disabled CTA and the /projects context menu. No browser runs in CI; nothing in this tree tests layout.
- **The tab-order change** from ~200 new anchor focus stops. Correct for a real link and an a11y gain over a `<div onClick>` row, but a visible interaction change.
- **`emptyStateCopy`'s third arm needs two edits, not one** — both call sites discard `copy.action` unconditionally, so passing `canCreate: false` alone would ship the hidden CTA the arm exists to prevent while its unit test stays green. Recorded in §11.29.
- **Owner question, al(5): does "today count as due"?** Refused rather than guessed. Adopting it inverts two deliberately-pinned assertions carrying their reasoning in comments **and** changes SQL, dragging R8/R6 into a "logic-only" ticket. Our store is timestamp-granular; the reference is date-granular.
- **A fence limit that binds every wave from here:** `vitest.config.ts` is `environment: "node"` with `include: ["src/**/*.test.ts"]` — `.tsx` tests are not collected and no jsdom/testing-library is installed, so **React rendering cannot be unit-tested in this tree at all.** Worth deciding alongside D-PM-15, since every rendering done-when in Wave 2 is review-only without it.

As-builts: **§11.28** al · **§11.29** am · **§11.30** bd. All three agents independently claimed §11.28 — the third such collision in two waves.

**Not merged, not deployed.** Merge and deploy are the owner's.

title: WS-26h: CRM stage discipline (entry requirements + rot) · WS-26i audited NO-GO
body:
Two commits: one shipped slice, one audit record.

## WS-26h — stage entry requirements + rot badges (`9102819`)

Generalizes the lost-reason gate into per-stage entry requirements, and adds the rot half of `crm_app.md` §5.1 system 3. **Migration 169** — number taken from the directory at build time (R1); every test finds the file by content, so a renumber at merge is free.

**Schema.** `crm_deal_statuses` gains `required_fields TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` and a nullable `max_dwell_days SMALLINT`. Deal-only, the same asymmetry `probability` already has: the allowlist is deal columns, and rot is measured off `status_changed_at`, which migration 144 gave deals and withheld from leads.

**Gate.** `pipeline.py::_require_entry_fields`, called from `apply_status_transition` immediately after the lost-reason refusal, so it inherits all three of that rule's properties — entry-only (the transition is entered only when `status_id` actually moves), refused before any of the three effects, and satisfiable by the *same* PATCH. That last one is what lets `MoveModal` send fields + status in one request; two requests can half-apply, and the half that lands is the one that moved the deal.

**UI.** Rot is presentation only — amber past the threshold, destructive past 2×, strictly-past so a card is fine *on* the allowance day. Nothing moves, closes or hides. `LostReasonModal` was absorbed into `MoveModal` rather than left beside it: a lost stage can also be a gated one, and two dialogs each raised by its own 422 is the shape where a user answers a question and is refused again.

### Deploys inert

Every existing stage lands with `required_fields = '{}'` and `max_dwell_days = NULL`, so no move is gated and no card rots until someone ticks a box in Pipeline settings. Dark by data rather than by flag. The only visible change on deploy is that the lost-reason dialog now renders through the shared `Button` components.

### Acceptance evidence

Against the ticket's own done-whens:

| Done-when | Evidence |
|---|---|
| move with missing fields → 422 naming them | `test_entering_a_gated_stage_without_the_field_is_422`, `test_the_refusal_names_every_missing_field_at_once` |
| same PATCH carrying the fields → succeeds | `test_the_same_patch_may_carry_the_missing_field` |
| non-move PATCH never blocked | `test_a_non_move_patch_is_never_blocked_by_requirements`, `test_a_patch_restating_the_current_status_is_not_an_entry` |
| unknown field name → 422 | `test_an_unknown_required_field_name_is_422` + a parametrized case per non-requirable column |
| rot thresholds pure-function tested (NULL, boundary, 2×) | `board.test.ts` → `rotLevel`, both boundaries and the no-timestamp case |
| settings grid edits both columns | `test_the_settings_grid_can_set_both_columns`, `test_the_requirements_can_be_cleared` |

### Verification

```
uv run pytest <15 CRM + access + tenancy suites> -q   → 1031 passed, 2 skipped
cd workbench/control_plane && npx tsc --noEmit         → clean
npx vitest run                                         → 79 files, 1802 passed
```

The 2 skips are `test_tenant_coverage`'s live-catalog checks, which need `DATABASE_URL`.

**R8 — run against a real database, not only against the fakes.** Stood up PostgreSQL 16, applied the ladder, replayed migration 169 three times for idempotency, and ran the package's own `insert_row` / `update_row` / `status_wire` against it. That covered the two things the hermetic fakes cannot answer: the `TEXT[]` round-trip through a bare Python list, and a zero `amount` reading back as `Decimal('0.00')` — which a falsiness test would have misread as "missing".

**Verified-red-first.** The entry gate (5 tests red when the call is removed), the deal-only field fence, and the new cross-language parity fence (red in both directions).

**Fences added (R7).** +25 pytest cases; `test_crm_migration.py` grew a WS-26h section and its `NOT_NULL_DEFAULTED` derivation now reads ALTER-added columns (the sync migration stays excluded with its existing reason — `zoho_dirty` is platform-written, this column is PATCHed by name); new `test_crm_stage_discipline_parity.py` reads `REQUIREABLE_FIELDS` out of `board.ts`, holding the two-language allowlist together the way `CATEGORY_HUES` is held; +14 `board.test.ts`, +13 `settings.test.ts`.

One of those fences is worth calling out: **a structural assertion that the Zoho pull never routes through the gate.** That loop is enabled in production, and a plausible "make the importer use the shared transition helper for consistency" refactor would have started failing every cycle for a whole Zoho module.

### Deferred, deliberately

**CREATE is not gated.** `POST /crm/deals` with an explicit `status_id`, and the convert path's `_create_deal`, both write without entering the transition. WS-26h scopes the rule to the move path, and widening it silently would make quick-create and every lead conversion refusable by a settings-grid edit made elsewhere. Recorded in the function docstring, the spec and the board row rather than fixed by ambush.

## WS-26i — audited NO-GO, recorded (`262f017`)

Docs only. The audit stopped at the gate and no implementer was dispatched; the verdict is committed so the next cycle does not re-derive it.

WS-26i fails the §1 contract at point 3 (no done-when, no tests line — the only ticket in §9 with neither), point 5 (no §10 verification block) and point 7 (unlabeled, so it reads AGENT-SAFE, while four of its six sub-behaviours write the live Zoho tenant). Per item: merge is doc-blocked on §7.1 merge semantics and is destructive upstream; bulk needs a `db`-taking patch seam extracted from `records.patch_record` first and collides with WS-26h's raw `HTTPException(422)`; CSV import has no precedent and no `UNIQUE` on `crm_leads.email` to dedupe against; saved views are pincered between a new migration and the parked `crm_*` `organization_id` naming call. CSV **export** is the one item clearable by a single doc edit, and the ready-to-paste done-when block plus its two measured traps are recorded in `crm_app.md` §9.

### Three status drifts corrected in the same pass

The important one: the spec header asserted *"Nothing has ever written the Zoho tenant — that is still true."* That has been **false since 2026-08-06**, when the sync loop was enabled, and the same file's own board record already struck it. It is the sentence an implementer reads before deciding whether a write is safe, on the very ticket where most sub-behaviours write that tenant. Also: bulk's "3.4k records" is really 3,993, and the cited "QuickFilters precedent" for saved-view persistence does not exist — that component persists nothing.

## Owner gates — none touched

No flag flipped, no credential, no prod reach, no `?apply=true`. Still outstanding and unaffected: `CRM_AUTO_LEAD`, the WS-26f stage-metadata repair, and the WS-26e cutover.

title: WS-26i-export: CRM filtered-list CSV export (+ fixes a BOM-stripping bug in the Projects proxy)
body:
One supervisor cycle: audit → doc remediation → build → verify → review → repair → re-verify. Four commits.

| | |
|---|---|
| `c1c9236` | docs — mint the ticket the WS-26i audit's NO-GO asked for |
| `3d98362` | feat — the CSV export |
| `244c85a` | fix — repair round 1 (the BOM never reached the browser) |
| `59525cd` | docs — say only what is evidenced about WS-27ae's deploy state |

## The slice

`GET /crm/export/{leads,deals,contacts,organizations}.csv`. No migration. Read-only. Four literal per-entity paths with `export/` first, because a `/crm/{entity}` template would shadow `PATCH /crm/activities/{id}`.

Filters come from the **same** `core.list_contract` the list endpoint uses, so the export is exactly the list you were looking at and its refusals are inherited rather than restated. Complete-or-refused, never truncated: a `count(*)` over the same WHERE runs before any row renders, and the render binds `cap + 1` so it refuses on the rendered set rather than trusting a count taken in a different snapshot.

Read-only is the load-bearing property, not a nicety — the Zoho sync loop is enabled, so a row this path dirtied would reach the real tenant within one 600s cycle. It's asserted three ways: an AST fence on the module's imports, a source scan for write verbs, and a behavioural check per entity that every statement begins with `SELECT`. The verifier defeated the two source fences with an obfuscated write (`"upd" + "ate crm_leads set zoho_dir" + "ty = true"`); the behavioural one still caught it, 4 red.

Two seams promoted rather than copied: `gateway/csv_export.py` server-side (a second copy of the formula-injection guard is a duplicated *security control*) and `src/lib/export.ts` client-side. Projects consumes both.

## The thing worth reading

**Every gate was green and the feature still didn't work.** 503 pytest, `tsc` silent, 1,813 vitest, theme suite clean — and the UTF-8 BOM never reached the user.

The gateway emitted it; the BFF proxy's `await res.text()` is a UTF-8 *decode*, which strips a leading BOM, and re-encoding never put it back. Measured, node v22: `[239,187,191,78,97,109]` upstream → `[78,97,109,101,44,69]` relayed. On the 3,993-row Zoho-India backfill that's every "Café", "Sørensen", "₹" and Devanagari name rendering as mojibake the moment someone double-clicks the file in Excel — exactly what the BOM exists to prevent, for the audience this feature is *for*.

Three fences were pointing the wrong way, which is why nothing caught it:

1. **A fence that pinned the defect.** `src/lib/export.test.ts` asserted the source *contained* `await res.text()`, commented "`res.text()` keeps the bytes" — it does not. The correct fix failed the test. It now runs both proxies end to end over a BOM'd body and compares bytes, and it survives the subtle mutant (`TextDecoder().decode(await res.arrayBuffer())` passes the static regexes; the behavioural half still goes red).
2. **A vacuous fence.** The done-when-1 parity test compared `route.dependant.query_params`, but both routes take filters via a class `Depends()` — it was asserting `set() == set()`. Proven: adding a `city` filter to `ListParams`, the exact drift it claimed to catch, left all 46 tests green. It now recurses sub-dependencies, goes red once per entity, and asserts its own precondition so it cannot silently go vacuous again.
3. **A no-op header.** `X-Export-Rows` was set "for anything reading this programmatically" and the proxy forwarded exactly two headers, neither of them that one.

**This also fixes the same bug in Projects.** The broken arm was copied *from* `api/projects/[...path]`, so `/projects/export/tasks.csv` has been serving BOM-less CSV since WS-27ae. Fixing only CRM would have left the new shared rule documenting the broken shape as correct. Recorded in `project_management_app.md` and the WS-27 row so it isn't read as scope creep.

## Verification

```
§10 block (8 files)              → 503 passed
test_projects_export.py          → 41 passed, file byte-unchanged
tests/unit (memory/calendar out) → 5788 passed, 51 skipped
tsc --noEmit                     → clean
vitest                           → 80 files, 1819 passed
vitest src/lib/theme/            → 364 passed, no baseline moved
ruff (selected) · xenon          → clean · rc 0
```

Independently re-derived by a verifier, not taken from the implementer's write-up. BOM survival measured byte-for-byte through both real route handlers, including a non-UTF-8 binary body. Header allowlist confirmed to have grown by exactly one — `set-cookie`, `etag`, `cache-control`, `x-request-id` all still dropped. Non-CSV proxy path checked across 200/201/400/404/409/422/500, empty bodies, 204s, 304s, missing `Content-Type`, GET retry-once and non-GET no-retry, both proxies.

Boundary check on `cap + 1`: `(50,50)`, `(7,7)`, `(1,1)` all export complete with no spurious 422 — an off-by-one there would silently refuse legitimate exports.

## Reviewer findings

Reviewer returned REQUEST-CHANGES (1×P1, 2×P2); all three repaired above. Verifier returned FAIL twice — first on the BOM and the vacuous fence, then on a docs claim — all cleared.

## Deferred, deliberately

- **The identical READ-COMMITTED race exists in Projects' exporter.** Not fixed here: `test_projects_export.py:310` actively asserts the old `LIMIT` shape, so the fix means editing a file this cycle must keep byte-unchanged. **That's a WS-27 ticket.**
- The other four WS-26i items — merge, bulk, CSV import, saved views — remain audited **NO-GO**. Do not widen into them.
- Board and Reports tabs get no Export control; neither has a row set an export could honestly call "what you were looking at".
- No browser theme-switch pass — no browser here. The change is proxy/gateway/test only and renders no new surface.

## One correction, on the record

An earlier draft of these docs called the Projects bug "live in production". Nothing in the tree established that, and the same file said thirteen lines above that WS-27ae was "NOT on `main` and NOT deployed" — both wrong, in opposite directions. The claim originated in my dispatch brief, not the implementer's initiative.

What is evidenced: WS-27ae is on `main` (`1de846a` ancestor via `ebf68f4`, PR #422) and `deploy` reported success on that SHA at 2026-08-10T23:53:53Z. That is a *green job*, which non-negotiable 8 says is precisely not delivery evidence. The docs now read **"almost certainly live, not proven live"** in all four places, and the stale not-on-main clauses on WS-27ab/ac/ae are struck.

## Owner gates — none touched

No flag, no credential, no prod reach, no `?apply=true`. `CRM_AUTO_LEAD`, the WS-26f stage-metadata repair and the WS-26e cutover are all unaffected.
