title: WS-26h2 + D-CRM-13: entry requirements on the CHOSEN create stage
body:
One supervisor cycle: audit → decision → build → verify + review in parallel → two repair rounds → re-verify PASS. Four commits.

| | |
|---|---|
| `591231d` | docs — D-CRM-13 and the WS-26h2 ticket, plus a miscount correction |
| `e522236` | feat — the create gate |
| `d345ca9` | fix — repair round 1 (AST siting fences + four doc corrections) |
| `0240d1d` | test — repair round 2 (pin the fence helper's whole-tree import walk) |

## The audit said no, and it was right

The ticket that started this was *"close the CREATE gap WS-26h recorded"*. The audit returned **NO-GO and refuted the premise.** Measured: `QuickCreateModal` sends no `status_id` and `ConvertDeal` has no such field, so **every deal the product creates lands in the default lane.** The recorded hole is reachable by direct API call only — not by any UI, and not by the CRM agent, which POSTs only `/crm/leads` and `/convert`.

Meanwhile gating the defaulted path would 422 quick-create and *every* lead conversion the moment an owner puts `required_fields` on the default lane, which `admin.py` permits unrestricted. Worse: `organization_id` is requirable and **neither surface can supply it** — `ConvertModal.tsx:126` renders "This lead names no company, so no organization is created" and offers no picker. A default lane requiring it would make those leads permanently unconvertible.

So the naive fix closes a hole nobody can reach and opens one every user hits.

## D-CRM-13

**Entry requirements gate the stage a caller CHOSE, never the stage the server DEFAULTED to.**

The principle, so this is a rule and not a workaround: *entry requirements exist to prove a deal earned its way into a stage, and a deal in the default lane has claimed nothing yet.* The default lane is where deals start, not somewhere they advance to; demanding proof of progress to enter it is a category error. Creating straight into a late stage by API **is** a claim worth checking, and that is what this gates.

This does not overturn `records._resolve_status`'s recorded doctrine — *"the gate belongs to the status, not to the verb that reached it."* That governs the **lost-reason** rule, a property of a TERMINAL status: a deal is lost or it is not, however it got there. Entry requirements are a property of an ENTRY lane. Same word, two questions.

Direction of travel is deliberate: this is the permissive reading and tightening later is one deleted condition. The strict reading is not cheaply reversible — it ships an organization picker, tells users conversion can be refused, and makes the ~1,516 imported leads a judgement call nobody can automate.

## The slice

Six lines of behaviour in `records._resolve_status`, beside the existing create-side lost-reason refusal: apply the gate **only when `values.get("status_id")` is truthy.** No migration, no UI, no SQL, no predicate. `_require_entry_fields` gained a `NO_EXISTING_RECORD` sentinel so "no row yet" is a stated case rather than `getattr(None, …)`.

## A miscount that could have caused an incident

Both `crm_app.md` and `pipeline.py`'s docstring said there were **two** ungated create paths. There are **three**. The third is `import_zoho.apply_record` → `core.upsert_by_zoho_id`, reached by the backfill route *and* by `sync_zoho.pull_phase` — the **enabled** 600s loop — and it must stay ungated forever. An implementer told there were two would find the third and gate it. Both sentences corrected.

## The thing worth reading: a fence that could not back its own docstring

Done-when 8 asked for a structural fence proving the gate never reaches the sync loop. As originally written — **by the audit, and pasted into the spec unchallenged** — it asserted a *syntactic* set (which files contain the literal `_require_entry_fields(`) while its docstring claimed a *reachability* property. Those are not the same thing:

```
baseline                                   -> ['pipeline.py', 'records.py']
import_zoho calls records._resolve_status  -> ['pipeline.py', 'records.py']   GREEN
gate imported under an alias               -> ['pipeline.py', 'records.py']   GREEN
```

The first mutation is the dangerous one. *"Make the importer use the shared create seam"* is the refactor this repo's own doctrine encourages — and `apply_record` **already sets `values["status_id"]` server-side** (`import_zoho.py:498-500`), so `chosen` would be truthy on every pulled deal. The gate lands on the enabled loop, and the first settings-grid save on a Zoho-named lane starts 422-ing rows from the live upstream tenant.

Neither Zoho suite would catch it: `grep required_fields` over both returns nothing, so `required` is empty and the gate is a silent no-op there.

Rebuilt as **two AST fences** — real `ast.Call` nodes with aliases, module-attribute forms and function-body imports resolved; plus a transitive call graph from `sync_zoho.pull_phase` and `import_zoho.apply_module` that prints the chain:

```
AssertionError: import_zoho.apply_module -> import_zoho.apply_record
                -> records._resolve_status -> pipeline._require_entry_fields
```

Every edge verified in the code by the verifier, not accepted as an assertion string.

## Verification

Independently re-derived by a verifier, twice, mutation-testing every done-when rather than accepting passing test names.

```
§10 WS-26h + WS-26h2 block (11 files)  -> 671 passed
both Zoho suites                       -> 136 passed, files byte-unchanged
tests/unit (memory/calendar deselected) -> 5934 passed, 51 skipped
ruff (blocking subset) · xenon         -> clean · exit 0
```

**The decisive measurement**, reproduced independently: move the gate to `core.insert_row` keyed on `crm_deals` — the tempting "one seam" — and both Zoho suites stay **136 green** while only the fence and done-whens 3/4 go red. `core.upsert_by_zoho_id` builds its own `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` and walks past `insert_row`. No example test in the repo would see it.

**Fence sensitivity, all seven cases re-measured against the real package:** red on a direct call in each of `import_zoho.py`/`sync_zoho.py`/`core.py`, red on an aliased import, red on the indirect route, green on baseline and on a comment merely *mentioning* the gate. The eight synthetic self-test cases were themselves probed by mutating the fence helpers — killing from-import resolution turns all eight red, so none passes because its fixture is inert.

**No production behaviour changed after the first commit.** Proven, not accepted: `records.py` is byte-identical since `e522236`, and `pipeline.py` was verified docstring-only by stripping docstrings from both revisions and comparing `ast.dump` — identical.

19 mutants measured red across three rounds, plus one deliberate green control.

## Deferred, deliberately

- **WS-26h's own fence has the same text-match defect** — blind to an alias, red on a comment. Left alone: a **wart, not an exposure**, because the new reachability fence covers its live-system property transitively (`apply_status_transition` calls `_require_entry_fields` unconditionally, so any path from the pull to the move gate is also a path to the entry gate — measured). Riders recorded: that coverage evaporates silently if that call is ever relocated, and the same helpers back both fences. ~10 lines once these helpers are on `main`.
- **The D-CRM-13 rider:** `admin.py` still accepts `required_fields` on the default status, which is now configuration that silently does nothing. Refusing it there would make the rule self-evident at the point of use. Banked, not built — it changes an existing settings surface and could reject config already saved. **Owner's call.**
- No UI: the create modal cannot yet prompt for missing fields when a user picks a late stage. Nothing shipped sends `status_id` on create, so nothing regresses.
- `_require_entry_fields` still raises a raw `HTTPException(422)`; the ticket said a typed error is a *may*.

## Corrections on the record

- Done-when 6 asked for a `Decimal("0.00")` case the type system makes unreachable — `DealIn.amount` is `float | None`, so Pydantic coerces to `0.0` before any route code runs. **Relabelled in the ticket, not weakened in the code**; the Decimal half belongs to the move path, where WS-26h measured it against a real `NUMERIC` column.
- The test-count claim was wrong twice before being collected rather than recalled. It is `pipeline 67→84, routes 121→131, convert 31→32` = **+28**.
- Three "Not deployed, not merged" sentences in `crm_app.md` were false — WS-26h merged in #425, WS-26i-export in #426. Corrected to state merge with its evidence and **explicitly withhold deploy**, which is not evidenced (non-negotiable 8).

Both contract defects above originated in the audit and were pasted into the spec unchallenged. The implementation followed the contract correctly in both cases.

## Owner gates — none touched

No migration, no flag, no credential, no prod reach, no Zoho code. The gate never touches a path `sync_zoho.pull_phase` traverses — which is the stated condition of the AGENT-SAFE label, and done-whens 8 and 9 are what prove it.

title: WS-26h-fence: convert WS-26h's siting fence to AST reachability (+ record the WS-26i-bulk contract)
body:
Test and documentation only. **Zero production code** — `apps/services/gateway/gateway/` is untouched across the whole range, verified by `git diff --name-status`, not asserted. No migration, no frontend, net `ruff` delta zero.

| | |
|---|---|
| `ce314e8` | the conversion + four doc drift corrections |
| `e7678eb` | record the spec-auditor's WS-26i-bulk contract verbatim |
| `d246045` | repair 1 — relative imports, the push half, an overclaiming limit block |
| `c179a3d` | repair 2 — pin `_merge_names`, pin the case count, correct the residual's reason |
| `5e73dcf` | the two numbers the count fence could not reach |

## What was wrong

`test_the_zoho_pull_never_enters_the_stage_gate` did a literal substring scan — `"apply_status_transition(" in path.read_text()` — while its docstring claimed a structural guarantee. It shipped with WS-26h and was already banked on the board as carrying the same defect fixed one function below it in WS-26h2.

Stakes: the Zoho sync loop is **enabled** and cycles every 600s. This fence is what stands between a plausible refactor — *"make the importer use the shared seam"*, which this repo's own doctrine encourages — and the loop refusing rows from the live upstream tenant.

## The conversion

One AST mechanism, two gates: `_GATE` became `_MOVE_GATE`/`_ENTRY_GATE` passed as an argument to `_gate_call_files` and `_gate_reached_from` over a shared `_crm_call_graph`. No fork, no third mechanism.

The reachability fence prints the chain:

```
import_zoho.apply_module -> import_zoho.apply_record -> records.patch_record
  -> pipeline.apply_status_transition -> pipeline._require_entry_fields
```

Every edge was verified in the code by a verifier rather than accepted as an assertion string.

## The part worth reading: the conversion regressed, twice, and neither was in the original finding

The reviewer measured one shape the conversion had lost. Reproducing it found **six**, all sharing a `node.level` cause — every one caught by the substring scan being deleted:

```
shape                                          OLD    NEW-before   NEW-after
B direct call, RELATIVE import                 RED    green        RED
C `from . import pipeline`                     RED    green        RED
F STAR import                                  RED    green        RED
G package __init__ RE-EXPORT                   RED    green        RED
H MODULE-LEVEL call                            RED    green        RED
I `from .. import crm` -> crm.pipeline.f()     RED    green        RED
E indirect, RELATIVE spelling                green    green        RED   <- the decisive one
J push half (apply_push_result)              green    green        RED
```

**Row E is the shape the entire fence exists for.** `apply_record → records.patch_record` respelled `from .records import patch_record` was green on *both* fences. One line onto the enabled 600s pull, everything green. Not hypothetical: `orchestrator` and `meeting_bot` already carry 19 relative imports, and no lint rule forbids them here.

Row J came from a second finding — `_PULL_ENTRY_POINTS` fenced only the pull, so a gate reached from `apply_push_result` ran against the live tenant every cycle with both fences reporting `[]`. Entry points now cover the whole cycle; reachable nodes went 41 → 79.

## Residual regressions: two, left open deliberately, disclosed as regressions

The discriminating axis is **not** expression-versus-name — it is whether the gate's own name is written immediately before a `(`, because the deleted fence was a pure substring test:

| shape | name before `(`? | OLD | NEW | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `getattr(pipeline, "apply_…")(…)` | no | GREEN | GREEN | not a regression |
| `_REGISTRY["move"](…)` · `Registry.move(…)` | no | GREEN | GREEN | not a regression |
| `_MOVE = apply_…; _MOVE(…)` | no | GREEN | GREEN | not a regression |
| `importlib.import_module("…").apply_…(…)` | **yes** | **RED** | GREEN | **REGRESSION** |
| `_GATES.apply_status_transition(…)` | **yes** | **RED** | GREEN | **REGRESSION** |

Left open because neither is a plausible refactor: `importlib.import_module` appears **once** in all of `apps/` + `packages/` (a plugin loader) and **zero** times in the gateway. It is deliberate evasion, and a fence cannot be built against someone who edits the fence file.

⚠️ **Round 1 justified this with a false technical reason** — that closing it required resolving unbound attributes against every top-level name, so `db.close()` would fabricate chains. The reviewer disproved it by *building* the fix: a ~12-line resolver reading only string constants adds **zero** edges to the real package and catches both forms. The decision stands; the recorded reason is now reach, not risk. A limit block giving a wrong reason is the same defect class as one under-listing holes.

## Verification

Two independent verifier passes and two reviewer passes. Every fence shape re-measured against the real package by agents that transcribed the superseded fence from `a06fa6a` and ran it side by side.

```
tests/unit (memory/calendar deselected)  -> 5954 passed, 51 skipped
test_crm_pipeline.py                     -> 103 passed
§10 fence selection                      -> 30 passed
both Zoho suites                         -> 136 passed, files byte-unchanged
ruff blocking subset · C901              -> clean · clean
```

**Fifteen mutants measured red** under a harness that aborts unless its anchor occurs exactly once. All 25 synthetic cases are load-bearing — each dies under at least one mutant, verified by mutating the helpers rather than reading the fixtures.

The `bulk_seam.py` extraction was performed for real, twice independently: the constraint survives the conversion and improves — `records.py` drops *out* of the set, so the failure names the relocation rather than growing a list.

## Also in here: the WS-26i-bulk contract

Authored by the spec-auditor, recorded verbatim, marked NOT STARTED so it dispatches nobody. Two of its criteria cited things this same branch changed; both carry dated correction notes beside the original text rather than silent edits. One of those notes caught a hazard: read literally against the new code, its *"passes with zero edits"* clause had stopped enforcing what it was written to enforce.

Plus four drift corrections — a stale anchor, a wrong justification (bulk needs N *sessions*, not one transaction — Projects' bulk is deliberately non-atomic), a non-blocker recorded as a blocker, and an undocumented constraint.

## Process findings, recorded because they recurred

- **Three consecutive rounds where the defect was a stale number in this spec.** Round 2 added a fence that reads the count back out of `crm_app.md` and fails on its *precondition* if the pinned phrase disappears. The two sites that went stale next were outside its regex — fixed by hand in `5e73dcf` and recorded rather than papered over.
- **The §10 block documented the count fence while its `-k` selector excluded it.** The fence built because §10's number drifted was the one §10 did not run. One token; 29 → 30 selected.
- The implementer's mutation harness silently no-opped on renamed anchors, reporting green — indistinguishable from a surviving mutant. Every reported number was independently reproduced and correct, but the harness is now anchor-asserting. This ticket's own defect wearing a different hat.

## Owner gates — none touched

No migration, no flag, no credential, no prod reach, no Zoho code, no production surface at all.

title: WS-27ak slice 1: the Modal primitive on Base UI, and /projects' six dialogs onto it
body:
**WS-27ak — Wave 2, slice 1.** The first headless primitive in the tree. Frontend only, **no migration**, zero `.py` files changed.

Before this, **70 files carried a `fixed inset-0` and none of them trapped focus.** That isn't seventy bugs; it's a primitive nobody had written.

## What shipped

- **`src/components/ui/Modal.tsx`** — a CommandCenter wrapper over **`@base-ui/react@1.7.0`** (MIT, verified by extracting the package, not by reading a manifest). It is the only file in the tree that names the library.
- **All six `/projects` dialogs converted** — `ShortcutsSheet`, `SearchPalette`, `ImportClickUp`, `FieldManager`, `TagManager`, `LifecyclePolicy`. That set wasn't a guess: a previous author had already enumerated it at `page.tsx:968-974`'s `overlayOpen`.
- **`page.tsx` is byte-identical to `main`**, which is the point — it owns a window-Escape listener that returns early on `overlayOpen`, and if a wrapper had taken ownership of open state, `g`-sequences would start navigating out from under a half-filled import form. The mutation for exactly that regression is in the fence.
- **Conformance rule 8** + a structural fence that none of the six may keep a `fixed inset-0`.
- **`e2e/modal.spec.ts`** — the first D-PM-21 browser fence.

## Verification

```
npx tsc --noEmit                        exit 0
npx vitest run                          exit 0 — 85 files / 1916 tests
npx next build                          exit 0
npx playwright test e2e/modal.spec.ts   exit 0 — 10 passed
```

Baseline re-derived by the verifier in a detached worktree rather than taken from the write-up: **1910 → 1916**, exactly the six tests added.

## 🔴 One acceptance criterion is NOT met — this is a board call

**"The background is `inert`, not merely covered."** `@base-ui/react@1.7.0` cannot deliver it. `FloatingFocusManager:339` passes `ariaHidden`; `markOthers` defaults `inert: false`; nothing in the package ever passes `inert: true`. The only real `inert` sits on the portal's own `InternalBackdrop` while **closed**. Measured in Chromium: `[inert] = 0`.

So: **screen readers cannot reach the background, Tab cannot leave the dialog — but Ctrl+F still finds the page behind the scrim.**

Closing it means an upstream change or the wrapper re-implementing `markOthers`, which is the parallel-seam move CLAUDE.md §5 forbids. The implementer stopped and wrote it down rather than reporting the criterion met.

## Two items in the dispatch brief were wrong, and only building found them

- **`outsidePressEvent="intentional"` is not a prop** in 1.7.0. It's computed, and resolves to `intentional` whenever a backdrop exists — so the fence pins the backdrop rather than a prop that doesn't exist.
- **`markOthers` does not set `inert`**, as above.

Both came from the audit; both were verified against the installed package.

## Review findings — one P1, fixed

**P1: the documented `finalFocus` fallback did not exist.** Base UI drops a disconnected opener and then focuses nothing, leaving `<body>` — the one outcome the docstring forbade. Reachable through a dialog in this very slice: **ImportClickUp's only trigger is the empty-state button**, and a successful import refetches the tree, replacing that trigger *while the dialog is still open*. Repair round 1 implements the fallback in the wrapper (explicit ref → captured opener if still connected → `<main>` landmark with a borrowed `tabIndex`) and states plainly what happens when none exists, instead of promising a guarantee.

**P2: `max-h-full` was baked into the popup's base classes**, so every call site's height was a dead knob — the importer rendered ~10% taller than designed.

## The record lied about the code in four places, including the auto-loaded contract

`Modal.tsx`'s own header and `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` §4a both asserted the `inert` property this slice disproved. `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` additionally named **conformance rule 8 as the fence against a hand-rolled scrim, which it does not catch** — rule 8 only forbids importing the substrate, and a `fixed inset-0` div imports nothing. That's an R7 violation: a rule naming a test that doesn't make breaking it fail. All four corrected, a real fence added, and the un-fenceable half labelled advisory.

**And one mutation record didn't reproduce.** The implementer claimed removing `Dialog.Backdrop` turned the outside-press test red; the verifier removed it, rebuilt, and got 8 passed — `DialogPortal` renders an internal backdrop whenever `modal === true`. The assertion *is* a genuine discriminator (red under backdrop-removed **plus** `modal="trap-focus"`), so it was a false ledger entry rather than a dead fence. The record now carries the reproducible measurement.

## Environment hazard, fixed

A stray untracked `zzprobe.config.ts` left in the shared checkout failed type-check and took `npx next build` down — and **a failed build leaves `.next` without a BUILD_ID, which stops Playwright's webServer starting at all.** One scratch file silently disables the entire browser fence. Removed; build back to 0.

Separately, `next build` twice failed on a Google-font fetch and passed on retry with no code change — a network transient here, not attributable.

## Deferred

- **The four-theme sweep** (Fluent → Material → Graphite) on `/projects` and a neighbour. Nothing in this tree tests layout, and the description-wrap and max-height changes are exactly what that pass would catch.
- **Items (2) Tooltip and (5) Skeleton stay NO-GO** — their done-when is a count of the problem, not a definition of done.
- The second `Modal` at `email/components/automation/ui.tsx:15` (five consumers), recorded for retirement, untouched.
- Combobox — and note D-PM-15's "Base UI has no Combobox" rider was **false**; 1.7.0 ships it. Corrected in this PR.

**Not merged, not deployed.** Merge and deploy are the owner's.

title: WS-1: route BO-1a's unrouted ClickUp writers + BO-1b's queued-write sync state (+ mints BO-1d)
body:
One supervisor cycle, two repair rounds. Four commits.

| | |
|---|---|
| `067020d` | feat — BO-1a: route the two unrouted ClickUp writers + derive the handler fence |
| `400e587` | feat — BO-1b: a broker-queued push writes `awaiting_approval`, never `synced` |
| `9a83d80` | fix — repair round 1: the flip is NOT safe, and four docs said it was |
| `19302da` | docs — the one anchor the repair-round-1 sweep missed |

## The audit inverted the premise

The board recorded the broker loop as "LIVE and writing" and BO-1a/BO-1b as closing a `failed`-row defect. The audit found `ACTION_BROKER_ENFORCE` set **nowhere** — no `.env.example`, no `deploy/`, no compose file, no systemd unit. Unset, the gate takes its auto-apply path and never reaches `broker.execute()`. So **both fixes are inert in production today**, and `clickup.archive_task` already executes a real ClickUp `PUT {archived:true}` immediately and unapproved on every purge/archive. The `failed` row is a counterfactual under enforcement, not current behaviour.

`ClickUpProvider.delete_task` has zero production callers — `items._delete_upstream` archives instead (pinned by `test_tasks_gtd.py:544`). The spec's "the two irreversible ones" was wrong twice over.

## The slice

**BO-1a**: `_WRITERS` gains `clickup.delete_task` → `_raw_delete_task` and `clickup.archive_task` → `_raw_archive_task`. The done-when-2 fence is rewritten to **derive** the expected set via an AST walk of `providers.py` rather than restating a literal, with its three limits stated in its own docstring (reachability-blind, non-literal-blind, `providers.py`-scoped).

**BO-1b**: `_push_pending_item` and `_push_child_subtasks` honour the broker's pending marker — a queued push now writes `sync_state='awaiting_approval'` with `provider_task_id` left unset, never a false `synced`. The UI criterion was rewritten at audit time: `workbench/control_plane` has zero `*.test.tsx`, no testing-library, no jsdom — every frontend test is a pure-function `lib/*.test.ts`. Delivered as exported pure functions in `syncState.ts` + a real `*.test.ts`, with the TSX conversion verified by diff-read rather than implied by a green suite.

## The thing worth reading: the branch nearly shipped a false safety claim

Round-1 build correctly closed both defects — every acceptance criterion was independently mutation-tested and met. But it rewrote the flip guidance to say the flip was now safe with one named residual. **It wasn't.** Reviewer, running the real `ClickUpProvider` with the env var set:

```
POST /tasks/accounts/{id}/projects       -> accounts.py:335  created["id"]  KeyError -> 500
POST /tasks/accounts/{id}/folders        -> accounts.py:403  created["id"]  KeyError -> 500
POST /tasks/plan/apply {clickup}         -> planning.py:377  created["id"]  KeyError -> 500
_push_patch_upstream                     -> items.py:790     queued update silently dropped
```

`create_project`/`create_folder` return the pending marker; all three sites index `["id"]` unconditionally. `planning.py:405` already defends against exactly this shape — the gap was known in that file and never extended.

**Fixed by correcting the claim, not by widening the diff.** Repair round 1 struck the false statement in **eleven** locations (four more than the reviewer named, found on sweep), replaced it with the true one, and minted **BO-1d** — a named, NOT-STARTED ticket for the four call sites, with file:line and failure mode for each. The flip stays owner-gated and now honestly documented as unsafe until BO-1d lands.

## Verification

Two independent verifier passes, two reviewer passes.

```
§BO-1 floor                    -> 36 passed  (was 32)
tasks pair                     -> 141 passed (was 136)
tests/unit (mem/cal deselected) -> 5944 passed, 51 skipped
ruff (touched files)           -> 8 findings, byte-identical to base — none on a line this PR wrote
tsc --noEmit · vitest          -> clean · 1915 passed
```

**The replacement reasoning was verified against a real Postgres 16, not by argument.** A prior comment claimed `provider_task_id=""` behaves like a real id everywhere downstream — false, and replaced with the actual mechanism: `uq_gtd_items_provider ON gtd_items(account_id, provider_task_id) WHERE source <> 'LOCAL'`, a partial unique index where NULL is exempt and `''` is not. Reviewer built the table from the real DDL and ran both branches: two `source='SYNCED'` rows with NULL both succeeded; the rejected alternative failed with `duplicate key value … already exists`. Right where its predecessor was confidently wrong.

**The AST fence's vacuity guard bites.** Making `create_folder` return before its gate — invisible to the AST walk — fails with `Extra items in the right set: 'clickup.create_folder'`.

**Consistency swept across 20 files.** No surviving "the flip is safe" claim anywhere in the tree.

## Deferred, deliberately

- **BO-1d** (4 sites: the 3 KeyErrors + the silent drop) — not fixed here. Scope decision, endorsed independently by the reviewer: BO-1a/BO-1b each close a defect that stands alone; folding BO-1d in means an agent inventing a response contract for three endpoints under time pressure (what does a queued create return — 202+`pending_action_id`? a `pending` flag? no mirror row?), each site answering differently. BO-1d's own table should be widened before it's built — see below.
- `routes/crm/*`, `routes/apps/tools.py`, `_broker_gate`'s auto-apply arm — untouched.
- Migration 48's inline comment describing `'pending'` still reads as the *other* state's description now. Applied migration, R6 — not edited in place; recorded as open in §BO-1b.
- No reconciliation of an approved write back onto `gtd_items` (BO-1b's own non-goal).

## Known findings not actioned in this PR (reviewer's final pass)

- **BO-1d's 4-row table is incomplete by its own inclusion criterion.** `items.py:465` (`_delete_upstream`) and `:493` (`_archive_upstream`) both call `provider.archive_task(...)` and discard the return — same "silently swallowed queued write" class as row 4. Should be added before BO-1d is built, or its own done-when-4 fence will flag them as a 5th/6th finding anyway.
- **The AST fence's blind-spot list should also name the keyword-argument call** (`self._broker_gate(action=..., ...)` leaves `node.args` empty and is silently skipped). Proven on a synthetic fixture; not yet closed.

Neither is a regression in what shipped — both are scoping notes for the next ticket.

## Owner gates — none touched

No migration, no flag flip, no credential, no prod reach. `ACTION_BROKER_ENFORCE` remains unset everywhere and the PR does not touch that. The pre-flight `SELECT action, status FROM pending_actions` is named in five places for whenever the owner does consider the flip.

title: fix(acb_auth): the owner bootstrap could not run on a fresh database
body:
## The bug

`ensure_owner_bootstrap()` used `ON CONFLICT (email)`. Migration 162 dropped
`app_user_email_key` and replaced it with `app_user_email_lower_key ON (lower(email))`.
There is no longer a unique constraint on the bare column, so the statement raises.

## Why nobody hit it

`_HAS_OWNER_SQL` short-circuits once an owner exists, so production never
reaches the broken path. It fires only on a database with no owner yet — a new
tenant, a restore to scratch, disaster recovery, or a laptop.

**The lockout-recovery path was itself locked out.** That is the whole severity
of this: it is fine until the day it is the only thing standing between you and
a database you cannot get into.

## Verification (R8 — against a real Postgres, not a fake)

Run inside a rolled-back transaction:

- provisions an owner on an empty database
- is idempotent — a second call creates no second row
- a mixed-case email does not create a duplicate (the `lower(email)` index is
  the one that must be honoured)

Fenced structurally so the mirror cannot rot again: the test asserts the
conflict target names the index that actually exists, rather than restating the
column name.

## Review notes

One commit, off `main`, independent of the two Projects PRs — it touches
`packages/acb_auth` only and can land in any order.

title: feat(WS-27): Project Operations — hierarchy, blockers, time tracking, and the management aggregates
body:
Implements the owner's Project Operations brief (`ProjectApp_Plan.md`, 2026-08-12),
slices **S1–S19**. Built on the owner's real 29-project portfolio, not invented data.

⚠️ **27 commits.** Large for one review, and that is a real cost — flagged rather
than hidden. It splits at a clean seam if wanted: migrations + gateway routes
(backend) and everything under `workbench/control_plane` (UI). Say the word and I
will restack it.

## What it adds

**Data** — migrations `171`–`174`: `pm_projects.kind` (the CLIENT → PROGRAM →
PROJECT hierarchy as *data*, one self-FK, per D-PM-2 — no per-level tables) ·
`pm_stages` + `pm_tasks.stage_id` (STAGE as a second axis, distinct from STATUS) ·
`pm_blockers` (11 kinds, resolution required by CHECK) · `pm_time_entries`
(`duration_secs` GENERATED, and a partial unique index enforcing **one open
session per actor** — the fence that makes start/pause/resume coherent) ·
`app_user.weekly_capacity_hours` · `pm_metric_snapshots`.

All expand/contract per R6: nullable with defaults, nothing renamed in place.

**API** — `work.py` (start · pause · complete · handoff · blockers · next action),
`ops.py` (six aggregates + stage history). Every number is computed in SQL, never
in the browser. **Every response carries a `basis` string** saying what it counted,
because a percentage against an invented denominator that does not say so is the
thing this feature exists to end.

**UI** — Control Center · My Work · Workload · Projects list · four operations views
· the panel operations block · stage Gantt · work timer dock.

## Decisions worth challenging in review

- **The stage Gantt derives from actual `stage_change` history, not planned dates**
  — a deliberate deviation from plan §26. A planned date is a column somebody must
  maintain; the first week nobody does, the chart shows a plan that never happened
  and quietly stops being read. Planned-vs-actual is additive later, *after*
  evidence the plan half will be kept.
- **No second detail page.** The operations block lives inside the existing
  `TaskPanel` rather than a new tabbed surface — building one would have made a
  second detail surface, the same trap that produced two things called "My Work"
  (D-OPEN-12).
- **D-OPEN-13**: two new nav panes (My Work, Control Center). I refused to widen
  `registration.test.ts` to pass my own change and built reachability from the
  board instead; when the owner chose "promote + narrow the fence", it was narrowed
  to the rule it actually cites and all three arms mutation-verified red.

## Six defects found by LOOKING, not by assertions

All six passed their unit tests: Graphite's `capitalize` overriding `uppercase` ·
the timer dock sitting on top of list pagination · the workload band labelling an
overloaded engineer "Light" (0 tracked hours → 0% → bottom band; now a distinct
`UNTRACKED` band) · `stage_change` being dead vocabulary with zero producers ·
`hand_off` accepting a recipient belonging to nobody · a swallowed `skipped` list
that let a handoff notify no one and still answer 200.

## Known red, named not hidden

Three mirror tests fail (`test_projects_filters`, `test_projects_import_tasks`,
`test_projects_notifications`). They regex the ORIGINAL `CHECK` out of the
migration that created each column, so they cannot see a later
`DROP CONSTRAINT`/`ADD CONSTRAINT`. Migrations 171/172 widened both vocabularies
and these fences never saw it. **The fence is stale, not the code** — it asserts
against a superseded source of truth rather than the live schema (R8). Needs
re-pointing at the database; deliberately not patched inside an unrelated commit.

## Not done, and owner-gated

**Nothing schedules `POST /ops/snapshot`.** Wiring a timer is deploy reach
(work_plan.md §6), so the endpoint is the mechanism and the scheduling is the
owner's act. Until then `ops_summary` shows a delta only for days it actually holds
— never extrapolated (D-OPEN-10).

## ⚠️ Review honestly

**I wrote and verified all of this**, which is exactly the arrangement this repo's
loop says not to trust. It needs a reviewer who is not me.

1081 backend projects tests (3 pre-existing red above) · tsc clean.

title: feat(WS-27bt/bu/ak-2): repaint RapidTool, name the people, add Tooltip
body:
**Stacked on #435** — base is `ws-27-project-ops`, so review that first. Three
commits, all design-layer.

Owner brief: *"Need good colours and contrast, make it look fresh and modern."*

---

## 1. `WS-27bt` — repaint RapidTool

The complaint looked like a component problem. It was twelve numbers.

`contrast.test.ts` already measured every ink pair and carried a baseline of
**seven known failures**, all in RapidTool, deferred with this note:

> *"fixing them means changing how the shipped product looks — a design decision
> for whoever owns the brand, not a side effect of adding a test."*

The owner has now made that decision, so they are fixed rather than excused.
`KNOWN_SHORTFALLS` is **empty for the first time**:

| pair | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `warningForeground` on `warning` | **1.50** | 5.55 |
| `successForeground` on `success` | 1.90 | 6.10 |
| `warning` on `card` | 1.57 | 5.55 |
| `success` on `card` | 1.99 | 6.10 |
| `accentForeground` on `accent` | 2.16 | 4.66 |
| `destructiveForeground` on `destructive` (light) | 3.59 | 6.47 |
| `destructiveForeground` on `destructive` (dark) | 3.63 | 5.12 |

1.50:1 is white text on bright yellow — not "slightly low", invisible, and it
shipped for as long as the product has existed.

### What actually made it look flat, which no test could see

`--background` and `--card` were **both `hsl(0 0% 100%)`**. A measured **1.00:1**.
A dashboard of seven cards was seven white rectangles on white, held apart by a
border at 1.23:1. Every ink pair on that screen passed. Two different questions —
"is this readable" and "is this a card" — and only the first had a fence.

### Two new fences (R7)

- **`mutedForeground` on `muted`** — the most common small-text pairing in the
  product, and the failing one at 4.33:1, while the same ink on a white card
  passed at 4.75 and made the token look fine. Measuring an ink against only its
  best background is how a palette ships unreadable in its most-used position.
- **"draws every card as a distinguishable surface"** — `max(elevation, border) ≥ 1.2`
  across all four themes × both modes. EITHER/OR because Material separates by
  tone and Fluent by a line; demanding both would force one idiom on a theming
  engine built to avoid that. ⚠️ Labelled a **design** floor, not WCAG — do not
  cite it as conformance.

### Judgement calls to challenge

**`warning` moved 47° → 32°.** Yellow cannot reach AA on white and still look
yellow; at the required lightness 47° reads olive-brown. Real brand change.
Sidebar tokens deliberately untouched — not in the failing set, and I would have
been guessing at the rail.

Tokens asserted **live in a browser** (fresh context per pair — a leaked init
script is how four "light" screenshots once came out dark and the run still
exited 0). `--cat-*` ramp re-measured against the new page: all 8 still clear AA.

---

## 2. `WS-27bu` — workload rows show a name

Every row read "kiruba", "jasim", "dev". Not a data problem: `/ops/workload`
already joined `app_user` for capacity and never selected `display_name`.

That join also filtered `WHERE weekly_capacity_hours IS NOT NULL` — so the naive
fix would have worked for whoever had capacity set and silently not for anyone
else. Filter removed; null hours were already handled downstream.

One `personLabel()` helper, not the same ternary at two call sites.

---

## 3. `WS-27ak-2` — Tooltip

Spec §9.4.2 item 2. Native `title` cannot be themed and **never opens on keyboard
focus**.

### 🔴 Finding: Base UI wires no ARIA association

Verified in a browser. With the tooltip open the trigger carries `id`,
`data-base-ui-tooltip-trigger`, `data-popup-open` — and **no `aria-describedby`**.
`Tooltip.Popup` renders a bare div with **no role and no id** to point at.

The wrapper sets `role="tooltip"` itself and that line is load-bearing — I found
the gap by removing it, believing I was letting the substrate own the ARIA, and
the test went 5/6 → 3/6.

**Consequence stated in the file:** an icon-only trigger MUST carry its own
`aria-label`. `describeOnly` is documented as **inert** rather than left looking
functional; wiring it properly is a separate slice.

Also re-derived from the package rather than recalled: **`delay` is not on
`Tooltip.Root`** — it is `Provider`'s, and nothing mounted one.

---

## Verified

tsc clean · **2067 frontend tests, 94 files** · 383 theme tests · both modes
captured and looked at.

⚠️ `FilterBar.tsx` carries one **pre-existing** eslint error
(`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, line 161) — confirmed identical with these
changes stashed.

Demo-data seeds live in untracked `.staging/seed/` and are not part of this diff.

title: WS-27bg: project run state, archive, and the indicator — plus the task-card data audit (D-PM-25…29)
body:
Owner-directed 2026-08-13: coloured run-state indicators per project (green ongoing / red stopped / orange paused, plus queued), the ability to archive a project and its tasks, and a data audit of the task card against the Tasks app.

**Migration 171.** R1 re-checked at PR time: 170 is still the highest on `main`, `main` has not moved since branching.

---

## The finding that matters most

`run_lifecycle_sweep` walked every root project with a policy and had **no project-status predicate anywhere**. That was harmless only for as long as `status` meant nothing — which is exactly how long it had been. The moment `on_hold` became real, a project paused for a quarter under a three-month close policy would have had its **entire open backlog moved to the cancelled lane**, written by `system:workflow:<id>` through `apply_status_transition` — so `completed_at` stamped, the `status_change` activity written, recurrence fired. Indistinguishable from a person doing it, and nobody would have found it for months.

Recurrence and agent dispatch carried the same hole. All three now consult one `is_runnable` rather than three copies of the rule.

## Second finding: the feature was half-built and invisible

`pm_projects.status` has been CHECKed, defaulted, indexed, validated on create **and** patch, returned by the tree read and declared in the frontend type **since migration 146** — and `ProjectTree.tsx` contained the string `status` zero times. `archived_at` existed and was never written; there was no archive endpoint, and the only removal path was an unrecoverable `DELETE` cascade.

That is the **fourth instance of one failure**, after `pm_task_statuses.color`, `estimate_mins` and (in the card audit below) `pm_task_types`. Each was stored correctly and reachable by the API, so every test passed and the only symptom was a UI plainer than its data.

---

## What ships

### Slice 1 — the axis, the endpoints, the guards

- Migration 171 widens `pm_projects.status` to the **union** of old and new values (R6 expand — the deploy applies migrations before restarting services, so the pre-restart gateway must keep validating `archived`). Its removal is a **named later release**, not folklore.
- **`archived_root_id`** makes archive reversible: archiving stamps the subtree with the id of the project the user actually archived, unarchiving clears exactly those rows. A subproject archived on its own **survives** its parent's restore; restoring a swept-in child is refused with the ancestor named.
- The write path validates against `RUN_STATES`, not `PROJECT_STATUSES`, so no caller can PATCH `status='archived'` and recreate the two-facts-one-column defect.
- **No `pm_tasks` row is written by any of it** (D-PM-26). The read path derives instead, under the existing `include_archived` flag.

### Slice 2 — the indicator and the first project-editing control

- `PROJECT_STATES` in `src/lib/statusAccent.ts` as a **closed lookup** that never falls through `resolveHue` — the trap being that `keywordHue` maps the literal word `active` to blue and `done` to green, i.e. the exact opposite of the ruling on two of five states.
- `effectiveState` derives a node's state from its ancestors **on the way down the render**, writing nothing. Inherited states draw at half emphasis and say so.
- The indicator replaces the generic folder glyph — in a tree where every row is a project, "this is a project" carried no information.
- A right-click menu gives the run-state picker and Archive/Unarchive on the promise-bound toast. **This app had no project-editing control at all before it.**

### Decisions recorded before building, so none is re-asked

| | |
|---|---|
| **D-PM-25** | Run state and archived are **two axes**. 146 stored one fact twice. |
| **D-PM-26** | Project state **derives** onto tasks, never cascades a write — D-PM-12 applied to a second surface, with the five costs enumerated. |
| **D-PM-27** | The hue map, **owner-ruled against the shipped vocabulary** — green means "running" on the tree and "finished" on the board beside it. Recorded as a decision to cite, not an inconsistency to repaint. |
| **D-PM-28** | Importance is **shared and already exists**; urgency is **derived**; only `leveraged` is personal. Overrides §7.5.1's row for `important`. |
| **D-PM-29** | Projects is the **master schema**; `/tasks` reproduces it and may only *add*. |

D-PM-28 surfaced a live conflict: `importance = 3` is labelled **"Urgent"** today, so shipping derived urgency beside it would put two disagreeing urgencies on one card. It is relabelled "Critical" in WS-27bh. The ruling also costs **one** new column rather than three — `pm_tasks.importance` is already a four-level scale, strictly richer than the boolean it would have sat beside.

---

## Verification

**R8 — a real Postgres 16, ladder replayed 01→171 into a throwaway database.**

- `tests/live/live_ws27bg.py` — **27 checks green**, driving the real endpoint functions.
- **Every automation check runs twice** — once paused (must not fire), once active (must) — because a guard that refuses everything passes a one-sided test.
- **Five mutants, each caught**, including replacing the subtree CTE with `id = :pid`, which turns four checks red and is the only thing that catches a quietly-non-recursive walk.
- The backfill was verified **on rows that actually exist**, not asserted empty: a database built to 170 and seeded with two `status='archived'` projects. Both moved; the one carrying a real 2024 filing date **kept it** rather than being overwritten by `now()`. Replay changed nothing.
- The new read `EXISTS` plans as a **join, never a per-row `SubPlan`** — a claim about shape, not duration (WS-27be's lesson).
- Also green **under FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY** with the generated phase-4 set applied. Not required by the current board state; worth knowing before it is.

**The four-theme sweep is now a test, not a promise.** `e2e/project-state.spec.ts` — **10 cases green** — drives real Chromium under Fluent, Material and Graphite and asserts five states resolve to five **distinct computed colours**, none transparent, inherited weaker, and five distinct **glyph paths** so the state survives a reader who cannot separate hues. Every slice since WS-27am owed this pass and several skipped it. Mutation-measured: making `on_hold` green turns it red in all three themes.

**Suites:** backend 5999 passed / 51 skipped · frontend 89 files / 2007 tests (baseline 1983) · `tsc` 0 · `next build` 0 · conformance green with **no new baseline entries**.

---

## Owed, and deliberately not claimed

- 🔴 **The count of `status='archived'` rows on prod.** Reading the live database is owner-gated reach (§6), so this is **asked of the owner at review**. The migration is correct at any population; claiming it affects no rows would be reporting a guess as a measurement.
- **The contraction** dropping `'archived'` from the CHECK and `PROJECT_STATUSES` — a later release, trigger named in the migration header.
- **Narrowed with reasons, not dropped:** Delete is deliberately *not* added to the new menu (an unrecoverable cascade that has never had a control stays as unreachable as it was); the bulk-close-on-Stop offer is deferred to its own slice; **rename is still owed** — a project still cannot be renamed.
- **Slice 3** (overdue across four predicates, My Work, calendar/timeline honest overflow) and **WS-27bh** (task type, derived urgency, recurring indicator, source badge) are minted and not in this PR.
- **Open owner question:** whether `actual_start`/`actual_end` are shared or personal — the difference between Projects being able to report estimate-vs-actual and not.

## A process note kept in the record

`git checkout` was used to revert a *mutation* in `tree.py` and reverted the **whole file**, because that one had no backup taken first. Caught immediately by `git diff --stat` and re-applied. Recorded in §11.35 because the cheap lesson is worth keeping: when mutation-testing, back up every file you touch and diff the tree afterwards rather than trusting the revert.

title: WS-28g/g-2: the person record, self-service editing, and People Center spec v2
body:
Closes the owner's 2026-08-13 directive on WS-28: *"set up all the personal details of a particular user with access control — an admin can edit every user, a person can edit only their own — primarily from the perspective of project management, so the AI can manage people, follow up, and say who can be assigned to what."*

Two shipped tickets and a spec rewrite. Nothing here is deployed, no flag is flipped, and nothing sends anything.

---

## The spec — `people_center_app.md` rewritten to v2

- **§3 — the field inventory.** Every field states the question it answers, its read tier and its write class. **§3.6 lists what is refused**: date of birth (`birthday` is `MM-DD`), compensation, performance ratings, home address, a free-text HR-notes field — each with a reason, so their absence is a decision rather than an oversight.
- **§4 — the access model.** Three read tiers (directory · HR · private), three write classes (admin · self · derived), and one self predicate: `lower(caller.email) = lower(person.email)`. It is safe **only because migration 148 made that column partially unique** — before it, "edit yourself" could have edited somebody else.
- **§5 — the sub-app roster**, including §5.7 rewritten as the people-management dashboard (projects per person, tasks with deadlines, behind/at-risk/overloaded/idle/on-track as arithmetic over dates, department rollup, idle↔behind rebalancing).
- **§6.5–§6.8 — the AI contract.** What a server-side heuristic may read versus what may be rendered to a human; a suggester that ranks candidates and **never assigns**; follow-ups **drafted and queued**, because sending is the existing owner-gated outbound-nudge item and this row may not flip it.
- **§12 — D-PC-1…D-PC-18.**

## WS-28g — the person profile and self-service editing

- **Migration 171** — 20 nullable columns, expand-half only (R6). No CHECK over live data, so the two new vocabularies are validated in the route against one shared tuple, exactly as `status` has been since 148.
- **`routes/people/fields.py`** — the one field-class authority. The fence (R7) **discovers every `gtd_people` column from the migrations** and fails an unclassified one, so a column added next month cannot default into the permissive answer.
- `GET /people/me` with three distinct states, `PATCH /people/{id}` authorized by class and **refusing by name** (a save that succeeds and discards half the form is worse than a refusal), self-service CV upload through the existing parse pipeline.
- `/people/me` and the person page render the same panels, **from the server's `editable_fields`** — the client never carries its own class map.

**Three silent defects found while building:** `create_person` accepted every profile field and stored none of them; the self write door was about to return the *admin* projection of whoever was patched; and the Center's icon had no Fluent/Material mapping and would have rendered in the wrong style.

## WS-28g-2 — your own profile is not behind the directory's gate

`feature:people` is `is_default false` and routes match by prefix, so `/people/me` inherited the directory's gate: **an ordinary colleague could not open their own profile.** The one surface built for "every person maintains their own record" was reachable only by people granted the org roster.

The rule now (D-PC-15): the directory is gated, your own row is not — the same argument that made `/access` the one ungated pane. The build improved on the plan: the ungated paths carry **no person id at all** (`/people/me`, `/people/me/resume`), so there is nothing to address but yourself. That is structural where "check the id is yours" is a check a refactor can drop. Ungated is not unchecked — the field classes apply unchanged.

`UNGATED_ROUTERS` joins the enforcement registry beside `GATED_ROUTERS`: *"deliberately open"* and *"nobody checked"* must not look the same to the next reader.

---

## Verification

```bash
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_people_profile.py tests/unit/test_people_directory.py \
              tests/unit/test_people_write.py tests/unit/test_people_key_shape.py \
              tests/unit/test_tasks_people_scoping.py \
              tests/unit/test_org_access_control.py tests/unit/test_org_access_enforcement.py
cd workbench/control_plane && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test && npx vitest run src/lib/theme/
```

- 144 hermetic cases · 2006 frontend tests · tsc and the theming conformance gate green.
- **36 live checks against a real Postgres 16** with all 171 migrations applied — `tests/live/live_ws28g.py`. Includes an ungranted member reading and saving their own row, and being refused their own department; the JSONB/array/date round trips a hermetic fake cannot see; and 171 applying idempotently on a re-run.

## Before merge

- ⚠️ **Re-check migration number 171** (R1) — another branch can take it while this sits.
- ⚠️ **`schema.generated.sql` regeneration is still due** — pre-existing debt, now one migration deeper. Needs a live database with the ladder applied (`infra/postgres/README.md` step 3).
- Deploying applies migration 171; that is the owner's act, not this PR's.

## Not in this PR

Specced and dispatchable, in dependency order: **WS-28p** work schedule → **WS-28q** display image → **WS-28k** absences → **WS-28j1/j2/j3** the dashboard. WS-28f's seats/roles write half stays owner-gated.

title: fix(WS-27bg): unify the three automation guards, answer D-PM-20, measure its R8 gate
body:
Follow-up to #437. One defect fix in already-merged code, the decisions that were owed, WS-27bi's R8 gate measured, and WS-27bj built.

> **Rebased onto `main` (`4934eb8`) on 2026-08-14.** Two conflicts, one of which git could not see — see **Merge with `main`** at the bottom. The R1 collision is the part worth reading.

## The defect: three guards, three different project rows

#437 gated automation on project run-state. Verifying that against a real database showed the three guards did not agree on *which* project they were asking about:

| Guard | Consulted |
|---|---|
| `run_lifecycle_sweep` | the **root** — too high |
| `recurrence` | the task's **immediate** project — too low |
| `agent_dispatch` | the task's **immediate** project — too low |

So a subtree between the root and the leaf was governed by nobody, and it failed in **both** directions: pausing a mid-tree project left its tasks still firing, while pausing only the root silenced descendants that were themselves active.

The fix puts one seam in `core.py` and points all three at it:

- `is_runnable(project)` — one row, knows nothing of ancestors
- `is_runnable_with_ancestors(db, project_id)` — `WITH RECURSIVE` walk reduced with `bool_and`, so a task runs only when its whole chain is runnable
- `_sweep_candidates` gained a `NOT EXISTS` chain predicate, so every task earns its own verdict rather than inheriting the root's

Recurrence deliberately does **not** stamp `recurrence_spawned_at` on the skip path — doing so would kill the series permanently at the moment of pause, rather than resuming it.

## The fence was dead, twice over

Worth calling out, because it nearly shipped as coverage that wasn't. The four new ancestor checks passed **with the recursion deleted** — the fixture tasks sat directly in the root, so pausing the root paused their own immediate project and the recursive walk was never exercised. Moving them into a grandchild and re-arming `recurrence_spawned_at` made re-mutation turn both checks red, as it should.

This is the second dead fence in this workstream. Both were found by deleting the code and watching the test stay green.

`tests/live/live_ws27bg.py` grew to 31 checks against real Postgres (R8), driving the real endpoint functions rather than fakes. Every automation check runs **twice** — paused must not fire, active must. `_projects_fakes.py` had to be taught the recursive verdict query explicitly; falling through would have answered `None` → `False` → "nothing is ever runnable", silently disabling recurrence and dispatch across the whole unit suite.

## D-PM-20 answered, WS-27bi minted

The board flagged this as fraught because migration 168's `updated_at` also serves the delta feed, so one semantic had to cover both. The audit dissolves that: there are exactly **two** `touch=False` sites, both stamping `recurrence_spawned_at`, and they are correct for *both* consumers at once — a bookkeeping stamp should neither wake a delta client nor invalidate a human's pending edit. No conflict to arbitrate.

Recorded shape: `If-Match:` → **412 with the current row** on mismatch. Two calls made deliberately —

- **No `version` column.** `updated_at` already does the job; a second monotonic fact about one row is the CLAUDE.md §5 defect, plus a migration and backfill for nothing.
- **Absent header still succeeds.** Advisory first, tightened later — R6's expand/contract discipline applied to an API instead of a schema.

## The R8 gate, measured (not assumed)

The ticket refused to let itself be built on an assumption about `timestamptz` precision. Measured on real Postgres 16 through asyncpg **and** `fastapi.encoders.jsonable_encoder`.

**Verdict: implementable.** Parse the token in Python, bind it as a `datetime`, let Postgres compare it as `timestamptz`. Exact for all three token shapes — ordinary microseconds, trailing-zero microseconds, and `microsecond == 0`.

Two fences the measurement moved, neither of which is visible from reading the code:

- 🔴 **A naive (offset-stripped) token silently compares `True`.** asyncpg reinterprets a tz-less `datetime` in the session zone, which on a UTC box happens to match. A client that drops the offset gets a precondition that *appears* to work and would start mis-comparing under any session-TZ change — exactly the "reports safety it does not have" failure this decision exists to prevent. Must be rejected with 400.
- 🔴 **`::text` and the JSON encoder disagree.** Postgres renders the trailing-zero case `.1`; the encoder renders `.100000`. Equal as `timestamptz`, different as strings. A string comparison passes every test written against ordinary microseconds and fails on a trailing zero.

## A finding for the board — `now()` can move backwards

Reproduced on a real database while measuring:

```
T1 txn now() = 09:22:18.560649      (starts first)
T2 txn now() = 09:22:18.762134      (starts 201ms later, writes, commits FIRST)
after T2 commit : 09:22:18.762134
after T1 commit : 09:22:18.560649   <-- WENT BACKWARDS by 201ms
```

`now()` is the **transaction-start** timestamp, so a transaction opening early and committing late stamps a time earlier than a row already written by a newer, faster-committing transaction.

**Harmless to the precondition** — an exact comparison still differs, so the client still gets its 412 and refetches. That is precisely why this does not expand WS-27bi's scope.

**It is a real gap in migration 168's keyset cursor**: a delta client whose cursor has advanced past the newer value will never be handed the row stamped behind it, and that change leaves the stream silently. Pre-existing and already merged, so per CLAUDE.md §5 it is recorded rather than refactored — the fix changes the delta feed's contract and owes its own row and its own decision.

## Merge with `main` (2026-08-14)

**1. `work_plan.md` — a union, not a choice.** Both sides edited the same table: this branch extended the WS-27 row through 2026-08-14, while `main` replaced the WS-28 row wholesale as #438/#440/#441 landed People Center g/g-2/p/q/k/j1/j2. Kept this branch's WS-27 row (a strict continuation of `main`'s, which ended at 2026-08-13) and took `main`'s WS-28 row over this branch's stale copy.

**2. 🔴 An R1 migration collision that merged clean.** This branch's `172_projects_org_vocabularies.sql` and `main`'s `172_people_profile.sql` both claimed **172** — different files, different trees, so git merged them side by side without a word. Renumbered to **175**, after `main`'s 172/173/174.

The vocabularies suite was already immune by construction: it finds the migration by **content** (`"org-wide vocabularies"`), never by number, precisely so a renumber that changed nothing does not turn it red. That held. The prose references in `core.py`, `tasks/people.py` and the two suites were updated to match; `live_ws28g.py`'s "migration 172" is `main`'s `people_profile` and is correctly left alone.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/ --ignore=tests/unit/test_memory_integration.py -k "not calendar" -q
6540 passed, 168 skipped
```

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. The ladder replay is CI's own job and is the authority on the renumber — replaying it locally goes through the deploy runner, which is owner-gated.

Live suite runs against a throwaway Postgres 16 cluster with the ladder replayed 01→175.

## Not in this PR

- **WS-27bi's endpoint change is not built** — this PR takes it as far as the measurement, which its own done-when puts first.
- **Still owed on WS-27bg**: rename (a project still cannot be renamed), the bulk-close-on-Stop offer, the Delete affordance, and slice 3's overdue suppression.
- **Still owed on WS-27bj**: the admin surface for managing org-wide vocabularies — which is also what would let one be edited or retired.

## Owner-gated, unchanged

Deploying #437 and this (migrations 171 and 175 are not applied on any box), and the `status='archived'` row count on prod.

title: feat(WS-28p/q/k): the working week, the display image, and availability
body:
Stacked on #438 (WS-28g / g-2) — **review that one first**; this PR's base is
`claude/people-app-spec-build-fpcdwo`, so the diff shown here is only the three
tickets below.

Together they are everything the people-management dashboard (WS-28j) needs to
compute a status pill: contracted hours, real availability, and a face on the row.

| Ticket | What lands |
|---|---|
| **WS-28p** | The company's working week — org policy, person override, derived hours |
| **WS-28q** | The display image — one server-side re-encode instead of four validation rules |
| **WS-28k** | Availability & absences — the hours somebody actually has before a deadline |

---

## WS-28p — the working week

Owner-directed: *"number of days that the company works, number of hours they're
supposed to work in a day, number of shifts… so accordingly even the calendar of
the personal center can set itself up."*

**No migration.** The org policy is a row in `org_settings` (migration 151's
existing key→JSON store); the person override is the `working_hours` column
WS-28g already shipped. Three layers, one direction:

```
org policy       org_settings['work_schedule']    the company's week
person override  gtd_people.working_hours         their exceptions
effective        computed, stored nowhere
```

`gateway/work_schedule.py` is the one model — a leaf module outside both route
packages, because `routes/people/*` imports from `routes/tasks/*` and never the
reverse, and the calendar needs to read it too.

- `contracted_hours_per_week` is now **derived** (D-PC-18). The typed
  `capacity_hours_per_week` stays (R6 — the importer writes it) and is *flagged*
  when it disagrees rather than silently corrected.
- **D-PC-16** settles the seam collision with the calendar: `working_hours`
  (People) and `gtd_settings.day_start_hour` (Calendar) answer different
  questions. People **seeds** Calendar once, at first read, and never mirrors it.
- `PUT /people/schedule` is a **dry run first** — the impact panel shows how many
  people's contracted hours change before you save.

## WS-28q — the display image

Owner-directed: *"a strict policy when it comes down to the size of the image so
that random image sizes are not uploaded"*, plus a crop.

**What is stored is what the server produced, never what the browser sent**
(D-PC-17). Every upload is decoded, centre-cropped square, resized to exactly
256×256 and re-encoded; the uploaded bytes are discarded. One decision removes
four problems instead of validating for them: size drift cannot exist, weight is
bounded by the output, the crop is enforced server-side even for a direct API
caller, and EXIF/colour profiles/trailing payloads do not survive a re-encode.

Three things measured rather than assumed, each of which would otherwise have
shipped as a defect:

- **MuPDF renders SVG** — `fitz.open(filetype="image")` opens one happily, so the
  decoder is not a type check. Bytes are sniffed against magic numbers first and
  SVG is refused by name.
- **The crop must be fractional** — a 1000×400 pixel image opens as a 750×300
  *point* page; a pixel rectangle produced a 256×192 "square".
- **`Matrix(scale, scale)` is not exact** — MuPDF rounds outward and a zoomed crop
  came back 257×257. `Rect.torect` maps the clip onto the target box exactly.

JPEG rather than WebP as the spec first said: the property that matters is the
re-encode, not the container, and PyMuPDF (already a gateway dependency) cannot
write WebP. Recorded in the migration.

## WS-28k — availability & absences

`working_hours_between(schedule, from, to, absences)` is the function WS-28j will
call. Fractional, because a `partial` reduces a day rather than removing it; a
full absence beats an overlapping partial; two overlapping partials take the
smallest.

**Availability, not leave management — with a fence.** The table is facts and
nothing else: no approver, no status, no balance, no accrual, no entitlement. A
test greps the migration for each of those words, because this becomes leave
management one reasonable-looking column at a time. Absences are **self-writable**
(requiring an admin to type them is how the data ends up missing, and then every
capacity figure reading it is quietly wrong); the delete is scoped
`AND person_id = …`, and that clause is the control, not belt-and-braces.

Two read tiers on one feature: the bare "away until the 20th" is **directory**
tier and is resolved for the whole page in one query, not one per row; the spans,
notes and hours-left figure are **HR** tier.

---

## Two fences were refined rather than worked around

- **The tenancy ratchet caught the new table.** `gtd_person_absences` declares
  `organization_id REFERENCES organization` on day one, defaulting from the
  session GUC so no call site passes it; an unbound insert fails the NOT NULL.
  One non-obvious constraint found the hard way: `REFERENCES` must come *before*
  `DEFAULT`, because the ratchet matches the two with no comma between them and
  every form of `current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)` contains one. Written
  the other way round, a table that **is** scoped reads as unscoped.
- **D-PC-15's fence** forbade any path parameter on the ungated router — a good
  proxy until a route needed to address a child row. `/me/absences/{absence_id}`
  names a *span*, not a person, so the fence now asserts the invariant itself
  plus the stronger half it stood in for: every ungated endpoint resolves the
  person through the self predicate.

## Migrations

> ⚠️ **Renumbered at merge (R1).** These shipped from this branch as 171–173, and
> the merge-time re-check found main had taken 171 for `171_projects_run_state.sql`
> (PR #437) while this stack sat open — the fourth collision in two weeks. The
> renumber to **172–174** landed with the stack's top PR (#441, commit `efc4f90`)
> before anything deploys, so production's ledger only ever sees the final names.

| # | Table | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| 172 | `gtd_people` | 20 nullable profile columns, expand half only |
| 173 | `gtd_people` | `avatar TEXT` + `avatar_updated_at` |
| 174 | `gtd_person_absences` | new, tenant-scoped, `ON DELETE CASCADE` |

All three are expand-only and nullable (R6) — old code meets new schema.

## Verification

- **Hermetic:** 60 (p) + 45 (q) + 41 (k) new backend cases; 1040 backend tests in
  the people/tasks/calendar/tenancy sweep.
- **Live, against a real Postgres 16 with the full ladder applied (R8):**
  `tests/live/live_ws28{g,p,q,k}.py` — 29 / 24 / 16 / 15 checks, all four re-run
  green together. They cover what a fake cannot: the tenant key defaulting from
  the GUC and failing closed without it, the CHECKs actually firing, real `date`
  binding, the scoped delete, `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and the data-URI round trip
  through the TEXT column.
- **Frontend:** 2063 vitest tests, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, theming conformance
  suite green.
- The q hermetic tests run the **real** encoder against real images — a fake
  codec would say nothing about the one that ships.

## Before merge

- [x] **R1** — re-checked at merge; collision found and renumbered (see Migrations above).
- [ ] `schema.generated.sql` regeneration is still due (owner's act).
- [ ] Deploying applies the People migrations 172–174; that is the owner's act, not this PR's.

title: feat(WS-28j1/j2): the workload dashboard and its department rollup
body:
Stacked on #440 (WS-28p/q/k), which is itself stacked on #438 — **review those first**;
this PR's base is `claude/ws-28p-work-schedule`, so the diff shown here is the two
dashboard tickets.

The surface the whole People Center spec serves. Owner-directed: *"the person looking at
this dashboard should have all the intelligence and needs to be able to actually make those
decisions."* So every figure a decision needs is on the row — projects, open tasks, next
deadline, committed vs contracted hours, the unestimated count, last activity — and the
pill states its own reason instead of asking anyone to take it on trust.

**No migration.** It is a *read* over the Projects tables (`pm_tasks`,
`pm_task_assignees`, `pm_task_statuses`, `pm_projects`, `pm_activities`) joined to the
People record on `lower(email)`. The classification lives in one pure module,
`gateway/workload.py`, so j3's suggester and §5.9's Center landing project it rather than
counting again — a projection that recomputes a number the app already renders is how two
numbers start disagreeing where nobody can see them.

---

## WS-28j1 — the person rows and the five pills

| Pill | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Behind** | ≥1 open task whose `due_at` is in the past |
| **At risk** | ≥1 open task due within the horizon whose *cumulative* remaining estimate exceeds the working hours before it |
| **Overloaded** | committed hours for the week > contracted hours |
| **Idle** | no open task, **or** committed below a quarter of contracted |
| **On track** | none of the above |

One pill by precedence; every applicable flag travels beside it.

**Five things the build settled:**

- **"At risk" is cumulative, and carries overdue work** (D-PC-19). Three twelve-hour tasks
  due Tuesday, with sixteen hours before Tuesday, is a week that does not fit — and
  per-task arithmetic calls all three fine, because none alone exceeds sixteen. A task that
  missed last Tuesday still has to be done, so its hours stay in the sum; dropping them
  makes every later deadline look reachable, which is how a slipping week becomes a
  surprise. Undated tasks are excluded: they carry no deadline to be late for, so counting
  them would pill somebody whose backlog is merely large.
- **"Partial" names the viewer's scope; the hidden delta is never computed** (D-PC-20).
  Reporting "12 of 20" means running the query without the scope, which is the query the
  scope exists to forbid. One integer per person is still a leak, and it is the one
  somebody would probe with.
- **One pill by precedence, every flag beside it** (D-PC-21). "Behind *and* overloaded" is
  a different conversation from "behind", and one word cannot say so.
- **Four aggregates, not four per person.** Every figure comes from one of four statements
  keyed by `lower(assignee)`, plus one absence query for the page. Built the obvious way,
  an eighty-person roster is three hundred round trips.
- **An assignee with no roster row still appears** — one mechanism covering agents
  (D-PM-4), people who left, and addresses nobody added. Work assigned to a departed
  colleague is invisible everywhere else in the product.

## WS-28j2 — the department rollup

Per department and then for the org: headcount, Σ contracted against Σ committed, people
in each pill, who is away this week, people with no open work at all, and **the spread**.

**No new query.** `rollup()` is handed `[r.model_dump() for r in rows]` — the exact payload
the client is about to receive — so §5.9's *"a projection, not a second count"* is a
property of the code path rather than a claim about it. The fence asserts **identity**
(`org["contracted_hours"] == sum(rows)`), not closeness; a second one greps the module for
`db.execute` / `SELECT` / `await`, because the cheapest way to introduce a second count is
a convenience `db` parameter on a pure module.

- **Strain is a share, not a count.** Three behind out of four is a different situation from
  three out of forty. Departments sort by it because *"a rollup nobody can act on is a
  table"* — an ordering of work, computed from pill counts, with no score on the panel.
- **The spread is stated in hours and names both people.** *"Priya has 46h due this week,
  Ravi has 6h — a 40h gap"* is arguable and actionable; a bare percentage gap is a score
  with two names attached. Computed only over rows whose hours mean something, or somebody
  holding thirty un-estimated tasks arrives at the bottom of it as though they were free.
  `None` under two usable rows: a spread over one person is not a spread, and "0h" there
  reads as a balanced team.
- **Agents are excluded and the exclusion is reported** (`org.agents`). Headcount is
  people; a silent omission is how a total quietly stops adding up.

`away_this_week` joins the person row for this — a wider window than `away` (today only),
because somebody back tomorrow and somebody leaving on Thursday are both answers to *"can I
give them a deadline this week"*.

---

## The tenant boundary does not rest on an owner's flip

The grant closure is applied to the `data:org:read` caller **too**, not short-circuited to
`TRUE`. `project_clause` already answers the tenant subquery for that caller (what WS-29b
changed it for), and the shortcut would make this endpoint's tenant boundary depend on
FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY being *enforced* — which is the owner's act.

Measured on a scratch cluster that has no FORCE RLS: with the shortcut, a second
organization's task lands on the row — **3 → 4 open tasks, 86h → 185h**. The live harness
asserts it both ways.

⚠️ `/people/{id}/work` still takes that shortcut. That is a finding for the board, not a
pattern to copy, and it is deliberately not fixed in this diff.

## Two fences were corrected, both self-inflicted

Each was a fence written over raw source, and each failed on correct code:

- The **no-ranking fence** (D-PC-14) grepped for `leaderboard`, `percentile` and their
  cousins — and fired on the docstrings that name those words in order to explain why the
  product refuses them. A fence that punishes the explanation makes deleting the reasoning
  the cheapest way to go green. It now strips comments and docstrings and matches only what
  runs, and it carries **its own fence**: four plausible guilty lines that must still trip
  it.
- The **route-order fence** read the live `router` — whose order inside pytest is the test
  session's import order, not the application's. Its first working version then compared
  bare paths, so `PATCH /people/{person_id}` in front of `GET /people/dashboard` read as a
  collision it is not. It now probes a fresh process and matches on path **and** method,
  stated as a general rule over the package so the next literal path inherits it.

Also corrected: **D-PC-17 said the avatar is WebP.** The build shipped JPEG and said so in
its commit; the decision row did not, and a decision row that disagrees with the code is
worse than none.

## Verification

- **Hermetic:** 64 backend cases + 38 vitest; 1728 backend tests in the
  people/projects/tenancy sweep; 2101 frontend tests; `npx tsc --noEmit`, eslint on the new
  files, and the theming conformance suite all clean.
- **Live, against a real Postgres 16 with the full ladder applied (R8):**
  `tests/live/live_ws28j.py`, 36 checks — the aggregates, the `date`-against-`TIMESTAMPTZ`
  and `make_interval(days => :n)` binds, the grant closure genuinely excluding an ungranted
  project, the visibility clause composing onto a `COALESCE(…)`, an agent surviving the
  whole path, the rollup's totals being the rows' sums over real data, and the cross-tenant
  check above. All five People harnesses (g, p, q, k, j) re-run green together.
- The scoped-viewer live assertion **first passed for the wrong reason** — a viewer with no
  `app_user` row binds `vis_org = NULL` and sees nothing at all. That is documented in the
  harness rather than left as a trap for the next person.

## Not in this ticket

WS-28j3 (rebalancing suggestions) is spec'd and dispatchable on top of this. Nothing here
writes an assignment (D-PC-13).
