title: feat(WS-31/30/32): the Control Plane, the billing console, and the organisation's own mark
body:
Three workstreams that were built as one chain, because each one needed the seam the previous one laid: **WS-31** built the Control Plane, **WS-30** put a console and a billing product on top of it, **WS-32** gave the organisation its own mark. 61 files, +10,634/−144.

## WS-31 — the Platform Control Plane

| Ticket | What landed |
|---|---|
| CP-0 | Auth **fails closed**. Previously an unconfigured auth environment failed *open* (D33). |
| CP-1 | Orgs, seats, credits and metering — `infra/platform/001_control_plane.sql` and `platform_api`. |
| CP-3 | The API key resolves the tenant, and nothing else may. Rebuilt after verification returned FAIL. |
| CP-4 | The Router — tier resolution and unpriced pass-through, plus a credential-exfiltration hole verification found and closed. |
| CP-2a | Account lifecycle, with Fracktal as customer zero (D36). |

Decisions recorded: **D32–D36**.

## WS-30 — the billing product and its console

D37 (the AI-credit product) and D38 (billing management + the tax invoice we had wrongly outsourced), then the first UI for the platform: the billing console at `/settings/billing`.

## WS-32 — organisation identity

- **OI-1** — logo upload. `gateway/image_probe.py` identifies PNG/JPEG/WebP from **magic bytes**, never the caller's declared MIME type, and the stored `data:` URI is rebuilt from what the server derived. SVG and PDF are named in the rejection message. Bounds: 128 KB, 32–2048 px per edge, 0.5–8.0 aspect.
- **OI-3a** — first-paint branding. The shell used to render *our* mark and swap to the customer's ~900 ms later, which inverts the feature. Now cached and revalidated behind the paint. `localStorage` is not a trust boundary, so a cache hit is validated exactly like a network body.

## What is NOT verified, stated plainly

- **`e2e/org-branding.spec.ts` is entirely `test.fixme`.** The app does not hydrate under Playwright in dev — measured: zero `/api/**` requests, a failing HMR handshake. An earlier run reported **9 of 18 passing** and every one of those was a fallback or outage case, which an un-hydrated page renders anyway; they would pass with the client bundle deleted. The partial pass was the dangerous part, so the file asserts nothing rather than asserting that.
- **OI-2 (tenant-scoped `org_settings`) is not done and is blocked on MT-1b.** `org_settings` has a single-column PK on `key`, so branding is org-wide today. This is a hard prerequisite for customer #2, and the source comment that claimed tenancy "comes free here" was false and has been corrected in place.
- `infra/platform/*.sql` is **not** applied by the deploy — the Control Plane database is Supabase (D34) and remains owner-gated, so `platform_api` ships inert.

## Fences added

`_required_permissions` reads the `require_permission` closure and asserts `admin:settings:manage` gates the branding writes — the 30 tests before it called handlers directly and would have passed with the gate deleted. It went red first, then was proved by mutation. Same treatment for the `captionClipped` probe, which originally matched the outer flex container and so could not fail in the case it was written for.

The BFF body bound was `content-length` only — a header a chunked-encoding caller simply declines to send, which is the attack its own comment claimed it stopped. It now bounds the **stream**.

body:
Board-only. No code changes. `work_plan.md` is the single current-state authority (CLAUDE.md §1), and three rows went stale within hours of being written.

## WS-31 — CP-0/1/2a/3/4 merged in #442 (`4934eb8`)

Records the ladder defect that **opening the PR is what caught**: five R8 suites each transcribed their own list of `infra/platform/00N_*.sql`, three stopped at `003`, and a real Postgres answered `column "client_ref" of relation "usage_event" does not exist` — from inside an assertion about *billing*, several steps from the missing migration. Fixed by discovery in the same PR (`d8f52e9`).

It had been wrong since `004` landed. The suites carrying the stale copy were the ones that would have caught it.

## WS-32 — OI-1 and OI-3a merged

Two corrections to what the row claimed:

- `scripts/theme-check.mjs` is no longer a second Playwright seam — folded into `e2e/org-branding.spec.ts`.
- **The folded spec cannot run.** The whole file is `test.fixme`, 18 skipped. Recorded with the part that matters: **9 of 18 had reported green**, and every one was a fallback or outage case that an un-hydrated page renders anyway — they would pass with the client bundle deleted.

Also recorded: the e2e suite had not booted at all since CP-0 (`8f6eb79`), because `next start` sets `NODE_ENV=production` and `authPosture` grants its dev bypass only when NODE_ENV is *not* production. Nothing noticed because nothing runs `e2e/` in CI. The next measurement is written into the spec's banner so nobody theorises about it a third time.

## WS-27 — merged as #439 (`aa0d7e3`), plus the R1 collision

`172_projects_org_vocabularies.sql` and main's `172_people_profile.sql` both claimed **172** — different filenames in different subtrees, so there was no textual conflict to show anyone. Renumbered to 175.

## The correction worth reading

**I first wrote into the board that the R1 guard could not see this. Then I tested it, and it can.** Putting the duplicate back turns `test_migration_prefixes.py` red.

The real gap is *when* it runs. `actions/checkout` resolves `refs/pull/N/merge` on a `pull_request` event; GitHub does not compute that ref for a conflicted PR; and #439 sat `dirty` reporting **`check_runs: 0`** — no jobs at all. So the guard was never handed a tree containing both files.

> **A conflicted PR runs no checks — so the window where a cross-branch collision is most likely is exactly the window where nothing is watching**, and the collision surfaces only once someone resolves the conflict, by which point they are hand-editing the very tree that hides it.

That is a sharper finding than "the guard is blind," and the opposite conclusion. It would have gone into the board as fact if the claim hadn't been checked.

## One pattern worth copying

The vocabularies suite finds its migration by **content** (`"org-wide vocabularies"`), never by number — written that way on purpose so a renumber that changed nothing cannot turn it red. It survived the rename untouched. The other migration-mirroring suites should do the same.

## Verification

`uv run pytest tests/unit/test_migration_prefixes.py -q` → 4 passed. Docs-only diff, so `pr-check` skips on `paths-ignore`.

title: feat(WS-28h/d): structured skills & credentials, and the capability search over them
body:
Two tickets, continuing the People Center buildout the morning's #438/#440/#441 merged.
Base is `main`; the branch already carries a merge of today's main (#439/#442/#444), so the
diff is only these tickets plus that resolution.

## WS-28h — structured skills & credentials (migration 176)

`skills TEXT[]` answers "do they know Python" and nothing else. The questions assignment
actually asks are HOW WELL, HOW RECENTLY, and ON WHAT EVIDENCE — one row per (person,
skill) in `gtd_person_skills`, plus `gtd_person_credentials` for "is this person actually
qualified to sign this off". Both tenant-scoped on day one.

**D-PC-6 as a mechanism:** the array does not go away — four live consumers read it — it
becomes a projection. `gateway/person_skills.py` (a leaf, because People routes AND the
tasks-side résumé ingest both write it) ends every write path in one `project()` inside the
caller's transaction:

- the structured replace (new editor on My Profile and the person page);
- the flat `PATCH {skills}` — now *reconciles* the table: retained skills keep their
  level, so the older door cannot strip what the newer one set;
- the résumé merge — add-only (a CV is evidence for what it contains and silent about
  everything else), now also writing credentials, deduped so re-uploading cannot double a
  degree.

**Found & fixed:** every hand-typed skill in the product rendered as "extracted from a
résumé" — the backend writes `manual`, the UI's `skillOrigin` tested the literal `stated`
which nothing ever wrote, and its own test had pinned the wrong word.

**Measured, not assumed:** batch inserts share `now()`, so the projection orders
deterministically-alphabetically, not by insertion (the live harness corrected the first
docstring); the parser's boundary regex eats a trailing period (`solidworks.`) — the same
lookahead protecting `node.js`.

## WS-28d — capability search (`/people/search`)

Three signals, each labelled on the result with its own points: structured skills weighted
by **level × recency** · the **newest CV's matching line, quoted**
(`DISTINCT ON … ORDER BY uploaded_at DESC`, verified live) · **semantic cosine**,
best-effort with its absence *reported*, never silent.

**Outside §5.5's EVAL-LOCK by construction:** no LLM ranking prompt exists — arithmetic
over named constants, recomputable by hand from the page. Fences: the module greps clean of
model calls; no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (D-PC-13 — a suggester with an UPDATE has become an
assigner); the client contains no `.sort(` (the server's order IS the ranking). Gated
whole-surface on `admin:members:read` (§4.2's oracle rule). Every result carries load,
contracted hours, and availability warnings — the *reader* decides, not the ranker.
`score_skills` is exported pure for WS-28j3's suggester: one ranker, not two answers.

## R1 fired again — fifth collision

While this branch was open, #439 merged `175_projects_org_vocabularies.sql` onto main.
Our `175_people_skills.sql` renumbered to **176** (commit `c4bbe81`), every reference
updated as counted replacements — including, caught during the merge resolution, the board
row's `(mig 175` spelling that the `migration 175|175_people` sweep pattern could not see.

## Merge conflict, resolved

`project-docs/work_plan.md` — the recurring region. Main's side brought the
WS-27bg/#439/WS-30/31/32 records plus a stale WS-28 row; ours brought the WS-28 row's
`…+h+d` update. Resolution (commit `206a78e`): **main's material wholesale, our WS-28 row
swapped in**, with the resolve script asserting marker-free + exactly-one-row + no stale
migration number *before* writing.

## Verification (all on the merged tree)

- **1854 backend** tests in the people/projects/tenancy sweep; **2206 frontend**; tsc,
  eslint, theming conformance all green.
- **All seven live harnesses** (`live_ws28{g,p,q,k,j,h,d}.py`) green together against a
  real Postgres 16 carrying the merged ladder — main's 175 applied *before* our 176.
- h: 28 hermetic + 14 vitest + 21 live · d: 18 hermetic + 10 vitest + 12 live.

- [ ] `schema.generated.sql` regeneration still due (owner's act).
- [ ] Deploying applies migration 176; that is the owner's act, not this PR's.

title: feat(D39): carry pending work across sessions in the repo, not in memory
body:
Owner-directed: *"I don't want to remember anything… create a system within the documentation and agent harness so that old sessions can put information into and remove information from the system prompt as needed."*

**No product code.** One hook, one command, one queue file, and the three documents that route to them.

## What lands

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `project-docs/HANDOFF.md` | The queue, seeded with the **10 items** currently open (6 agent, 4 owner-gated) |
| `.claude/hooks/session-handoff.mjs` | SessionStart hook — injects the open entries. Fails open and silent |
| `.claude/hooks/session-handoff.test.mjs` | 13 cases, **blocking in CI** beside `plan-guard`'s |
| `.claude/commands/handoff.md` | `/handoff check \| add \| done \| end` |
| `work_plan.md` D39 · `INDEX.md` · `CLAUDE.md` row 5a | The routing |

## The constraint that shaped every other decision

`work_plan.md` §2 is **the only current-state authority**. A mutable queue that *also* described state would be the CLAUDE.md §5 defect in its purest form: two descriptions of one truth, and the **stale** one trusted precisely because it is the one loaded into every prompt.

So an entry may never restate state. It carries a **Check** — a cheap read-only command whose output says whether it is still real. That inverts the failure mode: a stale entry costs one command and gets deleted, and it can never be *quietly* believed, because believing it requires running something that would have contradicted it.

## That is not theoretical — the mechanism caught itself three times

Running the ten Checks against `main`, which the protocol demands before other work, found **three defects in the Checks themselves**:

1. **H-9 pointed at `docs/schema.generated.sql`.** The file is in `infra/postgres/`. A `docs/` check would have silently "passed" on a missing file — a green light meaning nothing.
2. **H-1 restated a migration range** ("171–175"). It was stale within the hour — 176 landed inside it. H-1 now *derives* the range and carries a note saying why it must never name one.
3. **`ls infra/postgres/*.sql | tail -1` answers `schema.generated.sql`**, which sorts alphabetically after every numbered migration and is not one. Both H-1 and H-9 used it, so both were comparing a file to itself. Now `[0-9]*.sql | sort -V`.

Three wrong Checks, three commands, three repairs. Under any scheme where the file simply *asserted* status, all three would have read as true indefinitely.

## Why a hook rather than a line in `CLAUDE.md`

`CLAUDE.md` is the router: edited when the architecture changes, which is rarely. A queue changes every session. A mutable queue inside a stable document makes the stable document stop being trusted as stable — and a stale queue entry there is **indistinguishable from doctrine**.

The hook deliberately does **not** execute the Checks. Running commands out of a markdown file at session start would be an arbitrary-execution seam pointed straight at the one file every session loads, and a hanging check would block startup. The session runs them itself, under the permission model, having read them.

## R7 — the fence covers the silent failures, not the happy path

A broken listing is obvious the first time someone opens a session. These are not:

- **no `HANDOFF.md`** → must start normally. This runs in every session of every checkout; a crash here is a repo nobody can open.
- **garbage / half-edited file** → must not throw. It is edited by hand, by agents, and by merge resolution, so it *will* be malformed sometimes.
- **content below `# DONE`** → must never resurface. If the parser read past it, deliberately closed work would come back as live work every session.
- **`[OWNER]` surviving into the injected text** → that word is the difference between reporting a gate and walking through one.

```
node .claude/hooks/session-handoff.test.mjs   → 13/13 passed
node .claude/hooks/plan-guard.test.mjs        → all 21 cases passed  (unaffected)
```

## Also in this PR

The merge of the closed #443 branch. Two conflicts, both resolved toward `main`'s version because it was the fuller record — including a finding worth reading on its own:

> **A conflicted PR runs no checks at all.** `actions/checkout` resolves `refs/pull/N/merge`, and GitHub does not compute that ref while a PR is dirty. #439 sat `dirty` and reported `check_runs: 0` — no jobs ran. The R1 migration-prefix guard is *not* blind (verified by putting the duplicate back: it goes red); it was simply never handed a tree containing both files.

So the window in which a cross-branch collision is most likely is exactly the window in which nothing is watching. Filed as **H-10** rather than fixed here — changing CI triggers is its own change.

## What this changes for you

A new session opens with this already in context, no memory required:

```
## Handoff queue — 10 open (6 agent, 4 owner-gated)
- H-1 · Deploy: `main` is many migrations ahead of every box · [OWNER]
- H-2 · Count archived projects on prod BEFORE migration 171 applies · [OWNER]
- H-3 · Rotate the production SSH credentials pasted into a session · [OWNER]
…
```

⚠️ **Until this merges, the system does not exist for anyone.** The hook only fires from `main`, so the next session starts blind — which is the precise failure it was built to end.

## Owner-gated, unchanged

The four `[OWNER]` entries are `work_plan.md` §6 gates and stay yours: deploying, the pre-171 archived count, **rotating the SSH credentials** (a secret pasted into a transcript is a disclosed secret, even though it was refused and never used), and flipping `PROJECTS_ORG_VOCABULARIES`.

title: docs(WS-32): run the hydration measurement — three hypotheses dead, one left with a mechanism
body:
The banner asked for one measurement and said not to guess between the hypotheses. Ran it, then kept going until each was either eliminated or had a named mechanism.

## Eliminated — each by measurement, not reasoning

| Hypothesis | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Playwright's request interception | ✗ **Zero routes registered gives the identical result** — 0 `/api/**` requests, no hydration. The leading suspect is innocent. |
| The container's HTTP proxy | ✗ `--no-proxy-server` changes nothing. |
| A truncated RSC stream | ✗ `/chat` answers 200 in ~94 ms, 95 KB, closes cleanly, ends in `</body></html>`, carries its `__next_f.push` payload. |

(`proxy: {server: "direct://"}` only breaks navigation outright with `ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED` — not a control, and the banner says so.)

## What the page actually does

39 JS chunks load, **zero requests fail**, no page errors, `window.next` and the React DevTools hook both defined — React creates a root and attaches event delegation.

But of **422 elements, zero carry `__reactFiber` or `__reactProps`**, and `localStorage` is entirely empty, so not one mount effect ran. The root is created; the tree is never hydrated.

## I nearly reversed a correct finding on bad evidence

A mid-way probe counted keys starting with `__react`, found 6, saw `window.next` and a DevTools hook, and read that as *"it hydrates — the board is wrong."*

Six was too few for a 422-element shell, so I measured `__reactFiber` specifically: **zero**. A handful of `__reactEvents` on the container is exactly what an *un*-hydrated React root looks like.

Reporting one step earlier would have overwritten a correct finding with a false correction — the fifth of this session, and the only one that would have gone the wrong way.

## The one left, with a mechanism

The client opens `ws://<host>/_next/webpack-hmr` and the handshake fails `ERR_INVALID_HTTP_RESPONSE`, while the server is **Next 16.2.6 on Turbopack** serving a `[turbopack]_browser_dev_hmr-client` chunk — a webpack-shaped endpoint against a Turbopack dev server.

Recorded as a **lead, not a diagnosis**: a dead HMR socket does not normally block hydration, so whether this is the cause or the loudest symptom is the next measurement.

## Scope

No behaviour change. The suite stays `test.fixme` — this narrows the hunt, it does not fix it. `tsc` clean.

title: feat(WS-28e/j3): the directory-backed assignee picker, and the rebalancing suggestions
body:
Two tickets continuing the People Center buildout (#438/#440/#441/#447 all merged earlier).

## WS-28e — the assignee picker is directory-backed (§6.1/§6.4)

`GET /projects/assignees` + `AssigneePicker` in the task panel: people **and agents** in one
list under two headings (D-PM-4), each row carrying top skills, the derived load with its
unestimated caveat, and §6.1's line — away until the 20th, more committed than contracted,
engagement ending before the due date. Three rules the old free-text input silently got wrong:

- **Directory-only people are offered, and say so** — "no login — cannot see the task"
  *before* assigning (D-PC-12), not a silent week later.
- **Warnings are shown, never enforced** — free text still commits; the server accepts any
  non-empty string, and a picker refusing what the API accepts is a UI inventing a rule.
- **The HR half follows the caller's grant** (§4.2), with `hr_visible` naming which
  emptiness an empty field is.

**"Assign work"** (person page) and **"Assign to…"** (capability search) route through the
*ordinary* create flow: `/projects?assignee=…` arms a visible, dismissible chip, and the
assignment applies through the same assignees PUT the panel uses.

## WS-28j3 — the rebalancing suggestions (§5.7.4)

`GET /people/dashboard/suggestions` + the Rebalancing section on the workload dashboard:

- Candidates per at-risk task, ranked by **skill × spare × availability** — the skill half
  IS §5.5's `score_skills`, asserted **by identity** in the tests (one ranker, never two).
  All three factors travel on the row; the rank is their product.
- The **idle↔behind join**: an idle person's pickups are viewer-scoped unassigned tasks
  matching their skills *plus* the at-risk tasks where they are a credible candidate.
- Every suggestion ends in the confirmed assign §5.7.4 requires — `confirm()` then the
  Projects app's ordinary assignees PUT, existing assignees riding along. The People
  modules hold no write path (fenced); no cross-task score of people exists (D-PC-14).

**Measured on the first weekend live run:** "spare hours this week" is zero for the whole
roster every Saturday — the harness crossed midnight into Saturday and the suggester went
empty. The helper window is now the **risk horizon** (`spare_hours_horizon`, today → +14d):
help is needed before the deadline, not before Sunday.

Also fixed en route: `live_ws28k` pinned Monday 2026-08-10 as a constant and went stale at
midnight — now date-relative. A live harness that only passes on the day it was written is
a calendar, not a check.

## Verification

- 21 hermetic backend cases across the two tickets; 147 in the affected sweep; 2211
  frontend tests; tsc, eslint, theming conformance green.
- Live (R8): `live_ws28e.py` (8 checks — the real `app_user` login join, tier projection,
  away warnings, ILIKE folding) and `live_ws28j.py` extended to 41 (the suggester over real
  rows: right holder, skilled colleague as candidate, three factors and their product,
  holder never their own helper). **All nine People harnesses green together.**
- No migration in either ticket.

## Before merge

- [x] R1 — no new migration numbers taken.
- [ ] `schema.generated.sql` regeneration still due (owner's act).

title: WS-28m + WS-28l + WS-28c: coverage & data quality, the Center landing, and the org chart
body:
Three slices of the People Center (spec §5.10, §5.9, §5.4), no migrations.

### WS-28m — skills coverage & data quality (`/people/quality`)
- **Coverage:** bus factor of one · title terms nobody declares · declared-but-never-on-a-task. The unused check uses the §5.5 ranker's **own** word boundary (`skill_pattern`, extracted from `score_skills` and asserted by identity) so a skill cannot be *matched* by the ranker and *unused* by the panel at once.
- The task scan is **viewer-scoped** through the dashboard's own `_scope` (D-PC-20) and states its basis (`tasks_scanned` / `tasks_partial` / `scope_partial`); an **empty scan proves nothing** rather than declaring every skill unused.
- **Quality:** no email · migration 148's `email_conflict` quarantine paid off (listed distinct from no-email) · statuses outside the vocabulary · managers who left · unmanaged roots · empty AI-relevant fields (`timezone`, `working_hours`, `skills`).
- D-PC-13/14 structurally: never writes, no ranking, every list alphabetical **in Python**, pre-cap totals travel in `counts`.
- Gated `admin:members:read` (§4.2's oracle rule, whole surface).

### WS-28l — the Center landing (`/people/overview`)
- §5.9's "projection, not new arithmetic" as **identity**: the load half is `get_dashboard`'s own rollup verbatim (its `away` names are "who is away this week"), the quality half is m's `collect`, and the module's one query is the headcount GROUP BY — department × status, **alumni included**, the single figure no other surface computes.
- `centers.ts` "People dashboard" entry flipped **live** per spec §9.

### WS-28c — the org chart (`/people/chart`)
- Flat node list, **directory tier** (fenced to exactly the ten directory fields); alumni off the chart, so a manager who left resolves to no-manager and the orphan surfaces as a **visible root** — the same fact m lists as `manager_alumni`. NULL-status rows stay on the chart (`status <> 'alumni'` is NULL for NULL).
- Tree + both cycle guards live in the client where the recursion is: `buildTree` terminates on any input (a loop severs its smallest-id member into a flagged root, deterministically); `wouldCycle` refuses a re-parent **before** the request.
- Center overlay: `org_group` ⋈ `app_user` on lowered email, tints through the `--cat-1…8` ramp (`categoricalAccent`), and the department/group mismatch is **stated, not smoothed** (both sides slug-normalized).
- Re-parenting: drag behind `can_manage`, human-confirmed, through `PATCH /api/people/{id}` — the People router's own class-checked door, no new write path.

### Adversarial review — two passes, ten findings, all fixed and re-measured live
The worst: 🔴 **the chart legend's `org_group` read had no tenant predicate** — `org_group` is EXEMPT from the generated RLS (it has carried `organization_id` since 138), so the query listed every customer's groups and fabricated department-mismatch warnings from another tenant's slugs. Predicate now explicit and failing closed; asserted hermetically on the SQL shape and **measured live with a second organization**.

Also: coverage missed every array-only skill (the importer bypasses `gtd_person_skills` — declared is now the union of both sources; the importer backfill is a standing board finding) · the landing numbered unmanaged roots from the capped list instead of the §5.10 count (fenced) · a NULL status told three stories on one screen (now one: its own `(none)` bucket, listed, kept in the working set) · a failed task scan rendered as "no visible tasks" forever with nothing logged (`scan_ran`/`scan_error` travel; four states, four sentences) · the chart drag wrote through the tasks-app door needing `feature:tasks` · `ChartRow` was nested in the page component (rebuilt the tree DOM per keystroke) · slug matching normalizes both sides (`r_d` vs "R&D").

Advisory, recorded not fixed: the server accepts a manager cycle from a stale tab — the chart labels and survives it.

### Found on the way
- A literal NUL byte in a template-literal separator — `sourceHygiene.test.ts` caught what would have made ripgrep treat the file as binary and every source-scanning fence silently half-read it.

### Verification
- `tests/unit`: test_people_quality (24) + test_people_overview (8) + test_people_chart (6) + full people/projects sweep green (357).
- Frontend: `tsc` clean, vitest **2242** passed incl. eight-rule conformance suite.
- **R8:** 30 live checks on the scratch Postgres 16 with the full ladder (`tests/live/live_ws28ml.py`) — including "a status outside the vocabulary cannot even be seeded" (148's CHECK is VALIDATED live) and the §5.9 agreement measured (`landing quality counts ARE the §5.10 counts`).
